O merciful One, Lord of the world, my dear friend: dwell with me. Without you there is no life even for a moment; cursed is living in the world (so). O Giver of soul, breath and peace, every moment I am a sacrifice (to you). O God, give (me) the support of your hand; O Gopal, lift (me) out of the pit. I am without virtue, of little understanding; you are ever merciful to the meek. Which of your comforts can I recall? In what way can I reflect (on you)? O keeper of those who come to your refuge, lover of your servants, lofty, inaccessible and infinite (Lord). All treasures and the eight siddhis are in the great relish of the Naam. Those with whom Keshav is well pleased, those servants sing the virtues of the Lord. Mother, father, son and kinsman: you are (all) to me; you are the support of my life-breath. In the Saadh Sangat Nanak worships (you), and has crossed the poisonous world. ॥5॥
203.3: Raag Gauri Bairagan, in the ghar of the Chhants of the Rahoe, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. There is some rare one who sings of the beloved Ram; (Such a one) attains every blessing and comfort, and the True One. The renunciate roams from forest to forest, searching; (but) only some rare one has love for the One. Those who have found the Lord are of great fortune. Brahma and the other gods, Sanak and his brothers, long for (him); the yogis, the celibates and the Siddhas yearn for the Lord; (but) only the one who is destined to receive (it) sings the virtues of the Lord. (I seek) the refuge of those who never forget (him). Only the very fortunate meet the Lord's Sants; for them there is no birth and death at all. In your grace, meet (me), my dear Beloved. O God, lofty and infinite, listen to (my) plea: Nanak begs for the Naam as (his) support. ॥4॥
Rahoa (plural rahoe): a Punjabi folk song sung with a long-drawn call, chiefly by women at weddings; this hymn is to be sung in the ghar (tune) of their chhants.
Sanak and his brothers: Sanak, Sanandan, Sanatan and Sanat Kumar, in the Puranas the four sons of Brahma, sages held to remain children for ever.
204.1: Raag Gauri Poorbi, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. O my mother, by what virtues may I come to meet the Lord of my life? I am without beauty, lacking in understanding and strength; I am a stranger, come from far away. I have no wealth, nor am I intoxicated with youth; take me, who have no protector, into yourself. Searching and searching, I have become a bairagan (detached in longing); I wander, thirsting for the sight of God. O God, merciful to the meek and compassionate, says Nanak, in the Saadh Sangat my burning has been quenched. ॥4॥
204.2: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Love for meeting God has taken hold of my mind. If by great fortune some Sant should meet me, I would fall at (his) feet and make my plea (to him). I would offer (him) my mind and set my wealth before (him); I have given up all the counsel of my own mind. Whoever tells me the story of the Lord God, I would follow him night and day, detached (from all else). When the seeds of past deeds sprouted, I met the Being who relishes (all) and yet stands apart. Meeting the Lord, the darkness was wiped away; O Nanak, (the soul-bride) asleep for birth after birth has awakened. ॥2॥
204.3: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Come out (of the net of attachment), O bird; remember the Lord: (these are your) wings. Meeting the Saadh (the Guru), take hold of the refuge of the Perfect One, and keep the jewel of Ram (the Naam) close to your heart. (There is) the well of wandering doubt; the relish of craving is (its) mire; and the noose of attachment is very sharp. The One who can cut it is Gobind, the Guru of the world: make your dwelling at his lotus feet. In your grace, O Gobind, beloved God, Master of the meek, hear (my) prayer: take hold of (my) hand, O Lord of Nanak; soul and body, all are your capital. ॥2॥
204.4: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). My mind remembers the Lord, (longing) to behold him. Thirsting in hope, I think of (him) day and night: is there some Sant who would bring me close (to him)? I would serve the servants of (that Sant's) servants, and plead with him in many ways. Setting them on the scales, I have weighed all comforts: without the sight of the Lord, they are all too light. (Whoever), by the grace of the Sant (the Guru), has sung the virtues of the Ocean of virtue has been brought back from wandering birth after birth. Meeting the Lord there is bliss and peace; O Nanak, life fulfils its purpose and bears fruit in good time. ॥2॥
204.5: Raag Gauri Poorbi, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. O my sovereign Lord, in what way may the Master of the world be met? (May I find) some Sant, giver of the peace of Sahaj, who would show me the way. The Unseen is within (each one), yet cannot be seen, (for) the veil of Haumai has been drawn between. In attachment to Maya the whole world sleeps; say, how is this doubt to go? (The soul and God) keep the same company and dwell in the same house, yet they do not meet and speak together, brother. Without the one thing, the five (senses) are wretched; that thing lies in a place beyond the senses' reach. He whose house it is put the lock on it, and entrusted the key to the Guru. (One) makes countless efforts, yet without the True Guru's refuge does not find (him). O True Guru, those whose bonds (you) have cut have fixed their love (on God) in the Saadh Sangat. (Their) five (senses) have joined together to sing the song of joy; O Nanak, there is no difference (between them and) the Lord, brother. O my sovereign Lord, in this way the Master of the world is met: Sahaj came, doubt fled in an instant, and the light, meeting the Light, merged (in it). ॥1॥
205.1: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Such an intimacy (with God) have I gained, (that) the merciful Beethal showed grace and pointed me to the True Guru. Wherever I look, there you alone are: this faith has come to me. To whom (else) should I make my plea and prayer, when Raghurai (the Lord himself) is listening? The Guru broke the bonds, anxiety was lifted, and then I found the lasting peace of Sahaj. What was to be will come to be in the end; where then is pleasure or pain to be seen? All the realms and universes have one abode (in God); the Guru drew back the veil and showed (it). The treasure of the Naam, (all) the nine treasures, is in one place (within); to what place outside, then, should one go? (As) from one gold, ornaments of many kinds are fashioned, (so the Lord) has made (this world) in many forms. Says Nanak, the Guru has dispelled doubt, and so has merged the essence in the Essence. ॥4॥
Raghurai: the king of the line of Raghu, Rama; in Gurbani, a name of the one God.
205.2: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Day and night, the span of life wears away. O mind, meet the Guru and set your affairs right. I make one request, my friends; listen: this is the time to serve the Sants. Earn the Lord's profit here before you depart, and your dwelling hereafter will be at ease. This world is steeped in vice and caught in doubt; the Brahm Giani (one who knows God) has crossed over it. Whom (God) has awakened and given the sweet essence of the Lord to drink, that one has come to know the story of the Indescribable. Buy the very thing you came for; through the Guru, the Lord comes to dwell within the mind. In your own home within, in the peace of Sahaj, you will find (his) mansion, and there will be no more round (of birth and death). O Knower of hearts, all-pervading Being, Creator, fulfil the longing of my mind. Servant Nanak begs for this one joy: make me the dust of the Sants' feet. ॥4॥
205.3: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Protect (me), O God, my father; I am without virtue; all virtues are yours. The troublemakers are five, and I am one, and poor; protect (me), O Protector. They torment (me) and harass (me) sorely; I have come into your refuge. I have tried countless ways of every kind until I am worn out, yet they will not let (me) go at all. Hearing one thing, I looked to (that) shelter: in the Saadh Sangat they are wiped out. By (your) grace I met the Sants, and from them I have gained courage. The Sants gave me the mantra that makes one fearless, and I have lived by the Guru's Shabad. Through the Bani that brings Sahaj and comfort, (I) have conquered those great troublemakers. Says Nanak, light has dawned in (my) mind; (I) have attained the state of nirvana. ॥4॥
206.1: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (O Lord,) you are that King who never perishes. Those who dwell with you are without fear; from where could this fear come (to them)? In one body you are puffed up with pride, in another humble; in one body you are all in all yourself, in another poor. In one body you are a learned pandit and a fine speaker, in another you have become a fool; in one body you are the one who takes hold of everything, in another you take nothing at all. What can the poor wooden puppet do? The one who makes it play knows (how). Whatever guise the showman makes it wear, that very costume it puts on. (God) has made many little chambers (bodies) of many kinds, and he himself has become (their) keeper. In whatever body he keeps (a being), in that it has to live; what can this poor (being) do? The one who made (all) this, who fashioned this whole design, he alone knows (it). Says Nanak, the Master is beyond the farthest beyond; (he alone knows) the worth of his own works. ॥5॥
206.2: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Give up, O (man), give up the relishes of Maya's poison. You are caught up (in them), O crazed fool, like a beast in a green field of crops. What you take to serve your own ends will not go with you even an inch. Naked you came, naked you will depart; you have wandered round the cycle (of births), and death has seized you. Watching again and again, O (man), the play of the safflower, you are lost and absorbed in it and laugh along with those (things). Day and night the thread (of life) wears thin, yet you have done nothing at all for your soul. Busy like this, on and on, you have grown old; your speech has failed and your body has wasted away. As that enchantress (Maya) bewitched (you in your) youth, your fondness for her does not lessen one whit. The Guru has shown me that the world is like this; so I have given up pride and fallen into (his) refuge. The Sant (the Guru) has told (me) the way to God; servant Nanak has made devotion and the Lord's praise firm (within). ॥4॥
206.3: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Without you, (O Lord,) who is mine? O my Beloved, support of my life-breath. You alone know the state within me; you alone are (my) friend who brings comfort. I have received every comfort from you, O my Master, beyond grasp and beyond weighing. I cannot describe your wonders, O treasure of virtues, giver of peace. O God, unreachable, beyond the senses, imperishable, you are known through the perfect Guru. (The Guru) has cut away (their) doubt and fear and made (them) pure, ever since (they) killed their Haumai; (their) dread of birth and death has ended through the sight (of the Guru) in the Saadh Sangat. I wash (the Guru's) feet and serve the Guru; I am a sacrifice (to him) a hundred thousand times, by whose grace (I) have crossed this terrifying world-ocean; servant Nanak has met the Beloved. ॥4॥
207.1: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Without you, (O Lord,) who can win your favour? Beholding your form, all are enraptured. In heaven, the netherworld, the mortal world and the spheres of the earth, that One alone pervades all. Calling (you) Shiv, Shiv, the giver of good, all join their palms; O Master, merciful to all, they cry out to you alone. O Master, your Name purifies the fallen; (you are) the giver of peace, pure and cooling. O Nanak, converse (about you) with your Sants is itself knowledge, meditation and glory. ॥2॥
Shiv here means the auspicious One, the giver of good, not the god Shiva.
207.2: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Meet (me), O Beloved of all beings. O God, what you have done has come to be. Through countless births (the soul) has wandered in many species, suffering pain again and again. By your grace (it) has obtained the human body; grant (me) your sight, O sovereign Lord. That alone has happened which pleased him; no one else has done anything. By your will (the being) lies lured by doubt and attachment; asleep, he does not wake. Hear my prayer, O Lord of my life, O Beloved, treasure of mercy, compassionate one. Save (us), O God, my Father; cherish those who have no protector. Whomever you have shown your sight, (you have shown it) through the Saadh Sangat. Show grace and give (me) the dust (of the feet) of the Sants; this is the comfort Nanak longs for. ॥4॥
207.3: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). I am a sacrifice to those (Sants) whose one and only support is the Naam. How far can the glory be counted of those servants who are dyed in the love of the Supreme Lord? Peace, Sahaj and bliss are in their company; there are no other givers equal to them. Those servants who thirst for (the Lord's) sight, they alone have come to save the world. Whoever falls into their refuge is carried across; in the company of the Sants all hopes are fulfilled. When I fall at their feet, then I live; in the company of (such) servants I am filled with joy. Be merciful, O God, (that) my mind may become the dust (of the feet) of the devotees. Kingship, youth, life-span, whatever is seen, all of it wanes in the world. The treasure of the Naam is ever new and pure; O Nanak, (the Sants) have earned this wealth of the Lord. ॥4॥
208.1: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). I have come from the Guru, having heard the way of Yoga; the True Guru has made me understand (it) through the Shabad. The (Lord) of the earth's nine regions pervades this body; I bow (to him) at every moment. The Guru's initiation is the earrings in my ears; I have fixed the One Formless Lord firmly (in my heart). The five disciples (the senses) have come together as one; (I) have brought them under the sway of the One. The ten (organs) have become detached and obedient; then I became a pure yogi. Burning doubt, I have smeared (myself) with its ashes; to see the One (in all) is my sect. I have made the peace of Sahaj my food, which the Master wrote on my forehead. I have set my seat where there is no fear; the unstruck Bani is my horn (singi). I have made reflection on the essence my staff; love of the Naam in the mind is my way. Such a yogi is met by great good fortune; he cuts away the bonds of Maya. I serve and worship that embodiment (of God); Nanak licks his feet. ॥5॥

Each line takes an item of the yogi's garb and discipline (earrings, ashes, the sect, the food of his order, the seat, the horn, the staff) and gives its inner form. The five disciples are the five senses; the ten are the five senses and the five organs of action.
208.2: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Listen, all of you: the Naam is a treasure beyond compare; meditate on it, O friends. The one to whom the Guru has given the Lord's medicine, his mind becomes pure. Darkness is gone from the body of the one (within whom) the Guru has lit the lamp through the Shabad. The net of doubt is cut for the one who has faith in the Saadh Sangat. He has crossed the world-ocean, deep and hard to swim, with the company of the holy as the ship. The hope of the mind is fulfilled (for one) who has met the Guru, (steeped in) the Lord's love. The devotees have gained the treasure of the Naam; in mind and body they are filled and content. O Nanak, the revered Lord gives (it) to the one whom he makes accept his Hukam. ॥3॥
208.3: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Show kindness and mercy, O Lord of my life; I, without a protector, (have come to) your refuge, O God. Give me your hand and save (me) in the blind well (of Maya); no cleverness or argument of mine (avails). You alone do and cause all to be done; you are all-powerful, there is no other. Your state and extent you alone know; they alone are your servants who have good fortune (written) on their foreheads. O God, you are steeped in your servants; like warp and weft you are joined with your devotees. (Your devotee,) crying Beloved, Beloved, longs for your Name and your sight, as the chakor's gaze (is fixed on) the moon. There is no difference at all between Ram and (his) Sant; (yet such) a servant is one among many hundreds of thousands and millions. The one in whose heart God has become manifest sings (his) Kirtan with the tongue, night and day. You are all-powerful, infinite, most high, the giver of peace, O God, the support of life. Show grace, O God, to Nanak, (that he may stay) in the company of those Sants. ॥4॥
The chakor: a bird said in Indian lore to gaze at the moon all night long.
209.1: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). O Sants, you are dyed in the Lord. O all-pervading Creator, stand by me to the end; O Giver, carry (me) through to the goal. Your secret you alone have known; you are the perfect Being, the Creator. Keep (me), helpless and meek, in your refuge; grant me liberation. To cross the ocean, your feet are the ship; you know your own ways. Those whom you, in your grace, keep with you, each of them crosses over. Here and hereafter you are all-powerful, O God; all is in your hands. O servants of the Lord, give me such a treasure as will go along with me. Grant virtue to (me), the one without virtue, (that) my mind may repeat the Lord's Name. O Nanak, (those who) meet the Lord by the grace of the Sant (the Guru) are cooled and fulfilled in mind and body. ॥4॥
209.2: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). I have merged in Sahaj, O Divine Lord; the True Guru has become merciful to me, O Divine Lord. Cutting the noose (of Maya), (the Guru) has made me (your) humble slave and set me to serve the Sants. I have become the worshipper of the One Name; to me the Guru has shown a wonder. Light has dawned and all is radiant; the Guru has made (his) knowledge manifest in my mind. I have drunk the Amrit of the Naam, and my mind is satisfied; (I) have settled in the fearless (Lord). Obeying (the Guru's) command, (I) have found every comfort, and have lost the very home of sorrows. When God the Master was fully pleased, he showed (me) all as the form of bliss. Nothing comes and nothing goes; the sovereign Lord has made it all a play. Says Nanak, the Master is unreachable, unreachable; the Lord's Name is the support of his devotees. ॥4॥
209.3: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). O mind, take the shelter of the perfect Supreme Lord, the Supreme God. Repeat the Name of the Lord who upholds the universes and their regions. O servants of the Lord, give up the mind's own counsel; peace is found by understanding (his) Hukam. Whatever God does, accept it as good; in comfort and in pain, meditate on him alone. The Creator saves tens of millions of the fallen in an instant; it takes him no time. The Master is the destroyer of the pain and sorrow of the meek; whomever he pleases, him he honours. He is mother, father and sustainer of all, the ocean of peace for soul and life-breath. Giving, that Creator runs short of nothing; (he,) the mine of jewels, fills all. The beggar begs for your Name, O Master; that (Lord) is within every heart. Servant Nanak is in the refuge of the one from whom no one (goes away) empty. ॥4॥
210.1: Raag Gauri Poorbi, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Do not ever forget the Lord, Har Har, in (your) mind. He gives every comfort here and hereafter; he cherishes every heart. He cuts away great hardships in an instant (for the one whose) tongue remembers the Naam. In the Lord's refuge are coolness, calm and peace; he puts out the burning fire. He protects (one) from the hell-pit of the womb and ferries (one) over the world-ocean. When (one) worships his lotus feet in the mind, he destroys the dread of Jam. He is the perfect Supreme Lord, the Supreme God, lofty, unreachable and infinite. Singing the virtues of the ocean of peace and meditating on him, one does not lose life in a gamble. (My) mind is sunk in lust, anger, greed and attachment, O Giver to the meritless; show grace and give (me) your own Name; Nanak is ever a sacrifice (to you). ॥4॥
210.2: Raag Gauri Cheti, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. There is no peace, O (friend), without devotion to the Lord. Win (the game of) this priceless jewel, the human birth; in the Saadh Sangat repeat (the Naam), even for a moment. Sons, wealth, the delights of a wife, many people have left (such) pleasures and gone. Fine horses, fine elephants, the joys of kingship, the fool leaves (them all) and departs naked. (One) swells with pride in a body (anointed) with perfume and sandal; that body rolls in the dust. Lured by attachment, (one) supposes (God) to be far off; says Nanak, (he) is ever present. ॥4॥
210.3: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). O mind, the Lord's Name is the support for crossing over (the world-ocean). The world is an ocean whose waves are dread and doubt; the Guru is the ship that carries (one) across. In Kalyug there is the blackness of (ignorance's) darkness; the lamp of the Guru's wisdom (alone) gives light (in it). The poison of Maya's vices has spread far and thick; only by dwelling again and again on the Lord's virtues have (people) been saved from it. Drunk on Maya, (man) lies asleep; on meeting the Guru, (his) doubt and fear were dispelled. Says Nanak, (the one who) has meditated on the One has seen (him) in every heart. ॥4॥
210.4: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (O God,) you alone are my Diwan (my master and support); with the Guru's support I serve you. By countless ways I could not find (you); (now) the Guru has taken me and set me in (your) service. I have slain the five quarrelsome (foes, lust and the rest); by the Guru's grace I have subdued (their) army. As reward and as wages I have received the Name of the One, (and in it are) peace, Sahaj, bliss and rest. Good are those who are God's servants; O Nanak, their faces are radiant. ॥4॥
Diwan: a high officer of a ruler's court, in whose service men worked for pay; the hymn is a picture of service: chaakar (servant), vajahu (wages) and bakhsees (reward).
211.1: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). O my soul, (take) the shelter of the Name; in all else that is done and caused to be done, there is the fear of Jam. By no other effort is (God) found; only by great good fortune is the Lord meditated upon. One may know a hundred thousand clever devices, (but) hereafter (in the Lord's court) one is not honoured even a sesame seed's worth. Deeds done with a mind of ego are houses of sand that the water washes away. (When) God, the merciful, shows mercy, then, O Nanak, the Naam is found in the company of the Saadh (the Guru). ॥4॥
211.2: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice, a hundred thousand times (to the Lord's Name); O brother, the Master's Name, the Name alone, is the support of life. (O God,) you alone are the One who does and causes all to be done; all beings and creatures rest on you alone as their support. O God, you are the master of sovereignty and of youth; you are Nirgun, and you are Sargun. Here and hereafter you are the protector; by the Guru's grace a rare one understands (this). O God, you are the knower of hearts, the all-wise; you alone are Nanak's prop and strength. ॥4॥
211.3: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Let us worship the Lord, Har, Har, Har. In the company of the Sants the Lord comes to dwell in the mind, and doubt, attachment and fear are brought under control. The Vedas, the Puranas and the Simritis say, (and it is) heard, that (the Lord's) servants abide highest of all. All other places are seen to be gripped by fear; (the Lord) has made the servants of Ram free of fear. (Beings) wander through the eighty-four lakh wombs; Gobind's people are not born and do not die. (My own) strength, intellect, cleverness and Haumai are gone; Nanak has grasped the refuge of the Lord's Saadh (the Guru). ॥4॥
211.4: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). O mind, let us sing the Name of Ram and (his) virtues. Let us serve the Lord day after day, and meditate on the Lord with every breath. In the company of the Sants the Lord comes to dwell in the mind, (and) sorrow, pain, darkness and doubt take flight. (Whoever) repeats the Lord's Name by the grace of the Sant (the Guru), that person is not gripped by sorrow. The one to whom the Guru imparts the mantra of the Lord('s Name) has been saved from the fire of Maya. O God, show mercy to Nanak, (that) the Lord's Name may dwell in my mind and in my body. ॥4॥
211.5: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Let us repeat with the tongue the Name of the One; (by it there is) peace and great joy here, and hereafter it goes with the soul and serves it. (By it) your sickness of ego is cut away; by the Guru's grace, practise Raj Jog. The person who has tasted the sweet essence of the Lord('s Name) has been rid of craving. (The one who) has found the Lord, the treasure of rest, does not run off in any direction again. The one to whom the Guru has given the Name of the Lord, Har Har, O Nanak, is rid of fear. ॥4॥
Raj Jog: kingship and yoga together, union with God while living the householder's life.
212.1: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The one who forgets the Name of Ram is the very one who suffers pain; those who join the Saadh Sangat and remember the Lord become rich in virtue and profound. The one in whose heart, through the Guru, (the) understanding (of Simran) has come holds the nine treasures and the siddhis in the palm of his hand. Those who know the Lord God as the Master (of all) lack nothing in their house. (The one who) has recognised the Creator has enjoyed the delights of every comfort. Those in whose house (the heart) the wealth of the Lord('s Name) dwells: says Nanak, in their company sorrow takes flight. ॥4॥
212.2: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (O man, your) pride is great, (but your) origin is so slight; (you are) not to stay (here), yet how tight is (your) grip! What the Vedas and the Sants forbid, O brother, with that very thing (you) are in love. As a gambler loses at the game of dice, (so you are losing); the senses have brought (you) under their sway and won (you). From love for the lotus feet of the One fully able to take away and to fill up, (you) are empty. O Nanak, in the Saadh Sangat (people) are saved; the treasure of mercy has given (it) to me. ॥2॥
212.3: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). I am the lowly servant of the Master; I eat the grain that God gives. Such, O brother, is our Master: in an instant he fashions (beings) and adorns them. Should I be pleasing to the Master, I would do (his) work, (and) sing songs of God's wondrous deeds and (his) virtues. I have come into the refuge of the Master's ministers (the Sants); beholding them, my mind has taken heart. The One alone is (my) prop, the One alone (my) support; servant Nanak has set himself to the Lord's work. ॥4॥
212.4: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Is there anyone who would break (my) Haumai, (and) turn this mind (of mine) back from this sweet (Maya)? Man has become ignorant: what is not (to last), that he longs for. (Within him) is a black and dark night; what is the way by which (the day of wisdom) may dawn? Wandering and wandering, (I) grew weary; in countless ways I searched. Says Nanak, (God's) mercy came, (and) the Saadh Sangat (became) a treasure for me. ॥2॥
212.5: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (God) is the wish-fulfilling jewel (Chintamani), compassion itself. The Supreme Lord is merciful to the lowly; in remembering him there is peace. Akal Purakh (the Timeless Being) is of unfathomable wisdom; hearing his praise, millions of sins have been destroyed. O God, treasure of mercy, show kindness, (that) Nanak may take the Name of the Lord, Har Har. ॥3॥
Chintamani: the jewel that, by tradition, grants whatever is wished for in the mind.
212.6: Raag Gauri Poorbi, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). O my mind, (it is) in God's refuge (that one) finds peace; on the day the giver of life and peace slips from memory, that day goes to waste. You have come as guests for one night, (yet) you build hopes for many ages. House, mansion and wealth, all that is seen, is like the shade of a tree. This body is mine, all this wealth is mine, the gardens, the lands and all the places (are mine; so saying), (man) has forgotten the Master, the Giver (of them all); in an instant (they) become another's. (Man) bathes and puts on white clothes, and applies perfume and sandalwood; (but if) he has not recognised the Fearless, Formless One, (it is all) like bathing an elephant. When (God) becomes merciful, he unites (one) with the True Guru; all peace is in the Lord's Name. (The one whose) bonds the Guru has undone is set free; servant Nanak sings the Lord's virtues. ॥4॥
An elephant, once bathed, throws dust over itself again.
213.1: Raag Gauri Poorbi, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). O my mind, let us ever repeat Guru, Guru, Guru; the Guru has made (this) jewel of a (human) birth fruitful; let us be a sacrifice to (his) sight. As many breaths and morsels as one takes, so many times let us sing (God's) virtues; (but only) when one's own True Guru is merciful is this understanding and wisdom found. O my mind, by taking the Name (you) will be freed from Jam's bonds, and the peace above all peace is found; by serving the True Guru, the Master and Giver, the fruit the mind longs for comes into one's hands. The Creator's Name is (your) beloved, friend and son; O mind, (it alone) goes along with you. Serve your own True Guru; (this Name) comes into one's lap from the Guru alone. The merciful Guru, God, has shown mercy, (and) all anxieties have perished; Nanak has found peace through the Lord's Kirtan, (and his) suffering is all erased. ॥4॥
213.2: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Only a rare one's craving is quenched. (Man) amasses crores, lakhs upon crores, (yet) does not hold back the mind; he toils only for more and more. (Though he has) beautiful women of many kinds, he sins in another's home; he cannot see bad from good. (Bound in) Maya's many bonds, he wanders, led astray, and has not sung (the praises of) the treasure of virtues; (his) mind toils only in the vices. The one on whom (the Lord) shows mercy, O brother, he alone dies while living, (and) crosses (the ocean of) Maya in the Saadh Sangat; O Nanak, that person succeeds at the Lord's door. ॥4॥
213.3: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). O brother, the Lord is the (true) delight of all. Some (take to) yoga, some to enjoyment, some to knowledge, some to meditation; some carry the staff (of the sannyasi). Some to chanting, some to austerities, some to worship, fire offerings and daily rites; some roam about (as wanderers). Some to the riverbank, some to the waters (of the tiraths), some to the study of the Vedas; O Nanak, devotion is dear (to the Lord). ॥3॥
The staff-bearers (dandi) are sannyasis who carry a staff. Ho in this hymn is a call (O brother) that also fills out the tune.
213.4: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (O God,) singing the praise of your virtues is my treasure. You alone are (my) delight, you (my) renown, you (my) beauty, you (my) joys; O God, my hope and my support are in you alone. You are (my) pride, you (my) wealth, you (my) honour, you (my) very life; the Guru has taken what was broken and joined it (to you) once more. You are in the home, you in the forest, you in the village, you in the wilderness; O Nanak, (God) is near, nearer than near. ॥3॥
214.1: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). I am drunk, drunk with the love of the Lord. That (essence of the Name) alone have I drunk, by that alone am I elated; the Guru gave it, bestowed it as a gift; with that alone (my) mind is dyed. That (Name) is (my) still, that the cooling cloth, that the cup, that (my) longing; in (my) mind I have come to know that peace alone. There is the play of Sahaj and the sport of bliss; the rounds (of birth and death) are over, and union (with the Lord) has come; Nanak is threaded on the Guru's Shabad. ॥3॥
Pocha: the wet cloth or plaster laid on the pipe of a still to keep it cool, so that the vapour condenses and drips.
214.2: Raag Gauri Malwa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Take the Name of the Lord, my friend, take it; the road ahead is hard and fearsome. Serve (the Lord), keep on serving him, serve him always; death dwells right beside you. Serve the Saadh (the Guru), O brother; (so) the net of Jam is cut. Those who performed fire offerings, sacrifices and pilgrimages saw their vices only grow, caught in Haumai; they must taste both hell and heaven, and are born again and again. The city of Shiv, the city of Brahma, the city of Indra: none of these is a place that lasts. Without the Lord's service there is no peace; O brother, the Saakats keep coming and going. As the Guru has taught, so have I proclaimed it aloud. Says Nanak, listen, O mind: sing the Kirtan, and deliverance comes. ॥4॥
Shivpuri, Brahmpuri, Indrapuri: the heavens of Shiv, Brahma and Indra, which the Puranas promise as the reward of fire offerings, sacrifices and pilgrimages.
214.3: Raag Gauri Mala, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. With a child's (simple) understanding I have found peace, O brother; since meeting the Guru, joy and grief, loss and death, pain and pleasure are all alike to (my) mind. As long as I kept thinking and scheming (by my own wits), so long was I full of sorrows; when I met the merciful, perfect Guru, then bliss came in Sahaj. The more clever deeds I did, the more bonds fell (on me); when the Saadh (the Guru) placed his hand on (my) forehead, then I was set free. As long as I kept saying mine, mine, so long did poison hem (me) in; when (I) offered mind, body and intellect to the Master, then I slept in Sahaj. As long as I walked carrying the bundle (of attachment), so long did I pay fines; casting down the bundle, I have met the perfect Guru; then Nanak became free of fear. ॥4॥
214.4: Raag Gauri Mala, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). O sister, I have given up my own will (of liking and disliking), given it up; on meeting the Guru I have renounced it, renounced it. Accepting the will of Gobind, (I have) every comfort, bliss, joy and delight. Respect and (another's) arrogance are both alike (to me), for I have laid my forehead at the Guru's feet; wealth brings no elation, misfortune no grief; love for the Master has taken hold (of me). In every dwelling, O sister, is the one Lord; in the wilderness too (he) is seen; I have become fearless; the Sant (the Guru) has cast out (my) doubt; the all-knowing (Lord) pervades all. Whatever the Creator has brought about has not seemed ill to (my) mind; in the Saadh Sangat, by the grace of the Sants, (my) sleeping mind has woken. (O Lord,) servant Nanak has fallen into your shelter, has come to your refuge; (he) has enjoyed the love of the Name and the delight of Sahaj, and no sorrow has touched (him) since. ॥4॥
215.1: Raag Gauri Mala, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). I have found the ruby, found the jewel within (my) mind; my body has grown cool and my mind has grown cool, merged in the True Guru's Shabad. Hunger is gone, all thirst is gone, every anxiety is forgotten; the perfect Guru has laid his hand upon (my) forehead; I have conquered my mind, and (with it) the whole world. Within my heart I am satisfied and full; now I have ceased to waver; the True Guru has given (me) an inexhaustible treasure; it never runs short, O brother, and never runs out. Hear a wonder, O brother: the Guru has given (me) such understanding that when the veil was lifted and I met the Master, I forgot (all) envy of others. This wonder cannot be told; only the one who has tasted it knows it. Says Nanak, the light of the True One has dawned (within me); the Guru has brought the treasure (of the Name) and kept it in (my) heart. ॥4॥
215.2: Raag Gauri Mala, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). In the refuge of the Sovereign Lord, Ram, one is saved. All the worlds are realms of Maya; (beings) fall from them again and again to the ground. Having pondered the Shastras, the Simritis and the Vedas, the great ones have said this: without devotion to the Lord there is no release, and no one has ever found peace. (Though one) amass the wealth of the three worlds, the waves (of greed) do not subside; without devotion to the Lord, where can (one) find steadiness? (He) roams on, watch after watch. Indulging in many pleasures that charm the mind, (one's) desire is never fulfilled; burning and burning, (the fire) is never quenched; without the Name all is in vain. Repeat the Name of the Lord, my friend; this alone is the highest, the perfect peace. The Saadh Sangat does away with birth and death; Nanak is the dust (under the feet) of the Lord's servant. ॥4॥
215.3: Raag Gauri Mala, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Who can make this way (of things) plain to me? (Only one) who has become (one with) the Creator can make it known. In ignorance this (being) has done something (else); it has practised no japa and no austerity; it has sent this mind running in the ten directions. By what deeds is it bound? (It says:) I am the master of mind, body, wealth and land; I own this, this is mine; in doubt and attachment it sees nothing; hobbles (such as tie an animal's legs) are on its feet. What could it do then, when it was nothing at all, when the One, the stainless, formless God, did everything himself? He alone knows his own works, who has made this creation. Says Nanak, the Doer is he himself; the True Guru has removed (my) doubt. ॥4॥
216.1: Raag Gauri Mala, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Without the Lord, all other rites are in vain. Japa, austerity, self-discipline, the rites one performs: all these are robbed on this side (of the journey). One keeps to fasts, vows and restraints, (yet) has not received half a shell for them. What goes along ahead is something else, O brother; these were of no use there. Bathing at places of pilgrimage and roaming the earth, one finds no place ahead; such ways are of no use there; by them he only wins the trust of people. (One) recites the four Vedas by heart, (yet) the Mansion (of the Lord) is not reached ahead; (one who) does not grasp the one pure Word (the Name) only wears himself out in vain. Nanak speaks this thought; whoever lives by it crosses over: serve the Guru, meditate on the Naam, and cast pride out of your mind. ॥4॥
Robbed on this side: as a traveller's goods are plundered on the road, these deeds are lost before they reach the Lord's court. Aadh: half a cowrie shell, the smallest of values.
216.2: Raag Gauri Mala, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). O Madho, (grant) that we may utter Har, Har, Har with our mouths. Nothing can be done by us, O Lord; as you keep us, so we live. What can (this being) do? What is it able to do? What lies in the hands of this poor one? To whatever you attach it, to that it is attached, O my perfect Master. Show grace, O Giver of all; attune (me) in love to your one form. Nanak's prayer to the Lord is this: make (me) repeat your Name. ॥2॥
216.3: Raag Gauri Majh, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. O Damodar, my King, merciful to the meek, millions you have made your own and set to your service; to love your devotees is your age-old way, and you have kept to it; you pervade every place. How may I behold my Beloved? What is the good deed (that wins his sight)? (It is to be) the handmaid of the Sants and to serve at their feet; I would offer up this soul (to him), and be a sacrifice, a sacrifice; bowing low and lower still, I would fall at his feet. One, a pandit, searches the books and the Vedas; one turns renunciate and bathes at places of pilgrimage; one sings songs and melodies and the Kirtan; (but) I meditate on the fearless Name of the Lord. My Master has become merciful; the fallen have become pure, clinging to the Guru's feet; cutting away doubt and fear, (the Guru) has made (them) free of enmity; O Guru, you have fulfilled the hope of (my) mind. Whoever has found the Name is rich; whoever has meditated on God is honoured; whoever has the company of the Saadh (the Guru), all their deeds are good; O servant Nanak, (such a one) is absorbed in Sahaj. ॥5॥
217.1: Raag Gauri Majh, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Come to my (home), my beloved Ram; night and day, with every breath, I remember (you); falling at the Sants' feet, I give them a message (for you): without you, how is one to cross over? In your company I delight; in the woods, in every blade of grass, in the three worlds (seeing you), there is peace and supreme bliss; the bed (of my heart) is lovely, and this mind is in bloom; beholding (your) sight, this peace is found. Washing (the Sants') feet, I would serve (them) every day; (that would be my) worship of the Divine, my offering of flowers, my bow; as the slave of slaves, I would repeat the Naam; (O Sants,) convey this plea to the Master. My longing is fulfilled; my mind and body have turned green; beholding (his) sight, every sorrow has been dispelled; repeating and repeating the Name of the Lord, Har Har, I have crossed over; O Nanak, this unfading peace is (now) enjoyed. ॥4॥
217.2: Raag Gauri Majh, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Hear, O hear, my Friend, beloved companion of my mind: (my) mind and body are yours, and this life too is offered up (to you); never slip from (my) mind, O God, support of (my) breath; (I am) ever in your refuge. The One meeting whom the mind comes alive, O brother, that Lord, Har Har, is found by the Guru's grace. Everything is God's; all places are God's; I am ever a sacrifice to God. Only one of great good fortune repeats this treasure (of the Name); (that one's) love is fixed on the Name of the one Stainless Lord. (Whoever) has found the perfect Guru has erased all sorrow and has sung (God's) virtues at all hours. O Lord, your Name is a jewel, a precious thing; you are the true banker, (your) devotee the trader; the wealth of the Lord is (the devotee's) capital, and true is (his) trade; servant Nanak is ever a sacrifice (to you). ॥4॥
217.3: Raag Gauri Majh, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. O Creator, you are my great pride; you are my great pride. By your strength I dwell in peace; the true Shabad is my pass. (The mortal caught in Maya) has come to know all things, yet having heard them he keeps silent; enticed by Maya, he has never found awareness. (Someone) gives him riddles and hints, and he has seen those (things) with his own eyes; but he is such a greedy fool that he does not listen at all to what is said. Why should I count one, two or four? The whole (world) is cheated by one and the same relish. Only one here and there delights in the Name; rare is the place (of the heart) that is inhabited (by the Name). The devotees are radiant at the True One's door, and rejoice day and night. They are dyed in the love of the Supreme God; servant Nanak is a sacrifice to them. ॥4॥
218.1: Raag Gauri Majh, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Your Name, dear Lord, is the breaker of sorrows; your Name is the breaker of sorrows. At all hours it should be worshipped: such is the wisdom of the perfect True Guru. The heart in which the Supreme Lord dwells is the beautiful place; Jam's servant does not come near (one whose) tongue sings the Lord's virtues. I have not known the way of serving you, nor do I know how to worship you; O Life of the world, my Master, unreachable and unfathomable, your shelter is (all I have). When the Lord of the world became merciful, grief and anguish fled. Not even a hot wind touches those whom the True Guru himself has protected. The Guru is Narayan, the Guru is the merciful Lord; the Guru is the true Creator. With the Guru pleased, everything has been gained; servant Nanak is forever a sacrifice (to him). ॥4॥
218.2: Raag Gauri Majh, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The Lord, Ram, Ram, Ram, Ram: repeating (his Name), all tasks are fulfilled. Repeating (the Name of) Ram, Gobind, the mouth has become pure. He from whom one hears the Lord's praise is one's brother and friend. He in whom are all good things, all fruits and all virtues: why should that Gobind be forgotten from the mind, remembering whom sorrows depart? (He is the One) holding to whose hem one lives (in spirit) and is carried across the world-ocean; meeting in the Saadh's company, one is delivered, and faces shine in (the Lord's) court. The praise of Gopal is the very form of life; it is the capital of the Sants. O Nanak, by repeating the Naam they are saved, and at the True One's door they are acclaimed. ॥4॥
218.3: Raag Gauri Majh, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). O my soul, sing the Lord's sweet virtues; sing the Lord's sweet virtues. Imbued with the True One, even one without a place has found a place. All other tastes are insipid; (through them) body and mind become insipid; whatever one does without the Supreme God, a curse on that life. Holding the hem of the Saadh (the Guru), this world (-ocean) is crossed. When the Supreme Lord is worshipped, the whole family is saved. He alone is companion, kinsman and good friend who gives the Lord's Name (to keep) in the heart; who wipes out all faults and does good (to others). The Lord's feet are the treasures: (they are my) wealth, treasury, dwelling and home. O God, Nanak is a beggar at your door; he begs for you as his gift. ॥4॥
219.1: Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Raag Gauri, by the Ninth Guru (Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji). O holy ones, give up the pride of the mind. Lust and anger are the company of the wicked: flee from it day and night. (One who) holds pleasure and pain both as alike, and honour and dishonour too; who stays aloof from joy and grief: he has recognised the essence in the world. (One who) gives up both praise and slander, and seeks the state of nirvana, where desire is stilled — O servant Nanak, this is a hard game; only a rare one has come to know it through the Guru. ॥2॥
219.2: Raag Gauri, by the Ninth Guru (Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji). O holy ones, Ram has made (such) a creation that one perishes while another deems (himself) everlasting; this wonder cannot be described. In the grip of lust, anger and attachment, the mortal has forgotten the Lord's being; he has taken the false body to be true, like a dream in the night. Everything that is seen perishes, as a cloud's shadow does. O servant Nanak, (one who) has known the world to be false remains in Ram's refuge. ॥2॥
219.3: Raag Gauri, by the Ninth Guru (Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji). The Lord's praise does not enter the mortal's mind. Day and night he stays absorbed in Maya; tell me, how can he sing (the Lord's) virtues? With possessive love for sons, friends and Maya, in this way he binds himself; this world is false like a mirage (the deer's thirst), yet seeing it he rises and runs after it. The Master who is the source of (worldly) enjoyment and of liberation: the fool forgets him. O servant Nanak, only one in millions is granted the devotion of Ram. ॥2॥
219.4: Raag Gauri, by the Ninth Guru (Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji). O holy ones, this mind cannot be held in check. It dwells with fickle craving; therefore it does not stay steady. Harsh anger too is within the heart itself, and it has made all sense be forgotten; it has stolen everyone's jewel of wisdom; against it no one has any power. All the yogis have failed in their efforts; the learned have grown weary of singing praises. O servant Nanak, when the Lord became kind, then every way came right. ॥2॥
219.5: Raag Gauri, by the Ninth Guru (Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji). O holy ones, sing the praises of Gobind. (You) have been given a priceless human birth; why waste it in vain? The Lord purifies the fallen and is kin to the lowly; come into his refuge. Remembering him, the terror of Gaj (the elephant) was ended; why do you forget him? Giving up pride and the attachment of Maya, then fix your mind on Ram's worship. Says Nanak: this is the path of liberation; become Gurmukh, and you will find it. ॥2॥
Gaj: in the Bhagavat Purana, an elephant (Gajendra) seized in the water by a crocodile; when his strength failed he called on the Lord and was set free.
219.6: Raag Gauri, by the Ninth Guru (Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji). O mother, let someone counsel (this) strayed mind. Though it hears the Vedas, the Puranas and the way of the holy, it does not sing the Lord's praises even for an instant. Having gained the human body, so hard to obtain, it passes its life in vain. The attachment of Maya is a forest of great peril, and (the mind) grows fond of that very thing. God, who is ever with (it) within and without: with him it forms no love. Says Nanak: know him alone to be liberated in whose heart Ram dwells. ॥2॥
220.1: Raag Gauri, by the Ninth Guru (Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji). O holy ones, in Ram's refuge is rest. This is the merit of reading the Vedas and Puranas: that one remembers the Lord's Name. Greed, attachment, Maya, possessiveness and the indulging of the senses, joy and grief: the one whom these do not touch is the very image of God. Heaven and hell, nectar and poison, all these (are alike to him), and so are gold and a copper coin; to whom praise and slander are the same, and greed and attachment likewise; the one whom these, pain and pleasure, do not bind: know him to be a giani (one who truly knows). Says Nanak: know that mortal to be liberated who lives in this way. ॥3॥
220.2: Raag Gauri, by the Ninth Guru (Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji). O mind, why have you gone mad? Day and night the lifespan wears away, but (the mortal) does not know it; in greed's company he has become hollow. The body you have taken as your own, and your fine house and wife: none of these is yours, O (mind); reflect, consider and see. You have gambled away your jewel of a life, and have not known the way of Gobind. Not for an instant have you been absorbed in (his) feet; your life has run out in vain. Says Nanak: that man alone is happy who sings the praises of Ram's Name; the whole world besides is lured by Maya, and does not reach the fearless state. ॥3॥
220.3: Raag Gauri, by the Ninth Guru (Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji). O heedless man, fear sin. The One who is merciful to the lowly and destroys all fears: fall into his refuge. He whose praises the Vedas and Puranas sing: hold his Name in your heart. The Lord's Name is the purifier in the world; remembering him again and again, wash away all sins. You will not gain the human body again; make some effort for (your) liberation. Says Nanak: sing (the praises of) the Lord who is all compassion, and cross over the world-ocean. ॥2॥
220.4: Raag Gauri Guareri, Ashtapadis, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). There is one God, Ik Oankar, the One who pervades all and is ever the same; his Name is Sat (the One who truly is); he is the Creator, the Being who dwells in all, realised by the Guru's grace. Reflection on the pure Naam is (for me) the treasures and the siddhis; with the poison (of Maya) killed, (I see) the Perfect One filling all; in the Pure (Name) the trikuti (the mind's fretting) is gone; the Guru's counsel has proved of use within my soul. In this way, dwelling on Ram, the mind has been won over; through the Guru's Shabad I have recognised the collyrium of divine knowledge. (The mind) has come to prize the one peace (of the Name), and (it) has joined me in Sahaj; the pure Bani has ended doubt; (with the Name) we have turned deep red; Maya's colour is a (fleeting) pale red; (his) glance of grace has come, and the poison (of Maya) has been held back. (My attention) has turned around (from Maya); dying while alive, I have awakened; dwelling on him through the Shabad, the mind is attached to the Lord; gathering the nectar (of the Name), I have cast the poison far off and given it up; dwelling in (his) love, the fear of Jam has fled. Cravings for taste, quarrelling and pride have ceased; by the Hukam of the Infinite, the mind is dyed in the Lord; the rites of caste and of (worldly) honour are left behind; (his) gracious gaze has fallen, and the peace of the soul has taken hold. Without you, (O Lord,) I see no friend. Whom shall I serve? To whom shall I give my heart? Whom shall I ask? At whose feet shall I fall? By whose teaching shall I stay lovingly attuned? I serve the Guru; at the Guru's feet I fall; I practise devotion and am absorbed in the Lord's Name; love is (my) teaching, (my) initiation and (my) food; by (his) Hukam, through the union he ordains, I reach my own true home. Pride is gone; there is peace in the soul's meditation (on him); the light has dawned, and (my) light has merged in (his) Light; what is written (on the heart) is not erased: the Shabad is its mark; I have known both the Creator and the creation to be the Creator himself. I am no pandit, nor clever, nor wise; I do not stray, nor am I led astray by doubt; I do not speak idle talk; I have recognised (his) Hukam; through the Guru's teaching Nanak is merged in Sahaj. ॥8॥
221.1: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). The mind is an elephant, roaming in the forest of the body; the Guru is its goad; when the true Shabad is the mark (upon it), it is adorned at the King's gate and is held in honour. (The Lord) is not recognised through cleverness; unless (the mind) is slain, how is (his) worth to be found? Within the house (of the heart) is nectar, but the thief carries it off; no one says no (to him); the one whom (the Lord) himself protects, he blesses with honour. Fires (of craving) beyond all counting are gathered in one place; they were quenched with water (of the Name) when the Guru gave understanding; I have gained it by giving my mind, and joyfully I sing (his) virtues. As (the Lord) is at home, so is he outside; then, sitting in a cave, how could I say he is any different? The Fearless One is just the same in ocean and on mountain. Say, who can slay the one who has died (to self)? What fear, and of whom, can the fearless have? Through the Shabad he recognises (the Lord in) the three worlds. One who has only spoken has merely told a tale; one who has understood has recognised (him) in Sahaj; seeing and reflecting, my mind is won over. Glory, beauty and liberation lie in praising the One; there itself the Niranjan abides; he pervades his own home, his own place. Many a sage praises (him) with love, with pure body and mind, holding the True One in the heart. O Nanak, worship the Lord, day after day, for ever. ॥8॥
222.1: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). The mind does not die (to itself), nor is the work (of life) fulfilled, (for) the mind is in the grip of the demons (the vices), of evil intellect and of duality. When the mind is won over through the Guru, it becomes one (with God). The Lord, who is beyond the three qualities, comes under the sway of virtues; one who casts off self reflects on him. The mind gone astray thinks of vice upon vice; the mind gone astray takes a load (of sin) upon its head. When the mind is won over, it becomes one with the Lord, the One Creator, Ekankar. The mind gone astray goes into the house of Maya; entangled in lust, it does not stay in its place. O mortal, worship the Lord, with your tongue steeped in (the Name's) savour. Fine elephants and fine horses, gold, sons and wife: in much anxiety (over them) one loses the bout in the arena (of life) and departs. It is a gambler's game, in which the pieces stay unripe. Hoarding wealth, vices arise; joy and sorrow stand (ever) at the door. Peace comes in Sahaj by repeating (the Name of) Murari in the heart. When (the Lord) casts his glance of grace, he brings (one) into union (with himself); (then,) gathering virtues, one burns away faults through the Shabad, and through the Guru obtains the treasure of the Naam. Without the Name, every pain comes to dwell (in one); the foolish manmukh's mind dwells in Maya. Wisdom through the Guru (comes to one) for whom it is written from the start, by (the Lord's) grace. The fickle mind runs, and runs again; the True and Pure One is not pleased by (this) filth. O Nanak, through the Guru one sings the praises of the Lord. ॥8॥
222.2: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Living in Haumai, one finds no peace; the mind's own counsel is false; he (the Lord) is true. All who are fond of duality come to ruin; (yet) one does what is written (for him) from the start. Such a gambler is the world, as I have seen it: forgetting the Name, it begs for every comfort. Only if the Unseen is seen can (he) be described; to speak (of him) without seeing goes for nothing. Through the Guru he is seen, in Sahaj and in love, when the mind is set on service and attuned in love to the One. Begging for comfort, one only gets more pain, (for) one strings a garland of every vice. Without the One, the false find no release; the Creator makes and makes (all), and himself watches over it. One who puts out the fire of craving through the Shabad, and, in Sahaj and in love, (puts out) the doubt of duality too, enshrines the Naam in his heart through the Guru's teaching, and through the true Bani sings the praises of the Lord. The True One is within the body; love (for him) comes through the Guru. Without the Name, (the mind) has no home of its own. The Beloved Sovereign is ruled by love; when he casts his glance of grace, then one understands the Name. Attachment to Maya is nothing but entanglement; the manmukh is filthy, despised and fearsome. When one serves the True Guru, the entanglement ends, and the nectar of the Naam, peace for ever, stays with one. Through the Guru one understands, and attunes oneself in love to the One; one dwells in one's own home (within) and merges in the True One; one brings (the round of) birth and death to a halt; one gains this wisdom from the Perfect Guru. I speak (of him), but no end (of him) is reached; I have asked the Guru and seen: there is no other door. Pain and pleasure come by his will, by his command: so says lowly Nanak, attuned (to him) in love. ॥8॥
223.1: Raag Gauri, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Maya, which breeds duality, dwells in the minds of the world; lust, anger and pride (born of it) bring ruin. Whom shall I call a second? There is none; in all is that One, the Immaculate. The evil intellect of duality speaks of two; (one in its grip) comes and goes, and dying, stays apart (from God). In earth and sky I see no second, nor in woman or man, nor in all the world. I behold the light of the lamps (of the world), the sun and the moon: within all, through and through, is the ever-young Beloved. In his grace (the True Guru) has fixed my mind (on God); the True Guru has made me understand the One. Through the Guru the One, the Immaculate, is known; when duality is killed, he is recognised through the Shabad. The Hukam of the One alone prevails in all the world; from the One has all creation come. The paths are two, (but) know that the Master (of both) is One; through the Guru's Shabad, recognise (his) Hukam. (He who is) in all forms and colours, and in (every) mind: says Nanak, I praise that One alone. ॥9॥
The two paths: in the commentaries, the Guru's way and the way of the self-willed mind; Gurbani elsewhere names them liv and dhaat, attunement to God and running after Maya.
223.2: Raag Gauri, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). If one does the deeds of the spirit, then he is a true (yogi); what can the unripe one know of the secret of liberation? That yogi reflects on the (true) way who kills the five (vices) and holds the True One in his heart. One within whom (the Lord) makes the Truth dwell knows the worth of the way of Yoga. To him sun and moon, home and wilderness, are alike; his practice is the praise (of God), as natural to him as his everyday deeds. He begs for one alms alone, the one Shabad; (in him) wisdom, meditation, the (true) way and the Truth awaken. He stays steeped in the fear (of God) and does not stray outside (it); who can tell the worth of one who stays attuned in love? (The Lord) himself unites (him) and ends (his) doubt; by the Guru's grace he attains the supreme state. (He) serves the Guru and reflects on the Shabad, and kills Haumai: this is the finest practice. Repetition (jap), austerity, self-restraint, the reading of the Puranas: says Nanak, (all these lie in) accepting the Infinite One. ॥8॥
Sun and moon: heat and cold, harsh treatment and kind alike; to the yogis the words also name the right and left breath channels (pingala and ida).
223.3: Raag Gauri, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). (Such yogis) have taken up forgiveness; good conduct and contentment are their vow; no disease afflicts them, nor any torment from Jam; they are set free, (one with) God, who is without form or outline. What fear can there be for the yogi (for whom) he alone is in the trees and plants, in the home and outside? Fearless is the yogi who meditates on the Immaculate (Lord); night and day he stays awake, and keeps his mind attuned to the True One; that yogi is dear to my mind. In the fire of Brahm (God) he burns up the net of death; (the fear of) old age and death is gone, and he casts off pride; he crosses over himself, and carries his ancestors across as well. One who serves the True Guru is the yogi; one who stays steeped in the fear (of God) becomes fearless; as is the one he serves, so he becomes. The Name of the Fearless One makes a person pure; he makes masters of the masterless; I am a sacrifice (to him). (For me) there is no birth again and again: I sing (his) praises. He knows the One within and without; through the Guru's Shabad he recognises his own self; through the true Shabad he bears the mark (of acceptance) at (the Lord's) door. One who dies through the Shabad comes to dwell in his own home (within); he neither comes nor goes, and his hopes come to an end; through the Guru's Shabad, the lotus (of his heart) blossoms. Whoever is seen (in the world) is let down in his hopes, (gripped by) the poison of lust and anger, by hunger and thirst. O Nanak, rare are those found who stand detached. ॥8॥
224.1: Raag Gauri, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). If one meets such a servant (of the Lord), peace comes; pain is forgotten, and that one finds the True One. Beholding (his) sight, the understanding is made whole; the dust of (his) feet is (as) the bath at the sixty-eight places of pilgrimage. (His) eyes are satisfied, the thread of (his) attention held on the One; (his) tongue, (tasting) the Lord's sublime savour, is made pure. Truth is (his) conduct, and within (his) heart is (the Lord's) service; (his) mind is fulfilled in the Lord, unseen and unfathomable. Wherever I look, there is the True One; without understanding, the unripe world quarrels. When the Guru explains, understanding dawns; only some rare one understands (this) through the Guru. In your mercy, O Protector, save (us); without understanding, (people) have become beasts, out of step (with life's true rhythm). The Guru has said there is no other, no second; tell me, seeing whom should I worship another? God has upheld the three worlds for the Sants' sake; one who recognises his own self reflects on this essence. One in whose heart is the True One, in whom true love dwells: Nanak humbly prays: I am his servant. ॥9॥
224.2: Raag Gauri, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Brahma grew proud, and did not know (the Lord); when the calamity of (losing) the Vedas fell upon him, he repented; when he remembered God, only then was his mind convinced. Pride is such an evil in the world; whoever meets the Guru, (the Guru) removes his pride. King Bali, proud of his wealth (Maya), performed sacrifices, swollen with a heavy load of pride; without asking his guru, he went down to the netherworld. Harichand gave alms and won renown; (yet) without the Guru he did not find the end of the inscrutable (Lord). (God) himself leads astray, and himself gives understanding. Harnakhash, of evil mind, was a doer of evil deeds; God, Narayan, is the destroyer of pride: he showed mercy and saved Prahlad. Ravan, a fool, went astray in his heedlessness; Lanka was plundered, and his heads went with it; he perished in pride, without love for the True Guru. Sahasbahu, Madhu and Kaitabh, Mahikhasur, and Harnakhash, whom (the Lord) seized and tore apart with his nails: these demons were slain, without the practice of devotion. Jarasandh and Kalyavan were slain; Raktabij and Kalnem were torn apart; slaying the demons, (the Lord) carried the Sants across. He himself, as the True Guru, reflects on the Shabad; in the love of another, the demons were slain; and the Gurmukhs, through true devotion, he carried across. Duryodhan drowned, and lost his honour; he did not know the Lord, who alone is the Creator; for the pain he gives the Lord's servant, a man is consumed, and the pain is his own. Janmejay did not understand the Guru's word; lost in doubt, how could he find peace? He erred by no more than a sesame seed, and then repented. Kans, Keshi and Chandur, none was (their equal in might); (but) they did not recognise the Lord, and lost their honour; without the Master of the world, no one can save (anyone). Without the Guru, pride cannot be erased; through the Guru's teaching, (attuned) to the Lord's Name, one gains righteousness and patience; O Nanak, singing (God's) praises, one receives the Name. ॥12॥
Brahma: by the Puranic story, a demon carried off the Vedas while Brahma slept, and they were restored only when he turned to God.

Bali: a demon king who held sacrifices to win Indra's throne; heedless of his guru Shukra's warning, he granted Vishnu, come as the dwarf Vaman, the land of three steps, and was sent down to the netherworld. Harichand (Harishchandra): a king famed for truth and giving, who, put to the test by the sage Vishvamitra, gave away his kingdom and was sold into servitude.

Sahasbahu (the thousand-armed king), Madhu and Kaitabh, Mahikhasur, Jarasandh, Kalyavan, Raktabij and Kalnem: proud kings and demons of the Puranas, slain by Parashuram, Vishnu and Durga, or through Krishna (Jarasandh by Bhim at his side).

Duryodhan: the eldest of the Kauravas in the Mahabharata, slain in the war with the Pandavas. Janmejay: Parikshit's son, who by tradition set aside the counsel of his guru Vyas and was struck with leprosy. Kans, Krishna's uncle, and Keshi and Chandur, his champions, were slain by Krishna.
225.1: Raag Gauri, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). (If) I rub perfume and sandalwood upon my body, (and) put on silk and silken robes and wear them out, (still) without the Lord's Name, where could I find peace? Why should I wear (fine clothes)? Why put them on and show them off? Without the Master of the world, where can I find peace? (If I had) rings in my ears and a string of pearls at my neck, a red quilt and red flowers (strewn upon it), without the Master of the world, where would I seek peace? (If there were) a beautiful woman with lovely eyes, decked with the sixteen adornments and very dear (to me), without remembering the Master of the world, there is ever ruin. Gates, houses, palaces, a comfortable bed, on which a gardener strews flowers day and night: without the Lord's Name, that body is a home of suffering. Fine horses, fine elephants, lances, martial music, armies, deputies, royal servants, all this show: without the Master of the world, (such) displays are false. (If) I am called a Siddha, and summon the riddhis and siddhis, (if) I set a crown and a royal cap upon my head and a canopy over it, without the Master of the world, where would I find the Truth? (If) I am called a khan, an emperor, a king, (and) order (my servants) about, it is a false show; without the Guru's Shabad, (life's) purpose will not be fulfilled. Haumai and the sense of mine are forgotten through the Guru's Shabad; through the Guru's teaching I have known Murari in my heart. Nanak humbly prays: (I have come) to your refuge. ॥8॥
225.2: Raag Gauri, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). (He serves) the One alone, and knows no other; he gives up the bitter ills of the world's show; through love he meets the True One, and in the True One he becomes true, O brother. Such is the Lord's devotee, his servant: singing the Lord's praises, he meets (him), and washes away (his) filth. The (heart-)lotus of the whole world is upside down; the fire of evil counsel burns the world through and through; he alone is saved who reflects on the Shabad of the Guru. The bumble-bee, the moth, the elephant and the fish, and the deer die, each bearing (the fruit of) what it has done; absorbed in craving, they did not see what is real. The lover of women thinks only of lust, and anger destroys all who are given to vice; forgetting the Name, they lose their honour and their understanding. The manmukh lets his mind waver toward another's home; the noose is about his neck, and he is caught up in worldly affairs; through the Guru, singing the Lord's praises, he will be set free. As a widow gives her body to a stranger, and, for lust or for money, puts her mind in another's power, (yet) without her husband she is never satisfied; (so it is with the soul without the Lord). One reads and reads books, the Simritis, the recitations, reads the Vedas and the Puranas and hears their compositions, (yet) without being dyed in the (Lord's) sweet essence, the mind plays out many a show. As the chatrik thirsts in love for the water, as the fish delights in the water, O Nanak, (the Lord's devotee) is satisfied, drinking the Lord's sweet essence. ॥8॥

Each of these creatures dies through one sense: the bumble-bee through smell, shut in the closing lotus; the moth through sight, in the flame; the elephant through touch, lured into a pit by a she-elephant; the fish through taste, on the bait; the deer through hearing, drawn by the hunter's music.
226.1: Raag Gauri, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). One who wears himself out with hath (forced austerities) is not counted (in the Lord's account); he puts on many a garb and smears (his body with) ashes; forgetting the Name, he repents in the end. Keep the dear Lord in your mind, and you will have peace in your mind; forgetting the Name, you will suffer the pains (inflicted by) Jam. (One absorbed in) perfume, sandalwood, aloeswood and camphor is intoxicated with Maya, and the supreme state is far (from him); when the Name is forgotten, all is falsehood, utterly false. Lances, martial music, the throne, salutes: (with these) craving only grows, and lust takes hold; without begging (them) of the Lord, there is neither devotion nor the Name. In wrangling and in pride there is no meeting with God; giving your mind, you will receive the Name, the source of ease; in the love of another there is ignorance, the source of pain. Without money there is no buying in the shop; without a ship there is no way across the ocean; without serving the Guru there is loss upon loss. Praise, praise to the one (the Guru) who shows the way; praise, praise to the one who makes the Shabad heard; praise, praise to the one who unites (us) in union (with the Lord). Praise, praise to the One to whom this soul belongs; through the Guru's Shabad, churn (it) and drink the Amrit; in his will, he will give you the glory of the Name. Without the Name, how can I live, O mother? May I keep repeating (your Name) night and day, (staying) in your refuge. O Nanak, steeped in the Name, one gains honour. ॥8॥
226.2: Raag Gauri, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Acting in Haumai, the wearers of religious garb have not known (the Lord); through the Guru, rare is the one whose mind is won over to devotion. Crying I, I, the True One is not found; when Haumai goes, the supreme state is attained. In Haumai, kings march out time and again (against one another); in Haumai they are ruined; they are born, die and come again. Haumai is driven out (of one who) reflects on the Guru's Shabad; he gives up the fickle intellect, and slays the five (passions). Those with the True One within come home to Sahaj; knowing the Sovereign (Lord), they attain the supreme state. Truth becomes his way of life, and the Guru removes his doubt; he sits in deep absorption in the home of the Fearless One. Dying while crying I, I, what does one gain? One who meets the Perfect Guru puts an end to that strife. Whatever there is, all of it is nothing; the Gurmukhs, receiving (divine) wisdom, sing (the Lord's) praises. Haumai binds (beings) in bonds and makes them wander (in births); O Nanak, through devotion to the Lord one finds peace. ॥8॥
227.1: Raag Gauri, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). First of all, Brahma himself came into the house of death; (going down) to the netherworld, he did not find (the end of) the lotus of his birth; he did not heed the command; lost in doubt, he went astray. Whoever is born is slain by death; the Lord has kept me safe, for I have reflected on the Guru's Shabad. Maya has enticed all the goddesses and gods; death does not let (anyone) go without service of the Guru; he (the Lord) alone is imperishable, beyond sight, beyond knowing. Sultans, khans and kings are not to remain; one who strays from the Name must bear the pain (inflicted by) Jam; my support is the Name; as you keep me, so I remain. Chaudharis and kings: none has a lasting abode (here); bankers die, heaping up Maya and money; give me, O Lord, the wealth of the Amrit Name. Subjects, headmen, village heads and chiefs: none is seen to stay unmoved in the world; unstoppable death strikes the false upon the head. The One alone is unmoving, the truest True One; he who made and fashioned (the world), he alone destroys it all; when he becomes known through the Guru, then there is honour. Qazis, sheikhs, fakirs in religious garb call themselves great, (but) the pain of Haumai is in their bodies; death does not let (them) go without the support of the True Guru. The net of death lies in the tongue and in the eyes; death is in the ears, (when one) hears words of poison; without the Shabad, (all) are robbed day and night. When the True One dwells in the heart through the Lord's Name, death cannot even eye (one who) sings (his) praises; O Nanak, through the Guru one merges in the Shabad. ॥9॥
By the Puranic story, Brahma was born on a lotus that grew from Vishnu's navel; to find its root he went down its stalk into the netherworld, and could not reach its end.
227.2: Raag Gauri, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Those who speak the truth, with not a mustard seed of falsehood in them, who, through the Guru, walk in the Hukam of the Master of the Will, remain detached (from Maya), in the refuge of the True One. One who settles in the home of Truth is not eyed by death; but the manmukh, through attachment, suffers the pain of coming and going. Drinking the Amrit and speaking (the praise) of the Ineffable, one stays (in the true home); sitting in one's own home within, one finds the home of Sahaj; steeped in the Lord's essence, one can say: this is (true) peace. The way of living by the Guru's teaching is steadfast; it does not waver; by the Guru's teaching one utters (the Name of) the Lord, (rooted) in the True One, in Sahaj; he drinks the Amrit and churns out the essence. (I) beheld the True Guru and took (his) teaching; I offered (him) mind and body, and took (that teaching) deep within; I came to know (his) state and extent, (and) recognised my own self. The Name of the Stainless One is the finest food; (living on it, one) becomes a true Param Hans, (lit by) the Light of the Infinite; wherever I look, there is the One Creator, Ekankar. (Such a one) stays detached, leaning on no (worldly) support; (remembering) the One True Lord is his only practice; serving at the Guru's feet, he has attained the supreme state; his mind is won over from within itself, and the wandering of ego has ended. Who is there whom this way has not carried across? The Lord's praise has carried the Sants and devotees across. I have found God; I have sought no other. In the true mansion the Guru has made the Unseen seen (by me); that mansion is unshakeable; no shadow of Maya falls (there); content in the True One, (I) have been rid of doubt. Those in whose minds that True One has come to dwell — their company is found through the Guru; O Nanak, in the True Name (their) filth is washed away. ॥9॥
Param Hans (the supreme swan): of old, the name of a renunciant of the highest order; the swan is held to separate milk from water. Here it is the one whose food is the Naam.
228.1: Raag Gauri, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). One whose mind is dyed in the Lord, in the Name — on rising at dawn, one should have the sight of him. If you do not repeat (the Name of) Ram, it is your misfortune; age after age our God, Ram, is the Giver. The one who repeats (the Name of) Ram by the Guru's teaching is perfect; in that heart the unstruck music plays. Those who are (absorbed) in devotion to Ram, in love of the Lord — God, in his grace, has protected them. Those in whose hearts that Lord, Har Har, (dwells) — by having the sight of them, peace is found. The One pervades all beings; (yet) the proud manmukh wanders through births again and again. He alone understands (this) who finds the True Guru; he kills his Haumai, and through the Guru's Shabad finds (God). How can (one) know the union of the lower (soul) with the higher (God)? Through the Guru this union is found, and the mind is won over. (O God,) bless us sinners, devoid of virtue, with virtue; when God becomes merciful, servant Nanak crosses over. The sixteen Ashtapadis of Gauri Guareri.
228.2: Raag Gauri Bairagan, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. As a herdsman (guards) his cows, so you guard (your creatures) with care; day and night you nourish and protect (them), and grant the peace of the soul. Keep (me) safe here and hereafter, O Merciful to the meek; (I have come) to your refuge; look on (me) with your glance of grace. Wherever I look, you are pervading; keep (me), O Keeper. You are the Giver, you yourself the Enjoyer; you are the prop of the breath of life.
