Without reflection on divine wisdom, (one is tossed) down and up by the record of past deeds; without praising the Lord of the world, the darkness does not end. I have watched the world perish in greed and pride; by serving the Guru, God is found, and the true door of liberation. The mansion of the Infinite is in one's own home within; he is beyond the beyond. Without the Shabad no one stays steady; one who understands (this) finds peace. What did you bring, and what will you take away? (Yet) you are caught in the net of Jam; like a bucket bound fast to a rope, (you go up) to the sky and (down) to the underworld. If, by the Guru's teaching, the Naam is not forgotten, honour comes in Sahaj; within is the treasure, the Shabad; meeting (him), one sheds self-conceit. When God casts his glance of grace, (one) merges in the embrace of the Virtuous One. O Nanak, (that) union is never broken; (such a one) earns the true profit. ॥8॥
229.1: Raag Gauri, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). If, by the Guru's grace, you come to understand (this), then (your account) is settled: in every heart (dwells) the Name of the Stainless One; he is my Master. Without the Guru's Shabad there is no release; reflect and see. Though (you) perform a hundred thousand rites, without the Guru there is darkness. The blind, bereft of understanding — what can be said to them? Without the Guru the path is not seen; how is (the journey) to be carried through? (Such a one) calls the false coin true, and knows nothing of what the true is worth; the blind man is named an assayer — such is the strange way of Kalyug. (The world) calls the sleeper awake, and the wakeful asleep; it calls the living dead, and does not weep for the dead. The one coming (to God's path) it calls gone, and the one gone (from it) it calls arrived; it calls what is another's its own, and what is its own does not please it. It calls the sweet bitter, and the bitter sweet; (people) slander the one dyed (in the Lord's love) — this is how I have seen Kalyug. (People) serve the handmaid (Maya), and the Master is not seen (by them); if the water of a pond is churned, no butter comes of it. Whoever grasps the meaning of this verse, he is my Guru. O Nanak, one who recognises his own self is (one with) the Lord, beyond all and without limit. (God) himself is at work in all; he himself has led (beings) astray in doubt. By the Guru's grace it is understood that God is contained in all. ॥9॥
229.2: Raag Gauri Guareri, Ashtapadis, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. The mind's Sutak is the love of another (than God); strayed in (this) doubt, (people) keep coming and going. The manmukh's Sutak never departs, as long as he is not drenched, through the Shabad, in the Lord's Name. All is Sutak, as much as there is of attachment and the visible world; (caught in it, one) dies and is born, over and over. Sutak is in fire, in air and in water; Sutak is all the food that (people) eat. Under Sutak, no rite or worship can be done; imbued with the Naam, the mind becomes pure. By serving the True Guru, Sutak departs; (then one) neither dies nor is born, and death does not devour (him). Let anyone search the Shastras and Simritis and see: without the Name, no one is set free. In all four ages the Naam is supreme, (found) by reflecting on the Shabad; in Kalyug the Gurmukh reaches the far shore. The True One does not die, nor come and go; O Nanak, the Gurmukh remains merged (in him). ॥8॥

Sutak: in Hindu custom, the impurity held to fall on a household for some days after a birth (or a death), during which no worship or rites are performed. The Guru uses the word for the mind's impurity, the love of another.
229.3: Raag Gauri, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Through the Guru, (the Lord's) service is the prop of the breath of life; keep the dear Lord in your heart, held to your breast; through the Guru there is glory at the True One's door. O Pandit, read (the Name of) the Lord, and give up your vices; through the Guru, cross the terrifying world-ocean. Through the Guru, Haumai departs from within; through the Guru, no filth comes to cling (to the mind); through the Guru, the Naam comes to dwell in the mind. Through the Guru, (one's) deeds and dharam come to rest in the True One; through the Guru, (one) burns away pride and duality; through the Guru, imbued with the Naam, one is at peace. Awaken your own mind, and understand him; you instruct the people, (but) no one listens; understand through the Guru, and there will be lasting peace. The manmukh is full of show and cleverness; whatever he does is not accepted; he comes and goes, and finds no resting place. The manmukh performs rites, in great pride; like a crane he sits every day in meditation; when Jam seized him, only then did he repent. Without serving the True Guru there is no liberation; by the Guru's grace that Lord is met; in all four ages the Guru is the Giver (of the Name). For the Gurmukh, caste, honour and greatness lie in the Naam alone; (he) has torn apart and cast away the daughter of the ocean (Maya). O Nanak, without the Name all cleverness is false. ॥8॥
The daughter of the ocean: in the Puranas, Lakshmi, goddess of wealth, rose when the gods and demons churned the ocean; here, Maya.
230.1: Raag Gauri, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). O brothers, study the dharam of this age: the perfect Guru has given full understanding: here and hereafter the Lord's Name is the companion. Read (the Name of) Ram, and reflect (on him) in your mind; by the Guru's grace, remove (the mind's) filth. By argument and opposition (God) is not found; in the love of another, mind and body grow insipid; through the Guru's Shabad, fix your loving attention on the True One. This world is soiled with Haumai; it bathes daily at places of pilgrimage, (yet) its pride does not go; without meeting the Guru, Jam brings it to ruin. True is that person who kills his Haumai; who, through the Guru's Shabad, destroys the five (passions); he himself swims across and carries all his families across. Through attachment to Maya, the Juggler (God) has staged (the world's) show; the blind manmukhs stay clinging (to it); the Gurmukhs, their attention fixed (on God), remain untouched. The wearer of religious garb puts on many guises; (but) within him is craving, and he goes about in pride; he does not know himself, and loses the game (of life). Wearing (holy) garments, he plays clever; through attachment to Maya he is gravely misled by doubt; without serving the Guru he suffers great pain. Those imbued with the Naam are ever detached; even within the household, their loving attention stays fixed on the True One. O Nanak, great is the fortune of those who serve the True Guru. ॥8॥
230.2: Raag Gauri, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Brahma is the root of the study of the Vedas; from him the gods were born, (caught) in attachment and craving; they wandered in the three qualities, and did not come to dwell in their own home (within). The Lord has saved us, and brought us to meet the True Guru, (who) has made devotion, night and day, and the Lord's Name firm (within us). The word of Brahma (the Vedas) is of the three qualities, an entanglement (of Maya); reading it, (the pandits) hold forth in dispute, and Jamkaal strikes them on the head; they do not recognise the essence, and tie up bundles of straw. The manmukhs, through ignorance, are set on the wrong path; they have forgotten the Lord's Name, and hold fast to many rites; in the love of another, they have drowned in the world-ocean. One who is beholden to Maya calls himself a pandit; steeped in the poison (of Maya), he suffers great pain; around his neck is the noose of Jam, and death torments him always. Jamkaal does not come near the Gurmukh; through the Shabad he burns away Haumai and duality; dyed in the Naam alone, he sings the Lord's praises. Maya, (as) a maidservant, does the work of the devotees; whoever falls at (their) feet attains (the Lord's) mansion; he is ever pure, and remains merged in Sahaj. Those who listen to the telling of the Lord's praises are seen to be the wealthy in the world; all bow before them, and revere them night and day; (for) in Sahaj they dwell on the True One's virtues in their minds. The perfect True Guru made (one) hear the Shabad, erased (his) three qualities, and fixed (his) mind on the fourth (state); O Nanak, killing (his) Haumai, (the Guru) united (him) with Brahm (God). ॥8॥
231.1: Raag Gauri, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). (The pandit) reads Brahma's Veda, and holds forth in dispute; within him is the darkness of tamas, and he does not know himself; he finds God only when he utters the Guru's Shabad. I serve the Guru, and then death does not devour (me); the manmukhs, in the love of another, are devoured (by it). Through the Guru, (even) sinful mortals have succeeded; through the Guru's Shabad they are delighted within, in Sahaj; they have found my God; through the Guru's Shabad they have succeeded. Those whom the True Guru has joined, God himself has united (with him); they are dear to the mind of my True God; in Sahaj and in love, they sing the Lord's praises. Without the True Guru, (people) are led astray by doubt; the blind manmukhs eat poison always; they bear the rod of Jam, and suffer pain always. Poor Jam cannot even look at one who is in the Lord's refuge; killing his Haumai, he keeps his loving attention on the True One; he stays ever attuned to the Lord's Name. Those who serve the True Guru are spotless and holy; joining (their) mind to (the Guru's) mind, they have conquered the whole world; in this way, my friend, there will be well-being in you (too). Whoever serves the True Guru obtains (this) fruit: the Naam (dwells) in his heart, and he sheds self-conceit from within; he makes the Shabad, the unstruck Bani, resound (within). Who, who has not succeeded through the True Guru, my brother? through devotion they have succeeded, and won glory at (the Lord's) door; O Nanak, greatness lies in the Name of Ram. ॥8॥
Seedhe (sijhe): succeeded, their life brought to fulfilment; reedhe: delighted, won over.
231.2: Raag Gauri, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). One who expounds only the three qualities: his doubt does not go; his bonds do not break, and he does not obtain liberation; the giver of liberation in the world is the True Guru. Through the Guru, the mortal sheds his doubt; with loving attention fixed on the Lord, the strain of Sahaj wells up (within). Over the heads of (those caught in) the three qualities, death holds sway; they do not remember the Name of the Creator; they die and are born, again and again, time after time. From a blind guru doubt does not go; leaving the Root (God), (his followers) cling to the love of another; drunk on poison, (one) is absorbed in poison. Taking Maya to be the root (of life), creatures wander astray; in the love of another they have forgotten the dear Lord; the one on whom (God) casts his glance of grace attains the supreme state. Within him is the Truth, and outwardly too he deals in Truth; Truth does not stay hidden, though one may keep it hidden; the wise understand (this), in Sahaj and in love. The Gurmukh keeps his loving attention fixed on the True One; through the Shabad he burns away Haumai and Maya; my True God unites him in (his) union. (One whom) the True Guru, the Giver, makes hear the Shabad keeps the running (mind) safe, and holds it back and still; from the perfect Guru he obtains understanding. He himself is the Creator, who created the world and (himself) destroyed it; apart from him there is no other at all; O Nanak, through the Guru, a rare one understands (this). ॥8॥
232.1: Raag Gauri, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). The Gurmukh obtains the priceless Naam; he serves the Naam alone, and through the Naam remains merged in Sahaj; with his tongue he ever sings the Amrit Naam; the one on whom (God) shows grace obtains the Lord's sweet essence. Night and day I repeat (the Name of) the Lord of the world in my heart; through the Guru I attain the supreme state of peace. In (their) hearts there is peace, and light has dawned, who through the Guru sing of the True One, the treasure of virtues; they ever become the servants of the servants' servants; in household and family they remain ever detached. A rare Gurmukh becomes liberated while yet alive; he alone obtains the supreme treasure; erasing the three qualities, he becomes pure; in Sahaj, (absorbed) in the True One, he meets that very God. Attachment and love for family no longer hold (him) when that True One comes to dwell in the heart; through the Guru, the mind pierced (with love) becomes steady; he recognises (God's) Hukam, and understands that True One. (O God,) you are the Creator; for me there is no other; I serve you, and from you comes honour; if you show grace, I may sing of that God; the jewel of the Naam is the light in all the world. (One to whom) through the Guru the Bani has come to taste sweet: his heart within blossoms, and his loving attention stays fixed night and day; by (God's) grace he meets the True One in Sahaj; it is by perfect great fortune that the True Guru is found. Haumai, possessiveness, evil-mindedness and pain are destroyed when the Name of Ram, the treasure of virtues, (dwells) in the heart. Through the Guru, with God's praise, the intellect awakens, when (God) pervades the heart, and (one) dwells at (his) feet. He alone obtains the Naam to whom (God) gives it; the one whom (God) unites (with him) through the Guru sheds his self-conceit; he enshrines the True Name in his heart; O Nanak, in Sahaj he merges in the True One. ॥8॥
232.2: Raag Gauri, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). (One who) has set the mind right within itself, in (God's) fear, in Sahaj and in love, (who) has dyed the mind with the Shabad, fixing his loving attention, dwells in his own home (within), in God's will. Serving the True Guru, pride departs, and Govind, the treasure of virtues, is found. The mind becomes detached when, through the Shabad, it takes in (God's) fear; my pure God is pervading everywhere; by the Guru's grace, one whom (he) unites meets (him). The servant of the Lord's servants finds peace; in this way my Lord God is found; by the Lord's grace (he) sings the praises of Ram. Cursed is a long life in which love for the Lord's Name does not take hold; cursed is the comfortable bed with a wife, (if it is) only the pitch darkness of attachment; fruitful is the birth of those whose support is the Naam. Cursed, cursed are the home and family in which there is no love for the Lord; he alone is my friend who sings the praises of that Lord; without the Lord's Name I have no other. I have obtained liberation and honour from the True Guru; I have meditated on the Lord's Name, and erased all pain; with loving attention fixed on the Lord's Name, there is lasting bliss. Meeting the Guru, I have come to awareness of the body; the whole fire of Haumai and craving has been put out; anger is destroyed, and (I) have taken hold of forgiveness. The Lord himself shows grace and gives the Naam; a rare Gurmukh receives (this) jewel; Nanak sings the praises of the Lord, unseen and unfathomable. ॥8॥
233.1: Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Raag Gauri Bairagan, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Those who turn their faces from the True Guru, those faithless ones, look evil; bound (by attachment), they are beaten night and day, and do not get the chance again. O Lord, O Lord, show your grace and keep (me) safe; O God, O Lord, unite (me) with the Sat Sangat, that (I may) cherish the Lord's virtues in my heart. Those devotees are dear to the Lord who, through the Guru, walk in love; giving up self-conceit, they serve, and remain dead while living. He to whom body and breath belong: his service is laid on (our) heads; why should we forget him from the mind? Let us keep the Lord enshrined in the heart. When the Naam is found, honour is gained; when the Naam is taken to heart, there is peace; the Naam is obtained from the True Guru, and that God is met by (his) grace. Those who turn their faces from the True Guru wander, and never find rest; neither earth nor sky will bear them; they lie in filth and rot. This world, given the thugs' drug of attachment, is led astray by doubt; those who have met the True Guru: Maya does not come near to touch them. Those who serve the True Guru are beautiful, having shed the filth of Haumai; those dyed in the Shabad are pure, and walk in the True Guru's will. O Lord God, you alone are the Giver; you yourself forgive and unite (us with you); your servant Nanak has come to your refuge; as it pleases you, so set (him) free. ॥8॥
234.1: Raag Gauri Poorbi, Karhale, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. O camel-mind, O wanderer in foreign lands, how may one meet the Lord, the Mother? (One who) found the Guru through perfect fortune, the Beloved came and embraced (him). O camel-mind, meditate on the True Guru, the great Being. O thoughtful camel-mind, meditate on the Name of the Lord, Ram; where the account (of deeds) is called for, the Lord himself will set (you) free. O camel-mind, (you were) utterly pure; the filth of Haumai has come and stuck (to you). The beloved Husband is plainly present with (you), in (your own) home; (yet the soul,) parted (from him), suffers blows. O camel-mind, my beloved, search for the Lord in (your) heart, and search until you find (him). He is not found by any (other) means; it is the Guru who shows the Lord in the heart. O camel-mind, my beloved, keep your attention fixed lovingly on the Lord, day and night. (Then) you will go and find your home in the palace of delight; the Guru unites (you), brings (you) into union with the Lord. O camel-mind, you are my friend: give up hypocrisy and greed. The hypocrite and the greedy are beaten down; Jam's club deals out (their) punishment. O camel-mind, my very life, cast off filth, hypocrisy and doubt. The Guru has filled the pool of the Lord's Amrit (to the brim); joining the Sangat (and bathing there), the filth is washed off. O camel-mind, my beloved, listen to one teaching of the Guru: this attachment to Maya is spread (all around), (yet) at the end none of it goes along. O camel-mind, my friend, (whoever) took the Lord's (Name) as provisions (for the journey) gained honour; in the Lord's court he was robed (in honour), and the Lord himself took him in his embrace. O camel-mind, with faith in the Guru, do the work (he bids), through the Guru. Make your plea before the Guru, O servant Nanak: (O Guru,) unite me with the Lord. ॥10॥
Karhala: a camel (Sanskrit karabha). The mind is likened to the camel that roams foreign lands under its load, ever far from its home; from it these two hymns are named Karhale.
234.2: Raag Gauri, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). O thoughtful camel-mind, reflect, and look with care: the forest-dwellers have grown weary roaming the forests; (you,) through the Guru's teaching, behold the Husband (Lord) in your heart. O camel-mind, cherish the Guru, Govind, (in your heart). O thoughtful camel-mind, the manmukhs are caught in the great net (of Maya); a Gurmukh soul is free, cherishing the Name of the Lord, Har Har. O camel-mind, my beloved, seek out the True Guru in the Sat Sangat. Clinging to the Sat Sangat, let us meditate on the Lord; the Lord, Har Har, will go along with you. O fortunate camel-mind, the Lord looks (on one) with a single glance of grace; only if he himself sets (one) free is (one) freed; cherish the True Guru's feet. O camel-mind, my beloved, cherish the Light within the body. The Guru has shown the Naam, the nine treasures; the merciful Lord has bestowed (this) gift. O camel-mind, you are restless: give up your fearful cleverness. Cherish the Name of the Lord, Har Har; when the end comes, the Lord (alone) will set (you) free. O fortunate camel-mind, cherish the jewel of (divine) wisdom. (Whoever) has taken the sword of the Guru's wisdom in hand has struck Jam dead with (that sword,) the death of Jam. The treasure is within, O camel-mind, (yet) you wander in doubt, searching outside. (One who) met the Guru, the perfect Being, found the Lord, the Friend, right with (him). O camel-mind, steeped in (the world's) pleasures, cherish the Lord's love always. The Lord's love never fades; serve the Guru and cherish the Shabad. We are birds, O camel-mind; the Lord, the timeless Being, is the tree (we rest on). The fortunate have found (him) through the Guru; O servant Nanak, cherish the Naam. ॥10॥
235.1: Raag Gauri Guareri, Ashtapadis, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). There is one God, Ik Oankar, the One who pervades all and is ever the same; his Name is Sat (the One who truly is); he is the Creator, the Being who dwells in all, realised by the Guru's grace. When this (person) is proud in his mind, then he goes about crazed, a stranger (to all). When he became the dust (of the feet) of all, from then on he recognised the all-pervading Lord (Ramaiya) in every heart. The fruit of humility is the ease of Sahaj; my True Guru has given me (this humility) as a gift. When he thinks someone is bad, then everyone sets snares for him. When he put an end to mine and yours, from then on no one bears him enmity. When he held fast to his own (interest) alone, then he is in heavy trouble. When he recognised the Creator, then no burning envy at all is left in him. When he made his attachment (to the world) fast, he comes and goes (in birth and death), ever watched by Jam. When all his doubts were destroyed, he is no different from the Supreme Lord. When he took distinctions to be something (real), from then on (come) pain, punishment and torment. When he understood the One alone, from then on he came to understand everything. When he runs about, a beggar for Maya, he is never sated, and his thirst never leaves. When he turned away from her, Kaula (Lakshmi, Maya) rose and followed close behind him. When, showing his grace, the True Guru met (him), the lamp was lit in the temple of the mind; understanding came of victory and defeat, and then the worth of this house (the body) was known. The One alone does and causes all to be done, everything; he himself is the understanding, and he himself reflects and discerns. He is not far; he is near, with all. O Nanak, the Lord of all wonders is true and worthy of praise. ॥8॥
236.1: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Through serving the Guru one is joined to the Naam; (the Naam) comes to him on whose forehead (good) fortune is written. In his heart he (the Lord) comes to dwell, and (his) mind and body become cool and steady. Sing such Kirtan, O my mind, as will be of use to you here and there (hereafter). Repeating his Name, fear and misfortune depart, and the wandering mind comes to rest; repeating his Name, pain never touches one again; repeating his Name, this Haumai flees; repeating his Name, the five (passions) come under control; repeating his Name, Amrit is gathered in the heart; repeating his Name, this craving is quenched; repeating his Name, one succeeds in the Lord's court; repeating his Name, millions of wrongs are wiped out; repeating his Name, (people) become the Lord's Saadhs; repeating his Name, the mind becomes cool; repeating his Name, one rids oneself of all filth; repeating his Name, the jewel, the Lord, is found, and one grows so close to the Lord that one never leaves (him) again; repeating his Name, (one gains) a dwelling (as) in many Baikunths (heavens); repeating his Name, one dwells in peace and Sahaj; repeating his Name, this fire (of craving) does not touch one; repeating his Name, this death does not cast its eye on one; repeating his Name, your forehead will be spotless; repeating his Name, all pain is lifted; repeating his Name, no difficulty arises; repeating his Name, one hears the unstruck melody; repeating his Name, one gains this spotless renown; repeating his Name, the (inverted) lotus (of the heart) turns upright. The Guru has cast his kindly glance upon all; (but) he in whose heart (the Guru) places the mantra of the Lord has made the unbroken Kirtan his food, his churi (sweet crumbled bread); says Nanak, (this comes to him) whose True Guru is perfect. ॥8॥
236.2: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (One who) holds the Guru's Shabad within his heart, breaks off company with the five (passions), keeps the ten organs (of sense and action) under control, in his soul the light shines. Such firmness comes in him on whom is the kindness and grace of that God. To whom friend and foe are one and the same, all his speaking is (divine) wisdom, all his hearing is the Naam, all his seeing is meditation (on God). In Sahaj he wakes, in Sahaj he sleeps; whatever comes to pass comes to pass (for him) in Sahaj; in Sahaj is (his) sorrow, and in Sahaj too (his) laughter; in Sahaj (his) silence, and in Sahaj too (his) chanting (of the Name). In Sahaj (he takes his) food, in Sahaj (he gives his) love; in Sahaj all (his) concealment has gone; in Sahaj came the Saadh's company; in Sahaj he met the Supreme Lord face to face. In Sahaj he is at home, in Sahaj detached; in Sahaj the duality in (his) body has been destroyed. One in whose mind joy has arisen through Sahaj has met (the Lord), the Supreme Bliss. In Sahaj he has drunk the Amrit, the Naam; in Sahaj he has given (others) the gift (of the Naam); his soul has delighted in the discourse of Sahaj, and the Imperishable has come to dwell with him. In Sahaj the steady seat has pleased him; in Sahaj he has sounded the unstruck Shabad; in Sahaj the tinkling chime (of bliss) is lovely; in his home (within) the Supreme Lord is pervading. One on whom (the Lord's) grace has fallen in Sahaj has met the Guru in Sahaj, and (gained) the true dharma. Only one in whom Sahaj has arisen knows (it); servant Nanak is a sacrifice to him. ॥8॥
237.1: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). First (the creature) is released from its dwelling in the womb; (then) it is bound up with sons, wife and family; (it enjoys) food of many kinds and many clothes; (yet such) poor wretches will surely depart. What is that place which never passes away? What is that Shabad through which evil counsel is taken away? In Indra's city (too) death is certain; Brahma's city will not stay unmoved; Shiv's city (too) will come to its end; (the world) of Maya's three qualities, fallen out of tune, perishes. Mountains, trees, earth, sky and stars; sun, moon, wind, fire and water; day and night, fasts and their many rules; the Shastras, the Simritis and the Vedas: (all these) will perish. Places of pilgrimage, gods, temples, holy books; rosaries, frontal marks, the ritually pure kitchen, the priests of the fire offering; the yogi's cleansing (dhoti), prostrations, the pleasures of palaces; (all these and) the whole world will depart. Castes, varnas, Muslims and Hindus; beasts, birds, the creatures of countless species; all the expanse that is seen spread out: every visible form will perish. (Where there is) praise sung in Sahaj, devotion, and knowledge of the Essence (God), there is bliss for ever; that place is unmoving and true. There the Saadh Sangat savours (the Lord's) virtues; there the city without fear is ever inhabited. There, neither fear nor doubt, sorrow nor worry; no coming and going, and no death; there is bliss for ever, and gatherings where the unstruck (music) sounds; the devotees dwell there, upheld by Kirtan. The Supreme Lord has no end and no far shore; who can contemplate him? Says Nanak, the one on whom (God) bestows grace (finds) the unmoving place, and in the Saadh Sangat swims across (the world-ocean). ॥8॥
Dhoti here is the yogis' cleansing (neti-dhoti): a strip of cloth swallowed to clean the stomach; hoti (hotri) is the priest who performs the fire offering.
237.2: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Whoever kills this (duality), he alone is the hero; Whoever kills this, he alone is complete; Whoever kills this, to him comes honour; Whoever kills this, his pain departs. Rare is the one who kills duality and casts it out; killing it, he practises Raj Jog. Whoever kills this, he has no fear; Those who kill this merge in the Naam; Whoever kills this, his craving is quenched; Whoever kills this, he succeeds in the Lord's court. Whoever kills this, he is rich; Whoever kills this, he is held in honour; Whoever kills this, he alone is the (true) celibate; Whoever kills this, he attains the high spiritual state. Whoever kills this, his coming (into the world) is counted (as fruitful); Whoever kills this, he stands steady, a man of (true) wealth; Whoever kills this, he is greatly fortunate; Whoever kills this, he stays awake night and day. Whoever kills this, he is liberated while yet alive; Whoever kills this, his way of life is pure; Whoever kills this, he alone is truly wise; Whoever kills this, he keeps his meditation fixed in Sahaj. Without killing this, (one) is not accepted, though he performs millions of rites, chants and austerities; without killing this, (the round of) birth does not end; without killing this, (one) is not freed from Jam. Without killing this, there is no divine knowledge; without killing this, (the mind's) impurity is not washed away; without killing this, everything is soiled; without killing this, everything stays apart (from God). The one to whom (God), the treasure of mercy, has been merciful is set free, and has gained success in all. The one whose duality the Guru has killed, says Nanak, contemplates God. ॥8॥
Dubidha (duality): the divided mind, which sees mine and yours and loves another besides God; in every line, isu (this) is this duality.
238.1: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). If one is joined to the Lord, everyone is a friend; If one is joined to the Lord, the mind becomes steady; If one is joined to the Lord, no worry takes hold; If one is joined to the Lord, there is deliverance. O my mind, join yourself to the Lord; nothing else will serve you at all. The great men of the world, those fools, are of no use at all; the Lord's servant may be heard of as one of low birth, (yet) in his company (people) are saved in an instant. Hearing whose Name is (worth) millions of (holy) baths, meditating on whom is (worth) millions of acts of worship, hearing the Lord's Bani brings millions of merits; knowing from the Guru the way (to meet him) yields millions of fruits. Remember (him) in your mind again and again, (and) your attachments to Maya will perish; the imperishable Lord is with you; O my mind, stay steeped in Ram's love. In whose service all hunger is taken away, in whose service Jam's messengers do not (even) look (your way), in whose service great is your glory, in whose service you become immortal; whose servant suffers no penalty, whose servant has no evil habit, in whose register no account is called for: serve him above all. He who lacks nothing at all, who, himself the One, is in countless forms, by whose glance (of grace) one is happy for ever: O my mind, serve him. No one is clever (of himself), and no one a fool; no one is weak, and no one a hero; to whatever (God) attaches someone, to that he is attached; O Nanak, he alone is (God's) servant who is so fortunate. ॥8॥
239.1: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Without Simran (life) is like the (long) life of a snake; so live the Saakats, forgetting the Name. One who has lived even an instant in Simran (has, as it were, lived) millions of days, (and) has become steadfast for ever. Without Simran the deeds one does are cursed; like the crow's beak, (their) dwelling is in filth. Without Simran (people) become like dogs in their deeds; the Saakats are like a prostitute's son, who bears no (father's) name. Without Simran (one) is like a horned ram; the Saakats speak falsehood, (and their) faces are blackened. Without Simran (one) is like a donkey; the Saakats wander about in places of corruption. Without Simran (one) is like a rabid dog; the greedy Saakat knows no restraint. Without Simran (one) is the slayer of his own soul; the Saakat is low; he has no family and no caste. The one to whom (God) has been gracious, (God) has joined to the Sat Sangat; says Nanak, the Guru has carried the world across. ॥8॥
239.2: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). By the Guru's word I have reached the supreme state; the perfect Guru has kept my honour. By the Guru's word I have meditated on the Name; by the Guru's grace I have found a place (to rest). By the Guru's word I hear (the Lord's praise), and utter (it) with my tongue; by the Guru's grace, the ambrosial (Bani) has become my speech. By the Guru's word my self-conceit is erased; by the Guru's kindness great is my glory. By the Guru's word my doubt is erased; By the Guru's word I have seen God everywhere. By the Guru's word I have practised Raj Jog; in the Guru's company the whole world has swum across. By the Guru's word my tasks are accomplished; By the Guru's word I have found the treasure of the Name. Whoever has placed his hope in my Guru, the noose of Jam is cut for him. By the Guru's word my fortune has awakened; Nanak has met the Guru, the Supreme Lord. ॥8॥
239.3: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). I remember that Guru with every breath; the Guru is the very breath of my life; the True Guru is my capital. Beholding the Guru's sight again and again, I live; I wash the Guru's feet again and again, and drink (that water). I bathe every day in the dust of the Guru's feet, (and) wash away the filth of Haumai of birth after birth. I wave the fan over that Guru, (who) gave (me) his hand and saved (me) from the great fire. I carry water in the house of that Guru from whom (I) have come to know the state of the Indivisible (God). I grind (the corn) every day in the house of that Guru, by whose grace all enemies have (become) friends. The Guru who has given me (the spirit's) life has himself bought his humble servant as his own. He himself has given (me) his love; for ever and ever I bow to that Guru. Strife, anguish, fears, doubt and pain are gone; says Nanak, my Guru is all-powerful. ॥8॥
Akal: without parts (kala), the One who neither wanes nor waxes as the moon does; a name of God.
240.1: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Meet me, my Gobind; give me your Name. Without the Name, cursed, cursed is (every other) attachment. One who wears and eats without the Name is like a dog putting its mouth into leftovers. All the dealings carried on without the Name are as vain as the adorning of a corpse. One who forgets the Name and indulges in pleasures finds no peace even in dreams; diseases (beset his) body. One who abandons the Name and busies himself with other tasks comes to ruin; all (his) shows are false. One who does not join his mind in love with the Name goes to hell, though he performs millions of rites. One who has not worshipped the Lord's Name in his mind is bound like a thief in the city of Jam. Lakhs of pompous shows and a vast spread of things: without the Name, (all this) display is false. That servant alone takes the Lord's Name to whom, O Nanak, (God) gives it in his grace. ॥8॥
240.2: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The One who stands by (me) at the beginning, in the middle and at the end: that Friend my mind longs for. Love for the Lord goes along with (one) for ever; the merciful, perfect Being, present in all, cherishes (all). He does not perish, nor does he leave (us) and go; wherever I look, there he is pervading. (God) is beautiful, accomplished, wise, the Giver of life; brother, son, father and mother: God is (all these to me). (He is) the prop of (my) life and breath, my wealth; enshrining (him) in my heart, I have given (him) my love. Gopal has cut away (my) noose of Maya; looking on (me) with his glance of grace, he has made (me) his own. Remembering (him) again and again, all ills are cut away; meditation on (his) feet is the enjoyment of every comfort. The perfect Being is ever new, ever young; the Lord is within and without, with (us), our protector. Says Nanak: (the devotee) has recognised the state of (union with) the Lord, Har Har; (the Lord) has given the devotee the Name, which is everything. ॥8॥
240.3: Raag Gauri Majh, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Countless have wandered searching, (but none) has found (your) limit; they alone became devotees on whom (your) grace fell. I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice to the Lord. Hearing again and again that the road is fearsome, I was gripped by great fear; I have looked to the shelter of the Sants: save (me). O enchanting Beloved, incomparable, support of all, bowing low again and again, I fall at the Guru's feet: (O Guru,) show (me the Lord). I made friends of many, (but) it is to the One alone that I am a sacrifice; all virtues are found in no one (else); the Lord's storehouses (alone) are full. (Your) Name is repeated in all four directions; (those who repeat it) are made beautiful in peace. I have sought your shelter; Nanak is a sacrifice (to you). Stretching out his arm, the Guru has pulled (me) out of the well of attachment; I have won (the game of) this life of boundless worth, never to lose again. I have found (God), the treasure of all, whose story cannot be told; in the Lord's court (I) am honoured, and walk swinging (my) arms, free of care. Servant Nanak has found the priceless, boundless jewel (of the Name); by serving the Guru, one crosses the terrifying world-ocean: this I proclaim aloud. ॥8॥
241.1: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Dye (your mind) in the love of Narayan, the Lord; repeat (his Name) with your tongue, and ask for the one Lord alone. Give up Haumai and, through the wisdom the Guru gives, worship (the Lord); this is done, joining the Sangat, by one for whom grace was written from the Source. Whatever is seen has gone along with no one; the foolish Saakat clings to it and wastes away to death. The Name of the Enchanter pervades (all) for ever; among millions, only someone rare has found it, through the Guru. Bow, bow in reverence to the Lord's Sants; you will obtain the nine treasures and peace beyond measure. May (my) eyes behold the holy ones; sing in your heart of the treasure of the Name. Give up lust, anger, greed and attachment; (one who does) is spared both birth and death. Pain and darkness have gone from the home (of the heart), (since) the Guru has made divine wisdom firm (within), and the lamp is alight. Whoever served (the Lord) has crossed to the far shore; O servant Nanak, through the Guru the world crosses over. ॥8॥
241.2: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Uttering Har Har, Guru Guru, (my) doubts have gone; my mind has found every comfort. I was burning, ablaze; sprinkled with the Guru's sandalwood, I was cooled. The darkness of ignorance is gone: the Guru's wisdom has shone forth. The ocean of fire is deep; boarding the boat of the Sants, I have been carried across. I had no (good) deeds, no righteousness, no purity; God took (me) by the arm and made (me) his own. Destroyer of fear, dispeller of pain, is the Name of the Lord, the lover of devotion. O Master of the masterless, compassionate to the humble, almighty, shelter of the Sants, this is the prayer of one without virtue: grant (me) the sight of you, O Lord King. Nanak is in your refuge, O Master; (your) servant has come to your door. ॥8॥
242.1: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (One) takes delight in the pleasures of Maya; engrossed in them, the blind one understands nothing. I amass, I earn: (so) the whole span of life has passed. I am a hero, I am a chief; there is no one like me; I am young, of good conduct, of noble family: so (one) grows proud in (his) mind. As the one of fettered understanding stays entangled (in Maya), even while dying he does not forget (her). Brothers, friends, kin and companions: to them, afterwards, (all he gathered) is handed over. The desire the mind is attached to is the one that shows itself at the last. Performing rites of purity with a mind full of self, (one) is held fast in these bonds. O merciful Being, present in all, have mercy: Nanak is the slave of your slaves.
Jumla (the total): the closing figure 44 is the count of all the Ashtapadis in Raag Gauri.
242.2: There is one God, Ik Oankar, the One who pervades all and is ever the same; his Name is Sat (the One who truly is); he is the Creator, the Being who dwells in all, realised by the Guru's grace. Raag Gauri Poorbi, Chhants, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). For the young bride the night is full of pain; sleep does not come; the soul-bride has grown frail, sighing for her Husband. Sighing for her Spouse, the bride has wasted away: how might she see (him) with her eyes? Adornment, sweet tastes, pleasures and fine food: all is false, of no account. She who is drunk with youth as with wine is worn away by pride; milk once drawn does not come back to the teats. O Nanak, the soul-bride meets (her Husband) only when she is brought to meet (him); without the Husband, sleep does not come. Without her beloved Master, the young bride is forlorn. How will she find peace without holding (him) to her heart? Without the Husband the home is no home to dwell in; ask (your) friends and companions. Without the Name there is no love or affection (for him); those who dwell in the True One live at ease. With truth in the mind, and in contentment, comes the meeting with the Friend; through the Guru's teaching the Husband is known. O Nanak, the soul-bride who does not let go of the Name merges in Sahaj through the Name. Come together, my friends and companions; let us enjoy our Husband. Asking the Guru, I shall write (to him) a message through the Shabad. The Guru has shown the true Shabad; the self-willed (brides) repent. The (mind) that kept running off stays steady once the True One is recognised. The understanding of the True One is ever new; through the Shabad love stays ever fresh. O Nanak, by (his) glance of grace the True One (is met) in Sahaj; meet (him), my friends and companions. My wish is fulfilled: the Friend has come to my home. Groom and bride have met, and the song of joy has been sung. Singing the joyful song of (his) virtues, the young bride rejoices in love; her mind is full of eager delight. The friends rejoice, the wicked are distressed; meditating on the True One, the true profit (is gained). With palms joined, the soul-bride prays, drenched night and day in the relish (of his love). O Nanak, Husband and bride delight together; my wish is fulfilled. ॥4॥
Milk once drawn does not come back to the teats: the youth (and the chance of union) lost in pride do not return.
The friends and the wicked: in the commentaries, the virtues within, which flourish, and the vices, which are crushed.
243.1: Raag Gauri, a Chhant, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Hear me, O Husband, dear God: I am all alone in the forest (of this world). How will (your bride) take heart without her Husband, O carefree Lord? The bride cannot live without her Husband; the night is very hard (for her). Sleep does not come; (your) love is dear (to me); hear my prayer. Apart from the Beloved no one cares for (me); all alone, (the bride) cries out. O Nanak, the soul-bride meets (her Husband) only when she is brought to meet (him); without the Beloved she suffers pain. She whom the Husband has left: who can bring her to him? She who has met (him) in the relish of love is made beautiful by the Shabad. Made beautiful by the Shabad, she then gains honour; the lamp (of wisdom) lights up her body. Listen, my friend and companion: she is at ease in the True One who cherishes the True One's virtues. When the True Guru united her, the Husband delighted in her; through the Amrit Bani she blossomed. O Nanak, the soul-bride enjoys her Husband only when she is pleasing to his mind. Maya the enchantress has left her homeless; she who clings to falsehood is plundered by falsehood. How can the noose at her neck be loosed without the most beloved Guru? One who loves the Lord and reflects (on him) through the Shabad becomes his alone. How can charity, alms and countless bathings wash away the filth within? Without the Name no one is set free: not by stubborn will, not by curbing the senses, not by (living in) the wilderness. O Nanak, the true home is recognised through the Shabad; what can (one caught in) duality know of the mansion? Your Name is true, dear Lord; your Shabad is true, and reflection (on it). Your mansion is true, dear Lord; true is the trade in the Name. The trade in the Name is sweet; devotion is its profit, night and day. Apart from it, no other merchandise is worth a thought; take the Name each and every moment. The account is assayed, and (his) true glance of grace (falls); by (his) perfect grace (the Name) is obtained. O Nanak, the Name is the supreme relish, and sweet; through the Perfect Guru the True One has been found. ॥4॥
243.2: Raag Gauri Poorbi, Chhants, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). There is one God, Ik Oankar, the One who pervades all and is ever the same; his Name is Sat (the One who truly is); he is the Creator, the Being who dwells in all, realised by the Guru's grace. The soul-bride offers her prayer, cherishing the Lord's virtues; she cannot live a moment, an instant, without her beloved Lord. Without her beloved Lord she cannot live; (but) without the Guru (his) mansion is not found. Whatever the Guru says, that should be done in full; (thus) the fire of craving is quenched. The Lord alone is true; there is none but him; without service (to him), no peace is found. O Nanak, the soul-bride meets (her Husband) only when she is brought to meet (him): she whom he himself unites. The bride's night passes in ease when she fixes her mind on the Lord. She serves the True Guru with love, and sheds self-conceit from within. Shedding self-conceit from within, she sings the Lord's praises; night and day her love (for him) holds. Listen, my friend and companion, dear to my heart: merge in the Guru's Shabad. When she cherishes the Lord's virtues, she is dear to her Husband; she has set her love on the Name alone. O Nanak, the soul-bride is dear to her Husband, the Lord's Name a garland at her neck. Without her beloved Husband the bride is all alone; she is robbed through the love of another, without the Guru's mighty Shabad. Without the beloved Shabad, who can carry (her) across the ocean so hard to cross? Attachment to Maya has led her astray. When falsehood ruined her, her Husband cast her off; that bride does not reach (his) mansion. (She who is) dyed in the Guru's Shabad, absorbed in Sahaj, stays merged (in him) night and day. O Nanak, the bride who is ever dyed in (his) love is united (with him) by the dear Lord himself. One meets (him) only when the Lord brings (one) to meet; who but the Lord can unite? Without one's own beloved Guru, who can dispel doubt? The Guru dispels doubt; in this way, O mother, (he) is met, and then the soul-bride is at peace. Without service to the Guru, there is pitch darkness; without the Guru the path is not found. The bride dyed in (his) love, absorbed in Sahaj, reflects (on him) through the Guru's Shabad. O Nanak, through love for the beloved Guru, the bride has found the Lord as her Groom. ॥4॥
244.1: Raag Gauri, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Without my Husband I am utterly forlorn; O my mother, how can I live without him? Sleep will not come without the Husband, and no garment sits well on my body. A garment looks fair on the body when (she) pleases her Husband; through the Guru's teaching the mind is fixed (on him). When she serves the True Guru she is a happy wife for ever; it is in the Guru's embrace that one is absorbed. Through the Guru's Shabad comes union, and then I enjoy my Husband; the Name is the (true) profit in the world. O Nanak, the soul-bride is dear to her Husband when she cherishes the Lord's virtues. The soul-bride enjoys delight with her own Beloved. Day and night she is dyed in (his) love, and reflects on the Guru's Shabad. She reflects on the Guru's Shabad and kills Haumai; in this way, (friends,) meet the Beloved. That bride is a happy wife, ever dyed in (his) love, in love with the True Name. Staying joined to one's own Guru, one lays hold of the amrit (of the Name), and she kills duality and casts it out. O Nanak, the bride has found the Lord as her Groom, and has forgotten all her sorrows. The bride strays from her Husband, in love with attachment to Maya. False herself, she clings to the false; she who clings to falsehood is plundered by falsehood. (If) she casts out falsehood and holds to the Guru's teaching, she does not gamble her life away. She serves the Guru's Shabad, merges in the True One, and kills Haumai within. She enshrines the Lord's Name in her heart: such is the adornment she makes. O Nanak, the bride whose support is the True Name stays merged in Sahaj. Meet me, my dear Beloved; without you I am utterly forlorn. Sleep does not come to my eyes; neither food nor water pleases me. Water and food do not please; one dies in sighs; without the Husband how can peace be found? I make my prayer before the Guru: if it pleases the Guru, may he unite me (with the Lord) in whatever way he may be met. The Giver of peace himself unites (her with him); he himself has come home and met (her). O Nanak, that bride is a happy wife for ever: her Husband neither dies nor goes away. ॥4॥
245.1: Raag Gauri, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). The bride is pierced through by the Lord's essence, (steeped) in the Lord's Sahaj and love. The Enchanter has captivated her mind; her duality has dissolved in Sahaj. With her duality dissolved in Sahaj, the bride finds her Groom, and through the Guru's teaching she delights (in him). This body is filled to the throat with falsehood and deceit, and commits sins. Through the Guru comes the devotion by which the strain of Sahaj wells up; without devotion the filth does not go. O Nanak, the bride who sheds self-conceit from within is dear to her Husband. Through love for the beloved Guru, the bride has found her Husband. She sleeps the night in peace, holding (him) within, in her heart. Holding him within, in the heart, one meets the Beloved, who drives out pain night and day. The mansion is within; there the bride enjoys her Husband, reflecting through the Guru's teaching. Day and night she has drunk the amrit of the Name, and has killed duality and cast it out. O Nanak, through boundless love for the Guru, the happy wife has met the True One. Come in your mercy, O dearest Beloved. So the bride prays, having adorned herself with the True (Name) and the Shabad. Adorned with the True (Name) and the Shabad, she kills Haumai, and through the Guru she sets her affairs right. In every age the One alone is true; through reflection on the Guru's word she comes to understand him. The self-willed bride is gripped by lust and tormented by attachment: before whom can she go and cry out? O Nanak, without the dearest Guru, the self-willed bride finds no place. The young bride is unknowing, simple and without virtue; the Husband is unreachable and infinite. He is met (only) when he himself unites; he himself is the Forgiver. The bride's dear Husband pardons faults; he pervades every heart. He is found through love, affection and loving devotion: this understanding the True Guru has given. She stays ever in bliss, day and night; night and day she keeps her loving attention fixed (on him). O Nanak, in Sahaj she has found the Lord as her Groom; that bride has obtained the nine treasures. ॥4॥
245.2: Raag Gauri, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). The pool of Maya surges in its might; how can it be crossed, so hard to cross? Make the Lord's Name the ship, and set the Shabad in it as the boatman. When one sets the Shabad in it as boatman, the Lord himself takes (one) over; in this way the hard crossing is made. Through the Guru devotion is obtained; so one dies while yet alive. The Lord's Name cuts away sins in an instant, and the body is made pure. O Nanak, through the Lord's Name comes deliverance: even the slag of burnt iron is turned to gold. Women and men are gripped by lust; they have never learnt the way of the Lord's Name. They hold mother, father, sons and brothers very dear; they have drowned and died without water. Drowned and dead without water, they never knew the higher state; the world rushes about in Haumai. Whoever has come will depart, each one; those who reflect on the Guru's word have been saved. Whoever becomes Gurmukh and utters the Lord's Name crosses over himself and carries his family across. O Nanak, the Name dwells within (his) heart, and through the Guru's teaching he meets the Beloved. Without the Lord's Name nothing lasts; the world is a play. Fix true devotion firmly (in your heart), and make the Lord's Name your trade. The trade in the Name of the unreachable, infinite Lord: this wealth is gained through the Guru's teaching. Service and attention (fixed on the Lord): this is the true devotion, (by which) self-conceit is shed from within. We are without wisdom, foolish, ignorant and blind; the True Guru has set (us) on the path. O Nanak, the Gurmukhs are made beautiful by the Shabad, and sing the Lord's praises night and day. He himself causes (all) to be done, he himself does (it), and he himself embellishes (lives) through the Shabad. He himself is the True Guru, he himself the Shabad; in every age his devotees are dear (to him). In every age his devotees are dear (to him); the Lord himself embellishes them, and himself attaches them to devotion. He himself is the Knower, he himself the Seer; he himself has (his) service done. He himself is the Giver of virtues; he cuts away faults and makes the Name dwell in the heart. Nanak is ever a sacrifice to the True One, who himself does and causes all to be done. ॥4॥
246.1: Raag Gauri, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Serve the Guru, O my dear husband, and meditate on the Lord's Name. Do not go far from me, O my dear husband: sitting at home, one finds the Lord. Sitting at home one finds the Lord, keeping the mind ever fixed (on him), in Sahaj, in love for the True One. Service of the Guru brings great ease, (but only to the one) whom (the Lord) himself has do it. He sows the Name alone, the Name alone springs up, and he enshrines the Name alone in his mind. O Nanak, in the True Name is glory; one obtains (it) by what was written before. The Lord's Name is sweet, O my dear husband, when you taste it with your mind fixed (on it). O wretched tongue, taste the Lord's essence, and give up the savour of other tastes. When it pleases the Lord, the tongue tastes the Lord's essence for ever, and is made beautiful by the Shabad. Whoever meditates on the Name finds peace for ever, and keeps his loving attention fixed on the Name. Through the Name (the Lord's relish) springs up, through the Name (the pull of other tastes) is destroyed, and through the Name one merges in the True One. O Nanak, through the Guru's teaching the Name is found; (the Lord) himself sets (one) to it. This is service to another, O my dear husband: (a man) leaves his wife and goes off to foreign lands. In (the love of) another no one has found peace, O my dear husband; (one is) lured by greed for Maya, the poison. Lured by greed for Maya, the poison, and led astray by doubt, how can he find peace? Service to another is very painful: one sells oneself and loses one's righteousness. In Maya's bonds (the mind) finds no rest; every moment pain torments (it). O Nanak, the pain of Maya ends only when one fixes the mind on the Guru's Shabad. The manmukh is foolish and uncouth, O my dear husband; he does not enshrine the Shabad in his mind. Maya's illusion blinds him, O my dear husband; how is he to find the way to the Lord? How is he to find the way without love for the True Guru? The manmukh puts himself forward. The Lord's servants, their minds fixed on the Guru's feet, are ever at ease. The one on whom the dear Lord shows grace sings the Lord's praises for ever. O Nanak, the jewel of the Name is the (true) profit in the world; (the Lord) himself gives this understanding through the Guru. ॥4॥
In this hymn a wife speaks to her husband, who leaves home to serve another in foreign lands; in the commentaries this husband is the soul, which leaves its home within to wander after Maya.
The closing figure 7 is the total of these Chhants in Raag Gauri: two by the First Guru and five by the Third.
247.1: Raag Gauri, Chhants, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Bairag (longing for the Lord) has arisen in my mind: how may I behold you, O God, the Giver? O my friend and companion, dear Lord, O great Being, Maker of all! You are the all-pervading Being, the Maker, the One, Sridhar; how may I, forlorn, meet you? My hands do (your) service, my head (lies) at (your) feet; in my humbled mind is the hope of your sight. With every breath, day and night, you are not forgotten for a while, an instant or a moment. Says Nanak: we thirst like the rain-bird; how may God, the Giver, be met? I make one prayer: listen, O beloved Husband. Watching your wondrous plays, my mind and body have been captivated. Watching your plays I was beguiled; how can (this) forlorn bride now be consoled? O virtuous Husband, merciful and ever young, full of every virtue! The fault is not yours, O Husband, Giver of peace; it is I, the wrongdoer, who am separated (from you). Nanak prays: show mercy and come home, O beloved Husband. I would offer my mind, offer my whole body, offer all my lands; I would offer my head to that dear friend who brings me word of God. When I offered my head to the Guru, in that blessed place, he showed me God beside (me). In an instant all pain vanished; I obtained what my mind had wished. Day and night the bride delights; all her anxieties are gone. Nanak prays: the Husband has met (us), just such a one as we longed for. Bliss has arisen in my mind, and rejoicing resounds. The dear Darling has come home; all thirst is quenched. When I met the Darling, Gopal, the Master, my companions sang songs of joy. All my friends and kin were filled with joy, and the foes (the vices) lost their foothold. The unstruck music plays in the home; the bed has been spread (for union) with the Husband. Nanak prays: she abides in Sahaj, for she has met the Lord, her Husband, the giver of peace. ॥4॥
248.1: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). O Enchanter (Mohan), lofty are your temples, and your mansions are boundless. O Enchanter, beautiful are your gates, dear Lord: the dharamsalas (houses of worship) of the Sants. In (your) dharamsalas, O boundless, merciful Master, (the Sants) ever sing your Kirtan. Wherever Saadhs and Sants come together, it is you they meditate on. Show kindness and mercy, O merciful Master; be gracious to the meek. Nanak prays: (we) thirst for your sight; to meet you and behold you is the whole of peace. O Enchanter, your words are incomparable, your ways unlike any other. O dear Enchanter, (all) acknowledge you alone as the One; all else is dust. They acknowledge (you), the One, the indescribable Master, who has set his power in all (creation). Through the Guru's word (your devotees) have won you over, O Primal Being, Banwari (Lord of the world). You yourself are what moves, you yourself are what stays still; you yourself have set your power in all (creation). Nanak prays: save (our) honour; all (your) servants are in your refuge. O Enchanter, the Sat Sangat meditates on you, its attention fixed on your sight. O Enchanter, Jam does not come near those who repeat your Name, (even) at the end. Jamkaal cannot touch those who meditate (on you) with one-pointed mind. Those who worship you in mind, word and deed obtain all the fruits. Those who were dull and foolish, (as foul as) dung and urine, have grown wise on beholding your sight. Nanak prays: your rule is unshakeable, O perfect, all-pervading Lord. O Enchanter, you have borne fair fruit, together with your family. O Enchanter, you have carried across sons, friends, brothers and whole households. You have carried the world across; those who have had your sight are rid of pride. Those who have called you blessed: Jam has not come near them. Your endless virtues cannot be told, O True Guru, all-pervading Being, Murari. Nanak prays: I have taken hold of your support, holding to which the world has crossed over. ॥4॥
248.2: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (The Lord's Name) makes countless sinners pure; again and again I am a sacrifice (to it). O Nanak, repeat the Name of Ram: (that Name) is a fire that burns up sins as it burns straw. ॥1॥
248.3: O mind, repeat (the Name of) Ram, Narain, Govind, Har, Madho. O mind, meditate on Murari, on Mukand (the giver of liberation), (by whom) the noose of death and pain is cut. Let us worship the lotus feet of Sridhar, remover of pain, shelter of the meek. The hard road of Jam and the ocean of fire are overcome by remembering (him) for an instant. Worship day and night the One who burns away the filth of sin and makes (one) pure. Nanak prays: have mercy, O Gopal, Gobind, Madho. O mind, remember Damodar, the remover of pain, the destroyer of fear, the Lord, the King; Sri Rang, the merciful, the enchanter of the mind, whose very nature it is to love devotion. From the perfect Being who loves devotion, what the mind longs for is obtained. (If his) Name is enshrined in the mind, (he) lifts (one) out of the pitch-dark well. Gods, Siddhas, ganas, gandharvas and silent sages have sung (his) countless virtues in devotion. Nanak prays: have mercy, O Supreme Lord, O Lord King. O mind, keep in mind the Supreme Lord, the Supreme God, who upholds all with his power; the compassionate, all-powerful Master, the support of the breath of life in every heart; the Giver of breath, mind, body and life, infinite, inaccessible, boundless; the all-powerful, enchanting (Lord), able to shelter those who seek refuge, the destroyer of all faults. Disease, grief and all faults perish as one repeats the Name of Murari. Nanak prays: have mercy, O all-powerful One, who upholds all with your power. O mind, sing the praises of the unshakeable, the imperishable, highest of all, the merciful; he sustains the universe; he alone is the Giver; he cherishes all. The cherisher, the greatly merciful, the all-knowing, shows compassion to everyone. (The fear of) death, piercing like a thorn, and greed and attachment are destroyed for the one in whose heart God dwells. (When) the divine Lord is well pleased, service bears fruit and the labour is fulfilled. Nanak prays: repeating (the Name of the One) merciful to the meek, (my) wish has been fulfilled. ॥4॥
249.1: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Listen, my friend: let us come together and strive to win over the Lord, our Husband. Giving up pride, let us make devotion our love-charm, and enchant (him) with the mantra of the Saadh (the Guru). Friend, once he comes under (love's) sway, he does not leave again: such is the Lord's good way. O Nanak, (he) takes away the fears of old age, death and hell, and makes that being pure. Listen, my friend: this is a good plea; let us make this resolve firm: that in Sahaj and in love, free of all guile, we sing the songs of Govind. (So) strife and anguish are ended, doubts are dispelled, and the fruit the mind longs for is obtained. O Nanak, let us meditate upon the Name of the Supreme Lord, the perfect Supreme God. Friend, I long, and every day I make vows, that God may fulfil my hope. Thirsting for (his) feet, yearning for (his) sight, I search every place. Searching, I find the company of the Lord's Sants, (which) unites (one) with the all-powerful Being. O Nanak, those who have met the Friend, the giver of peace, are fortunate indeed, O mother. Friend, I dwell (now) with my beloved Husband; my mind and body have grown one with the Lord. Listen, my friend: (even) my sleep is sweet, (for) I have met my own Beloved. The Master has dispelled (my) doubt; (I abide) in peace and Sahaj; light has dawned, and the lotus (of the heart) has blossomed. O Nanak, I have found God, the knower of hearts, as my Groom; (my) wedded joy never passes away. ॥4॥
250.1: Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Raag Gauri, Bavan Akhri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The Gurdev is mother, the Gurdev is father, the Gurdev is the Master, the Supreme God. The Gurdev is the friend who destroys ignorance; the Gurdev is kinsman and brother born of the same womb. The Gurdev is the Giver who teaches the Lord's Name; the Gurdev's mantra is one whose power nothing can stop. The Gurdev is the embodiment of peace, truth and wisdom; the Gurdev is a paaras whose touch surpasses even the paaras. The Gurdev is the tirath, the pool of Amrit; to bathe in the Guru's wisdom is beyond all else. The Gurdev is the Creator, the remover of all sins; the Gurdev makes the fallen pure. The Gurdev is from the beginning, from the start of the ages, in every age; repeating the Gurdev's mantra, the Lord's Name, one is saved. O God, in your grace join (us) to the Gurdev's company, holding fast to which we foolish sinners may swim across. The Gurdev is the True Guru, the Supreme Lord, the Supreme God; O Nanak, salutation to the Gurdev, the Lord. ॥1॥

Bavan Akhri (fifty-two letters): a composition in which each pauri opens with a letter of the alphabet (Ong, Sassa, Dhadha, Nganga and the rest); each salok gives the thought that the pauri after it unfolds.
250.2: (God) himself has done (all) and caused (all) to be done; he himself has the power to do (all). O Nanak, the One alone pervades all; there has been no other, and there will be none. ॥1॥
250.3: Ong: salutation to Oankar, to the Saadh, the True Guru, who in the beginning, in the middle and at the end is the Formless One. He himself is in Sunn; he himself is seated in bliss; he himself hears (his praise); he himself is the glorious One. He himself brought himself into being; he himself is (his own) father, he himself (his own) mother. He himself is the subtle (unseen), he himself the gross (the visible world). O Nanak, (his) play is beyond understanding. Show grace, O God, merciful to the meek, that (my) mind may become the dust of your Sants' feet.
Ong: the first letter of the alphabet, here also the name of Ik Oankar, the One God. Sunn (the void): the state before creation, when there was nothing but God.
250.4: The Formless One himself is (all) form; Nirgun and Sargun, he is the One. The One is spoken of as the One alone; O Nanak, the One is the many. ॥1॥
Nirgun: God beyond the three qualities of Maya; Sargun: God made manifest in the creation, with its qualities.
250.5: Ong: Oankar made the world of forms (for beings to become) Gurmukh; he is the One who strings (all) on a single thread. (He) has spread out the three qualities, each apart; from Nirgun (he) has come into sight as Sargun. (O God,) making every kind (of being, you) have brought forth (the world); (you) have made the mind's attachment, (the root of) birth and death, grow. (Yet you) yourself are apart from both (birth and death). O Nanak, (he) has no end, no near shore and no far shore. ॥2॥
250.6: They alone are bankers, they the wealthy, (who have) the wealth of truth, the capital of the Lord's (Name). O Nanak, truth and purity are found with such Sants. ॥1॥
250.7: Sassa: True, true, true is he; no one is apart from the True Being. He alone comes to (God's) refuge whom (God himself) brings there; remembering (him) again and again, he sings (his) praises and makes (others) hear them. Fear and doubt do not touch him at all; to him the glory of that (Lord) alone is plainly seen. He who reaches this (state) is the Saadh; Nanak is ever a sacrifice to him. ॥3॥
250.8: Why do (you) cry out, wealth, wealth? All attachment to Maya is false. O Nanak, without the Name all are turning to dust. ॥1॥
251.1: Dhadha: (O God,) the dust (of the feet) of your servants is pure; blessed are those whose mind longs for this (dust). (They) do not want wealth, nor do they wish for heaven; (they) are absorbed in the love of the most dear (Lord), and in the dust (of the feet) of the Saadh. How can worldly entanglements take hold of those who do not leave the One to go anywhere else? The one in whose heart God has placed (his) Name, O Nanak, that Saadh is the perfect Lord's own form. ॥4॥
251.2: By many religious garbs, by (talk of) knowledge and by meditation, by stubbornness of mind, no one has met (God). Says Nanak, the one on whom (God's) grace has come is the devotee, is the wise one. ॥1॥
251.3: Nganga: spiritual wisdom (does not come) by words of the mouth, nor by the many devices of the Shastras and their (many) ways. He alone is wise in whom that (Lord) is firmly fixed; by mere saying and hearing, no union (with God) comes about at all. He is wise in whom (God's) command stays firm; to him, heat and cold are all one. He is wise who, through the Guru, reflects on the essence, O Nanak, (the one) on whom (God) has bestowed his grace. ॥5॥
Nganga: for the acrostic, giaan (spiritual wisdom) and giaani (the wise) are spelt here with the letter ਙ.
251.4: Those who came into the world without understanding came in name only; they are beasts and cattle. O Nanak, he alone understands, through the Guru, on whose forehead (good) fortune is written. ॥1॥
251.5: (One) has come into this age for the One (Lord) alone, (yet) from birth Maya the enchantress has enchanted (him). In the hollow of the womb (beings) practise austerity upside down, (and there) they keep remembering God with every breath; (but once born) they are entangled in what they must leave behind, and they forget the Giver from their minds. O Master of the world, the one on whom (you) bestow grace says Nanak, does not forget (you) here or hereafter. ॥6॥
251.6: By (God's) Hukam (one) comes, by Hukam (one) perishes; no one is outside (his) command. Coming and going ends for him, O Nanak, in whose mind that (Lord dwells). ॥1॥
251.7: These beings dwell in many wombs; absorbed in sweet attachment, (they) are snared in births. This Maya has brought (them) under the three qualities; (she) has put her own attachment into every heart. O friend, tell (me) some remedy by which I may cross this hard (ocean of) Maya. (Whom God) in his grace joins to the Sat Sangat, O Nanak, Maya does not come near him. ॥7॥
251.8: The deeds that are done, good and bad, that God himself has done; (yet) the beast (of a man) cries, I, I, of himself; O Nanak, without the Lord what can (anyone) accomplish? ॥1॥
251.9: The One himself causes (all) to be done; he himself has spread out sin and virtue. In this age, to whatever (God) himself has attached (each one), that alone (each one) has received which he himself has caused to be given. No one knows his limit; whatever he does, that alone comes to pass. From the One alone comes the whole expanse; O Nanak, (he) himself is the One who sets (all) right. ॥8॥
251.10: (People) stay engrossed in the amusements of women; (yet) this clamour of poison (Maya) is (as fleeting as) the safflower's colour. Nanak seeks the refuge of that (Lord), through whom the sense of I and mine is destroyed. ॥1॥
252.1: O mind, wherever you lose yourself apart from the Lord, there, in each place, bonds are laid (on you). The Saakats practise the very ways by which there is no release anywhere. Those devoted to ritual deeds keep on saying I, I; the burden of that (ego) is beyond bearing. Without love for the Naam, these very deeds are vices. Through the pleasures of sweet Maya they are bound with the rope of Jam. Beguiled by delusion, they do not see that God stays with (them) always. When the account is reckoned, there is no release; a wall of unbaked clay does not become clean (by washing). O Nanak, the one to whom (God himself) gives understanding gains, through the Guru, a pure intellect. ॥9॥
252.2: The one whose bonds are broken has found the company of the Saadh. O Nanak, those who are dyed in the love of the One: deep (and fast) is their colour. ॥1॥
252.3: Rara: dye this mind of yours (in the Lord's love); repeat with your tongue the Name of the Lord, Har Har; keep up its repetition. (Then) in the Lord's court no one will call out to you with contempt; (rather, all) will greet you with honour: come, be seated. You will gain a dwelling in that mansion (of the Lord); (there) is no birth and death, nor any perishing. The one on whose forehead (the Lord's) grace is written from the very beginning: O Nanak, the wealth of the Lord (the Name) is in that one's home. ॥10॥
252.4: Greed, falsehood, vice and attachment hold sway over the blind fools; O Nanak, in the bonds of Maya they lie clinging to what is foul. ॥1॥
252.5: Lala: clinging to the pleasures of the senses, (people) are steeped in them; with an intellect full of ego, they are drunk on the wine of Maya. Caught in this Maya, they are born and die; as (God's) Hukam is, so do (beings) act. (Of oneself) no one is lacking and no one is complete; no one is wise and no one a fool. (O God,) to whatever you attach (them), to that they are attached. O Nanak, the Master is for ever untouched (by it all). ॥11॥
252.6: God is the Beloved, Gopal, Gobind; deep, profound and unfathomable is he. There is no other, none second (to him); O Nanak, he is the carefree Lord. ॥1॥
252.7: Lala: there is no one equal to him; he alone is, himself; there will be no other. Ever-existent, he has been for ever; no one has found his end. He fully pervades the worm and the elephant; the all-pervading Being is known to be manifest in every place. The one to whom the Lord has given his own sweet essence, O Nanak, repeats (the Name of) the Lord, Har Har, through the Guru. ॥12॥
252.8: Those who have known the relish of the spirit savour the Lord's love in Sahaj; O Nanak, blessed, blessed, blessed are those people; their coming (into the world) is approved. ॥1॥
252.9: That one's coming (into the world) alone should be counted fruitful whose tongue utters the praise of the Lord, Har Har. Those who come and dwell in the Saadh's company meditate on the Naam night and day with love. That person, coming (into the world), stays dyed in the Naam on whom the Creator bestows kindness and mercy. He comes but once, and does not enter the cycle of births again; O Nanak, he is absorbed in the sight of the Lord. ॥13॥
252.10: The One by repeating whom bliss wells up in the mind and the love of another perishes, and pain, suffering and craving are quenched: O Nanak, merge in his Name. ॥1॥
253.1: Yaya: burn away evil-mindedness and duality; abandoning it, you will abide in peace and Sahaj. Yaya: go and seek the refuge of the Sants, with whose support this world-ocean is crossed. Yaya: that one does not come into birth (again) who takes the Name of the One and strings it into his mind. Yaya: with the support of the Perfect Guru, (this human) life is not lost; O Nanak, that one has found peace in whose heart is the One. ॥14॥
253.2: The Friend of this world and the next dwells within mind and body; the Perfect Guru has taught (this); O Nanak, one should repeat (his Name) every day. ॥1॥
253.3: Night and day remember him who will be your helper at the end. This Maya lasts but four or six days; everyone leaves it and goes. Whose are mother, father, son and daughter? Home, wife, anything at all: (no one) has taken it along. Gather such (wealth) as does not perish, (so that) you go with honour to your own home. Those who in Kalyug have sung (the Lord's) Kirtan in the Saadh Sangat: O Nanak, none of them has come (into birth) again. ॥15॥
253.4: (Though they be) very handsome, of noble birth, clever, eminent, learned and wealthy, O Nanak, those with no love for the Lord are called dead. ॥1॥
253.5: Nganga: (one may) be versed in the six Shastras, practise drawing in, holding and letting out the breath (purak, kumbhak, rechak), be given to knowledge and meditation, and bathe at places of pilgrimage, cook his own food (for purity), let no one touch him, and live in the wilderness; (but if) there is no love in his mind for the Name of the Lord, Ram, all that he has done is perishable. Higher than him I count the chandal in whose mind Gopal dwells, says Nanak. ॥16॥
Purak, kumbhak and rechak are the three parts of the yogis' breath control (pranayam). A sompaak cooks his own food for ritual purity; an aparas lets no one touch him.
253.6: (People) wander the four quarters and the ten directions by the line drawn by the deeds they have done; O Nanak, pleasure and pain, liberation and the cycle of births (come) by the writ that is written. ॥1॥
253.7: Kaka: he alone is the Creator, the maker of all causes; no one can erase the writ he has written. Nothing has to be done (by him) a second time; the Maker is not one who errs. To one he himself shows the path; another he makes to wander in the wilderness and repent. He himself has made his own play; O Nanak, whatever he has given, that is what (each) has received. ॥17॥
253.8: (His servants) go on eating, spending and enjoying, (yet his) storehouses are never used up. O Nanak, countless people repeat (the Name of) the Lord, Har Har; there is no counting them. ॥1॥
253.9: Khakha: nothing is wanting with that almighty (Lord); whatever he is to give, he keeps giving, whatever place (one) may go to. The wealth of the Naam is their provision and their treasure; this is the devotees' capital. In forgiveness, humility, bliss and Sahaj, they keep repeating (the Name of) the Treasure of virtues. Those to whom (God) is merciful play and blossom in bliss; they are ever rich and graceful: the riches of the Lord's Name are in their home. No anguish, no pain, no penalty is theirs on whom he has cast his glance of grace. O Nanak, those who are pleasing to God have come through in full. ॥18॥
254.1: Count and measure, and see within your own mind: people must surely depart. Through the Guru, hope in passing things is erased; O Nanak, the Naam (alone) makes one whole. ॥1॥
254.2: Gaga: sing the virtues of Gobind; repeat (his Name) with every breath, every day. What trust can be placed in the body? Do not delay, my friend. Childhood, youth or old age: at none of these is there any bar (to death). No one knows the hour when the noose of Jam will come and fall. See: the learned, the meditative, the clever, (none) is to stay in this place. That which all the world has left behind and gone, to that the fools cling. By the Guru's grace, the one with (good) fortune on the forehead keeps remembering (the Lord). O Nanak, those granted the wedded love of the Beloved: their coming (into the world) bears fruit. ॥19॥
254.3: All the Shastras and Vedas have been searched through; none of them tells of any other (than him). In the beginning, from the start of the ages, now and in time to come, O Nanak, he alone is. ॥1॥
254.4: Ghagha: set this firmly in your mind: apart from the Lord there is no other. There has been none, nor will there be; everywhere he alone is contained. O mind, you will melt into (him) only when you come to (his) refuge. In Kalyug the Naam is the essence, (and it is the true) act of atonement.
