a13.p6: One who maligns a Sant cries out in pain, as a fish writhes without water. One who maligns a Sant stays hungry and is never filled, as fire is never sated by fuel. One who maligns a Sant is left all alone, like a barren sesame stalk, forlorn in the field. One who maligns a Sant is without dharma (righteousness). One who maligns a Sant ever speaks lies. The slanderer's lot, shaped by his deeds, was set from the very start. O Nanak, whatever pleases the Lord, that alone comes to pass. ॥6॥
a13.p7: One who maligns a Sant becomes deformed. One who maligns a Sant is punished in the Lord's court. One who maligns a Sant is kept ever in agony. One who maligns a Sant neither dies nor is allowed to live. The hopes of one who maligns a Sant are never fulfilled. One who maligns a Sant rises and departs in despair. By maligning a Sant, no one is ever satisfied. As one's inclination is, so one becomes. No one can erase the record of deeds once it is written. O Nanak, the True One alone knows. ॥7॥
a13.p8: All hearts are his; he is the Doer. Salutations to him for ever and ever. Sing God's praise day and night. With each breath and each mouthful, meditate on him. Everything that happens is his doing. As he makes a person, so that person becomes. He himself is the player of his own play. Who else could offer counsel? To whom he shows grace, he gives his own Naam (the Name, God's presence remembered). Very fortunate, O Nanak, are those servants. ॥8॥
a14.salok: Give up your cleverness, O good people, and remember the Lord, the King, in Simran (meditative remembrance of God). Keep in your mind the hope of the one Lord alone; then, says Nanak, pain, doubt and fear depart. ॥1॥
a14.p1: Know that all reliance on human beings is in vain. The one Lord God alone is the Giver. By his gifts one remains satisfied, and craving does not come to cling again. He alone kills and preserves. Nothing is in human hands. By understanding his Hukam (God's will and command), one finds peace. Keep his Naam (the Name, God's presence remembered) strung around your neck. Remember, remember, remember that God. O Nanak, then no obstacle stands in the way. ॥1॥
a14.p2: In your mind, praise the Formless Lord. O my mind, carry on true dealings. With a pure tongue drink the nectar, and make your soul ever at peace. With your eyes behold the play of the Master. In the Saadh Sangat (the company of the holy), all other attachments fade away. With your feet walk on the path of Gobind (the Lord of the universe). Sins are wiped out when one repeats the Lord's Name for even a moment. With your hands do the Lord's work, and with your ears listen to the story of the Lord. Then, O Nanak, the forehead shines bright in the Lord's court. ॥2॥
a14.p3: Fortunate are those people in this world who sing the Lord's virtues for ever and ever. Those who reflect on the Lord's Name, they are wealthy and free from want in the world. Those eminent ones who utter the Lord with mind, body and mouth: know them to be at peace for ever and ever. One who recognises the One, the One alone, has understanding of this world and the next. One whose mind is at one with the Naam, O Nanak, he has known the Immaculate Lord. ॥3॥
a14.p4: One who, by the Guru's grace, comes to understand his own self: know that his craving is quenched. One who speaks the praises of the Lord in the Saadh Sangat, that servant of the Lord stays free of all disease. One who night and day utters only Kirtan (songs of God's praise), he alone is free of attachment while living as a householder. The person whose hope rests on the One alone, he has Death's noose cut away. One who hungers in his mind for the Supreme Lord, O Nanak, no sorrows cling to him. ॥4॥
a14.p5: One into whose mind and consciousness the Lord God comes, that Sant (saint) is at peace and does not waver. One upon whom his God shows grace, tell me, whom should that servant fear? He has been seen just as he is; he himself pervades his own creation. Searching, searching, searching, I have succeeded; by the Guru's grace I have understood the whole essence. Whenever I look, everything I see is the Root, the source of all. O Nanak, the subtle is he, and the tangible too is he. ॥5॥
a14.p6: Nothing is born and nothing dies; he alone performs his own play. Coming and going, the seen and the unseen: the whole creation he has made obedient. He himself is all in all; he himself is in all. He creates in many ways, establishing and overthrowing. He is imperishable; nothing of him is ever broken. He gives his support and holds up the universe. The Being, unseen and unfathomable, is glorious. O Nanak, if he himself makes one repeat his Name, then one repeats it. ॥6॥
a14.p7: Those who have known God are glorious; their counsel carries the whole world across. God's servants save all. God's servants make sorrow forgotten. The merciful one joins them to himself; repeating the Guru's Shabad (the Word), they are filled with bliss. He alone comes to serve them, the fortunate one on whom God bestows grace. Repeating the Naam, they find rest. Says Nanak, regard those persons as the most exalted. ॥7॥
a14.p8: Whatever such a servant does, he does in God's love. For ever and ever he dwells with the Lord. Whatever happens, happens in its natural course; he recognises that one Doer. What God does seems sweet to his servant. God is seen just as he is. From whom they sprang, into him they merge. They become treasures of peace; this state befits them alone. He himself has given honour to himself. Says Nanak, know God and his servant to be one. ॥8॥
a15.salok: God is full of every power and knows all pain. By remembering him in Simran (meditative remembrance of God) one is saved; Nanak is a sacrifice to him. ॥1॥
a15.p1: Gopal (the sustainer of the world) mends what is broken. He himself cherishes all beings. He who holds the care of all in his mind, from him no one goes away empty-handed. O my mind, ever repeat the Lord's Name. God, who never perishes, is himself everything. Nothing happens by one's own doing, even if a mortal longs for it a hundred times. Apart from him, nothing can serve your purpose. O Nanak, salvation comes by repeating the Name of the one Lord. ॥1॥
a15.p2: Being beautiful, let no one be vain; it is God's light that adorns every heart. Being wealthy, why should anyone be proud, when all wealth is his gift? If someone calls himself a great hero, without God's power where can he run? If someone sets himself up as a giver, the Giver knows him to be a fool. One whose sickness of Haumai (ego) is broken by the Guru's grace, O Nanak, that person is ever healthy. ॥2॥
a15.p3: As a pillar holds up a building, so the Guru's Shabad (the Word) is the mainstay of the mind. As a stone crosses over aboard a boat, so the mortal who clings to the Guru's feet is carried across. As a lamp brings light to darkness, so at the sight of the Guru the mind blossoms. As one finds the path in a great wilderness, so, joining the Saadh Sangat (the company of the holy), one makes the inner light shine forth. I long for the dust from the feet of those Sants (saints). O Lord, fulfil Nanak's longing. ॥3॥
a15.p4: O foolish mind, why do you wail? What was written long ago is what one receives. Pain and pleasure are given by God; leave all others and keep him in mind. Whatever he does, accept it as happiness. Why do you wander astray, ignorant one? What thing came with you? You are caught up in pleasures like a greedy moth. Repeat the Lord's Name in your heart; then, says Nanak, you will go home with honour. ॥4॥
a15.p5: The merchandise you came to buy, the Lord's Name, is found in the house of the Sants. Give up pride and buy it at the price of your mind; weigh the Lord's Name in your heart. Load this cargo and travel with the Sants; give up all other snares of poisonous Maya (the world's illusion and lure). Everyone calls such a one blessed, blessed, and his face is radiant in the Lord's court. Only a rare one trades in this trade. Nanak is ever a sacrifice to such a one. ॥5॥
a15.p6: Wash the feet of the Saadh (holy one) again and again, and drink that water. Offer your soul to the Saadh. Bathe in the dust of the Saadh. Give yourself as a sacrifice to the Saadh. Service of the Saadh comes through great fortune. In the Saadh Sangat, people sing the Lord's Kirtan (songs of God's praise). The Saadh keeps one safe from many obstacles. Singing the Lord's virtues, one tastes the nectar. One who took the shelter of the Sants and came to their door, O Nanak, he has gained every comfort. ॥6॥
a15.p7: He brings the dead to life. He gives sustenance to the hungry. All treasures lie within his glance; people receive the share written for them beforehand. Everything is his; he is able to do all. Besides him there has been no other, nor will there be. Repeat his Name, O servant, for ever and ever, day and night; this is the highest and purest deed of all. One to whom he graciously gave the Naam (the Name, God's presence remembered), O Nanak, that person became pure. ॥7॥
a15.p8: One in whose mind there is faith in the Guru, into that person's consciousness the Lord God comes. He is heard of in the three worlds as a devotee, a devotee, in whose heart is the One alone. True are his deeds, true is his way of life; truth is in his heart, and truth he speaks with his mouth. His vision is true, and to him all form is true; truth prevails, and true is the whole expanse. One who has known the Supreme Lord as true, O Nanak, that person merges into the True One. ॥8॥
a16.salok: Without form, outline or any colour, God stands apart from the three qualities (gunas). O Nanak, he gives understanding to the one with whom he is well pleased. ॥1॥
a16.p1: Keep the Imperishable God in your mind. Give up your love for people. Beyond him there is nothing and no one; within all, the One alone is present. He himself sees all, he himself knows all; he is deep, profound, unfathomable and all-wise. O Supreme Lord, Supreme God, Gobind (the Lord of the universe), treasure of mercy, compassionate and forgiving One, may I fall at the feet of your Saadhs (holy ones): such is the longing in Nanak's mind. ॥1॥
a16.p2: He fulfils desires and is able to give refuge. What he has ordained comes to pass. In the blink of his eye he destroys and replenishes; no one else knows his secret counsel. He is the embodiment of bliss, and rejoicing is ever in his house; all things are said to be in his house. In kingship he is the king, in Yoga the yogi; in austerity he is the great ascetic, in household life the enjoyer. Meditating on him again and again, the devotees have found peace. O Nanak, no one has ever reached the end of that Being. ॥2॥
a16.p3: His play has no limit; all the gods have grown weary plumbing it. What does a son know of his father's birth? He has strung all upon his own thread. Those to whom he gives good understanding, wisdom and meditation, those servants and slaves of his meditate on the Naam (the Name, God's presence remembered). Those whom he makes wander in the three qualities, they are born and die, and come and go again and again. All places, high and low, are his. O Nanak, as he makes one know, so one knows. ॥3॥
a16.p4: Many are his forms, many his colours; he takes on many guises, yet is of one hue. In many ways he has made the expanse: God, the imperishable, Ekankar (the One Creator). In an instant he stages many plays; the Perfect One fills every place. He has shaped his creation in many ways; his own worth he alone knows. Every heart is his, every place is his. Nanak lives by repeating the Lord's Name again and again. ॥4॥
a16.p5: Upheld by the Naam are all creatures. Upheld by the Naam are the worlds and universes. Upheld by the Naam are the Simritis, the Vedas and the Puranas. Upheld by the Naam are listening, wisdom and meditation. Upheld by the Naam are the skies and the nether worlds. Upheld by the Naam are all forms. Upheld by the Naam are the realms and all the worlds. Through the Naam, by hearing it with their ears, people have been saved. One whom he graciously attaches to his own Naam, O Nanak, that person attains salvation in the fourth state (beyond the three qualities). ॥5॥
a16.p6: His form is true, his place is true. True is the Being, he alone supreme. His deeds are true, his word (Bani) is true. The True Being is contained in all. True is his grace, true his creation. True is the root, and true is what springs from it. True is his conduct, pure and utterly pure. One whom he makes understand finds it all good. God's Name is true, and it gives peace. O Nanak, true faith is gained from the Guru. ॥6॥
a16.p7: True is the word, the teaching of the Saadh. True are the people in whose hearts it comes to dwell. If anyone comes to understand love for the True One, by repeating the Naam he attains salvation. He is true himself, and true is everything he has made. His own measure and state he alone knows. Whose creation it is, he is its maker. Know that no other takes thought for it. The Creator's limit is not known by what he has created. O Nanak, what pleases him is what comes to pass. ॥7॥
a16.p8: Wondering at his wonder, one is struck with awe. Whoever has understood this has come to taste its relish. God's servants remain dyed in his love; through the Guru's word they have gained the priceless treasures. They are givers and removers of pain; in their company the world crosses over. The servant of such a servant is very fortunate; in the company of such a servant, one's mind is fixed in love on the One. That servant sings Kirtan (songs of God's praise) of the virtues of Gobind. By the Guru's grace, O Nanak, he gains the fruit. ॥8॥
a17.salok: True in the beginning, true at the start of the ages; true he is now, and, O Nanak, true he will ever be. ॥1॥
a17.p1: His feet are true, and those who touch them are true. His worship is true, and those who serve him are true. The sight of him is true, and those who behold it are true. His Naam (the Name, God's presence remembered) is true, and those who meditate on it are true. He himself is true, and all that he upholds is true. He himself is virtue, and he himself bestows virtue. His Shabad (the Word) is true, and the one who speaks of God is true. Attentive hearing is true, and the one who listens to his praise is true. For the one who understands, everything is true. O Nanak, true, true is that God. ॥1॥
a17.p2: One who has believed in his heart in the Embodiment of Truth, he has recognised as the root the one who does and causes all to be done. One into whose heart faith in God has come, in his mind the essence of wisdom is revealed. Freed from fear, he lives without fear; he merges into the One from whom he sprang. When one thing is taken and blended into its own substance, it can no longer be called separate. One with understanding understands this discernment. O Nanak, meeting the Lord, he becomes one with him. ॥2॥
a17.p3: The Master's servant is obedient. The Master's servant ever worships him. In the mind of the Master's servant there is faith. Pure is the way of life of the Master's servant. The servant knows the Master to be with him. God's servant is steeped in the love of the Naam. God is the one who sustains his servant. The Formless Lord keeps his servant's honour. He alone is a servant on whom God bestows mercy. O Nanak, such a servant remembers him with every breath. ॥3॥
a17.p4: He keeps his own servant's faults covered. He surely protects his own servant. He gives greatness to his own slave. He makes his own servant repeat the Naam. He himself guards his own servant's honour. No one can perceive that servant's state and stature. No one can equal God's servant. God's servants are higher than the highest. One whom God has set to his own service, O Nanak, that servant is made known in all ten directions. ॥4॥
a17.p5: He places power in a tiny ant, and it reduces armies of millions upon millions to ashes. One whose breath he himself does not take away, him he protects, giving him his hand. A person makes efforts of many kinds, but his efforts go in vain. No one else kills or preserves; he alone is the protector of all beings. Why do you worry, O mortal? Says Nanak, repeat the Name of God, the Unseen, the Wondrous. ॥5॥
a17.p6: Again and again and again, one should repeat God's Name. Drinking the nectar, this mind and body are sated. One who as a Gurmukh (one who follows the Guru) has gained the jewel of the Naam, he sees nothing else. His wealth is the Naam; the Naam is his beauty and his joy. His peace is the Naam, and the Lord's Name is his companion. Those who are satisfied with the relish of the Naam, they have their minds and bodies absorbed in the Naam alone. Rising, sitting, sleeping, the Naam: says Nanak, this is ever the occupation of the Lord's servant. ॥6॥
a17.p7: Day and night, speak his praise with your tongue. God has bestowed this gift on his servants. They perform devotional worship with the eagerness of their soul, and remain absorbed in their God. Such a one knows what has been and what is coming to be. He recognises the Hukam (God's will and command) of his God. How could I describe the glory of such a one? I do not know how to tell even one of his virtues. Those who dwell at all hours in God's presence, says Nanak, they are the perfect ones. ॥7॥
a17.p8: O my mind, take their shelter; hand over your mind and body to those servants. The servant who has recognised his God, he is the giver of all things. In his refuge you will find every comfort; through the sight of him you will be rid of all sins. Give up all other cleverness; devote yourself to the service of that servant. Your coming and going will end. Says Nanak, worship the feet of that servant for ever. ॥8॥
a18.salok: Whoever has known the True Being bears the name of True Guru. Keeping his company, the Sikh is saved; says Nanak, sing the virtues of the Lord. ॥1॥
a18.p1: The True Guru cherishes the Sikh. To his servant the Guru is ever merciful. The Guru removes the filth of the Sikh's evil thinking. Through the Guru's words, the Sikh utters the Lord's Name. The True Guru breaks the Sikh's bonds. The Guru's Sikh turns away from vice. The True Guru bestows on the Sikh the wealth of the Naam (the Name, God's presence remembered). The Guru's Sikh is truly fortunate. The True Guru makes good the Sikh's life here and hereafter. O Nanak, the True Guru cares for the Sikh with all his heart. ॥1॥
a18.p2: The servant who lives in the Guru's house, he accepts the Guru's command in his mind. He does not make himself out to be anyone. He ever meditates on the Lord's Name in his heart. When a servant sells his mind to the True Guru, his affairs come right. One who serves without desire for reward, he attains the Master. One on whom he himself bestows his grace, O Nanak, that servant takes the Guru's teaching. ॥2॥
a18.p3: One with whom the Guru's mind is wholly satisfied, in full measure: that servant comes to understand the state of the Supreme God. He is the True Guru in whose heart is the Lord's Name. I offer myself to the Guru as a sacrifice, many times over. He is the giver of all treasures and of life. At all hours he is steeped in the love of the Supreme Lord. The servant dwells in God, and the Supreme Lord dwells in the servant. He himself is the One; no doubt remains. By a thousand clevernesses he cannot be won. O Nanak, such a Guru is found by great good fortune. ॥3॥
a18.p4: Fruitful is the sight of him; beholding him, one becomes pure. Touching his feet, one's state and way of life become pure. Meeting him in his company, one dwells on the virtues of the Lord, and arrives at the Supreme Lord's court. Hearing his words, the ears are satisfied. Contentment comes into the mind, and the soul is at rest. Perfect is the Guru, everlasting his teaching. One upon whom he looks with his nectar glance becomes a Sant (saint). Endless are his virtues; his worth cannot be assessed. O Nanak, whoever pleases him, him he unites with himself. ॥4॥
a18.p5: One tongue, and his praises are many. The True Being is perfect in discernment. No mortal's words can reach him. God is unreachable, beyond the senses, free of all attachment. He needs no food, has no enmity, and is the giver of peace; no one has found his worth. Countless devotees bow to him daily. They remember his lotus feet in their hearts. I am ever a sacrifice to my True Guru, O Nanak, by whose grace one repeats the Name of such a God. ॥5॥
a18.p6: Only a rare person obtains this essence of the Lord. One who drinks the nectar becomes immortal. That person never perishes in whose mind the Treasure of virtues is revealed. At all hours he takes the Lord's Name. He gives true teaching to his servant. He is not stained by attachment to Maya (the world's illusion and lure). He keeps the one Lord in his mind. In the darkness a lamp has given light. O Nanak, doubt, attachment and pain have fled from there. ॥6॥
a18.p7: In the burning heat, coolness has spread. Bliss has come, and the pains have fled, O brother. The anxieties of birth and death are gone through the perfect teachings of the Saadh (holy one). Fear is ended, and they dwell fearless; all ailments are destroyed and have fled from the mind. The One to whom one belonged has shown grace. by repeating the Name of Murari (the Lord) in the Saadh Sangat (the company of the holy), Stability is found and the wandering of doubt is ended, O Nanak, by hearing with the ears the praises of the Lord. ॥7॥
a18.p8: He himself is beyond all qualities (Nirgun), and he is also with qualities (Sargun). Assuming his power, he has enchanted the whole creation. God himself has made his own wondrous plays. He alone knows his own worth. Besides the Lord there is no other. The One alone is present within all. Through and through he pervades all forms and colours. He is revealed in the Saadh's company. Having made the creation, he has placed his own power within it. Nanak is a sacrifice to him many times over. ॥8॥
a19.salok: Nothing goes along with you but the worship of God; all the poison of worldly vice is ashes. Earning the Lord's Name, Har Har: O Nanak, this is the wealth of real worth. ॥1॥
a19.p1: Meet with the Sants (saints) and reflect together. Remember the One, and make the Naam (the Name, God's presence remembered) your support. Put all other efforts out of your mind, my friend; keep the lotus feet of the Lord enshrined in your heart. That God is all-powerful, the cause of all creation. Hold firmly to the Lord's Name, the true merchandise. Store up this wealth and become fortunate; this is the Sants' pure counsel. Keep your hope in the One alone, within your mind. O Nanak, then all ills are cured. ॥1॥
a19.p2: The wealth for which you rise and run to the four corners of the earth, that wealth you will find by serving the Lord. The peace you long for every day, my friend, that peace lies in love for the Saadh Sangat (the company of the holy). The honour for which you do good deeds, for that honour, hurry to the Lord's refuge. The illness does not go away with countless remedies; the illness is cured when the medicine of the Lord is applied. Of all treasures, the treasure is the Lord's Name. Repeat it, says Nanak, and be accepted in the Lord's court. ॥2॥
a19.p3: Awaken the mind through the Lord's Name; running in the ten directions, it comes back to rest in its place. No obstacle troubles the one in whose heart that Lord dwells. This dark age of Kali is burning hot; the Lord's Name is cool. Remember it again and again, and have peace for ever. Fear is destroyed and hope is fulfilled; through loving devotion the soul is lit from within. In that heart the Imperishable Lord comes to dwell. Says Nanak, Death's noose is cut. ॥3॥
a19.p4: The one who speaks reflection on the Essence (God) is the true servant; whoever is (only) born and dies is unripe, utterly unripe. Coming and going in birth and death ends by serving God: give up self-conceit and take refuge with the divine Guru. In this way the jewel of human birth is redeemed; remember the Lord, Har Har, the mainstay of life. No one is released by countless efforts, nor by pondering the Simritis, Shastras and Vedas. Worship the Lord with your mind fixed on him. O Nanak, one receives the fruit one's heart desires. ॥4॥
a19.p5: Wealth will not keep you company on your way; why, foolish mind, do you cling to it? Sons, friends, family and wife: tell me, which of them will be your protector? Kingly power, pleasures and the vast spread of Maya (the world's illusion and lure): tell me, who has ever been freed by these? Horses, elephants and riding in chariots: this is a false pomp, and false (perishing) is the one who spreads out this show. The ignorant one does not recognise him who gave all this; forgetting the Naam, O Nanak, he comes to regret. ॥5॥
a19.p6: Take the Guru's teaching, ignorant one; without devotion many clever people have drowned. Worship the Lord with devotion, my mind, my friend, and your consciousness will become pure. Keep his lotus feet in your mind, and the sins of birth after birth will leave. Repeat the Naam yourself and have others repeat it; by hearing it, speaking it and living by it you will reach liberation. The Lord's Name is the very essence, the truth. Sing his praises, says Nanak, in poise and natural love. ॥6॥
a19.p7: Singing his praises, your filth will be washed away, and the spreading poison of Haumai (ego) will be destroyed. You will be free of care and live in peace; hold the Lord's Name dear with each breath and each morsel. Give up all your cleverness, my mind; in the Saadh Sangat the true wealth will be yours. Gather the capital of the Lord and trade with it; here you will have peace, and in the Lord's court acclaim. See the One alone within all. Says Nanak, this comes to the one on whose forehead it is written. ॥7॥
a19.p8: Repeat the One alone, praise the One alone. Remember the One, and long, my mind, for the One alone. Sing the endless virtues of the One. With mind and body repeat the one Lord's Name. The Lord himself is the One, the One alone. God is fully pervading, filling all. The countless expanses of creation came from the One. Through worship of the One, sins have gone. Mind and body are dyed deep within in the colour of the one God. By the Guru's grace, O Nanak, the One has been known. ॥8॥
a20.salok: After much wandering I have come, God, and fallen into your refuge. Nanak makes this one prayer, God: join me to your devotion. ॥1॥
a20.p1: Your servant, a beggar, begs you, God, for a gift: in your grace, Lord, grant me your Name. I beg for the dust from the feet of the Saadhs (holy ones). Supreme Lord, fulfil my longing: may I sing God's praises for ever and ever; with every breath, God, may I meditate on you. May love for your lotus feet take hold of me; may I worship God with devotion day after day. The One is my only shelter, the One my only support. Nanak asks for God's Name, the most excellent of all. ॥1॥
a20.p2: By God's glance of grace comes great peace. Only a rare one finds the sweet essence of the Lord. Those who have tasted it are content; they are complete beings, and they do not waver. They are filled to the brim with the joy and colour of love; in the Saadh's company, longing for him wells up. Giving up all else, they have fallen into his refuge; within them is light, and night and day their minds are fixed on him. By great fortune they have repeated that God's Name. O Nanak, imbued with the Naam (the Name, God's presence remembered), one is at peace. ॥2॥
a20.p3: The servant's wish has been fulfilled; from the True Guru he has received pure understanding. God has become merciful to his servant and he has made him joyful for ever. His bonds are cut and the servant is free; the pain of birth and death has left him, and doubt with it. His desire is met, his longing wholly fulfilled; the Lord pervades all, ever with him, ever present. He to whom he belonged has united him with himself. O Nanak, through devotion he merges in the Naam. ॥3॥
a20.p4: How can he be forgotten, who does not let our toil go to waste? How can he be forgotten, who recognises what we have done? How can he be forgotten, who has given us everything? How can he be forgotten, who is the life of all beings? How can he be forgotten, who keeps us safe in the fire (of the womb)? By the Guru's grace only a rare one perceives this. How can he be forgotten, who draws us out of poison, and joins again those parted from him for lifetimes? The perfect Guru has made this essential truth clear. O Nanak, his servants have meditated on their God. ॥4॥
a20.p5: Friends, Sants (saints), do this work: give up all else and repeat the Lord's Name. Remember, remember, remember him, and find peace. Repeat the Naam yourselves and have others repeat it. Through loving devotion the world-ocean is crossed; without devotion the body will turn to ashes. The Naam is the treasure of every blessing and comfort; even one who is drowning finds rest in it. Every sorrow is destroyed. Says Nanak, repeat the Naam, the treasure of virtues. ॥5॥
a20.p6: Love has welled up in me, the sweetness of love, and longing; within mind and body this alone is my aim: to behold the sight of him with my eyes and be at peace. The mind blossoms as it washes the feet of the Saadhs. The devotees are dyed in his love, mind and body; only a rare one gains their company. Be merciful and give me one thing: that by the Guru's grace I may repeat the Naam. His praise cannot be told. O Nanak, he is present in all. ॥6॥
a20.p7: God is forgiving, merciful to the meek. He loves his devotees and is ever kind. He is Master of the masterless, Gobind (the Lord of the universe), Gopal (the sustainer of the world); he cherishes every heart. He is the Primal Being, the cause of all, the Creator, he is the mainstay of his devotees' lives. Whoever repeats his Name becomes pure, fixing the mind's love on him in loving devotion. We are without virtue, lowly and ignorant. Nanak is in your refuge, Lord, Supreme Being. ॥7॥
a20.p8: All the heavens, freedom and liberation are gained by singing the Lord's praises for a single moment. Many kingdoms, pleasures and honours belong to one whose mind delights in the telling of the Lord's Name. Many foods, garments and music are his whose tongue repeats Har Har every day. Good are his deeds, glorious and rich is he in whose heart dwells the perfect Guru's teaching. God, let me dwell in the Saadh Sangat (the company of the holy). O Nanak, there every comfort shines forth. ॥8॥
a21.salok: He himself has qualities and is beyond qualities; he is the Formless One, absorbed in the trance of the void (sunn samadhi). O Nanak, he himself made all this, and he himself, in turn, meditates on himself. ॥1॥
a21.p1: When none of this visible world could be seen, where then could sin and merit come from? When he himself had entered his own trance of the void, then with whom could anyone practise hatred and strife? When the world had no colour or mark to be seen, then tell me, whom could joy and grief take hold of? When the Supreme Lord was all alone, by himself, then where was attachment, and who could have doubt? He himself has set his own play in motion. O Nanak, there is no other doer. ॥1॥
a21.p2: When God the Master alone existed, then tell me, who could be counted bound or free? When there was only the Lord, unreachable and infinite, then tell me, who could be born into hell or heaven? When God was beyond qualities, in his own natural poise, then tell me, where were Shiva and Shakti (spirit and matter)? When he kept his own light within himself, then who was without fear, and who feared what? He himself performs his own wondrous plays. O Nanak, the Master is unreachable and infinite. ॥2॥
a21.p3: When the Imperishable was seated at ease in his own place, then tell me, where were birth, death and destruction? When there was only that perfect Creator God, then tell me, who could feel the terror of the messenger of Death? When God, unmanifest and beyond the senses, was the One alone, then of whom could Chitra and Gupta (the recorders of deeds) ask an account? When there was only the Master, stainless, beyond the senses and unfathomable, then who was set free, and who was tied in bonds? He himself, by himself, is the wonder. O Nanak, he himself gave rise to his own form. ॥3॥
a21.p4: Where the pure Being, Master of all beings, was alone, there was no dirt; tell me, what could be washed? Where there was only the stainless, formless One, free of all desire, there who had honour, and who had pride? Where the Lord of the world was present in his own form alone, there, tell me, whom could deceit and fault cling to? Where the One whose being is light was merged in his own light, there who was hungry, and who could be satisfied? He is the Creator, who does and causes all to be done. O Nanak, the Creator is beyond all reckoning. ॥4॥
a21.p5: When he had made his glory with himself alone, then who was mother, father, friend, son or brother? Where he himself was master of every power, there where were the Vedas and the Katebs (the Semitic scriptures), and who was there to recognise them? When he held himself within himself, then who could weigh good omens and bad? Where he himself was the high and himself the near, there who could be called master, and who servant? We are lost in wonder upon wonder, amazed. Says Nanak, you alone know your own state. ॥5॥
a21.p6: Where the One who cannot be deceived, pierced or divided was absorbed in himself, there whom could Maya (the world's illusion and lure) take hold of? He bowed in homage to himself alone; the three qualities of Maya had no entry there. Where there was only the One, the one Lord alone, there who was free of care, and who could be touched by care? Where he himself was content within himself, there who was to speak, and who to listen? He is vast and endless, higher than the highest. O Nanak, he alone can reach himself. ॥6॥
a21.p7: When he himself fashioned the visible expanse of the world, he spread it out within the three qualities. Then came talk of sin and merit; one is bound for hell, another longs for heaven. The snares of household life and the entanglements of Maya, the burdens of Haumai (ego), attachment, doubt and fear, pain and pleasure, honour and dishonour: all these came to be told of in many ways. He himself stages his own play and watches it. When he winds up the play, O Nanak, then he alone remains. ॥7॥
a21.p8: Where the Unmanifest is, there is his devotee; where the devotee is, there he himself is. Where he spreads out the expanse of creation, it is for the glory of his Sants (saints). He is himself the Master of both sides; his glory befits him alone. He himself performs his plays, his joyful wonders; he himself enjoys every pleasure and yet remains untouched. Whom he pleases, he attaches to his Name; whom he pleases, he makes play the game of the world. He is beyond count, fathomless, numberless and beyond weighing. As you make him speak, so your servant Nanak speaks. ॥8॥
a22.salok: Master of every being and creature, you yourself are present and at work in all. O Nanak, the One alone is spread out everywhere; what other can be seen? ॥1॥
a22.p1: He himself speaks, and he himself listens. He himself is One, and he himself has spread out as all. When it pleases him, he brings forth the creation; by his own will he draws it back into himself. Nothing is apart from you; you have strung the whole world on your own thread. The one to whom God himself gives understanding, that servant receives the true Naam (the Name, God's presence remembered). He looks on all alike and knows the essence of reality. O Nanak, he is the conqueror of the whole world. ॥1॥
a22.p2: He holds all beings and creatures in his hands; merciful to the meek, he is the Master of the masterless. One whom he protects, no one can kill; that one is dead whom he puts out of his mind. Forsaking him, where else can one go? Above every head is the one stainless King. He in whose hand lie all the ways of every being, know him to be with you, within and without. He is the treasure of virtues, endless and infinite. His servant Nanak is ever a sacrifice to him. ॥2॥
a22.p3: The merciful one fills every place to the full, and he shows kindness to all. He alone knows what he does; the knower of hearts is present throughout. He cherishes his beings in many ways; whatever he has created meditates on him. Whom he pleases, he unites with himself; they worship him, singing the Lord's praises. With faith in their hearts they have believed in him. O Nanak, they have known the one Creator. ॥3॥
a22.p4: The Lord's servant is attached to the Name of the one Lord, and his hope does not go in vain. To the servant, service comes naturally; understanding the Hukam (God's will and command), he attains the supreme state. There is no thought higher than this for one in whose mind the Formless Lord dwells. Breaking their bonds, they have become free of enmity; night and day they worship the Guru's feet. They are happy in this world and at ease in the world hereafter. O Nanak, the Lord God himself has united them with himself. ॥4॥
a22.p5: Join the Saadh Sangat (the company of the holy) and rejoice; sing the praises of God, the supreme bliss. Reflect on the Lord's Name, the essence of all, and redeem this body so hard to obtain. Sing the Lord's praises, words of nectar; this is the way for the soul to cross over. At all hours see God near you; ignorance will end and darkness be destroyed. Hear the teaching and enshrine it in your heart. Says Nanak, you will receive the fruit your heart desires. ॥5॥
a22.p6: Set right both this life and the life hereafter: keep the Lord's Name enshrined deep in your heart. The teaching of the perfect Guru is perfect; one in whose mind it dwells has recognised the Truth. With mind and body repeat the Naam, attuned to him in love; pain, suffering and fear will leave the mind. Trader, deal in the true trade, and your cargo will come safely through to the Lord's court. Within your mind keep the One alone as your support. Says Nanak, you will not come and go again. ॥6॥
a22.p7: Where can anyone go far from him? One is saved by meditating on the Protector. When one repeats the Name of the Fearless One, all fear is erased; by God's grace a mortal is set free. One whom God protects has no pain; repeating the Naam, the mind finds peace. Anxiety goes and pride is erased; no one can equal that servant. The valiant Guru stands over his head. O Nanak, his tasks are all fulfilled. ॥7॥
a22.p8: Perfect is the wisdom of him whose glance is nectar; at the sight of him the world is saved. Matchless are his lotus feet; fruitful is the sight of the Lord, and beautiful his form. Blessed is his service, and his servant is accepted; he is the knower of hearts, the Supreme Being. One in whose mind he dwells is filled with joy; death does not come near him. They have become immortal and attained the immortal state, O Nanak, who meditated on the Lord in the Saadh Sangat. ॥8॥
a23.salok: The Guru has given the salve of divine knowledge for the eyes, and ignorance and its darkness are gone. When by the Lord's grace one meets the Sant (saint), O Nanak, the mind is lit up. ॥1॥
a23.p1: In the company of the Sants I have seen God within; God's Name tastes sweet to me. All things are within the heart of the One, though they appear in many colours and kinds. God's Name is the nectar, the nine treasures; its resting place is within the body. There is the trance of the void, and there the unstruck melody sounds, the divine music that no instrument makes; its wonder and amazement cannot be told. He alone has seen it to whom God himself has shown it. O Nanak, that servant gains understanding. ॥1॥
a23.p2: The Infinite One is within, and he is without; the Lord pervades every heart. In the earth, the sky and the regions below, in all the worlds, he is the perfect sustainer. In forest, grass and mountain is the Supreme Lord; as his command is, so is every deed. He is in air, water and fire; he fills the four corners and the ten directions. There is no place apart from him. By the Guru's grace, says Nanak, find peace. ॥2॥
a23.p3: See him in Vedas, Puranas and Simritis; the One is in moon, sun and stars. Everyone speaks the speech of God; he himself is steady and never wavers. With all his powers he plays his play; he cannot be bought at any price, and his virtues are priceless. He whose light is in every light, that Master upholds all, woven through like warp and weft. By the Guru's grace doubt comes to an end. O Nanak, in them this faith becomes firm. ॥3॥
a23.p4: To the Sants all they behold is God; in the hearts of the Sants is all righteousness. The Sants hear words of good; they are merged in the Lord who pervades all. Such is the conduct of one who has known him: all that the Saadh (holy one) says is true. Whatever happens, he accepts it gladly; he knows God as the one who does and causes all to be done. For him God dwells within, and outside too it is he alone. O Nanak, at the sight of him all are enchanted. ॥4॥
a23.p5: He is true himself, and true is everything he has made; from that God came the whole creation. When it pleases him, he spreads out the creation; when it pleases him, he is Ekankar (the One Creator) alone again. His many powers cannot be grasped; whom he pleases, he unites with himself. Who can be called near, and who far? He himself is all, filling everything. One whom he himself makes aware of his presence within, O Nanak, to that servant he himself gives understanding. ॥5॥
a23.p6: He himself is at work in all beings; through all eyes he himself is the one who sees. All creation is his body; he himself hears his own praise. The One has made coming and going a play; he has made Maya (the world's illusion and lure) obey his command. Amid all he remains untouched; whatever there is to say, he says it himself. By his command one comes, by his command one goes. O Nanak, when it pleases him, he takes them back into himself. ॥6॥
a23.p7: Whatever comes from him is not bad; tell me, apart from him, has anyone done anything? He himself is good, and his works are excellent beyond measure; he alone knows his own heart. He himself is the Truth, and all he upholds is true; woven through and through, he is absorbed in his own creation. No one can tell his state or his extent; only if there were another like him could that one understand. All that he does is to be accepted. By the Guru's grace, says Nanak, know this. ॥7॥
a23.p8: One who knows this has peace for ever; that God himself unites him with himself. He is wealthy, of noble family and honoured; liberated while living is the one in whose heart the Lord dwells. Blessed, blessed, blessed is that servant's coming, by whose grace the whole world is carried across. This is the purpose of such a servant's coming: that in his company the Name comes to mind. He himself is free, and he sets the world free. O Nanak, salutations for ever to that servant. ॥8॥
a24.salok: I have worshipped the perfect God, whose Name too is perfect. Says Nanak, I have found the Perfect One; sing the praises of the Perfect One. ॥1॥
a24.p1: Listen to the perfect Guru's teaching, and behold the Supreme Lord near you. Remember Gobind (the Lord of the universe) with every breath; the worry in your mind will lift. Let go of the waves of fleeting hope; ask, my mind, for the dust of the feet of the Sants (saints). Set aside self-conceit and make your prayer; cross the ocean of fire in the Saadh Sangat (the company of the holy). Fill your storehouses with the Lord's wealth. O Nanak, salutations to the perfect Guru. ॥1॥
a24.p2: For well-being, happiness, poise and bliss, worship the Lord of supreme bliss in the Saadh Sangat. Ward off hell and save your soul; drink the nectar of Gobind's praises. In your heart dwell on the one all-pervading Lord, whose form is one and whose colours are many. He is Gopal (the sustainer of the world), Damodar (a name of the Lord), merciful to the meek, destroyer of pain, wholly kind. Remember, remember the Naam (the Name, God's presence remembered), again and again. O Nanak, this alone sustains the soul. ॥2॥
a24.p3: The words of the Saadh (holy one) are verses of the highest praise; they are priceless rubies and gems. Hearing them and living by them, one is saved; such a one crosses over and carries others across. Fruitful is the life, and fruitful the company, of one whose mind is dyed in the Lord's love. For him the unstruck Word of victory resounds; hearing it again and again he rejoices, and God thunders forth within him. Gopal shines forth on the foreheads of the great souls. O Nanak, in their company people are saved. ॥3॥
a24.p4: Hearing that he is able to give refuge, we have come to his refuge; in his grace God has united us with himself. Enmity has vanished, and we have become the dust of all; in the Saadh Sangat we receive the Naam, which is nectar. The divine Guru is well pleased, and his servant's service is fulfilled. We are kept free of household entanglements and vice, hearing the Lord's Name and repeating it with the tongue. In his kindness God has shown mercy. Says Nanak, our cargo has come safely through. ॥4॥
a24.p5: Sants, friends, sing God's praise, with a mind alert and fixed on him alone. The Sukhmani, the jewel of peace, is poise, Gobind's praises and the Naam; one in whose mind it dwells becomes a treasure-house. All his desires are fulfilled; he becomes the foremost of men, renowned in all the world. He reaches the highest place of all, and he comes and goes no more. that servant alone departs having earned the wealth of the Lord: O Nanak, the one to whom it is granted. ॥5॥
a24.p6: Well-being, peace, prosperity and the nine treasures; wisdom, knowledge and every spiritual power; learning, austerity, yoga and meditation on God; the highest knowledge and the most purifying bath; the four great blessings and the blossoming of the heart-lotus; living amid all and yet detached from all; beauty, insight and knowledge of the essence of reality; looking on all alike and seeing the One alone: these fruits come to that servant who utters with his mouth and hears with his mind, O Nanak, the Guru's word and the Naam. ॥6॥
a24.p7: Whoever repeats this treasure in the mind, he is liberated, in every age. This Bani, the Guru's word, holds the praises of Gobind and the melody of the Naam, of which the Simritis, Shastras and Vedas speak. The Lord's Name alone is the essence of all creeds; it rests in the minds of Gobind's devotees. In the Saadh Sangat millions of sins are erased; the Sant's grace frees one from the messenger of Death. Those on whose foreheads God has written his grace, O Nanak, they come to the refuge of the Saadh. ॥7॥
a24.p8: One in whose mind it dwells, who hears it lovingly: into that servant's mind the Lord God comes. His pain of birth and death is taken away; this body, so hard to obtain, is redeemed at once. Spotless is his glory, and his speech is nectar; the one Name fills his mind. Pain, sickness, fear and doubt are gone; he is called a Saadh, and his deeds are spotless. His glory rises above all. It is for these virtues, O Nanak, that its name is Sukhmani, the jewel of peace. ॥8॥
296.1: Thiti: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. The Master, the Creator, fills the water, the land and the sky; O Nanak, the One Creator (Ekankar) has spread out in many forms. ॥1॥

Thiti (lunar days): the days of the moon's fortnight, Ekam (the first), Dutiya (the second), Tritiya (the third) and the rest. Each pauri of this bani opens with a lunar day's name, and instead of the day's observances the Guru draws a teaching from the name (Ekam: the One Creator; Dutiya: duality and evil-mindedness; Tritiya: the three qualities).
296.2: Ekam: I meditate on God, the One Creator, and bow (to him); I (sing) the virtues of Gobind, Gopal, God, and fall at the refuge of the Lord King. Hope in him, from whom all things come, (brings) salvation and peace. I have wandered the four corners and the ten directions: without him there is no other. I have heard the Vedas, the Puranas and the Smritis, and I reflect in many ways: the Formless (alone) is the saviour of the fallen, the remover of fear, the ocean of peace. He is the Giver, the Enjoyer, the Bestower; without him there is no other place. O Nanak, singing the Lord's virtues, you obtain whatever you wish. Let us sing the praise of Gobind, the Lord, every day; let us join the Saadh Sangat and worship (him), my friend.
296.3: I bow (to him) many times, and fall at the refuge of the Lord King. O Nanak, in the Saadh Sangat doubt is cut away, as the love of another is erased. ॥2॥
296.4: Dutiya: drive out evil-mindedness, and serve the Guru every day. The jewel of Ram (his Name) will dwell in your mind and body, if you give up lust, anger and greed, my friend. Death is ended, (true) life is found, and all troubles perish. Give up self-conceit, worship Gobind, (and) love and devotion enter (within). Profit is gained, loss is taken away, (and one is) honoured in the Lord's court. Whoever gathers the wealth of Ram's Name is a true banker, fortunate indeed. Standing and sitting, worship the Lord, and love the Saadh. O Nanak, evil-mindedness has left (those) in whose mind the Supreme Lord has come to dwell. ॥2॥
297.1: The three (qualities of Maya) hold the world in their grip; rare is the one who reaches the fourth state (turiya). O Nanak, the Sants in whose minds he has come to dwell have become pure. ॥3॥
297.2: Tritiya: under the three qualities (beings reap) the fruits of vice: now high, now low. (They) wander a great deal through hell and heaven, (and) death ever strikes them down. Joy, grief and dread: (such is) the world; (life) passes in crying I, I. They do not know the One who made them, and think up countless schemes. Through (the world's) pleasures come ills of mind, ills of body and troubles; the fever never breaks. (The mortal) does not grasp the glory of the Supreme Lord, the perfect Master. Very many are drowning in attachment and doubt; (their) dwelling is in the great hell. Have mercy, God, and save (me); Nanak's hope is in you. ॥3॥
297.3: Clever, wise and skilful is the one who has given up pride. The four great gifts (padaarath) and the eight siddhis (are) the Lord's Name: O Nanak, repeat the Lord's Name. ॥4॥
297.4: Chaturthi: I have listened to all four Vedas and sifted out the essence of their thought: to repeat the Name of Ram is the best, the treasure of all well-being and salvation. (The Name) wards off hell and takes away pain, (and through it) countless troubles break away. The one within whom the Lord's Kirtan comes to dwell is done with death and freed from Jam. Those dyed in the love of the Formless lose their fear, and the Amrit (of the Name) permeates them within. With the Name for support, sorrow, want and impurity are destroyed. Gods, men and silent sages go searching for Gopal, the ocean of peace; O Nanak, through the dust of the Saadh's feet (he is found), the mind becomes pure and the face bright. ॥4॥
297.5: The five vices dwell in the minds (of those) absorbed in Maya. O Nanak, in the Saadh Sangat, (dyed) in God's love, (one) becomes pure. ॥5॥
297.6: Panchami: they alone are the Panch (the chosen), they the foremost, who have known (this) spread of the world (for what it is): (it is like) the scent of flowers; for all its many colours, it is all a passing deceit. (But the world) does not perceive (this), does not understand, and gives it no thought at all; pierced through by tastes, attachment and pleasures, the world is sunk in ignorance. (Mortals) wander through birth and death and many wombs, and have done countless deeds, (but) have not remembered the Creator, nor weighed (right and wrong) with discernment in the mind. (Those whose) love and devotion are with the Lord are not stained by Maya in the least; O Nanak, rare are they to be found who are not caught up in the world's show. ॥5॥
297.7: The six Shastras proclaim aloud: (God) has no end, no near or far shore. O Nanak, singing (his) virtues at God's door, the devotees are adorned. ॥6॥
297.8: Khastami: the six Shastras tell, and many Smritis expound, that the Supreme Lord is the most exalted and the highest; not even Shesh Nag knows the end of his virtues. Narad, the silent sages, Suk and Vyas sing the praise of Gobind; the devotees, steeped in the relish (of the Name) and pierced through by the Lord, remain absorbed in him. Their attachment, pride and doubt have perished, for they have found the refuge of the Merciful; (his) lotus feet dwell in (their) mind and body, and beholding (him) they are in bliss. Profit is gained, loss is taken away, by fixing (one's) attention (on him) in the Saadh Sangat. O Nanak, meditate on the Naam, and earn the treasure of the Lord, the store of virtues. ॥6॥
Sekh: Shesh Nag, the thousand-headed serpent of the Puranas, held to utter a new Name of God with every tongue. Suk (Shukdev), the son of the sage Vyas, recited the Bhagavat Purana to King Parikshit.
298.1: The Sants, in their gatherings, tell the Lord's praise, and with love speak of the True One. O Nanak, the mind is brought to contentment by fixing (one's) attention on the One. ॥7॥
298.2: Saptami: gather the wealth of the Name, whose stores are never used up. (It) is found in the company of the Sants; (he) has no end, no near or far shore. Give up self-conceit, worship Gobind, (and) fall at the refuge of the Lord King. (Such a one) is rid of pain, crosses the world-ocean, and obtains the fruit the mind longs for. Whoever repeats (the Name of) the Lord in the mind at all hours: fruitful is (that) life, (and it is) accepted. Know the Creator to be ever with (you), within and without. He alone is a friend, he a companion and comrade, who gives the counsel (to remember) the Lord. Nanak is a sacrifice to the one who repeats the Name of the Lord, Har Har. ॥7॥
298.3: If (his) virtues are sung at all hours, and all other entanglements given up, O Nanak, (then) God is merciful, and Jam's servant cannot so much as cast his eye (on that one). ॥8॥
298.4: Astami: the eight siddhis, the nine treasures, all good things, a perfect understanding, the opening of the (heart's) lotus, bliss for ever, a pure way of life, a mantra whose power nothing can stop, every righteous duty, the purifying bath, (and) the highest, most excellent wisdom of all: (all lie in) worshipping the Lord, Har Har, in the perfect Guru's company. O Nanak, repeating the Name in the Lord's love, one swims across. ॥8॥
298.5: (One who) has not remembered Narayan is lured away by the tastes of vice. O Nanak, when the Name is forgotten, there are births (again and again) in hell and heaven. ॥9॥
298.6: Naumi: all nine openings (of the body) are unclean (in those) who do not repeat the Lord's Name, and act against the right way. They enjoy other men's wives, and babble slander of the holy; with their ears they do not hear the Lord's praise even for a moment. For the sake of the belly they steal what belongs to others, (yet the) fire (of greed) does not leave them, and the thirst is not quenched. Without the Lord's service, these are the fruits they bear; O Nanak, forgetting God, the luckless die and are born (again). ॥9॥
298.7: I have wandered, searching, in all ten directions; wherever my eyes turn, he is there. O Nanak, the mind comes under control (only) if (his) perfect grace is given. ॥10॥
298.8: Dasmi: (those who) have brought the ten doors (of the senses) under control have found contentment of mind by repeating the Name. With the ears the praise of Gopal is heard, with the eyes the merciful Saadh is beheld, the tongue sings the virtues of the Infinite, (and one) dwells in the mind on the all-pervading Lord; with hands and feet the service of the Sants is done. O Nanak, this discipline is gained by God's grace. ॥10॥
299.1: Let the One, the only One, be praised; rare is the one who knows its taste. The virtues of Gobind cannot be known; O Nanak, all (of him) is wonder. ॥11॥
299.2: Ekadasi: see the Lord, Ram, near (you); bring the senses under control and listen to the Lord's Name; (let there be) contentment in the mind and compassion for all beings: in this way the fast is fulfilled. (One who) holds the wandering mind in one place is made pure in mind and body, absorbed in the Lord's Name as he repeats it. The Supreme Lord pervades all; O Nanak, sing the Lord's Kirtan: this is the dharma that never fails. ॥11॥
On Ekadasi, the eleventh day of the moon's fortnight, many Hindus fast from grain; here the Guru tells what the true fast is.
299.3: (Those who) met the merciful Saadh did (his) service, and (their) evil-mindedness was taken away. O Nanak, they remain united with God, and all (their) entanglements have perished. ॥12॥
299.4: Duadasi: (practise) giving, the Naam and the cleansing bath; give up pride and worship the Lord with devotion; drink the Lord's Amrit in the Saadh Sangat; the mind is satisfied by Kirtan in God's love. Gentle words bring contentment to everyone, (and) the mind, born of the five elements, is nourished by the relish of the Lord's Name. These (gifts) are surely obtained from the perfect Guru; O Nanak, dwelling on Ram, one does not come into the womb again. ॥12॥
Panch bhoo atma: the mind, held to be formed from the subtle part of the five elements (earth, water, fire, air and ether).
299.5: Gripped by the three qualities (of Maya, the mortal) never sees (his) desires fulfilled. O Nanak, when the saviour of the fallen dwells in the mind, (one) is set free through the Name. ॥13॥
299.6: Traudasi: the world (is gripped by) the three fevers; (it) keeps coming and going, born into hell. Worship of the Lord, Har Har, has not entered (its) mind, nor has it sung, even for a moment, of God, the ocean of peace. Making its body (a home) of joy and sorrow, it lies bound; (it has) the long sickness of Maya, past all cure. By day it wears itself out doing evil, (and by night), when sleep fills its eyes, it raves in its dreams. Such is the state when the Lord is forgotten. Nanak (has come to) the refuge of God, the merciful Being. ॥13॥
The three fevers: adhi (ills of the mind), biadhi (ills of the body) and upadhi (troubles and calamities that come from without).
299.7: The four quarters, the fourteen worlds: Ram pervades them all. O Nanak, no lack is seen (in him); his works are complete. ॥14॥
299.8: Chaudahi: in the four quarters is God himself; his glory fills all the worlds. The One God pervades all ten directions; see God in earth and sky, in all. Water, land, forests, mountains, the underworlds: the merciful Supreme God dwells in them (all). In all, the subtle (unseen) and the gross (the visible world), is the Lord. O Nanak, through the Guru, recognise God (Brahm). ॥14॥
299.9: (One who) has conquered the self through the Guru's teaching, and sung the virtues of Gobind: O Nanak, by the Sant's grace (his) fears are erased, and anxiety has perished. ॥15॥
299.10: Amavas: (those) to whom the Gurdev gave contentment have come to peace within. Mind and body are cooled, (there is) peace and Sahaj, (for one who) has taken to God's service. The bonds of many vices are broken; his works are fruitful and complete. Evil-mindedness is erased and Haumai is shed, as he remembers the Lord's Name. (One who) has taken hold of the refuge of the Supreme Lord is done with coming and going. Uttering the virtues of Gubind, God, he has crossed over himself, together with (his) family. Let us do the Lord's service and repeat God's Name. O Nanak, the home of peace (God) has been found from the perfect Guru. ॥15॥
300.1: One made whole by God himself is whole, and never wavers. Day by day he rises higher; O Nanak, he never falls short. ॥16॥
300.2: Puranma: the One God (alone) is perfect, the Cause of creation, all-powerful. (He is) the Being merciful to all creatures, whose hand is over all. (He is) the treasure of virtues, the great Gobind, by whose doing (all) comes to pass. He is God, the knower of hearts, all-wise, the Unseen, the Immaculate. The Supreme Lord, the Supreme God, knows every way; (he is) the helper of the Sants, able to give refuge; salutation (to him) at all hours. (His) story cannot be told, nor understood; remember the Lord's feet. Nanak (has come to) the refuge of God, the saviour of the fallen, the Master of the masterless. ॥16॥
300.3: (For those who) have grasped the refuge of the Lord King, pains are destroyed and dread is gone. O Nanak, singing the Lord's virtues, (they) have obtained the fruits their minds longed for. ॥17॥
300.4: Whoever sings (the Lord's praise), whoever hears it, whoever reflects on it, whoever teaches it (to others), whoever makes it firm (within): that one is saved. (He) cuts away his sins and becomes pure, and the filth of birth after birth departs. His face is bright in this world and the next, and Maya does not take hold of him. He is the one of true awareness, he the Vaishnav, he the wise one, he the wealthy; he is the hero, he alone is of noble family, who has worshipped the Lord (Bhagvant). Khatri, Brahmin, Shudra, Vaish or chandal: (each) is saved by remembering (him). Nanak is the dust of the feet of the one who has known his own God. ॥17॥
300.5: Gauri ki Vaar: by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Salok, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). The True Guru is a merciful being, to whom everyone is alike. He looks on all with the same eye; (yet) fulfilment comes by the faith in one's mind. In the True Guru is the Amrit (of the Name) of the sublime Lord; that is the state of (union with) the Lord. O Nanak, only by (his) grace is the Lord meditated on; some rare one obtains (this Amrit) through the Guru. ॥1॥
300.6: By the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). Haumai and Maya are poison through and through; (because of them) there is ever loss in the world, in the universe. Through the Guru, reflecting on the Shabad, (one) earns the profit, the wealth of the Lord. The poison, the filth of Haumai, is washed away by enshrining in the heart the Lord's Amrit, the Lord. All the tasks of those are fulfilled on whom (the Lord) has shown mercy through the Guru. O Nanak, those united from the very first stay united; the Lord, the Creator, has united them (himself). ॥2॥
301.1: You are the True Master, ever true; you are the True One, ever true, the Lord of the world (Gosain). All (creation) meditates on you, all falls at your feet. Your praise is beautiful in form; whoever has sung it, it has carried him across. To the Gurmukhs you give (its) fruit: absorption in the True Name. O my great Master, great is your glory. ॥1॥
301.2: Salok, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). To praise anything other than the Name: all such talk has an insipid taste. The manmukhs praise their pride; (all their talk) is Haumai, possessiveness and strife. Those whom they praise waste away and die, and all the wrangling comes to nothing. O servant Nanak, (those) are saved who, through the Guru, repeat (the Name of) the Lord, Har Har, the Supreme Bliss. ॥1॥
301.3: By the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). O True Guru, tell (me) of the Lord God, that I may meditate in my mind on the Name of the Lord. O Nanak, the Lord's Name is pure; may I utter it with my mouth and cast off all pain. ॥2॥
301.4: You yourself, you alone, are the Formless, O Niranjan, O Lord King. Those who have meditated on you, the True One, with a single mind: all their pain you have taken away. You have no rival, whom one could set beside you and speak of (as your equal). As great a Giver as you, O Niranjan, you alone are; you, the True One, are pleasing to my mind. O my True Master, O True One, true and lasting is your glory. ॥2॥
301.5: Salok, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). Within the mind is the disease of Haumai; the manmukhs, the wicked, are lost in doubt. O Nanak, meet the True Guru, the Saadh, the friend, and be rid of this disease. ॥1॥
301.6: By the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). Through the Guru, (one's) mind and body stay dyed with love for the Lord, the treasure of virtues. O servant Nanak, those who have come to the Lord's refuge, the Lord unites (with himself), with the Guru's approval. ॥2॥
301.7: You are the Creator, the all-pervading Being, beyond reach; with whom could you be compared? If any were as great as you, he could be named (as your like); as your like, only you yourself are spoken of. You alone are at work in every heart; through the Guru you are revealed. You are the True Master of all; you are higher than all. O True One, what you do will come to pass; why then should we grieve? ॥3॥
301.8: Salok, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). In my mind and body is love for the Beloved; (mind and body) stay fixed (on him) through all the eight watches. O servant Nanak, by God's mercy (they) dwell in the peace the True Guru gives. ॥1॥
301.9: By the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). Those within whom is love for the Beloved look beautiful, however they speak. O Nanak, the Lord himself knows (this), the Beloved who has instilled the love. ॥2॥
301.10: O Creator, you yourself are infallible; you are not subject to error. What you do, O True One, is good; through the Guru's Shabad you make (this) understood. You are the Cause of causes, all-powerful; there is no other. You are the Master, beyond reach and merciful; all meditate on you. All beings are yours, you are (the Master) of all; you set all free. ॥4॥
302.1: Salok, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). Hearing the Friend's message of love, (their) eyes stay fixed (on him, waiting); the Guru, pleased, has united (them) with the Friend; O servant Nanak, (now they) sleep in peace. ॥1॥
302.2: By the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). The True Guru is the merciful Giver, in whose heart compassion ever dwells. The True Guru is without enmity within; everywhere he sees the one Brahm alone. Of those who carry on enmity against the ones without enmity, not one has found rest. The True Guru wishes good for all; how can harm come to him? As one is minded towards the True Guru, so is the fruit one receives. O Nanak, the Creator knows everything; nothing is hidden from him. ॥2॥
302.3: (The soul-bride) whom the Master makes great is the one known as great. Whoever pleases the Master, he forgives; she is dear to the Master's heart. If anyone imitates her, she is foolish and ignorant. She whom the True Guru unites (with the Lord) dwells on (his) virtues, and speaks of virtues alone. O Nanak, the True One is ever true; understanding (this), she merges in the True One. ॥5॥
Jaani, bhaani, ajaani, vakhaani and samaani are feminine: this pauri speaks of the soul-bride.
302.4: Salok, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). The Lord is true, Niranjan, immortal, fearless, without enmity and formless. Those who have repeated (his Name) with one mind and one attention: their burden of Haumai has been lifted. Those who have worshipped the Lord through the Guru: those Sants are acclaimed. If anyone slanders the perfect True Guru, the whole world cries shame, shame on him. In the True Guru the Lord himself is at work; the Lord himself is the protector. Blessed, blessed is the Guru, who sings the Lord's virtues; to him be homage for ever and ever. Servant Nanak is a sacrifice to those who have repeated (the Name of) the Creator. ॥1॥
302.5: By the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). He himself fashioned the earth, and he himself the sky. Within it he himself created beings, and he himself puts food in their mouths. He himself, he alone, is at work everywhere; he himself is the treasure of virtues. O servant Nanak, meditate on the Naam: (the Lord) cuts away all the sins of (the one who does). ॥2॥
302.6: You are the True Master, ever true; truth is pleasing to you, the True One. Those who praise you, the True One: Jam's servant does not come near them. Bright at (the Lord's) door are the faces of those in whose hearts the True Lord is dear. The false are thrown behind; with falsehood and deceit in the heart, (each) suffers great pain. The false have blackened faces; the false one ends as nothing but falsehood. ॥6॥
302.7: Salok, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). The True Guru is the soil of dharam; as one sows in it, so is the fruit one reaps. The Gursikhs have sown Amrit (the Name), and have obtained the fruit of Amrit, the Lord. In this world and the next their faces are bright; they are robed in honour in the Lord's true court. Some have falseness within, and practise falseness every day; as one sows, so is the fruit one eats. When the True Guru, the assayer, looks closely, all the self-seekers are laid bare. As they think every day, so they receive; the Lord has shown them up for just what they are. O Nanak, on both sides the Master himself is at work; ever making all these plays, he watches them. ॥1॥
303.1: By the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). The mind is one, and works one way (at a time); to whatever it is attached, that it obtains. Someone may talk a great deal, but he eats only the thing that is in his house. Without the True Guru understanding does not come, and pride does not leave from within. Pain and hunger cling to the proud; they hold out their hands and beg from house to house. Falsehood and fraud do not stay hidden; the gilt and the pretence peel away. One for whom it is written from (deeds) past: the True Guru, God, comes and meets him. As iron touching the paaras (turns to gold), so joining the Sangat one turns to gold. O God of servant Nanak, you are the Master; as it pleases you, so you lead (us). ॥2॥
303.2: Those who have served the Lord in their hearts, the Lord himself has united (with himself). (Whoever) has made a partnership in virtues with them has burned away all faults through the Shabad. To sell faults off for the price of straw, (this partnership) is obtained, O True One, by the one to whom you give it. I am a sacrifice to my Guru, who has wiped out faults and brought virtues to light. The great glory of the Great One is uttered through the Guru. ॥7॥
303.3: Salok, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). In the True Guru is this great glory: night and day he meditates on the Name of the Lord, Har Har. His purity and self-discipline is to dwell on the Name of the Lord, Har Har; with the Lord's Name alone he is content. The Lord's Name is his strength, the Lord's Name his support; the Lord's Name alone keeps him safe. Whoever, with the mind fixed, worships the Guru's form obtains the fruits the mind desires. Whoever slanders the perfect True Guru, the Creator has him punished. That moment never comes into his hands again; he himself eats what he has sown. With blackened face he is taken to the terrible hell, like a thief with a rope round his neck. Should he again fall at the True Guru's refuge, then (only) is he saved, when he meditates on the Name of the Lord, Har Har. Nanak speaks and tells the Lord's words: so it pleases the Lord, the Creator. ॥1॥
303.4: By the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). One who does not obey the command of the Perfect Guru, that ignorant manmukh, is robbed by the poison of Maya. Falsehood is within him, and he takes (all) as false; the Lord has hung baseless quarrels round his neck. He peddles talk a great deal, but what he says pleases no one. He roams from house to house like a forsaken wife; whoever keeps company with him is stained as well. One who becomes Gurmukh stays apart; leaving his side, he goes and sits beside the Guru. Whoever hides (disowns) his own Guru is not good, O Panch (chosen ones); he has lost profit and capital, all of it. Nanak first tells (what) the Agam and the Nigam (the Shastras and the Vedas say); the word of the Perfect Guru has risen above (them). The glory of the Perfect Guru is pleasing to the Gursikhs; the manmukhs have not had that moment in their hands. ॥2॥
304.1: The True One, ever true, is greatest of all; he alone receives (him) whom the True Guru marks with the tikka (of blessing). The True Guru is the one who meditates on the True One; the True One, ever true, and the True Guru are one. He alone is the True Guru, the Purakh, who has reined in the five enemies and brought them under control. Those who count themselves (great) without serving the True Guru have falsehood within; shame, shame (on them), their faces are pale. What they say pleases no one; their faces are black, (for) they have fallen away from the True Guru. ॥8॥
304.2: Salok, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). The whole (world) is the Lord God's field; the Lord himself has set (all beings) to farm it. For the Gurmukhs he has, in his grace, made (the crop) spring up; the manmukhs have lost even the capital. Everyone sows for his own good, (but) the Lord makes that field spring up which pleases him. The Gursikhs have sown the Lord's Amrit, and have gained the fruit of Amrit, the Lord's Amrit Name. Jam, the mouse that ever gnaws at the crop, the Lord, the Creator, has struck down and driven out. The crop, (sown) with love, has sprung up, and the Lord has heaped up the pile of his grace. (God) has lifted all fret and worry from those who have meditated on the True Guru, the Being. O servant Nanak, whoever has worshipped the Naam has crossed over himself and carried the whole world across. ॥1॥
304.3: By the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). All day the manmukh, smeared with greed, talks of other things (than the Name). At night he lies crushed by sleep, and all the nine openings (of the body) go slack. Over the manmukhs' heads is the command of their women; every day they bring them good things. Men who carry out what their women tell them are unclean, witless and foolish. Impure men, in the grip of lust: they are the ones who ask their women and go by it. One who walks by the True Guru's word is a true man, the best of the good. Women and men, all of them, he himself created; every play is the Lord's own playing. All this is of your making, (O Lord); says Nanak, all of it is good, the best of the good. ॥2॥
304.4: (O Lord,) you are free of all need and unfathomable; you are beyond weighing: how can you be weighed? Fortunate are those who meditate on you, those who come to meet the True Guru. The True Guru's Bani is the very form of Truth; through Gurbani one becomes (the same). Others, aping the True Guru, babble half-baked words; those false ones, through their falsehood, wither and fall. Within them is one thing, in their mouths another; for the poison of Maya they wear themselves out to death in anguish. ॥9॥
304.5: Salok, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). Service of the True Guru is pure; one who is pure performs that service. Those within whom are deceit, vice and falsehood, the True One himself has set apart and cast out, (as) lepers. The truthful Sikhs sit by the True Guru and toil (in his service); the false are not found (there) anywhere, however one may search. Those who do not like what the True Guru says go about with defiled faces, rebuked by the Master. Those within whom there is no love for the Lord: how long can they be humoured, these manmukhs out of step (like goblins)? One who meets the True Guru keeps his own mind in its place, and himself has the use of what is his own. O servant Nanak, (God) unites some with the Guru and gives them peace; others, the cheats, he himself sets apart and casts out. ॥1॥
305.1: By the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). Those within whom is the treasure of the Lord's Name: the Master has brought their affairs to fulfilment. Their dependence on people is ended; the Lord God has taken their side and sits beside them. When the Creator is on (their) side, everyone is on (their) side; all who look on them acclaim them. Bankers and emperors are all of the Lord's making; all come and make supplication to the Lord's servant. Great is the glory of the Perfect Guru: serving the great Lord, (his servant) has found peace beyond weighing. The Perfect Guru has given the gift of the Lord('s Name), which never fails; the Lord bestows it every day, and it grows ever greater. Any slanderer who cannot bear to see (this) glory, the Creator himself has consumed. Servant Nanak speaks the virtues of the Creator, who has always kept his devotees safe. ॥2॥
305.2: (O Lord,) you are the Master, beyond reach and merciful, the great Giver, the Wise One. I see no other as great as you; you alone, the accomplished one, are pleasing to my mind. Attachment and family, all that is seen, is bound to pass; (it is all) coming and going. Those who set their minds anywhere but on the True One are false, and their pride is false. O Nanak, meditate on the True One; without the True One the ignorant burn and burn away to death. ॥10॥
305.3: Salok, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). First (the manmukh) gives (the Guru) no regard; what he says afterwards is of no use. The poor manmukh wanders, caught halfway; how can he find peace by talk? One within whom there is no love for the True Guru comes in falsehood and goes in falsehood. If my Lord God, the Creator, shows grace, then (one) sees the True Guru as the Supreme Lord. Then he drinks the Amrit, the Guru's Shabad, and puts an end to all fret, worry and doubt. He stays in bliss for ever, day and night; O servant Nanak, he sings the Lord's virtues night and day. ॥1॥
305.4: By the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). One known as a Sikh of the Guru, the True Guru, rises early and meditates on the Lord's Name. He makes the effort, early in the hours before dawn; he bathes, and dips in the pool of Amrit. By the Guru's teaching he chants the Name of the Lord, Har Har, and all his sins, misdeeds and faults are washed away. Then, as the day rises, he sings Gurbani; sitting down and rising up, he meditates on the Lord's Name. Whoever, with every breath and every morsel, meditates on my Lord, Har Har: that Gursikh pleases the Guru's mind. The one to whom my Master is merciful: to that Gursikh the Guru imparts his teaching. Servant Nanak begs for the dust of that Gursikh's feet, who repeats the Naam himself and has others repeat it. ॥2॥
Amrit sar, the pool of Amrit: in Gurbani, the Naam pictured as a pool of Amrit; after the outward bath, the Sikh dips in it.
306.1: (O Lord,) those who meditate on you, the True One, are rare, and few. Those who worship the One with mind and heart: countless millions eat by their blessing. All (creation) meditates on you, (but) those alone are accepted whom the Master wants. Those who eat and clothe themselves without serving the True Guru are lepers: they die, and having died are born (again). To one's face they speak sweetly, but behind one's back they spit out poison mixed in their mouths. The false at heart the Master has cut off (from himself). ॥11॥
306.2: Salok, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). A blue-black blanket full of dirt and lice: that renegade (one turned away from the Guru) put it on the renegade (his servant). No one in the world lets him sit near; having fallen in filth, the manmukh came back smeared with still more dirt. Made a renegade, he was sent to slander others and tell tales; there too the faces of both renegades were blackened. At once it was heard all over the world, O brother, that the renegade and his servant were beaten with shoes, and, dazed, he got up and came home. After that the renegade was not allowed to mix in gatherings or among his in-laws; then his wife and his niece brought him and laid him in the house again. Both this world and the next are lost (to him); he cries out every day, hungry and thirsty. Blessed, blessed is the Master, the Creator, the Being, who himself sat and had true justice done.
