Reflect within the body, and grasp this truth. Says Kabir: (my) mind is won over by the cheat; the drug's spell is gone, (for I) have recognised the cheat. ॥3॥
Thagauri (the thugs' stupefying drug, 61.1) here is the attachment by which the Lord holds the world spellbound.
331.2: Now Ram, the King, has become my helper; cutting away birth and death, I have attained the supreme state. He has joined me to the Saadh Sangat, and set me free from the five enemies. With my tongue I chant the Naam, the nectar of life; he has made me his own servant, without price. The True Guru has done (me) a great kindness: he has drawn me out of the world-ocean. Love for (the Lord's) lotus feet has taken hold (of me); Gobind dwells in my mind day after day. The live coal of Maya's burning heat has gone out; there is contentment in the mind, and the Naam is (its) support. God, the Master, is present in water and on land; whichever way I turn my eyes, the Knower of hearts is there. He himself has made his devotion firm (in me). O my brother, the writ of the past has come to me. Whomever (God) blesses with grace, for him all is made complete; Kabir's Master is the One who raises up the poor. ॥4॥
331.3: Sutak is in the water, Sutak is on the land; Sutak keeps arising (everywhere). At birth there is Sutak, and at death again Sutak; by Sutak the people are ruined. Tell me, O pandit, who is pure? Dwell on such knowledge, O my friend. In the eyes is Sutak, in speech is Sutak, and Sutak is in the ears; rising or sitting, Sutak clings (to one); Sutak falls on the kitchen (too). Everyone knows the way to be caught; the way to get free, hardly one (knows). Says Kabir: one who reflects on Ram in the heart is not touched by Sutak. ॥3॥
331.4: Raag Gauri, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji. Settle one dispute (for me), O Ram, if you have any work for your servant. Is this mind the greater, or he in whom the mind has come to trust? Is Ram the greater, or one who has come to know Ram? Is Brahma the greater, or the One who brought him forth? Is the Veda the greater, or the source from which it came? Says Kabir: I have grown uneasy (over this): is the place of pilgrimage the greater, or the servant of the Lord? ॥3॥
331.5: Raag Gauri Cheti, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji. Look, O brother: the storm of (divine) knowledge has come; all the thatch of doubt has blown away; tied though it was by Maya, it does not stay. The two posts of double-mindedness have fallen, the ridge-beam of attachment has snapped; the roof-thatch of craving has come down to the earth, and the vessel of evil counsel is smashed. In the rain that pours down after the storm, your servant is soaked through. Says Kabir: light filled my mind when I recognised the risen sun. ॥2॥
332.1: Raag Gauri Cheti, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji. Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. (Some) neither listen to the Lord's praise nor sing of the Lord's virtues, yet by talk alone they pull the sky down. What is there to say to such people? Those whom God has kept outside devotion: let us always stay wary of them. They themselves give no one even a palmful of water, yet they slander the one who brought the Ganga down (to earth). Sitting or rising, they walk in crooked ways; lost themselves, they bring others to ruin too. Apart from evil talk they know nothing else; they do not heed even what Brahma says. Lost themselves, they lead others astray too; they set fire to the house and sleep inside it. They mock others, though they are one-eyed themselves; seeing them, Kabir feels ashamed. ॥6॥
By the Puranic story, King Bhagirath brought the Ganga down from heaven to the earth.
332.2: Raag Gauri Bairagan, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji. Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. No one honours his forebears while they live; once they are dead, people have the shraadh done for them. Tell me, how can the poor forebears receive (that food)? Crows and dogs eat it. Let someone tell me what well-being is. Crying for well-being, well-being, the world perishes; how can well-being come at all? They shape gods and goddesses from clay, and before them offer up a life. Such are those called your forebears: they take nothing by asking for it with their own mouths. They kill the living and worship the lifeless; at the last hour it will weigh heavy (on them). They have not known the state that Ram's Name brings; the worldly are drowned in fears. They worship gods and goddesses and stay unsteady; the Supreme Lord they have not known. Says Kabir: they have not remembered the Lord who has no lineage (Akul); they cling to the poison (of Maya). ॥4॥
Shraadh: the rite for dead forebears (pitars), in which food is given to Brahmins and set out for crows, in the belief that it reaches the forebears.
Akul: without kul (lineage); the Lord, who has no forebears.
332.3: Raag Gauri, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji. One who dies while living, and, so dying, lives again, is thus absorbed in Sunn (the stillness where no worldly thought stirs): amid the black stain of Maya one dwells in the Niranjan, and is not cast into the world-ocean again. O my Ram, let the milk be churned in this way: keep the mind steady through the Guru's teaching; this is how the Amrit is drunk. By the Guru's arrow (of the Word) the adamant-hard (veil of illusion) has been pierced, and the state of light has shone forth; the illusion of the rope (taken for a snake) in the darkness of Shakti (Maya) is ended, and the dwelling is fixed, unmoving, in the home of Shiv (the Lord, the source of good). She (Maya) has pierced this world, O brother, drawing her bow without an arrow; the wind tosses the kite about in all ten directions, but (my) string has stayed tied in loving attention. In the state of unman the mind is absorbed in Sunn; duality and evil-mindedness have fled. Says Kabir: I have seen a wonder known from within; my attention is fixed on Ram's Name. ॥4॥
333.1: Raag Gauri Bairagan, Tipade of Bhagat Kabir Ji. As the wind (of the mind) is turned back, the six chakras are pierced, and the attention falls in love with Sunn. He neither comes nor goes, neither dies nor is born: seek him, O bairagi. O my mind, the mind itself, turned back (from the world), has merged (in the Lord). By the Guru's grace the understanding has become other; else (it) was a stranger (to the Lord). The near grows far, and the far grows near again, for one who has known (the Lord) as he truly is. It is like a syrup made from sugar-candy: only one who has drunk it knows (its taste). To whom can the tale of you, beyond the qualities (nirgun), be told? Rare is one so discerning. Says Kabir: whoever has put fire to the fuse has seen a flash to match. ॥3॥
The six chakras: in yoga, six centres in the body, from the base of the spine to the point between the brows, through which yogis draw the breath upward.
Palita: the fuse that fires the powder of a gun.
333.2: Raag Gauri, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji. There, there is neither rain nor sea, neither sun nor shade; there, nothing is created or dissolved. Neither life nor death, pain nor pleasure touches (one) there; Sunn and Samadhi, neither of the two, is there. The tale of Sahaj cannot be told; it is unlike any other: it goes on no scale, and is never used up; it seems neither light nor heavy. Below and above, neither of the two is there; neither night nor day is there. Water is not there, nor wind, nor fire either; there the True Guru abides. The Lord, beyond reach and beyond the senses, dwells there unbroken; by the Guru's grace he is found. Says Kabir: I am a sacrifice to my Guru; let us stay joined in the Sat Sangat. ॥3॥
333.3: Raag Gauri, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji. Sin and virtue, a pair of oxen, have been bought; the breath has been laid out as capital; within the body the sack is filled with craving: in this way the caravan (of laden oxen) has been bought. Such a master-merchant is our Ram: he has made the whole world a banjara (a travelling trader). Lust and anger, the two, have become toll-collectors; the mind's waves are the robbers on the road; the five elements, joining together, settle the toll, and the caravan has crossed to the far side. Says Kabir: listen, O Sants, this is how it has now turned out: climbing the steep pass, one ox has tired, and has gone off, throwing down its load. ॥3॥
Tanda: a trader's caravan of laden oxen; nayak: the master of the banjaras (travelling traders); jagati: the collector of tolls on the road.
333.4: Raag Gauri, a Panchpada of Bhagat Kabir Ji. In the parents' home there are but four days; to the in-laws' home (the soul-bride) must go. The blind world, foolish and childish, does not know this. Tell me: the bride stands still in her workaday wrap (dadia), and the guests have come to the house: those come to take her away in the muklava have arrived. That little well that is seen: who is it lowering the rope into it? The rope has broken along with the pitcher, and the water-carrier has risen and gone. If the Master becomes kind and shows grace, (the soul-bride) accomplishes her own task; then she is known as a happy wife, (when) she reflects on the Guru's Shabad. All (the world) wanders bound by its past deeds: reflect, and see. What is to be said to her? What can the poor thing do? Without hope she has risen and gone; her mind finds no steadiness to hold. Stay at the Lord's feet; run to his refuge, O Kabir. ॥5॥
334.1: Raag Gauri, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji. Yogis say: yoga is good and sweet, there is nothing else, O brother. The shaven ascetics, the shorn sannyasis, and those who cry the one word (Alakh): these all say they have attained siddhi. Without the Lord, the blind wander lost in doubt; those to whom I go to get myself released are themselves bound in many nooses. (The soul) merges back into that from which it sprang only when this way (of pride) is forgotten: these all say: we are pandits, men of virtue, warriors, givers; we alone are great. Only the one whom (the Lord) gives understanding understands; without understanding, how can one live? (When) the True Guru is met, the darkness ends; in this way the ruby (of the Name) is found. Casting off the vices to left and right, let us hold fast to the state of (union with) the Lord. Says Kabir: the mute has eaten molasses; asked about it, what can he say? ॥4॥
334.2: Raag Gauri Poorbi, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji. Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Where once there was something, nothing remains; nor are the five elements there. Ida, Pingala and Sukhmana: O man, where have these flawed (practices) gone? The thread is broken, the sky (the Tenth Gate) has perished; where has the one who spoke in you been absorbed? This doubt troubles me night and day; no one explains it to me. Where the universe (was beheld), the body is not there; nor is the mind, the maker (of it all), there. The Joiner is ever detached; in whom, then, can this (speaker) be said to be? (The body) is not held together by joining, nor broken apart by breaking, until its time to perish comes. Who is whose master, and who whose servant? Who will go to whom? Says Kabir: (my) attention stays fixed (there) where (the Lord) dwells day and night. His secret he alone truly knows; he is forever imperishable. ॥4॥
334.3: Raag Gauri, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji. Attention (fixed on the Lord) and remembrance (of him) are the earrings in my two ears; true knowledge (of him) is the patched coat I wear. My seat, where I sit, is in the cave of Sunn; to be free of (worldly) imaginings is my path. O my King, I am a bairagi yogi; I neither die, nor grieve, nor know separation. Through all the realms and the universe (sounds) my horn (singi); the whole world is my pouch for ashes. My trance has set in: the three qualities are turned back, and one is freed even while living amid the world's spread. Mind and breath, the two, I have made the gourds, and (the Lord) of all the ages the stem (of my kingri); the string has grown steady and will not break; the kingri sounds, unstruck (Anhad). Hearing it, the mind is wholly absorbed, and Maya's shaking does not reach it. Says Kabir: there is no birth again for the bairagi who has played (this game) and departed. ॥4॥
Kingri: the yogis' stringed instrument, a stem set on two gourds; batua: the yogi's pouch for ashes; tari: the yogic trance.
335.1: Raag Gauri, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji. Nine yards, ten yards and twenty-one yards: one full warp has been stretched (on the loom of the body); (in it are) sixty threads and nine joined pieces, and a weft of seventy-two (threads) is added over and above. Maho, (the mind's craving,) has gone to have (this cloth) woven; when (his true) home is left, the weaver (the soul) sets out (into birth). It is not measured in yards, nor weighed on scales, (yet each day) its sizing is two and a half seers; if it does not get its sizing in good time, it raises a quarrel within the house itself. For a stay of a few days (the soul) turns against the Master; how will this hour come (again)? The troughs are left behind, the bobbins stay wet, and the weaver departs in vexation. The bobbin is empty, no thread comes out, and the beam stays tangled (in the threads) no more. Says Kabir, teaching her: poor wretch, leave this spread (of entanglement) and stay here. ॥4॥

The body here is cloth on a loom: the commentators read the nine yards as the body's nine openings, the ten as the senses, the twenty-one as the elements, the vital airs and the mind, the sixty threads as the main channels of the body, the nine pieces as its joints and the seventy-two as its finer channels.

Maho: the mind's craving, which takes the soul off again and again to have a body woven; sizing (pachan): the paste that stiffens the warp, here the daily food; the troughs (kunde): the pots in which the bobbins are kept soaking; the beam (tur): the roller on which the woven cloth is wound.
335.2: Raag Gauri, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji. When one's light has merged in the One, does (a separate self) remain? It does not. The one in whose heart the Naam does not spring up, that person bursts (with ego) and dies. O dark and beautiful Ram, my dear one, my mind is fixed on you. When the Saadh (the Guru) is met, fulfilment is attained, whether one lives in yoga or in the world's enjoyments. When the two (the Guru and the disciple) meet, the work bears fruit: union through the Name of Ram. People take this for a song, but it is reflection on God (Brahm), like the teaching given in Kashi to a man at the hour of his death. Whoever sings or hears the Name of the Lord with the mind attuned, says Kabir: there is no doubt; in the end he attains the supreme state. ॥4॥
Kashi: by the Puranas, Shiva whispers the saving mantra (the Name of Ram) into the ear of one who dies in Kashi (Benares), and he is liberated.
335.3: Raag Gauri, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji. All who make (such) efforts have drowned; (these efforts) have not carried (them) across the world-ocean, O brother. Performing rites, religious duties and many disciplines, (their) mind is burnt up by the ego-intellect, O brother. The Master is the giver of breath and food; why have you forgotten him from your mind, O brother? (Human) birth is a diamond, a priceless ruby; you have lost it in exchange for a cowrie shell, O brother. Through wandering, craving, thirst and hunger cling to you; you have not reflected in your heart, O brother. Intoxicated, robbed by pride within your mind, you have not held the Guru's Shabad (within), O brother. Greedy for tastes, driven by the pleasures of the senses, you take the heady relish of vices, O brother. Those whose destiny holds good deeds join the Sants; (the Lord) saves them, as wood carries iron across, O brother. Running, wandering through species and births, I am weary; now, worn by suffering, I have given up, O brother. Says Kabir: on meeting the Guru (I found) the supreme relish; loving devotion has carried (me) across, O brother. ॥4॥
335.4: Raag Gauri, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji. Like the she-elephant built on a frame (to trap an elephant), O crazed mind, is the play the Lord of the world has staged: through the lure of lust the elephant is caught, O crazed mind, and bears the goad upon his head. Keep clear of vices and merge in the Lord; understand this, O crazed mind. You have not become fearless and worshipped the Lord, O crazed mind; you have not taken hold of the ship of Ram. The monkey stretched out his hand and grabbed a fistful of grain, O crazed mind; then the worry of getting free fell on him, O crazed mind, and he was made to dance at the door of house after house. As the parrot is caught by the nalini, O crazed mind, such is the dealing of Maya. As is the colour of safflower (bright, and soon gone), O crazed mind, so is this expanse spread out. There are many tiraths to bathe at, O crazed mind, and many gods to worship; says Kabir: (by these) there is no release, O crazed mind; release lies in the service of the Lord. ॥4॥
A monkey is trapped with grain put in a narrow-mouthed pot: the full fist will not come out, and the greedy monkey will not let go, so he is caught, and the showman makes him dance from door to door.
Nalini: a parrot trap, a turning tube baited with grain over water; when the parrot perches, the tube turns over, and in fear of falling he clings to it and is caught.
336.1: Raag Gauri, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji. Fire does not burn it, wind does not blow it away, no thief comes near it: gather the wealth of the Name of Ram; that wealth goes nowhere. My wealth is Madho, Gobind, who upholds the earth; this, it is said, is wealth of the finest kind. The peace that lies in serving God, Gobind, is not to be had in kingship. For this wealth Shiv and Sanak and his brothers searched, and became detached (from the world). With Mukand in the mind and Narayan on the tongue, the noose of Jam does not fall (on one). The Guru has given (me) wealth truly my own, divine knowledge and devotion; with good understanding (my) mind is fixed on it. (It is) water for the burning, a pillar for the running mind; the fear of doubt's bonds has fled. Says Kabir: O you drunk with desire, reflect and see in your heart: your house holds lakhs and crores of horses and elephants; my house holds the one Murari. ॥4॥
336.2: Raag Gauri, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji. As the monkey, in his greed, would not let go the fistful of chickpeas in his hand, (so) whatever deeds were done in greed, those in turn fell around (one's) neck. Without devotion, life has gone in vain; without the Saadh Sangat and the worship of the Lord (Bhagvan), the True One has abided nowhere. As a flower blossoms in the wilderness and no one takes its fragrance, so (beings) wander through many species, and are slain by death again and again. This wealth, youth, sons and wife, which (the Lord) gave (only) to behold: those who stick fast in these very things and are entangled, the senses have pulled them along. The passing of life is a fire, the body a house of straw; on all four sides this is how it is built. Says Kabir: to cross the terrifying ocean, I have taken refuge with the True Guru. ॥4॥
Tin ko mandar: tin is straw or grass; the body is a house of straw, set alight by the fire of passing life.
336.3: Raag Gauri, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji. The water (the father's seed) is unclean, the clay (the mother's blood) is red; of this clay a puppet has been put together. I am nothing, and nothing is mine; body, wealth and all (its) life-sap are yours, O Gobind. Into this clay the breath (of life) has entered, and (on it) a false show has been put together and set going. Someone has amassed five lakh (in wealth); at the last hour the pitcher (of the body) broke. Says Kabir: the foundation that has been raised is destroyed in an instant, O proud one. ॥4॥
337.1: Raag Gauri, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji. O my soul, let me repeat (the Name of) Ram in such a way, as Dhru and Prahlad repeated (the Name of) the Lord. O merciful to the meek, trusting in you I have put all my family aboard the boat. When it pleases him, he makes (them) obey his Hukam, and carries this boat across. By the Guru's grace such understanding has entered (me) that coming and going (in births) again has ended. Says Kabir: worship Saringpani; on this shore and the far shore, know the One alone in all. ॥4॥
Dhru: the child prince who, slighted by his stepmother, gave himself to devotion and was given an unmoving place as the Pole Star.
337.2: Raag Gauri 9, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji. When, leaving the womb, (a being) came into the world, as soon as the air (of the world) touched it, it forgot the Master. O my soul, sing the praises of the Lord. In the womb it practised austerity, hanging head down; then it lived (unharmed) in the fire of the belly. Wandering through the eighty-four lakh forms of life, it has come (to this birth); if it misses this time, there is no place or resting place (for it). Says Kabir: worship Saringpani; (a being) is seen coming, but its going is not known. ॥4॥
It was believed that the child in the womb, hanging head down like an ascetic doing penance upside down, remembers God.
337.3: Raag Gauri Poorbi, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji. Let us not crave a dwelling in heaven, nor fear a dwelling in hell; what is to be will be; let us not build hopes in the mind. Let us sing the praises of the dear Lord (Ramaiya), from whom the supreme treasure is obtained. What use is chanting, what use austerity and self-discipline, what use fasting, what use bathing (at tiraths), as long as the way of loving devotion to the Lord (Bhagvan) is not known? Let us not be elated at the sight of prosperity, nor weep at the sight of adversity; as prosperity is, so is adversity: what the Creator has ordained comes to pass. Says Kabir: now I have come to know (that the Lord dwells) within the hearts of the Sants; those servants are good in (their) service in whose hearts Murari dwells. ॥4॥
337.4: Raag Gauri, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji. O mind, no one is yours; do not drag (others') burden onto yourself. Like the birds' night-roost in a tree, such is this world. I have drunk the relish of Ram, O brother, through which relish all other relishes are forgotten. Why weep when others die, when one's own self does not stay fixed? Whatever is born will perish; let misfortune weep in grief, not I. (My soul) is absorbed in the One from whom it sprang, drinking (this relish) in the company of the brave (devotees). Says Kabir: I have kept (Ram) in my mind; remembering Ram, (I have found) detachment. ॥3॥
337.5: Raag Gauri, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji. The woman watches the road; her eyes brimming (with tears), she heaves deep sighs; her heart is not soothed, her foot does not stir, in the hope of the sight of the Lord. Fly away, O black crow, that I may soon meet my beloved Ram. Says Kabir: to attain the state of (true) life, let devotion to the Lord be practised; the Name of Narayan is the one support: let the tongue repeat Ram. ॥2॥
A woman awaiting her husband from abroad shoos the crow from the roof: if it flies off, her beloved is said to be coming. In udahu na, the na is not a negative but a fond entreaty.
338.1: Raag Gauri 11, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji. (He) around whom grew thick clumps of tulsi (holy basil), who sang with love in the midst of the woods: beholding his form, the milkmaid was enchanted (and said): do not leave me to come or go (elsewhere). My mind is fixed on your feet, O Saringdhar (the Lord who bears the bow); he alone meets you who is greatly fortunate. In Brindaban, he who steals the mind, the enchanting Krishna, grazes the cows; O Saringdhar, (I am the one) whose Master you are; my name is Kabir. ॥2॥
Kabir takes the longing of the milkmaid of Gokul, enchanted by Krishna in Brindaban, as the picture of his own love for the Lord.
338.2: Raag Gauri Poorbi 12, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji. Many have put on ample (holy) robes; what (comes) of living in the forest? What came of it, O man, if gods were worshipped with incense? What, if (the body) was knowingly drowned in water? O soul, you will depart: this I know. Understand the Unmanifest (Lord), O ignorant one. Whatever I look upon, I do not see again; (yet you) are wrapped up in Maya. The learned, the meditative, the great preachers: this whole world is (caught in Maya's) entanglement. Says Kabir: lacking the Name of the one Ram, this world goes blind in Maya. ॥2॥
338.3: Raag Gauri 12, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji. O mind, you whom this Maya holds to punishment, give up doubt and dance in the open. What warrior is he who shrinks from the battle he faces? What sati is she who gathers up her pots? Give up wavering, O crazed mind; now that the sindhaura has been taken in hand, fulfilment comes only by burning and dying. Seized by lust, anger and Maya, in this way the world is ruined. Says Kabir: I will not forsake Ram, the King, the highest of all the high. ॥2॥
Sindhaura: the coconut smeared with vermilion that a widow took in her hand as she went to be burned on her husband's pyre; once she had taken it, there was no turning back.
338.4: Raag Gauri 13, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji. I bear your command upon my head; I do not turn round to weigh it. You are the river, you are the boatman; from you alone comes deliverance. O man, take up the worship (of the Lord), whether the Master shows anger or love. Your Name is my support, as the flower lives in water. Says Kabir: I am the slave of your house; keep me alive or kill me, as you please. ॥2॥
338.5: Raag Gauri, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji. (You say that) Nand grew very weary, wandering among the beings of the eighty-four lakh forms of life, and for (his) devotion (God) took birth (in his house): great was the fortune of that poor man. You who say, O brother, that (God became) the son of Nand: whose son, then, was that Nand? When there was neither earth nor sky, nor the ten directions, where then was this Nand? He falls into no affliction (of birth and death) and enters no womb, the One whose Name is Niranjan. Such is Kabir's Lord and Master: he has neither mother nor father. ॥2॥
Nand: the cowherd of Gokul in whose home, by the Puranas, Krishna was brought up; Kabir answers the belief that God was born as anyone's son.
339.1: Raag Gauri, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji. Let people slander me, slander me, slander me (as much as they like); to (the Lord's) servant, slander is truly dear; slander is (his) father, slander (his) mother. If slander comes, one goes to Baikunth, and the treasure of the Naam is made to dwell in the mind. If slander comes while the heart is pure, the slanderer washes my clothes. Whoever slanders me is my friend; my mind stays on the slanderer. The (true) slanderer is the one who holds back slander (of me); the slanderer wants my life (to be made good). Slander of me is love and affection (to me); slander brings about my deliverance. For the servant Kabir, slander is the best (of things): the slanderer has drowned, and I have crossed over. ॥3॥
339.2: O Ram, the King, so fearless are you; you are the boat that carries (beings) across, O Sovereign Ram. When I was (in my ego), you were not (in me); now you are, and I am not. Now we two, you and I, are one; beholding the One alone, my mind is at rest. When (pride in my own) cleverness held sway, what strength (of spirit) was there? Now (pride in) cleverness and strength no longer holds. Says Kabir: (the Lord) has taken away my (proud) intellect; my intellect is changed, and (I) have reached fulfilment. ॥2॥
339.3: Raag Gauri, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji. Of six rings (the five elements and the mind) the little room (of the body) has been built, and an incomparable thing has been placed within it; the breath of life has been made its lock and key; in making it, (the Creator) took no time. Now stay awake, O mind, O brother: heedless, (you) have wasted your life; the thief goes in and plunders the house. Five watchmen (the senses) stay at the door, but there is no trusting them. Keep (the Lord) in mind, stay alert in your thought, and then you will receive the light, the brightness (within). The soul-bride who, seeing the nine houses (of the body), went astray has not found the incomparable thing. Says Kabir: when the nine houses are plundered (their hold stripped away), in the tenth the essence (of the Lord) is found abiding. ॥3॥
339.4: Raag Gauri, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji. O mother, I have known no other, none besides (the Lord): my breath of life dwells in him whose virtues Shiv and Sanak and the others sing. By the wisdom the Guru has imparted, the heart is lit, and attention is fixed in the realm of the sky (the Tenth Gate). The diseases of the senses' pleasures, fear and bonds have fled; in its own home the mind has known peace. (My) good understanding is in love with the One; knowing God and trusting him, (I) bring no second into my mind. The mind's cravings given up, there is (within) the fragrance of sandalwood, and pride has dwindled. The servant who sings and meditates on the Master's praise: in him God makes his dwelling. Great is the fortune of one in whose mind (God) has come to dwell; the highest destiny is on his forehead. Shakti (Maya) cut away, the Sahaj of Shiv (the Lord) has shone forth, and (the mind) has merged in the One alone. Says Kabir: in meeting the Guru there is supreme peace; the wandering has ended, and the mind is at rest. ॥4॥
340.1: Raag Gauri Poorbi, Bavan Akhri: the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji. There is one God, Ik Oankar, the One who pervades all and is ever the same; his Name is Sat (the One who truly is); he is the Creator, the Being who dwells in all, realised by the Guru's grace. Fifty-two letters (serve) the three worlds; all things are (held) in these alone. These letters will wear away; those letters (that could tell of union with the Lord) are not among them. ॥1॥
340.2: Where there is speech, letters come in; where (the state) beyond speech is, there the mind itself does not remain. In speech and in the speechless alike, he alone is; (yet) as he truly is, so no one can perceive him. ॥2॥
340.3: If I find the Unfindable, what can I say (of him)? And if I do speak, what good is it? As the banyan lies in its seed, so he pervades (all), the One whose spread is the three worlds. ॥3॥
340.4: Seeking the Unfindable, (my) sense of separateness has been destroyed, and I have grasped something of (his) mystery. With separateness overturned, the mind is pierced (with the Lord), and (I) have found the One who cannot be broken or pierced. ॥4॥
340.5: The Turk (the Muslim) is known by the tariqat, the Hindu by the Vedas and the Puranas; (but) for the mind's instruction, one should read something of (divine) wisdom. ॥5॥
Tariqat: the second of the four stages of the Sufi path to God (shariat, tariqat, marifat, haqiqat), the stage of the heart's purification.
340.6: Oankar (the all-pervading Lord) I have known as the Origin (of all); the one whom he writes and erases I do not accept (as God). If anyone perceives Oankar, then, having perceived him, (that one) is not destroyed. ॥6॥
340.7: Kaka: if I bring the ray (of the sun of wisdom) into the lotus (of the heart), then in the light of the moon (of Maya) it does not close (again). And if there I taste the nectar of the flower, it is beyond telling: what can I say? What can I explain by speaking? ॥7॥
The lotus opens to the sun's ray and closes when the moon rises.
340.8: Khakha: (when) this mind comes into the hollow (of its own true self), it does not leave the hollow to run off in the ten directions. One who, knowing the Master, abides in forbearance then becomes imperishable and attains the undying state. ॥8॥
340.9: Gaga: one who has recognised the Guru's word lends no ear to any other talk. He lives like a bird (unattached), and strays nowhere; he takes hold of the Ungraspable (in his heart), and, holding him, keeps to the sky within (the Tenth Gate). ॥9॥
340.10: Ghagha: in every body he alone dwells; when the pitcher (of the body) breaks, he is never lessened. When one finds within that very body the ford (for crossing over), why would he leave that ford and run into pathless ravines? ॥10॥
340.11: Nganga: restrain (the senses), love (the Lord), and cast out doubt. Do not run away on seeing that (it seems) it cannot be done: this is the highest wisdom. ॥11॥
340.12: Chacha: (this world) that he has made is a vast picture; leave the picture and keep the Painter in mind. This is the snare: the picture is wondrous (and enticing); leave the picture, and keep your mind on the Painter. ॥12॥
340.13: Chhachha: the Sovereign of the royal canopy is right here beside (you); why not stay absorbed (in him)? Why not give up (other) hopes? O mind, every moment I counsel you: leaving him, where are you getting yourself bound? ॥13॥
340.14: Jaja: when one burns (the cravings of) the body while still alive, burning away (the pride of) youth, he finds the (true) way (to live). When, burning away (the sense of) mine and others', he lives on, enduring (all), then he goes on (to the higher state) and finds the brightness of the (divine) Light. ॥14॥
341.1: Jhajha: one who (learned only) to be entangled, and never knew how to get free, stayed hesitating, and was not accepted. What (use) is it to wrangle and wrangle to instruct others? By quarrelling, only quarrels are gained. ॥15॥
341.2: Nyanya: he dwells close by, in the heart; forsaking him, where do you go so far? The One for whom I searched the world, I found close at hand. ॥16॥
341.3: Tatta: the hard ford (to the Lord) is within the heart itself; why not open the doors (of Maya) and go into (the Lord's) mansion? Seeing the Unmoving One, (the mind) does not waver and go elsewhere; it stays clinging (to him), and in the heart comes to know him intimately. ॥17॥
341.4: Thattha: this (Maya) is deceiving water seen from afar (a mirage); looking closely, again and again, I have made (my) mind steady. The cheat who by cheating has swallowed the whole world: by cheating that cheat, (my) mind has come to its place of rest. ॥18॥
341.5: Dadda: when (God's) fear arises, (worldly) fear goes; in that fear (every other) fear is absorbed. If one shrinks in fear from (God's) fear, then (worldly) fear clings again. One who has (so) become fearless: whatever fear is in his heart runs away. ॥19॥
341.6: Dhaddha: (the Lord is) near; why search for (him) elsewhere? In the very searching, the breath of life is spent. When, having climbed Sumer and searched, (I) came back, the One who built the fortress (of the body) I found within the fortress. ॥20॥
341.7: Nanna: the man who, engaged on the battlefield, holds firm, who neither bows down (to the vices) nor goes along (with them): his birth alone (the world) counts blessed, (for he) slays the one (the mind) and leaves the many (vices) behind. ॥21॥
341.8: Tata: (the world-ocean) is uncrossable; it cannot be crossed, (while) the body (with its senses) stays sunk in (the things of) the three worlds. When the three worlds are absorbed within the body, then essence (the soul) merges with essence (the Lord), and the True One is found. ॥22॥
341.9: Thatha: the depth of the Fathomless cannot be found; he is fathomless, and this (mind) does not stay still. On a little patch of ground it sets about (building great) towns, and would hold up a mansion with no pillars at all. ॥23॥
341.10: Dada: all that is seen is bound to perish; keep in your thought the One who is unseen, as he is. When the key is turned in the Tenth Gate, then one has the sight of the Merciful One. ॥24॥
341.11: Dhadha: the lower (the soul) finds its settlement in the Higher (the Lord), (when) the lower dwells within the Higher. When (the soul) leaves the lower (state) and comes up to the higher, then the lower and the Higher meet, and peace is found. ॥25॥
341.12: Nana: night and day pass in watching (for the Lord); watching, the eyes have grown red (with love). When, watching and watching, (one) at last finds (him), then the One watched for takes the watcher and unites (him with himself). ॥26॥
341.13: Pappa: the end of the One beyond whom there is none cannot be found; one who has formed a bond with the Supreme Light holds all five senses in check, and puts away both sin and virtue. ॥27॥
341.14: Phapha: without flowering (into pride), the fruit (of life) comes; if anyone perceives even a sliver of that fruit and reflects on that sliver, he does not fall into the valley (of birth and death); a sliver of that fruit tears apart all (attachment to) the body. ॥28॥
341.15: Babba: (as) a drop merges with a drop, (so the soul) that comes to know (the Lord) even for a moment cannot be parted (from him again). One who becomes (the Lord's) servant and holds fast to his worship, becoming one who sings his praise, sees through the bonds (of Maya). ॥29॥
342.1: Bhabha: (the one who) has pierced the gulf (between him and the Lord) and joined (his mind to him), now, with fear shattered, has come to trust (in the Lord). The (Lord) who is outside (in all the world) he has known (dwelling) within; (when) the secret was opened, he recognised the Master of the earth. ॥30॥
342.2: Mamma: holding fast to the Root (of all), the mind is won over (and stops wandering); one who knows this secret comes to understand the mind. When the mind is coming to meet (the Lord), let no one delay: absorbed (in him), one finds the True (Lord). ॥31॥
342.3: Mamma: (one's real) task is with the mind; by disciplining the mind, success is won. Says Kabir: (the dealing) is with the mind alone, with the mind; I have met no other like the mind. ॥32॥
342.4: This mind is Shakti (Maya), this mind is Shiv (the Lord, the giver of good); this mind is what gives life to the body of five elements. When (one) takes this mind in hand and dwells in the state of unman, then he speaks of (the Lord who fills) the three worlds. ॥33॥

Shakti and Shiv: in Hindu thought the Goddess (the power of Maya) and Shiv; the Darpan and the Faridkot Teeka read that the mind becomes what it joins: Maya with Maya, the Lord with the Lord, the body with the body. Unman: the state of the mind raised above the world's thoughts and settled in the Lord.
342.5: Yaya: if you would know (the way), destroy your evil-mindedness and bring the village of the body under your rule. Locked in battle, if (you) do not run away, (only) then do you bear the name of hero. ॥34॥
342.6: Rara: (the one who) has known the relish (of Maya) as tasteless, becoming free of (these) relishes, has recognised that relish (of the Name). By giving up these relishes, that relish has been found; (whoever) has drunk that nectar, this relish does not please (him). ॥35॥
342.7: Lala: if the mind fixes its attention (on the Lord) in such a way that it goes nowhere else, it finds the Supreme, the True (Lord); and if there it fixes the attention of love, then it finds the Unfindable (Lord), and having found him, merges in his feet. ॥36॥
342.8: Vava: again and again remember Bisan (the Lord); remembering Bisan, one does not come away defeated (in the game of life). I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice, to the son of Bisan (his devotee) who sings his praise; meeting Bisan, one finds the True (Lord) everywhere. ॥37॥
Bisan (Vishnu) is here a name of the one Lord; the Bisantana, the son of Bisan, is his devotee, who like a child knows him alone as his keeper.
342.9: Vaava: him alone should we know; by knowing him, this (soul) becomes (one with him). When this (soul) and that (Lord) meet, then, once met, no one can know them apart. ॥38॥
342.10: Sassa: search him out (and remember him) with all care; hold (the mind) to the words by which the heart is won over (to the Lord). When the heart is won over and love wells up, there the King of the three worlds is (seen) filling all. ॥39॥
342.11: Khakha: if anyone sets out to search (for the Lord), whoever finds (him) does not come (into birth) again. If (one) understands the signs (of the Lord) and reflects (on his virtues), then (he) is not long in crossing the world-ocean. ॥40॥
342.12: Sassa: she (the soul-bride) adorns the bed (of the heart) for her Husband Lord; she alone, the friend, is rid of (her) doubt, (who) has given up petty pleasure and gained the supreme bliss; then this one is called the wife, and that one the Husband. ॥41॥
342.13: Haha: having come into (human) being, (one) has not known (the Lord) who truly is. Only when (the certainty of his being) comes is the mind won over. He surely is, if anyone could perceive it; then (the soul) is he himself, and is no longer this (separate self). ॥42॥
342.14: All the world goes about crying, Let me take, let me take; for its sake, great sorrow besets (them). When (one) fixes his attention on the Husband of Lakshmi (the Lord), sorrow is wiped out, and he finds every comfort. ॥43॥
342.15: Khakha: wasting and wearing away, many (lives) have gone by; wasting and wearing away, (one) does not remember (the Lord) even now. Now, if knowing (what) the world (is), the mind holds steady (in the Lord), it finds a firm place there, (in the Lord) from whom it was parted. ॥44॥
343.1: (People) have brought the fifty-two letters and joined them together, (but) they could not recognise the One Akhar (the Imperishable). Kabir speaks the Shabad of the True (Lord); one who is a (true) pandit abides in the direct experience (of the Lord). For pandits (these letters) are a trade, for the wise, (a means of) reflecting on the essence. As the understanding is in one's heart, Says Kabir: so will that one know. ॥45॥
343.2: Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Raag Gauri, Thiti: the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji. (People keep) the fifteen lunar days and the seven weekdays; Says Kabir: (I sing the Lord, who has) neither a near shore nor a far one. When seekers and Siddhas come to know his secret, (they see that) he himself is the Creator, he himself the Lord of light. ॥1॥
343.3: Amavas: on the new-moon day, let go of the hopes (you set on fasts and rites); remember Ram, the Knower of hearts. (So) while yet alive you will reach the gate of liberation, and the Shabad, known by direct experience, (will be) the finest essence of your own self. ॥1॥
343.4: One who is dyed with love for the lotus feet of Gobind, by the grace of the Sant (the Guru) has become pure in mind; night and day he stays awake in the Kirtan of the Lord.
343.5: Pariva: reflect on (the virtues of) the Beloved, who, bodiless and boundless, plays within every body. The dread of death never eats away at (the one who reflects on him), (for) he stays merged in the Primal Being. ॥2॥
343.6: Dutiya: (such a one) knows (the world) as made of two parts, Maya and Brahm (God); (God) pervades along with all. He neither grows nor wanes; without lineage, the Niranjan stays ever the same. ॥3॥
343.7: Tritiya: one who brings the three (qualities of Maya) into balance attains the supreme state, the source of bliss. In the Saadh Sangat faith wells up (in him) that outside and within there is always (the Lord's) light. ॥4॥
343.8: Chauthahi: keep hold of the fickle mind, and never sit in the company of lust and anger. He who is himself all in all, in the water and on the land: (joined) to him, repeat the chant that is truly your own. ॥5॥
343.9: Panchai: (this world) is a spread of the five elements; (in it) the business of the two, gold and woman, (goes on). Rare is the one who drinks the nectar of love (for the Lord); the pain of old age and death does not come (to him) again. ॥6॥
343.10: Chhath: the six wheels (the five senses and the mind) run in all six directions; unless won over (to the Lord), they do not stay still. Erase duality and hold fast to forbearance, (and) do not suffer the torment of rituals and rites. ॥7॥

Khat chakra (the six wheels): taking the name of the yogis' six chakras, here, by the Darpan and the Faridkot Teeka, the five senses and the mind; the six directions are the four quarters, below and above.
343.11: Saatain: know the Word (of the Guru) as true, (and) take the all-pervading Lord (Atam Ram) to heart. (So) doubt is cast off, sorrows are wiped away, and in the pool of Sunn you will find peace. ॥8॥
343.12: Astami: the body is (made) of eight elements; within it dwells the (Lord) without lineage, the King of the great treasure. The one to whom the wisdom of the Guru, who has reached (him), tells this secret turns back (from love of the body) and dwells in the Indestructible, the Impenetrable. ॥9॥
The eight elements (dhatu): in the old count, the eight constituents of the body (by the Darpan: chyle, blood, flesh, fat, bone, marrow, semen and the nerves).
343.13: Naumi: discipline the nine doors (of the body), and keep bound the desires of the mind that flow out (through them). Forget greed, attachment and all (the vices); (then) you will live through the ages and eat the fruit that never perishes. ॥10॥
344.1: Dasmi: there is bliss in all ten directions, doubt departs, and Gobind is met, who is the embodiment of light, the essence (of all), beyond compare, stainless, without any stain; (there) is neither shade nor sunshine. ॥11॥
344.2: Ekadasi: if (the mind) runs in one direction (to the One), then (one) does not come into the anguish of births again. (One's) body becomes cool and pure; the (Lord) said to be far off is found close by. ॥12॥
344.3: Baras: twelve suns rise (within, as it were); day and night the unstruck trumpets sound; (one) sees the Master of the three worlds; a wonder comes to pass: from a (mere) creature he becomes Shiv (one with the Lord). ॥13॥
Twelve suns: the Puranas count twelve suns (the Adityas); here they are the full light of knowledge risen within.
344.4: Teras: (one who) on the thirteenth (day) tells of the Unreachable (Lord) recognises (him) as the same, from below to above. (For him) there is no low or high, no honour or dishonour: Ram (is seen) pervading all alike. ॥14॥
344.5: Chaudas: in the fourteen worlds, in every hair (of them), dwells Murari (the Lord). Fix your mind on truth and contentment, (and) speak the words (that bring) the knowledge of Brahm (God). ॥15॥
344.6: Puniu: (as on the full-moon night) the moon is full in the sky, (and all its) phases spread out, (so within) shines the light of Sahaj. (The Lord) stays unmoving at the beginning, at the end and in between; Kabir delights in (him), the ocean of peace. ॥16॥
344.7: Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Raag Gauri, Vaar Sat (the seven days): the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji. Again and again I sing the virtues of the Lord; reaching the Guru, I find that secret of the Lord. Aadit: (one who) makes a beginning of devotion, and in the temple of the body holds desire in check, (his) attention flows on unbroken, day and night; then the unstruck flute plays in Sahaj. Somvar: the Amrit of the moon (its cool peace) trickles (within); the moment it is tasted, it takes away every poison. Held back by the Bani, (the mind) stays at (the Lord's) door; then the mind, intoxicated, becomes the drinker (of that Amrit). Mangalvar: (one) draws a wall (around the mind), and comes to know the ways of the five thieves (lust and the rest). Do not leave (this) house and go outside, or else the King (the Lord) will be sorely angered. Budhvar: (one) brings the light (of the Name) to the intellect, (and) makes the heart-lotus the dwelling of the Lord. Meeting the Guru, (one) holds the two (the soul and the Lord) as one, (and) takes the upturned lotus (of the heart) and sets it upright. Brihaspati: (one) washes away the poison (of Maya), (and) joins the three gods to the One. (Those who live) in the trikuti, (the fretting of Maya,) are (swept along) there in the three rivers (of the three qualities); day and night they do not wash away (their) sins. Sukrit: one who makes good deeds his support climbs (the steep path of) this vow: night and day he fights against his own self; he keeps all five senses in check; then the eye of duality never enters (him). Thavar: (one) keeps it steady, the little lamp of (the Lord's) light that (burns) in the heart; outside and within, light shines; then all (past) karma is destroyed. As long as the heart leans on another, so long is there no entering the mansion (of the Lord). Remembering Ram, love for Ram takes hold; Says Kabir: then every limb becomes pure. ॥8॥

Vaar Sat (the seven days): each stanza opens with a day of the week: Aadit (Sunday), Somvar (Monday), Mangalvar (Tuesday), Budhvar (Wednesday), Brihaspati (Thursday) and Thavar (Saturday); Friday's (Shukarvar's) stanza opens with the like-sounding sukrit, good deeds. In place of each day's fasts and observances, Kabir draws a lesson in devotion from its name.

The upturned lotus: the heart turned away from the Lord. Trikuti (the knitted brow, 18.2) the Darpan reads as the mind's fretting; yogis give the name trikuti to the point between the brows, where the ida, pingala and sukhmana are held to meet, and the Faridkot Teeka and the Santhya read the line as bathing there day and night in that inner Triveni to wash away sins.
345.1: Raag Gauri Cheti, the hymn of Bhagat Namdev Ji. Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. O Lord, you carried even stones across (the sea); why then should your servants, uttering the Name of Ram, not cross over? You saved the courtesan, and Kubija who had no beauty; you saved Ajamal, sick with sin; the hunter who struck (Krishna's) foot with his arrow: even such people were set free. I am a sacrifice, again and again, to those who have uttered the Name of Ram. Bidar, the son of a maidservant, (became) your servant, and Sudama too; to Ugrasain you gave the kingdom. Without recitations, without austerities, without high birth, without good deeds: O Master of Namdev, even they crossed over. ॥2॥
Stones: the stones of Ram's bridge to Lanka, said to have floated because his Name was written on them.

Ganika: a courtesan, saved by teaching a parrot to say Ram; Kubija: the hunchbacked maid of Kans, made straight and fair by Krishna; Ajamal: a fallen Brahmin, saved when at death he called his son Narayan; the hunter: Jara, who shot Krishna in the foot, taking him for a deer.
Bidar (Vidura): born of a maidservant, a devotee of Krishna; Sudama: Krishna's poor Brahmin friend, made rich by him; Ugrasain: the father of Kans, restored to the throne when Krishna slew Kans.
345.2: Raag Gauri, Pade of Bhagat Ravidas Ji: Gauri Guareri. There is one God, Ik Oankar, the One who pervades all and is ever the same; his Name is Sat (the One who truly is); he is the Creator, the Being who dwells in all, realised by the Guru's grace. The company I keep is low, and this worry stays with me day and night; my deeds are crooked, and my birth is lowly. O Ram, Gusaiya (Master of the earth), you who are the life of my soul, do not forget me; I am your servant. Take away my distress, and make your servant one of good heart; I will not let go of your feet, even if the strength of my body goes. Says Ravidas: I have come into your keeping; come and meet your servant soon; make no delay. The city's name is Begampura (the town without sorrow); in that place there is neither pain nor grief; there is no anxiety there, no tax and no property; no fear, no wrongdoing, no dread, no decline. Now I have found a fine homeland to live in; there, my brother, all is always well. Its rule stands firm and lasting, for ever; none there is second or third (in rank); all are alike. It is ever peopled and renowned; those who dwell there are rich and fulfilled. They go about wherever they please; they are intimates of the (Master's) palace, and no one holds them back. Says Ravidas the Chamar (of the leather-working caste), who has been set free: whoever lives in our city is our friend. ॥3॥
Begampura (be-gham, without sorrow): the city is the soul's own state in union with the Lord, reached in this life, set against the heaven that others promise after death.
345.3: Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Raag Gauri Bairagan, the hymn of Bhagat Ravidas Ji. The mountain passes are very hard to cross, and the one ox I have is good for nothing; I make one prayer to the beloved Lord (Ramaiya): O Murari, protect my capital. Is there any trader of the Lord (to go along with me), O brother? My caravan is laden and on its way. I am a trader of the Lord; my trade is in Sahaj; The load I have taken on is the Lord's Name, my wealth; poison is the load the world has taken on. O knowers of (the deeds of) this world and the next, write (about me) whatever idle stuff you like; Jam's punishment does not touch me, for I have given up all entanglements. As is the colour of safflower, so is this world; the colour of my beloved Lord's (love) is the (fast) colour of madder, says Ravidas the Chamar. ॥4॥
The trader is the seeker: his ox is the mind, his capital and cargo the Lord's Name, and the hard mountain passes the lures of the senses on the way.
The knowers of this world and the next: Chitr and Gupt, who write down each one's deeds for Jam.
346.1: Raag Gauri Poorbi, the hymn of Bhagat Ravidas Ji. Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. As frogs fill a well and know nothing of any land, their own or another, just so my mind is bewitched by Maya, and it can see nothing of this shore or the far one. O Master of all the worlds, let me see you, if only for a moment. My understanding has grown soiled, O Madhav (Lord); your state cannot be known (by me). Have mercy, that my doubt may end; teach me, and give me right understanding. Even the masters of yoga do not reach (the end of) your virtues; the telling of them has no limit. Says Ravidas the Chamar: (I ask for your sight) for the sake of loving devotion. ॥3॥
346.2: Raag Gauri Bairagan, the hymn of Bhagat Ravidas Ji. Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. (The scriptures say:) in Satjug (the way was) truth, in Treta sacrifices, in Duapar the rites of worship; the three ages held firmly to these three; in Kalyug the Name alone is the support. How then will (one) reach the far shore, O brother? No one explains to me clearly (the way) by which coming and going (birth and death) would end. Religious duties are set out in many ways, and the whole world is seen performing them; (but) by which deed is one set free, the deed whose practice brings complete fulfilment? If one weighs the deeds enjoined and the deeds forbidden, hearing the Vedas and Puranas (only) raises doubt; doubt dwells always in the heart; who (then) will take away the pride? The outside (of the body) is washed with water, (but) within the heart are vices of many kinds; in what way will (one) become pure? Such purity is like the way of the elephant (which bathes and then throws dust on itself). As the whole world knows how night passes away when the sun gives its light, and know that copper touched by the paaras takes no time to become gold, (so,) if it is written on the forehead from before, one meets the Guru, the supreme paaras; the mind, in the state of unman, meets (the Lord) within itself, and the adamant doors open. Whoever, by the way of devotion, has made his understanding true, cutting away doubt, bonds and vices, he alone, dwelling (in the Lord) in joy, meets him in the mind, reflecting on the One who is both with qualities and beyond them. Many efforts at restraint are made, (yet) the noose of doubt does not go, however one tries to remove it; loving devotion does not spring up (from them); therefore Ravidas has turned away from them. ॥8॥
Satjug, Treta, Duapar and Kalyug: the four ages of the Puranic count; the scriptures give each age its own way to liberation, which Ravidas questions here.

151.1: Raag Gauri Guareri, Chaupade and Dupade, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).

There is one God, Ik Oankar, the One who pervades all and is ever the same; his Name is Sat (the One who truly is); he is the Creator, the Being who dwells in all, without fear, without enmity, his form beyond time, unborn, self-existent, realised by the Guru's grace.
The fear of God is very heavy; its weight is great.
The mind's own counsel is light, and (one who follows it) speaks light words.
If one walks with (this fear) set upon the head and bears its weight,
then, by (God's) glance of grace and his favour, the Guru's wisdom is gained.
No one crosses (the world-ocean) without the fear (of God).
(Only they cross who,) living in that fear and adorning (their lives) with love, have kept the fear (in the heart).
In the fear (of God) the fire within the body blazes, and with that fear it keeps ablaze;
in the fear, and adorned through the Shabad, a life of reverent fear is fashioned.
Without the fear, what is fashioned is raw, utterly raw:
the mould is blind, and blind is the hammer's stroke.
In (the self-willed one's) intellect arises a craving for the play (of the world);
for all its thousand clevernesses, the heat (of the fear) does not reach it.
O Nanak, the speech of the manmukh is (empty as) the wind;
his word is blind, idle wind and worthless. ॥3॥
151.2: Raag Gauri, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Through the fear (of God) one finds the home (within), and in that home dwells the fear; through that fear, (every other) fear departs.
What sort of fear is that, if in it some (other) fear still takes hold?
(O Lord,) apart from you there is no other place (of refuge);
whatever happens is all your will.
One would be afraid if there were some other to fear;
to live in fear upon fear is only the turmoil of the mind.
The soul does not die, nor does it drown or swim across.
He who made (all) this does everything.
By his Hukam one comes, and by his Hukam one goes;
in this world and the next, one abides within his Hukam.
Where there is cruelty, attachment, desire and pride,
there hunger (craving) runs high, like a river (in flood).
The fear (of God) is (the soul's) food and drink, its support;
without eating it, the foolish waste away and die.
Rare, very rare, is the one who has someone (to call his own);
everyone is yours, and you are the one who cares for all.
He to whom belong all beings and creatures, all wealth and property:
O Nanak, to describe him and to reflect on him is hard. ॥4॥
151.3: Raag Gauri, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Make wisdom your mother and contentment your father,
and make truthful living your special brother.
There is something to say, but it cannot be said:
(O Lord,) the worth of your creation cannot be reckoned.
Effort and awareness, these two, have become the parents-in-law,
and, O mind, good conduct has been taken as the wife.
Union (with the holy) is the wedding day, and parting (from the world) the marriage;
truth is the offspring: says Nanak, this is the union (with God). ॥3॥
152.1: Raag Gauri, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
(The body) is a union of air, water and fire,
the play of a restless, fickle intellect.
(It has) nine doors, and the Tenth Gate:
O wise one, understand this thought.
He (the Lord) alone is the one who speaks, utters and hears.
The one who reflects on his own self becomes truly wise.
The body is clay; it is the air (the breath) that speaks.
O wise one, understand: who is it that has died?
What has died is the awareness (that ran after Maya), strife and pride;
the One who beholds (all) has not died.
That for which (people) go to the banks of tiraths,
that jewel, that treasure, is within the heart itself.
Reading and reading, the pandit voices his arguments,
but does not know the thing that is within (him).
I have not died; what has died is my demon (of mine-ness).
The One who pervades all has not died.
Says Nanak, the Guru has shown me Brahm (God),
and (now) I see no one dying or being born. ॥4॥
152.2: Raag Gauri Dakhani, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
The one who, hearing again and again, understands and accepts the Name,
to him I am ever a sacrifice.
Those whom (the Lord) himself leads astray find no place, no refuge;
(O Lord,) you give understanding, and join (us) in union (with you).
May I receive the Naam, that it may go with me;
without the Name, all are bound by death.
The support of the Name is (my) farming and (my) trade;
sin and merit are a bundle of seed (that will sprout).
Those within whose hearts lust and anger strike their blows
forget the Name and depart with falseness in their minds.
True is the teaching of the True Guru:
(by it) body and mind are cooled, and the True One is recognised.
The mark (of those who receive it) is that they live untouched, like the water-lily and the lotus in water;
steeped in the Shabad, they are sweet as the juice of the sugarcane.
By (his) Hukam, through the joining (of destiny), the fortress (of the body) with ten gates (is made);
in it the five (elements) dwell, joined with the infinite Light.
He is himself the goods that are weighed, and himself the trader;
O Nanak, through the Name he is the one who adorns (all). ॥4॥
152.3: Raag Gauri, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
How can it be known where (the soul) comes from,
where it springs from, and where it goes and merges?
How is it bound, and how does it win liberation?
How does it merge in the imperishable (state of) Sahaj?
One who has the Naam in the heart and the ambrosial Name on the lips
through the Name of the Lord (Narhar) becomes, like the Lord, free of desire.
(The soul) comes of itself, by the natural order, and of itself it goes;
it springs from the mind and merges into the mind.
The Gurmukh is free; no bond holds him.
Reflecting on the Shabad, he is released through the Lord's Name.
On a tree many birds make their home for the night;
some happy, some sad, they are ruined by attachment in the mind.
As evening passes into dawn, they look to the sky,
and fly off in the ten directions; (so beings) run about as their deeds have written.
Those joined to the Name (take this world as) a brief halt in a goil (a pasture);
(in them) the poisoned pot of lust and anger bursts.
Without the goods (of the Name), house and shop (of the heart) lie empty;
meeting the Guru, the hard shutters are opened.
The Saadh (the holy Guru) is met through destiny from the past;
the perfect people of the Lord rejoice in the True One.
Giving their minds and bodies, they receive (the Name) in Sahaj and with love;
Nanak touches their feet. ॥5॥
153.1: Raag Gauri, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
(In me are) lust and anger, and my mind is in Maya;
my mind's love wakes to falsehood and vice;
I have gathered a capital of sin and greed.
(O Lord, your) purifying Name in the mind is the raft and the boat (to cross over).
Wonderful, wonderful are you, O True One; I lean on you (alone).
I am a sinner; you alone are pure.
Like water set on the fire, (the mortal) seethes and bubbles in his speech;
the tongue and each sense has its own craving;
the gaze is on vice; there is neither fear nor love (of God).
Only by killing self-conceit does one obtain the Name.
One who dies through the Shabad does not die again;
without dying (so), how can one become perfect?
The mind stays caught in the world's show and in duality;
Narayan is eternal: whatever he does, that comes to pass.
I can board the ship (of the Name) only when my turn comes;
those held back from the ship are beaten in the Lord's court.
I praise the True One; blessed is the Guru's door.
O Nanak, at (the Guru's) door and in the home (of the heart) is the One Creator, Ekankar. ॥4॥
153.2: Raag Gauri, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Reflecting on God (Brahm), the (inverted) lotus (of the heart) has turned upright;
in the sky of the Tenth Gate the stream of Amrit flows;
the Lord (Murari) himself pervades the three worlds.
O my mind, do not wander in doubt;
when the mind is won over, the essence of Amrit is drunk.
Having won (the game of) life, the mind has accepted death (to self);
self-conceit has died, and the mind has come to know (this) from within itself;
(the Lord's) glance of grace has fallen, and within one's own home the home (of the Lord) is known.
Continence, truthful living, pilgrimage and holy bathing lie in the Name;
why should I make a great show (of anything else)?
The Lord, Nar Narayan, knows every heart from within.
Were I to believe in any other, only then would I go to another's house;
of whom should I ask? There is no other place.
Through the Guru's teaching, Nanak is absorbed in Sahaj. ॥4॥
153.3: Raag Gauri, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
If the True Guru is met, he shows (one) that death (to self)
whose joy, the joy of dying (so) and (truly) living, becomes dear within;
casting off pride, one reaches the city in the sky (the highest state of the spirit).
(All) have come with death written (for them); no one is to stay (here).
By repeating and meditating on the Lord, one finds a lasting abode in the Lord's refuge.
If the True Guru is met, duality runs away;
the lotus (of the heart) blossoms, and the mind clings to the Lord God;
one who dies while living has the supreme joy before him.
When the True Guru is met, one becomes pure through the discipline of truth;
(climbing) the Guru's ladder, one rises higher and higher;
by (God's) grace (this) is found, and the fear of Jam comes to an end.
When the Guru is met, one meets (the Lord) and merges in his embrace;
in his grace (the Guru) has shown (him) the home, the mansion (of the Lord);
O Nanak, (the Guru) has killed his Haumai and united him (with the Lord). ॥4॥
154.1: Raag Gauri, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
What has fallen (to one's lot) from past deeds, no one can erase;
what can I know of what lies ahead?
Whatever pleased him is what has come to pass;
there is no second, no other, who does anything.
(O Lord,) I do not know how great your grace is, how great your gift;
your Name is my deeds, my dharma and my caste.
You are so great a Giver, the One who gives to all;
your storehouses of devotion never run short.
The pride one takes is of no avail;
soul and body, all is in your keeping.
You slay and bring to life again; forgiving, you unite (with yourself);
as it pleases you, so you have (beings) repeat your Name.
You are the Knower, the Seer, the True One over my head;
(you) give the Guru's teaching; I rest my trust in you.
No filth remains in the body of one whose mind is dyed (in your love);
through the Guru's words, through the Shabad, he has recognised the True One.
Your strength is (his support), and the glory of your Name (his honour);
O Nanak, (he) dwells in devotion, in (the Lord's) refuge. ॥4॥
154.2: Raag Gauri, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
One who speaks of the Unspeakable and has others speak of him, who drinks the nectar (of the Name) and gives it to others to drink,
forgets every other fear and is absorbed in the Name.
Why should such a one fear? (All his) fear has merged in the fear (of God),
(for he) has come to know (the Lord) through the Shabad of the Perfect Guru.
The one in whose heart the Lord dwells, whose capital is the Lord (Hari),
abiding in Sahaj and in love, receives (the Lord's) approval.
Those whom (the Lord) keeps asleep (in Maya) evening and morning,
those manmukhs are bound by death, here and hereafter.
Those with the Lord in their hearts day and night are perfect;
O Nanak, meeting the Lord, they are rid of their doubts. ॥4॥
154.3: Raag Gauri, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
One who loves (Maya of) the three qualities is born and dies (again and again);
the four Vedas tell (only) of the visible form;
they expound the three states;
(but) the fourth state is (union with) the Lord: know him through the True Guru.
Through devotion to the Lord and service of the Guru one swims across (the world-ocean);
(then) there is no birth again, and no death.
Everyone talks of the four great gifts;
the Simritis, the Shastras and the pandits have the same on their lips;
(but) without the Guru, (their true) meaning and understanding are not found;
the gift of liberation is found through devotion to the Lord.
The one in whose heart that Lord has come to dwell
has received devotion through the Guru.
In devotion to the Lord is the bliss of liberation;
through the Guru's teaching one finds supreme bliss.
Whoever has found (this bliss), the Guru, having seen (the Lord himself), has shown (him) to that one,
and has taught him to stay free of hopes while living amid hopes.
(That Lord) is the Master of the lowly, the Giver of every comfort;
O Nanak, (that one's) mind stays dyed in (love of) the Lord's feet. ॥4॥
154.4: Raag Gauri Cheti, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
The body, (thinking itself) immortal, lives at its ease; (but) this world is (only) a play.
(O body,) you practise greed, avarice and much falsehood, and carry a great load (of sin).
O body, I have seen you scattered like ashes over the ground.
(O soul,) listen, listen to my counsel:
only the good you have done will stay (with you), my soul; this turn will not come again.
I tell you, O my body, listen to my counsel:
you brood on slander of others and carry false tales;
you cast your eyes on another's wife, O soul, and you steal and do evil.
When the swan (the soul) departs, you (O body) will be left behind, like a deserted wife.
O body, you have lived as if in a dream; what deeds have you done?
When I stole and brought something home, it seemed good to (your) mind;
(so) there is no honour here and no shelter hereafter; the precious (human) life is wasted.
(The body says:) I have become most wretched, O brother; O Nanak, no one asks after me now.
Horses of Arab and Turki breed, gold and silver, loads of fine clothes:
(none of them) has gone along with anyone, O Nanak; they have dropped away (and stayed here), you fool.
Rock sugar and dried fruits, I have tasted everything; your Name alone is Amrit.
Laying foundation upon foundation, the walls are raised, (but those) mansions (become) a heap of ashes;
(one) piles up hoards and gives nothing to anyone; the blind one thinks it is all his own.
Lanka of gold, palaces of gold (did not last): wealth stays with no one.
Listen, foolish and ignorant mind:
his will alone shall prevail.
Our Master is the great Banker, and we are his traders;
soul and body, all of it, is his capital; he himself slays and he himself brings to life. ॥6॥
155.1: Raag Gauri Cheti, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
The others (the foes: lust, anger, greed, attachment and pride) are five, and I am one alone; how can I guard my house and home, O mind?
Day after day they beat and rob (me); before whom can I cry out, O brother?
O mind, utter the Name of Sri Ram (the Lord);
ahead of you stands the army of Jam, vast and terrible.
(God) built the hut (of the body) and set doors in it, and within it sits the soul-bride;
(thinking herself) immortal, the bride revels every day in her pleasures, while those other five go on robbing (her).
(Jam's army) pulled down the hut and plundered the temple, and the bride was seized, all alone;
Jam's club (struck), the chain fell about her neck, and those five ran away.
A wife craves gold and silver; friends crave things to eat;
O Nanak, for their sake (a man) commits sins, and will go bound to the city of Jam. ॥4॥
155.2: Raag Gauri Cheti, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
(O yogi,) the (true) earrings are those within the heart; make the body itself your patched coat;
bring the five disciples (the senses) under control, O Raval, and make this mind your staff.
In this way you will find the way of Yoga:
there is one Shabad, and no other; set your mind on that (as your food of) roots and tubers.
If by shaving the head the Guru is found, we have made the Guru our Ganga;
you do not remember the one Lord, the Saviour of the three worlds, O blind one.
Making a show, you win (people's) minds with (mere) talk; your (own) doubt does not leave you at all.
If you fix your consciousness on the feet of the One, why would you chase after greed and avarice?
With your mind absorbed (in him), repeat (the Name of) the Niranjan;
why, O yogi, do you speak so much deceit?
The body is crazed and the swan (the soul) a child; life goes by in crying, mine, mine.
Nanak humbly prays: when the naked (body) burns, then, afterwards, (the soul) repents. ॥4॥
156.1: Raag Gauri Cheti, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
O mind, the One alone is the root of all medicine and every mantra, if you make your consciousness firm (in him);
take (the Name of) the One who cuts away the sinful deeds of birth after birth.
O brother, the Master of the mind is the One alone;
(while) your three qualities stay engrossed in the world, the Unseen cannot be perceived.
Maya tastes sweet to the body, like sugar; we have taken up (its) bundle;
the night is dark and nothing can be seen, and the mouse (of time) gnaws away at the rope (of life), O brother.
As much as the manmukhs act (by their own will), so much pain befalls them; the Gurmukh receives honour.
What he has done, that alone has come to be; the record of past deeds cannot be erased.
Those who are dyed (in the Lord), having given (him) their love, are full to the brim and never run dry;
if Nanak becomes the dust of their feet, then (this) fool too may gain something. ॥4॥
156.2: Raag Gauri Cheti, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Since when has (anyone) been our mother, since when our father? From what place have we come?
We took shape in the fire (of the womb), from the water (of the seed): for what purpose were we made?
O my Master, who knows your virtues?
How many lives as trees and plants we have seen; how many times we were made beasts;
how many times we came among the families of snakes; how many times we were made to fly as birds.
(Man) breaks into the town's shops and its solid houses, and having stolen, comes home;
he looks ahead and looks behind, (but) where can he hide from you, (O Lord)?
We have seen river banks and tiraths, the nine regions (of the earth), shops, towns and bazaars;
(at last) the trader took up the scales and began to weigh within his own heart.
As full as the ocean is of water, so many are our faults.
Show mercy, show some kindness: you have carried sinking stones across.
The soul burns like fire; a knife (of craving) cuts within;
Nanak humbly prays: (one who) recognises the Hukam has peace day and night. ॥6॥
156.3: Raag Gauri Bairagan, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
You have wasted the night in sleep and the day in eating;
this life is (precious) as a diamond, yet it goes in exchange for a cowrie shell.
You have not known the Name of the Lord;
(Man) buries endless wealth in the earth, (but) the Endless One is not longed for;
those who went off longing for endless (wealth) came back having lost the Endless One.
If it came to whoever reached out and took it, everyone would be rich;
it is settled by deeds, however much everyone may long (for it).
O Nanak, the One who made the creation takes care of it;
no one can tell the Master's Hukam, to whom he will give glory. ॥4॥
157.1: Raag Gauri Bairagan, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Were I a doe, I would live in the forest, picking roots and tubers to eat,
and if by the Guru's grace my Husband (the Lord) met me, I would give myself up to him again and again.
(O Lord,) your Name is my merchandise and my trade.
Were I a koel (the Indian cuckoo), I would dwell in the mango tree and reflect on the Shabad in Sahaj;
in Sahaj and in love my Husband would meet me, whose sight and form are beyond all measure.
Were I a fish, I would live in the water (of the Lord), who takes care of all beings and creatures;
my Husband dwells on this shore and on the far shore; I will meet him with my arms spread wide.
Were I a she-snake, I would dwell in the earth; (if) the Shabad dwelt (within me), fear would go.
O Nanak, they are ever happy soul-brides, whose light merges in the Light. ॥4॥
157.2: Raag Gauri Poorbi Deepaki, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
In the house where (God's) praise is spoken and the Creator is reflected upon,
in that house sing the Sohila and remember the Creator.
Sing the Sohila of my Fearless Lord.
I am a sacrifice to the Sohila by which there is peace for ever.
Day after day all beings are cared for; the Giver will watch over (each one).
(O soul,) you cannot set a value on his giving; what measure can be taken of that Giver?
The year and the day (of my wedding) have been written; gather, (friends,) and pour the oil (of the wedding rite).
Give me your blessings, friends, so that I may be united with my Master.
To every house this same summons comes; these calls go out every day.
Let us remember the One who sends the call; O Nanak, those days are coming (for us too). ॥4॥
157.3: Raag Gauri Guareri, Chaupade, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
When the Guru is met, union with the Lord comes about;
that (Lord) himself brings (one) into his union.
My God himself knows every way;
by his Hukam he unites (one), who then recognises (him) through the Shabad.
In the fear of the True Guru, doubt and dread depart;
one steeped in that fear merges in the love of the True One.
When the Guru is met, the Lord comes to dwell in the mind, of his own loving nature.
My God is great; his worth cannot be found.
Whoever praises him through the Shabad, him who has no end and no near or far shore,
my God, the Forgiver, forgives (that one).
When the Guru is met, all wisdom and understanding come;
that True One dwells in the mind made pure.
When the True One dwells (within), all one's work is true;
reflection on the Shabad is the noblest conduct.
True service comes from the Guru;
through the Guru, some rare one recognises the Naam.
The Giver, who bestows all gifts, lives for ever;
O Nanak, (by his gift) love for the Lord's Name takes hold. ॥4॥
158.1: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Some rare one receives spiritual wisdom from the Guru;
the one who comes to understand from the Guru succeeds.
From the Guru come Sahaj and reflection on the True One;
from the Guru one finds the door of liberation.
By perfect fortune the Guru comes and meets one,
and one merges in true Sahaj, in the True One.
When the Guru is met, one quenches the fire of craving;
from the Guru, peace comes to dwell in the mind.
From the Guru come purity, holiness and cleanness;
from the Guru, union (with God) comes about through the Shabad.
Without the Guru, all (the world) is led astray in doubt;
without the Name, it suffers great pain.
One who becomes Gurmukh meditates on the Naam;
through the sight of the True One, true honour is gained.
To whom else should one speak? That One alone is the Giver;
when he shows grace, union comes about through the Shabad.
Having met the Beloved (Guru), may I sing the True One's praises;
may Nanak, becoming true, merge in the True One. ॥4॥
158.2: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
True is that place (the Sat Sangat), where the mind becomes pure;
one makes one's dwelling in the True One, and becomes true.
The true Bani is manifest through all four ages;
the True One is himself everything, of his own self.
When (God's) grace comes, he brings one into the Sat Sangat,
and, seated in that place, one sings the Lord's praises.
Let this tongue burn that is in the love of another,
that does not taste the Lord's sweet essence and utters insipid words.
Without understanding (that taste), body and mind become insipid;
without the Name, the wretched one departs weeping.
One whose tongue has tasted the Lord's sweet essence abides in Sahaj and in love;
by the Guru's grace, that one merges in the True One.
