God himself is the Master of both sides;
the one he unites (with himself), O Nanak, is liberated. ॥4॥
185.3: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
In Kalyug (husband and wife) come together through the bonds (of past deeds);
for as long as (God's) command lasts, they share the joys (of the world).
By burning (on the husband's pyre), the beloved Lord is not found;
(yet), driven by the bond of her past deeds, (the widow) rises and becomes a sati.
Copying others, out of the mind's stubbornness, (she) burns herself;
(but) she does not win the beloved's company, and is made to wander through many births.
She who, in gentle conduct and self-restraint, obeys her beloved's command:
that woman suffers no pain from Jam.
Says Nanak, she who has known her beloved as the Supreme Lord
is a blessed sati, accepted in the Lord's court. ॥4॥
185.4: Raag Gauri Guareri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Through the True Name we are wealthy and fortunate;
we sing the praises of the Lord in Sahaj and in love.
When I opened and looked into the treasure of my father and grandfather,
then my mind was filled with treasure.
(In it are) jewels and rubies beyond any price;
the storehouses are full, never to be exhausted, beyond weighing.
O brother, (those who) eat and spend (from it) together
find it never runs short; it goes on increasing.
Says Nanak, the one on whose forehead such destiny is written
is taken in as a sharer in this treasure. ॥4॥
186.1: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
While (God) is thought to be far away, we die of fear again and again;
when (we) saw (him) pervading everywhere, the fear ended.
I am a sacrifice to my True Guru,
who never leaves (me), and surely carries (me) across.
When the Naam is forgotten, (then come) pain, disease and grief;
when the Lord's praises are sung, there is bliss for ever.
No one should be called bad or good;
giving up pride, one should grasp the Lord's feet.
Says Nanak, keep the Guru's mantra in mind,
and you will find peace in the True Court. ॥4॥
186.2: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
One whose friend and companion (God) is present everywhere alike:
tell (me), what can that person lack?
One whose love is fixed on Gobind:
his pain, suffering and doubt run away.
One who has come to taste the relish, the relish of the Lord,
does not cling to other pleasures.
One whose word holds good in the Lord's court:
whom (else) does he take any notice of?
One who belongs to him to whom everything belongs
has peace for ever, O Nanak. ॥4॥
186.3: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
One to whom pain and pleasure seem alike:
how can worry take hold of him?
In the Lord's holy one dwell Sahaj and bliss;
he lives obedient to the Lord King, Har Har.
One in whose mind the carefree (Lord) comes to dwell
has no anxiety anywhere at all.
One from whose mind the wandering (of doubt) has perished
has no fear of Jam at all.
One into whose heart the Guru has given the Naam:
says Nanak, within him are all treasures. ॥4॥
186.4: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The (Lord) of inaccessible form has his dwelling in the mind;
by the Guru's grace, some rare one has come to know (this).
There are springs of Amrit, of the story of Sahaj;
the one to whom they are granted takes and enjoys them.
(Where) the unstruck Bani (sounds), that place is unlike any other;
Gopal is enchanted by its melody.
There, countless and endless gatherings of Sahaj (are held);
(there) the Sants are companions of the Supreme Lord.
(There) is endless joy, and no grief, nor any other (care).
That home the Guru has given to Nanak. ॥4॥
186.5: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(O Lord), which form of yours shall I worship?
Taking up which yoga shall I discipline the body?
Which virtue (of yours) shall I take up, to sing of you?
With what words shall I please you, O Supreme Lord?
What is that worship of you that I should perform?
What is that way by which I may cross the world-ocean?
What is the austerity by which one becomes a (true) ascetic?
What is that Name which washes away the filth of Haumai?
Praise, worship, wisdom, meditation, all such labour, O Nanak, (bears fruit for the one)
whom the merciful True Guru, in his grace, meets.
His alone is the merit, he alone has known God,
whose (prayer) the Giver of peace accepts. ॥36॥
187.1: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The body, of which (you are) proud, is not your own;
kingdom, land and wealth are not your own.
(None of these) is your own; to what are you clinging?
Your own is the Naam, which is found from the True Guru.
Sons, wife and brothers are not your own;
nor are dear friends, father and mother.
Gold, silver and money too are not (your own);
the choicest horses and elephants serve you nothing.
Says Nanak, the one whom the Guru, in his grace, has united (with the Lord),
everything is his, to whom the Lord King belongs. ॥4॥
187.2: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The Guru's feet are upon my forehead;
by them all my sorrows have been taken away.
I am a sacrifice to my True Guru;
recognising my self, I enjoy the supreme joy.
The one whose face the dust of the Guru's feet has touched
has given up all the intellect of ego.
The Guru's Shabad has come to taste sweet to my mind;
through it I have beheld the Supreme Lord.
The Guru is the bestower of peace, the Guru is the Creator;
O Nanak, soul and breath of life rest on the Guru as their support. ॥4॥
187.3: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
O my mind, long for him
O mind, my friend, take such a one as the Lord for your beloved;
keep him, the support of the breath of life, ever in your mind.
the Primal Being, beyond the farthest beyond, the radiant Divine One.
O mind, place your hope in him,
on whom (all) have relied from the beginning, from the start of the ages.
Through whose love there is lasting peace,
Nanak, meeting the Guru, sings of him. ॥4॥
187.4: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Whatever the Friend does, that I accept;
the Friend's doings are (to me) as joy itself.
In my mind and heart there is one support alone:
that he who does all things is my Friend.
My Friend is free of all care;
by the Guru's grace I have come to love (him).
My Friend is the Knower of hearts;
the almighty Being, the Supreme Lord, the Master.
(O God), I am (your) servant, you are my Master;
says Nanak, O God, my honour and greatness are yours. ॥4॥
188.1: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
O all-powerful Lord, the one whose side you take
is touched by no stain at all.
O Madho, the one whose hope is in you
has no need of anything from the world.
The one in whose heart the Master dwells
is left with no anxiety at all.
O God, the one to whom you have given fortitude:
Says Nanak, I have found such a Guru
as has shown (me) the Supreme Lord, pervading all. ॥4॥
188.2: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The rare (human) body is received by great good fortune;
those who (even so) do not repeat the Naam are slayers of their own soul.
Why do they not simply die, those who forget the Lord?
Of what use is a life without the Name?
Eating, drinking, playing, laughing, and all the display:
what good is the adorning of a corpse?
Those who do not listen to the praise of (God, who is) supreme bliss
are worse than beasts, birds and the creatures that creep.
Says Nanak, (the one in whom) the Guru has made the mantra (of the Name) firm:
in his heart the Naam alone stays absorbed. ॥4॥
188.3: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
All these relations are in name only, and false.
Why, you fool, do you babble (like one talking in his sleep)?
Joined (with them) by the union (of past deeds), you have come (into the world) by (God's) Hukam.
The clay (of all) is one, the light is one,
the breath of life is one: why, then, should anyone weep?
(but) this soul is not one that dies.
Says Nanak, (those for whom) the Guru has opened the doors
have been set free, and the structures of (their) delusion have been destroyed. ॥4॥
188.4: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The people who look great and mighty
are gripped by the disease of anxiety.
Who becomes great by Maya's greatness?
Great is the one who has fixed his loving attention on the Lord.
The landowner fights over land day after day;
(in the end) he leaves (it) and goes, yet (his) thirst is not quenched.
Says Nanak, (I) have reflected on this essence:
without the worship of the Lord there is no release. ॥3॥
188.5: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
perfect is all (he does), (the one) with the Naam in his heart.
(Their honour) stayed whole when the Perfect One kept (it):
(those) servants had looked to the shelter of the Supreme Lord.
perfect (his) austerity, and perfect both (his) rule and (his) union (with God).
On the Lord's path even sinners become pure;
(their) glory is complete, and complete (their) dealings with the world.
The Creator ever dwells close beside (them);
says Nanak, my True Guru is perfect. ॥4॥
188.6: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
By the dust (of the feet) of the Sant, millions of sins are erased;
by the Sant's grace comes release from birth and death.
The sight of the Sant is the perfect (pilgrim's) bath;
by the Sant's grace the Naam is repeated.
In the Sant's company pride is erased,
(and) everywhere the One Creator, Ekankar, is seen.
When the Sant is well pleased, the five (passions) come under control,
(and one) takes the Amrit Naam and stores it up in the heart.
Says Nanak, the one whose destiny is full
comes to touch the feet of the Saadh (the Guru). ॥4॥
189.1: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Repeating the Lord's virtues, the lotus (of the heart) blossoms;
remembering the Lord, all fear is destroyed.
That understanding is perfect by which (one) sings the Lord's virtues;
(it comes to the one who) by great good fortune finds the company of the Saadh.
The Naam's treasure is found in the Saadh Sangat;
in the Saadh Sangat all tasks are fulfilled.
Devotion to the Lord makes one's birth approved;
by the Guru's grace (one) utters the Naam.
Says Nanak, that person is approved
189.2: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The one whose mind is dyed with the One (God)
that Creator alone does and causes all to be done.
(The one who) practises (the Name) with his mind and says Har Har with his mouth:
that person never wavers anywhere, here or hereafter.
Whoever has the wealth of the Lord is a true banker;
the Perfect Guru has made (his) credit good.
(He) has met the Lord King, the Being who is the life (of all);
says Nanak, (he) has attained the supreme state. ॥4॥
189.3: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The Naam is the support of the devotee's life-breath;
the Naam alone is (his) wealth, the Naam alone (his) trade.
Through the greatness of the Naam the servant wins honour:
(the one) to whom (God), in his grace, himself causes (it) to be given.
For the devotee, the Naam is the abode of peace;
dyed in the Naam, such a devotee is approved.
The Lord's Name upholds his servant;
with every breath the servant cherishes the Naam.
Says Nanak, the one whose fortune is full:
his mind clings to the Naam. ॥4॥
189.4: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
By the Sant's grace (I) have meditated on the Lord's Name;
from then on (my) restless mind has been content.
Singing (his) virtues, (I) have found the resting place of peace;
(my) weariness is gone, and my demon has been slain.
Worshipping the lotus feet of God,
through the Lord's Simran my anxiety has been erased.
Forsaking all, (I,) the helpless one, came to the shelter of the One;
then in Sahaj (I) attained the high abode.
Sorrow, pain, doubt and fear have fled;
O Nanak, the Creator has come to dwell in (my) mind. ॥4॥
189.5: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
With (my) hands I do service, with (my) tongue I sing (God's) virtues;
with (my) feet I hasten on the Master's path.
Good is (this) time (of human birth): it is the turn for Simran;
remembering the Naam, (one) crosses beyond (all) fears.
Let (your) eyes behold the sight of the Sants;
write the imperishable God into (your) mind.
Go to the Saadh and listen to the Kirtan,
(and) be rid of the fear of birth and death.
Enshrine the Master's lotus feet in (your) heart;
O Nanak, carry (this) rare body across (the world-ocean). ॥4॥
190.1: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The one on whom (God) bestows his grace:
that person utters the Naam with his tongue.
Forgetting the Lord, anxiety and sorrow take hold;
remembering the Naam, doubt and fear run away.
The one who listens to the Lord's Kirtan and sings the Lord's Kirtan:
sorrow does not come near that person.
Serving the Lord, his servant is made beautiful;
(The one with) the Name of the merciful Lord in mind, body and mouth:
O Nanak, (he) has cast off all other entanglements. ॥4॥
190.2: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Give up (your) cleverness and all (your) cunning,
(and) take the support of the Perfect Guru.
Singing the Lord's virtues, sorrows perish and peace (comes),
(when) the Perfect Guru is met (and one) fixes (one's) loving attention (on God).
The Guru has given (me) the Lord's Name as the mantra;
grieving is over and anxiety has lifted.
Meeting the merciful Guru, there is joy;
in (his) grace (he) has cut the nets of Jam.
Says Nanak, (the one who) has found the Perfect Guru:
because of (that Guru), Maya does not grip (him) again. ॥4॥
190.3: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The Perfect Guru himself has saved (us);
it is the manmukh who has been struck by torment.
Repeat Guru, Guru, O my friend:
(your) face will shine bright in (the Lord's) court.
Enshrine the Guru's feet in (your) heart;
(he) will slay (your) sorrows, (your) enemies and your demon.
The Guru's Shabad is with you as (your) helper;
all beings have become kind (to you), O brother.
When the Perfect Guru showed grace,
says Nanak, my (striving) bore its full fruit. ॥4॥
190.4: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(One without the Saadh Sangat) eats many tasty things, as a beast does,
and is tied up with the rope of attachment, like a thief.
A body that is without the Saadh Sangat is a corpse;
(such a one) keeps coming and going through the life-forms and wastes away in pain.
He is dressed in many fine clothes,
(yet is) like a scarecrow put up in a field to scare (creatures) off.
Every body (even a beast's) comes of some use;
(but) fruitless is the human who does not repeat the Naam.
Says Nanak, those to whom (the Lord) becomes merciful
gather in the Saadh Sangat and dwell on Gopal in devotion. ॥4॥
190.5: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The Guru's Shabad has driven off the strife and anguish (of the mind);
coming and going has ended, and every comfort (is found).
Fears have perished (for those) who have meditated on the fearless Lord
and sung the Lord's virtues in the Saadh Sangat.
(Those who) have set (the Lord's) lotus feet within their hearts,
the Guru has carried (them) across the ocean of fire.
(They) were going under, and the perfect Guru has pulled (them) out;
those broken off (from the Lord) for birth after birth he has joined (to him) again.
Says Nanak, I am a sacrifice to that Guru,
on meeting whom our liberation has come about. ॥4॥
191.1: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(O brothers,) in the Saadh Sangat seek the sanctuary of him (God);
lay your mind and body before him.
Drink the Naam that is Amrit, my brothers;
remembering it again and again, all the burning (within) has been quenched.
Give up pride, and put an end to birth and death;
bow your head at the feet of the Lord's servant.
With every breath hold God dear in (your) mind;
gather that wealth which goes along with (you).
(This wealth) comes only to one on whose forehead good fortune is (written);
says Nanak, fall at that one's feet. ॥4॥
191.2: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(The Guru) has made the withered green in an instant;
watering (them) with his glance of Amrit, he has brought (them) to life.
The perfect Gurdev (the divine Guru) has cut away the troubles;
he has given his servant his own service.
Worry is wiped out, the mind's hope is fulfilled,
(once) the True Guru, the treasure of virtues, showed mercy.
Sorrows have fled, and comforts have come to settle (within);
there was no delay once the Guru gave the word.
Those who met the perfect Guru have had their wish fulfilled;
O Nanak, those people have borne good fruit. ॥4॥
191.3: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The fevers are gone; God has brought calm (within);
(we) have been cooled; God has given (this) gift.
By God's grace (we) are at ease;
(he) has united (with himself) those separated for birth after birth.
the very seat of every disease has been destroyed.
In Sahaj and with love, (such a one) utters the Lord's Bani;
O mortal, remember God at all hours.
Neither sorrow nor pain nor Jam comes near (the one),
says Nanak, who sings the Lord's virtues. ॥4॥
191.4: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Blessed are the days, blessed the occasions,
in which the Supreme Lord, the unattached, is met.
I am a sacrifice to that hour
in which my mind repeats the Lord's Name.
Fruitful is that moment, fruitful that hour,
in which the tongue utters the Lord's Name, Har Hari.
Fruitful is the forehead that bows before the Sant;
holy are the feet that walk on the Lord's path.
Says Nanak, blessed is my fortune,
through which I have met the feet of the Saadh (the Guru). ॥4॥
192.1: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Keep the Guru's Shabad in your mind;
remember the Naam, and every worry goes.
Apart from the Lord God there is no other;
he alone kills, and he alone preserves.
Enshrine the Guru's feet in your heart, within your breast;
repeating (the Name), you will cross the ocean of fire.
Fix your attention on the Guru's form (the Shabad);
you will be honoured here and hereafter.
Leaving all (else), (Nanak) has come to the Guru's sanctuary;
(his) anxieties are gone, and Nanak has found peace. ॥4॥
192.2: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(God is the one) remembering whom all sorrow departs
and the jewel of the Naam comes to dwell in the mind.
O my mind, repeat the Bani of Govind (his praise),
the Bani in which holy people have told of Ram with their tongues.
Besides the One there is no other,
by whose glance (of grace) there is lasting peace.
Take the One alone as your beloved, friend and companion;
write the letters of Har Har (the Lord's Name) in your mind.
Nanak sings the virtues of (him,) the knower of hearts. ॥4॥
192.3: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The whole world is steeped in fear;
the one whose support is the Naam has no fear.
(O God,) in your sanctuary fear takes no hold;
what pleases you, that alone is done.
Caught in grief and joy, (beings) keep coming and going;
peace is found by the one who is pleasing to God.
(The world) is an ocean of fire, and Maya grips (all) hard;
those who have found the True Guru stay cool.
says Nanak, what can the poor creature (do)? ॥4॥
192.4: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(O God,) by your grace (your) Name is repeated;
by your grace a place is found in your court.
Apart from you, O Supreme Lord, there is no one;
by your grace there is lasting peace.
When you dwell in the mind, sorrow does not touch (one);
by your grace doubt and fear take flight.
you know the inner being of every heart.
I make my prayer before my True Guru,
that Nanak may receive the Naam, the true capital. ॥4॥
192.5: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
As husks without grain are hollow,
so empty are those mouths that lack the Naam.
O mortal, repeat the Name of the Lord, Har Har, every day;
without the Naam, cursed is the body, which is not (truly) your own.
Without the Naam no good fortune (shines) on the brow;
without the husband, where is a wife's married joy?
One who forgets the Naam and is drawn to other tastes
has not one of his hopes fulfilled.
O God, in your grace (grant) your gift,
so that Nanak may repeat the Naam day and night. ॥4॥
193.1: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
You are all-powerful; you alone are my Master;
all things come from you; you are the knower of hearts.
O perfect Supreme Lord, (you are) the shelter of your servants;
in your sanctuary millions of people are saved.
As many beings as there are, all are yours;
by your grace (they have) comforts in plenty.
Whatever takes place is all your will;
one who understands the Hukam merges in the True One.
Show grace, O God, and give (this) gift,
that Nanak may remember the Naam, the treasure. ॥4॥
193.2: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
By great good fortune one gains the sight of the one
whose loving attention is held on the Lord's Name.
One in whose mind the Lord has come to dwell
knows no sorrow, even in a dream.
(God) has placed all treasures within his servant;
in his company sins and sorrows depart.
The glory of (such) a servant cannot be told;
the servant stays merged in the Supreme Lord.
Show grace, O God, and hear (my) plea:
give Nanak the dust (of the feet) of your servant. ॥4॥
193.3: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Remembering the Lord, the evil that haunts you departs,
and every kind of well-being comes to dwell in the mind.
O my mind, dwell in devotion on the Name of the One alone;
(it is this) that serves your soul.
Night and day sing the virtues of the Infinite;
(this is) the perfect Guru's spotless mantra.
Give up (other) devices and lean on the One alone;
taste the essence of Amrit, the supreme treasure.
They alone have crossed the treacherous ocean
on whom, O Nanak, (God) casts his glance of grace. ॥4॥
193.4: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Those who have set God's lotus feet in their hearts
have met the Perfect True Guru and been carried across (the world-ocean).
Sing the praises of Govind, O my brother;
meeting the Saadh (the Guru), meditate on the Lord's Name.
(Their) human body, so hard to come by, has been accepted (at the Lord's door),
(for they) have received from the True Guru the Naam, the seal (of passage).
Remembering the Lord, (they) have attained the perfect state;
in the Saadh Sangat (they) have rid themselves of fears and doubts.
servant Nanak is in the Lord's refuge. ॥4॥
193.5: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
I am a sacrifice to the sight of the revered Guru;
I live by repeating the True Guru's name again and again.
O perfect Supreme Lord, O divine Guru,
be gracious, that I may keep to your service.
I hold (the Guru's) lotus feet within my heart, in my breast;
(the feet of) the Guru are the support of (my) mind, body, wealth and life-breath.
(Thus) life bears fruit and is accepted (at the Lord's door):
know the Guru, the Supreme Lord, to be near (you).
The dust (of the feet) of the Sant (the Guru) is found by great good fortune;
O Nanak, on meeting the Guru, loving attention is fixed on the Lord. ॥4॥
194.1: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(One who in secret) does evil deeds and shows (the world) something else
is bound as a thief in the court of the Lord.
He alone belongs to the Lord who remembers the Lord,
the One who pervades water, land and sky.
(One who has) poison within, yet recites Amrit (words) with his mouth,
is bound in the city of Jam and suffers blows.
Behind many veils he commits vices,
(but) in an instant they come to light before the world.
The one who within is steeped in the True Name and its delight:
O Nanak, the Creator is gracious to him. ॥4॥
194.2: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The dye of the Lord's love never comes off
(for the one) to whom the Perfect Guru gives understanding.
The mind dyed in the Lord's love is true (fast in its colour);
(it bears) the deep crimson (of the love) of the Perfect Being, the Creator.
(One who) sits in the company of the Sants and sings (God's) praises:
his dye (of love) never comes off.
Without remembering the Lord, (no one) has found peace;
all other dyes, those of Maya, are pale and tasteless.
Those whom the Guru has dyed (in love) are made joyful;
says Nanak, the Guru has shown mercy (to them). ॥4॥
194.3: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Remembering the Master, sins are destroyed,
and peace, Sahaj and bliss come to dwell (within).
The Lord's servants rely on the Lord;
repeating the Naam, all (their) anxiety has been wiped away.
In the Saadh Sangat there is no fear at all and no wandering (of mind);
(there) the praises of Gopal are sung day and night.
In his grace God has granted release from bonds,
and has given the shelter of (his) lotus feet.
Says Nanak, faith (in God) has arisen in (their) minds;
the servants ever drink in (God's) pure praise. ॥4॥
194.4: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
One whose mind is attached to the Lord's feet:
his pain, suffering and doubt have fled.
The trader in the Lord's wealth is whole and perfect;
the one whom (God) honours is the hero.
Those to whom the Lord of the world has been gracious,
those servants have fallen at the Guru's feet.
(Theirs are) peace, Sahaj, calm and bliss;
they live by repeating (the Name of) the Lord of supreme bliss again and again.
(Those who) have earned the capital of the Naam in the Saadh Sangat:
says Nanak, God has cut away (their) affliction. ॥4॥
194.5: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Remembering the Lord, all troubles are wiped away,
and (God's) lotus feet enter and dwell in the mind.
Utter the Lord's Name a hundred thousand times,
and drink God's Amrit essence, O dear (tongue).
Peace, Sahaj, delight and great bliss are theirs
who live by repeating (the Name of) the Lord of supreme bliss again and again.
(They) have cast off lust, anger, greed and pride;
in the Saadh's company all (their) sins have been washed away.
Show grace, O God, merciful to the meek,
and grant Nanak the dust (of the feet) of the Saadh. ॥4॥
195.1: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The One whose gifts (a person) wears and eats:
how can it be right, O mother, to be slack towards him?
(Those who) forget the Master and busy themselves with other things
give up a jewel in exchange for a cowrie.
Forsaking God, they cling to greed for other things;
where is the honour in saluting the handmaid (Maya)?
They eat and drink fare as sweet as Amrit,
(yet) the dogs do not know the One who gave (it).
Says Nanak, we are untrue to (your) salt (ungrateful);
forgive (us), O God, knower of hearts. ॥4॥
195.2: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
To keep the mind in meditation on God's feet
is the dip and the bath at all places of pilgrimage.
Remember the Lord every day, O my brother;
(so) the filth of millions of births is washed off.
(One who) has enshrined the Lord's story in the heart
has obtained every fruit the mind longs for.
Accepted (at the Lord's door) are the life, the death and the birth
of the one in whose heart God dwells.
Says Nanak, they alone are perfect
who have received the dust (of the feet) of the Saadh. ॥4॥
195.3: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(One who) eats and wears (what God gives) and yet denies (him):
the messengers of Dharam Raj keep their eye on him.
(You) have turned your face from him who gave (you) soul and body;
(so) you will wander through many species for millions of births.
Such is the way of the Saakat:
whatever he does is all perverse.
The One who upholds soul and breath, mind and body:
that very Master (he) has put out of his mind.
(His) vices have grown; many sheets have been written (with them).
Save Nanak, O ocean of mercy and of peace.
O Supreme Lord, (whoever comes) to your refuge
cuts (his) bonds and crosses over (the world-ocean) through the Lord's Name. ॥78॥
195.4: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(Whoever) made (God) a friend, even for his own gain,
was given all he longed for, and the state of liberation (too).
Let everyone make such a friend,
from whom no one goes away empty.
(Whoever) took (him) into the heart, even for his own ends,
had all (his) pain, suffering and disease destroyed (by God).
(One whose) tongue has grown used to uttering the Lord's Name:
Nanak is a sacrifice many times over;
fruitful is the sight of our Gobind. ॥4॥
195.5: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
In an instant millions of obstacles are taken away
(for those) who hear the story of the Lord, Har Har, in the Saadh Sangat.
One who drinks the Lord's essence, the Amrit of (his) virtues:
meditating on the Lord's feet, his hunger is gone.
All blessings, the treasures of peace and Sahaj, are his
in whose heart you dwell, O God.
Medicines, mantras and tantras are all mere ash;
enshrine the Creator in your heart.
(One who) has cast off all doubts and worshipped the Supreme Lord:
says Nanak, this dharma (of his) never wavers. ॥4॥
196.1: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
By (God's) grace I have met that Guru,
by whose strength no disease takes hold (of me).
To remember the Lord is to cross the ocean of fear;
in the refuge of the valiant (Guru), the papers (of account) of Jam are torn up.
The True Guru has imparted the mantra of the Lord's Name;
with this support (all) tasks have been fulfilled.
The full glory of japa, austerity and self-restraint (has been gained),
(since) the Guru was gracious and the Lord became (my) helper.
The Guru has done away with pride, attachment and doubt;
behold, O Nanak, the Supreme Lord spread out (everywhere). ॥4॥
196.2: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Better the blind man than one who lords it in sensual pleasures,
(for) when pain strikes, he remembers the Lord's Name.
(O Lord,) for your servant you alone are glory;
(but) Maya takes the one engrossed in her into hell.
One gripped by disease (too) remembers the Name,
(but) one drunk on the poison (of vice) has no shelter (here) and no place (hereafter).
(One whose) love is fixed on the lotus feet (of the Lord)
does not call other pleasures to mind.
May I remember (you) for ever and ever, O God, my Master;
meet Nanak, O Lord, knower of hearts. ॥4॥
196.3: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
At all hours the highwaymen (lust and the other vices) keep (one) company;
God in his grace has driven (them) off.
Let everyone savour the sweet essence of such a Lord;
that God is full of every power.
The world-ocean burns with fierce heat (of the vices);
God can carry (one) across (it) in an instant.
The bonds are many, and (by one's own effort) they cannot be broken;
remembering the Name, (people) gain the fruit of liberation.
No argument or cleverness of this (mortal) can do anything;
O Nanak, (when God) shows grace, (mortals) sing (his) praises. ॥4॥
196.4: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(If you) have gained the purse (of wealth) of the Lord's Name,
move about the world (free of care): all (your) tasks will be fulfilled.
It is by great good fortune that the Lord's Kirtan is sung;
O Supreme Lord, only if you give is (this gift) received.
Keep the Lord's feet enshrined in your heart, deep within;
climbing aboard (them, as on a ship), you will cross over the world-ocean.
Let everyone keep the company of the Saadh (the Guru);
(there) is lasting well-being, and sorrow comes no more.
With loving devotion, worship the treasure of virtues (the Lord);
O Nanak, (so) honour is gained in the Lord's court. ॥4॥
196.5: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The Lord, our friend, fills the water, the land and the sky;
as (his) praises are sung day by day, doubts have perished.
Waking and sleeping, the Lord stays at (one's) side as a watchman,
he by whose remembrance the fear of Jam is gone.
God's lotus feet have come to dwell in the heart,
The One (Lord) alone is hope, honour, strength and wealth;
in the mind is the support of the True King (God).
Those who were very poor and without support, (once they became) servants of the Saadh (the Guru),
O Nanak, God gave (them his) hand and saved (them). ॥4॥
197.1: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Bathing in the Name of the Lord, Har Har, (mortals) become pure;
(its) rewards are greater than the merit (earned) at millions of eclipses.
(The one in whose) heart the Lord's feet have come to dwell:
(his) sins of birth after birth have fled.
(The one who) has gained the fruit of Kirtan in the Saadh Sangat
has not even caught sight of the road of Jam.
(The one whose) support in thought, word and deed is Govind,
from him (the hold of) the poisonous world has fallen away.
(The one whom) God in his grace has made his own,
O Nanak, (he) repeats the Lord's chant, and repeats the Lord alone. ॥4॥
197.2: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Take refuge with the one who has come to know the Lord;
dyed in the love of the Lord's feet, mind and body grow cool and calm.
(Those who) do not enshrine in the mind God, the destroyer of fear,
pass through many births, ever trembling with fear.
The one in whose heart the Lord's Name has come to dwell:
all his wishes and tasks are fulfilled.
He in whose power are birth, old age and death:
remember that all-powerful (Lord) with every breath and every morsel.
The One God alone is friend, companion and comrade;
the Master's Name is Nanak's support. ॥4॥
197.3: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Out (in the world, the Sants) keep (the Lord) cherished in the heart;
coming back home, (they) bring Govind along.
The Name of the Lord, Har Har, is (ever) at the side of the Sants;
(their) mind and body stay dyed in the colour of Ram's love.
By the Guru's grace (they) have crossed the (world-)ocean,
(and) all the sins of birth after birth are taken away.
Fortunate (is he): glory (is his), and (his) awareness (rests) in the Name,
(in whose heart dwells) the pure mantra of the Perfect Guru.
Meditate on (God's) lotus feet in the heart;
197.4: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Blessed is this place (where) Govind's praises are sung;
God himself has made peace and well-being dwell (there).
Misfortune is there where the Lord is not remembered;
where the Lord's praises are sung, (there) are joys by the million.
When the Lord is forgotten, a host of sorrows and diseases (close in);
when God is served, Jam comes nowhere near.
Fortunate and unshakeable is that place
where God's Name alone is repeated.
Wherever one goes, my Master is there alongside;
Nanak has met the Knower of hearts. ॥4॥
197.5: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The mortal who meditates on Govind,
lettered or unlettered, attains the highest spiritual state.
In the company of the Saadh (the Guru), remember Gopal;
without the Name, wealth and possessions are (all) false.
He alone is handsome, clever and wise,
the person who has accepted God's will.
His coming into the world is approved
(who) knows his Master (to dwell) in every heart.
Says Nanak, the one whose fortune is perfect:
his mind is fixed on the Lord's feet. ॥4॥
198.1: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The Saakat has no fellowship with the Lord's servant;
the one (the Saakat) is given over to vice, while the other (the servant) is dyed in Ram's love.
(Their fellowship is) like riding an adorned mare in the mind alone,
(or) like an impotent man fondling a woman.
(Or as if one) were to rope an ox's legs and milk it,
(or) mount a cow and drive (it) after a lion;
(or) take a sheep and worship (it) as Kamdhenu,
(or) rush off to trade without capital.
O Nanak, repeat Ram's Name in your mind;
remember the Master, the Lord: (there is no) friend like (him). ॥4॥
198.2: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
That understanding is called pure and steadfast, O brother,
(through which) Ram('s Name), the home of all delights, is drunk.
Make the Lord's feet (your) shelter in the heart;
(so) release from birth and death is won.
Pure is the body in which no sin springs up;
in Ram's love (shines) a spotless radiance.
In the Saadh Sangat the vices are erased;
this is the highest blessing of all.
(Those) dyed in loving devotion to Gopal:
Nanak begs for the dust of the feet of (such) holy ones. ॥4॥
198.3: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(Those whose) love for Govind has grown like this:
(God) has united (with himself) those of perfect good fortune.
As a wife blossoms at the sight of her husband,
so the Lord's servant lives by calling the Name to mind.
As a mother lives by the sight of her son,
(so) the servant is steeped in the Lord, through and through, like warp and weft.
As the greedy man delights at the sight of wealth,
(so) the servant's mind clings to (God's) lotus feet.
O Giver, do not slip from (my) mind even for a moment;
O God of Nanak, (you are) the support of (his) life-breath. ॥4॥
198.4: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Those who are absorbed in Ram, the home of all delights,
stay pierced through with loving devotion to (God's) lotus feet.
All other pleasures look (to them) like ashes;
without the Name, the world (seems to them) fruitless.
(God) himself has drawn (them) out of the blind well (of Maya);
wondrous is the glory of Govind's virtues.
Gopal fills the forests, every blade of grass and the three worlds;
(all) is God's own expanse; the merciful (Lord) is with every being.
Says Nanak, that is the best of speech
198.5: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Day after day, let one bathe in the pool of Ram('s Name);
stirring it well, let one drink the Lord's Amrit, the supreme delight, (with relish).
The Name of Govind is pure water;
as one bathes (in it), all one's tasks are fulfilled.
There, in the company of the Sants, (God's) discourse goes on,
(which) wipes out the sins of millions of births.
supreme bliss (God, its source) pervades (their) mind and body.
The one who has received the treasure of the Lord's feet:
servant Nanak is a sacrifice to him. ॥4॥
199.1: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Do that by which no filth (of vice) clings (to the mind),
(and) this mind stays awake in the Lord's Kirtan.
Remember the One (Lord) alone, with no love for another;
in the company of the Sants, repeat the Name alone.
Rituals, religious duties, observances, fasts and worship:
count none (of these) a second (support) beside the Supreme Lord.
His toil has borne its full fruit
whose love is with his own God.
Supreme beyond all, boundless, is that Vaishnav (the true devotee),
says Nanak, who has given up the vices. ॥4॥
199.2: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(Maya's goods) leave (a person) while he is still alive, O madman;
once he is dead, who gains anything from them?
Remember Govind in mind and body: this is the lot written (for you) from the start;
Maya's poison serves no purpose at all.
Whoever has eaten the swindler's drug of the senses' pleasures,
The world (-ocean) is full of terrible pain and hard to cross;
without the Name of Ram, how will you get across?
Join the Saadh Sangat and set right both worlds (this one and the next);
O Nanak, worship the Name of Ram. ॥4॥
199.3: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The beard that bristles (in arrogance) against the poor
the Supreme Lord has burnt in the fire.
he is the protector of his own servant.
From the beginning, from the start of the ages, (God's) glory has been made manifest:
the slanderer has died, a great torment rising up (within him).
He has been struck down by the One whose stroke no one can ward off;
hereafter and here (his) name is evil.
(God) keeps his servants clasped to his bosom;
O Nanak, take (his) refuge and meditate on the Lord's Name. ॥4॥
199.4: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The mahzar (a complaint signed by many, drawn up against his servant) God himself has proved false;
To the one whose helper is my Gobind
(He who) tells lies in the True Court,
that blind fool beats (his) head with his hands.
Those who commit sins are gripped by diseases;
God himself sits as the judge.
By their own doings (people) are bound by their own hand;
all their wealth went along with their life.
Nanak has taken refuge at (the Lord's) court;
199.5: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The dust (of the feet) of (the Lord's) servant tastes sweet to the mind of that mortal
for whom (it) is written from the start, by (his) deeds of the past.
Through the intellect of ego, the mind was coated with grease;
with the dust of the Saadh, (that intellect) has been scoured clean.
If (one) washes the body in many waters,
(the mind's) filth does not come off; no one is made pure that way.
(The one who) has met the True Guru, ever merciful,
has cut away the fear of death by remembering the Lord again and again.
The Lord's Name is liberation, it is enjoyment, it is the way (of life);
O Nanak, sing (his) virtues with loving devotion. ॥4॥
200.1: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The servants of the Lord hold the rank of true life;
meeting them, the soul is filled with light.
O mind, listen with (your) ears to the Simran of the Lord;
O mortal, (so) you will find peace at the Lord's door.
Let us meditate on Gopal at all hours;
O Nanak, beholding (his) sight, (the mind) is filled with delight. ॥2॥
200.2: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Calm has come: the Guru, who is Gobind (in form), has bestowed it;
afflictions and sins have perished, O my brother.
Utter the Name of Ram with the tongue every day;
(by it) diseases have perished and joy has come.
Reflect on the virtues of the inaccessible Supreme Lord;
in the company of the Saadh (the Guru) lies deliverance.
Sing the pure virtues (of God) day after day;
O friend, the servants (who sing them) are rid of disease and are saved.
(Be gracious, O Lord,) that I may meditate on my God in thought, word and deed;
servant Nanak has come to your refuge. ॥4॥
200.3: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The divine Guru has given light to the eyes;
doubts are gone, and (the) service (done) has borne its fruit.
Bihari (the Lord who sports in his creation) has given protection from smallpox (Sitala);
the Supreme Lord God has shown grace.
O Nanak, the one who repeats the Naam truly lives;
in the Saadh Sangat he drinks the Lord's Amrit. ॥2॥
200.4: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(O Lord,) blessed is that forehead (which bows to you), blessed are the eyes (that behold) your (sight);
blessed are those devotees who love you.
Without the Naam, how can peace be found?
(So) let the tongue speak the praise of the Name of Ram.
Let us be a sacrifice to those,
O Nanak, each one who has meditated on the (Lord) beyond all desire. ॥2॥
200.5: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(O Lord,) you alone are (my) counsel, you alone are with (me);
you yourself protect (me), watching over and caring for (me).
Such is Ram, the helper in this world and the next:
he keeps the honour of (his) servant, O my brother.
He in whose control is this world is himself (the helper) in the world hereafter;
(my) mind repeats (the Name of that) Lord at all hours.
Honour is his, he is accepted (in the Lord's court), and the True Name is his pass,
for whom you yourself issue the command.
(God) himself is the giver, himself the one who sustains;
O Nanak, cherish the Name of Ram (in your heart) every day. ॥4॥
200.6: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
When the Perfect True Guru became merciful,
Gopal came to dwell in the heart for ever.
Remembering Ram, lasting peace has been found;
the perfect Lord, the King, has shown mercy.
Says Nanak, the one whose destiny is perfect
has the Name of the Lord, Har Har, as (his) lasting wedded bliss. ॥2॥
201.1: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(The priest, at his patron's house,) loosens his dhoti and spreads it beneath him,
and like a donkey he stuffs (everything) into his belly.
Without (the) deeds (of remembrance), liberation is not attained;
let us meditate on the Naam, the treasure (that brings) liberation.
(He) takes his ritual baths, marks his brow with the tilak and performs worship,
(yet) with a knife drawn (pitilessly) he takes the offerings into his hand.
He reads the Veda in a sweet voice from his mouth,
(yet that) mortal does not shrink from butchering living beings.
Says Nanak, the one on whom (God) shows grace
is pure in heart and reflects on Brahm (God). ॥4॥
201.2: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Sit steady in the home (of your heart), O beloved servants of the Lord:
the True Guru has set your affairs right.
The Supreme God has struck down the wicked foes;
the Creator has kept the honour of (his) servant.
(God) has brought emperors and kings, all of them, under the sway (of his servants);
(they) have drunk the supreme essence of the Amrit Naam.
on (your) joining the Saadh Sangat, (God) has granted (this) gift.
O God, knower of hearts, (I) have come to (your) refuge;
Nanak has grasped (your) support, O God, my Master. ॥4॥
201.3: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Dyed in the love of the Lord, one does not burn in the fire (of craving);
Dyed in the love of the Lord, one is not deceived by Maya;
Dyed in the love of the Lord, one does not drown in the water (of the world-ocean);
Dyed in the love of the Lord, (one's life) bears good fruit.
(O Lord,) through your Name all fears are wiped away;
on meeting (the holy) company, one sings the virtues of the Lord, Har Har.
Dyed in the love of the Lord, one is rid of all anxiety;
(but) only that one is absorbed in the Lord who has the teaching of the Saadh (the Guru).
Dyed in the love of the Lord, one has no dread of Jam;
Dyed in the love of the Lord, one's hopes are fulfilled.
Dyed in the love of the Lord, one is touched by no sorrow;
One dyed in the love of the Lord stays awake night and day;
One dyed in the love of the Lord dwells in the home of Sahaj;
Dyed in the love of the Lord, one's doubt and fear take flight.
Dyed in the love of the Lord, one's understanding becomes noble;
Dyed in the love of the Lord, one's renown is spotless.
Says Nanak, I am a sacrifice to those
who never forget my God. ॥4॥
201.4: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Those who make the effort (on the Lord's path) have become calm in mind;
walking on (that) way, all their sorrows have gone.
Repeating the Naam, bliss has filled their minds,
as they have sung with love the virtues of the (Lord of) supreme bliss.
There is well-being; they have come into the home of joy;
on meeting the Saadh Sangat, the curse (of Maya) has gone.
The eyes become pure the moment they behold (the Lord's) sight;
blessed are the foreheads that touch (his) lotus feet.
In the service of Gobind this body bears its fruit;
by the grace of the Sant (the Guru) the supreme state has been attained.
The servant whom (God) himself has helped
has found peace by falling at the feet of (the Lord's) servants.
When selfhood was gone, they became (one with the Lord) himself,
(when) they came into the refuge of the treasure of mercy.
When (one) has found the very One he longed for,
where else would he go then to search (for him)?
(Such ones) have become steady; they dwell on the seat of peace;
O Nanak, by the Guru's grace (they) have come to live in peace. ॥4॥
202.1: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(He has, as it were,) bathed with millions of dips (at places of pilgrimage),
and given away hundreds of thousands, billions and trillions in charity:
the one in whose mind the Name of the Lord has come to dwell.
Singing the virtues of Gopal, all (beings) become pure;
in the refuge of the merciful Saadh (the Guru), sins are wiped away.
(He has, as it were,) performed many austerities hanging upside down, and every discipline,
and gained countless profits and the wishes of the heart:
the one who has worshipped with his tongue the Name of the Lord, Har Har.
(He has, as it were,) recited the Simritis, the Shastras and the Vedas,
and known Yoga, divine knowledge and the joys of the Siddhas:
the one whose mind, repeating the Naam, has come to trust in God.
The Lord is of unfathomable understanding, inaccessible and infinite;
(the one he favours) repeats the Naam and reflects on the Naam in the heart.
O God, show (this) mercy to Nanak. ॥4॥
202.2: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Remembering, remembering, ever remembering (God), peace has been found,
(when) the lotus feet of the Guru were enshrined in the heart.
The Guru, Gobind, is the perfect Supreme Lord;
worshipping him, my mind has grown steady.
Night and day I repeat (the Name of) the Guru, the Guru's Name;
through it, all my tasks have been accomplished.
Beholding (his) sight, minds have become cool,
and the sins of birth after birth have gone.
Says Nanak, where are the fears now, brother?
(The Lord) himself has kept the honour of his servant. ॥4॥
202.3: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(God) himself is the helper of his servant;
he always cherishes (him), as a father and mother (cherish their child).
In God's refuge everyone is saved;
that True One is the Doer and the cause of all that is done, pervading all.
Now the Creator has come to dwell in (my) mind;
fears are destroyed, and (I) relish the peace of the soul.
In his grace (God) has protected his servants;
(their) sins of birth after birth have been removed.
The greatness of God cannot be told;
O Nanak, (his) servants remain in (his) refuge for ever. ॥4॥
202.4: Raag Gauri Cheti, Dupade, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
The might of Ram is complete (everywhere), brother;
so no pain can take hold (of his servant).
Whatever the Lord's servant thinks of, O mother,
the Creator himself brings it about.
God has taken away the slanderer's honour;
O Nanak, (the Lord's servant) sings the virtues of the Lord, free of fear. ॥2॥
203.1: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
O Hero of mighty arms, O Brahm, ocean of peace: (I am) slipping into the pit; grasp (my) finger.
(My) ears have no power to hear, (my) eyes are not fair; afflicted and lame, (I) cry out at your door.
O Master of the meek, full of compassion for the helpless; O friend, companion, father and mother:
Says Nanak: holding your lotus feet in their hearts, the Sants have crossed the ocean of fear. ॥2॥
203.2: Raag Gauri Bairagan, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
O merciful One, Lord of the world, my dear friend: dwell with me.
Without you there is no life even for a moment; cursed is living in the world (so).
O Giver of soul, breath and peace, every moment I am a sacrifice (to you).
O God, give (me) the support of your hand; O Gopal, lift (me) out of the pit.
I am without virtue, of little understanding; you are ever merciful to the meek.
Which of your comforts can I recall? In what way can I reflect (on you)?
O keeper of those who come to your refuge, lover of your servants, lofty, inaccessible and infinite (Lord).
All treasures and the eight siddhis are in the great relish of the Naam.
Those with whom Keshav is well pleased, those servants sing the virtues of the Lord.
Mother, father, son and kinsman: you are (all) to me; you are the support of my life-breath.
In the Saadh Sangat Nanak worships (you), and has crossed the poisonous world. ॥5॥
203.3: Raag Gauri Bairagan, in the ghar of the Chhants of the Rahoe, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
There is some rare one who sings of the beloved Ram;
(Such a one) attains every blessing and comfort, and the True One.
The renunciate roams from forest to forest, searching;
(but) only some rare one has love for the One.
Those who have found the Lord are of great fortune.
Brahma and the other gods, Sanak and his brothers, long for (him);
the yogis, the celibates and the Siddhas yearn for the Lord;
(but) only the one who is destined to receive (it) sings the virtues of the Lord.
(I seek) the refuge of those who never forget (him).
Only the very fortunate meet the Lord's Sants;
for them there is no birth and death at all.
In your grace, meet (me), my dear Beloved.
O God, lofty and infinite, listen to (my) plea:
Nanak begs for the Naam as (his) support. ॥4॥
204.1: Raag Gauri Poorbi, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
O my mother, by what virtues may I come to meet the Lord of my life?
I am without beauty, lacking in understanding and strength; I am a stranger, come from far away.
I have no wealth, nor am I intoxicated with youth; take me, who have no protector, into yourself.
Searching and searching, I have become a bairagan (detached in longing); I wander, thirsting for the sight of God.
O God, merciful to the meek and compassionate, says Nanak, in the Saadh Sangat my burning has been quenched. ॥4॥
204.2: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Love for meeting God has taken hold of my mind.
If by great fortune some Sant should meet me, I would fall at (his) feet and make my plea (to him).
I would offer (him) my mind and set my wealth before (him); I have given up all the counsel of my own mind.
Whoever tells me the story of the Lord God, I would follow him night and day, detached (from all else).
When the seeds of past deeds sprouted, I met the Being who relishes (all) and yet stands apart.
Meeting the Lord, the darkness was wiped away; O Nanak, (the soul-bride) asleep for birth after birth has awakened. ॥2॥
204.3: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Come out (of the net of attachment), O bird; remember the Lord: (these are your) wings.
Meeting the Saadh (the Guru), take hold of the refuge of the Perfect One, and keep the jewel of Ram (the Naam) close to your heart.
(There is) the well of wandering doubt; the relish of craving is (its) mire; and the noose of attachment is very sharp.
The One who can cut it is Gobind, the Guru of the world: make your dwelling at his lotus feet.
In your grace, O Gobind, beloved God, Master of the meek, hear (my) prayer:
take hold of (my) hand, O Lord of Nanak; soul and body, all are your capital. ॥2॥
204.4: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
My mind remembers the Lord, (longing) to behold him.
Thirsting in hope, I think of (him) day and night: is there some Sant who would bring me close (to him)?
I would serve the servants of (that Sant's) servants, and plead with him in many ways.
Setting them on the scales, I have weighed all comforts: without the sight of the Lord, they are all too light.
(Whoever), by the grace of the Sant (the Guru), has sung the virtues of the Ocean of virtue has been brought back from wandering birth after birth.
Meeting the Lord there is bliss and peace; O Nanak, life fulfils its purpose and bears fruit in good time. ॥2॥
204.5: Raag Gauri Poorbi, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
O my sovereign Lord, in what way may the Master of the world be met?
(May I find) some Sant, giver of the peace of Sahaj, who would show me the way.
The Unseen is within (each one), yet cannot be seen, (for) the veil of Haumai has been drawn between.
In attachment to Maya the whole world sleeps; say, how is this doubt to go?
(The soul and God) keep the same company and dwell in the same house, yet they do not meet and speak together, brother.
Without the one thing, the five (senses) are wretched; that thing lies in a place beyond the senses' reach.
He whose house it is put the lock on it, and entrusted the key to the Guru.
(One) makes countless efforts, yet without the True Guru's refuge does not find (him).
O True Guru, those whose bonds (you) have cut have fixed their love (on God) in the Saadh Sangat.
(Their) five (senses) have joined together to sing the song of joy; O Nanak, there is no difference (between them and) the Lord, brother.
O my sovereign Lord, in this way the Master of the world is met:
Sahaj came, doubt fled in an instant, and the light, meeting the Light, merged (in it). ॥1॥
205.1: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Such an intimacy (with God) have I gained,
(that) the merciful Beethal showed grace and pointed me to the True Guru.
Wherever I look, there you alone are: this faith has come to me.
To whom (else) should I make my plea and prayer, when Raghurai (the Lord himself) is listening?
The Guru broke the bonds, anxiety was lifted, and then I found the lasting peace of Sahaj.
What was to be will come to be in the end; where then is pleasure or pain to be seen?
All the realms and universes have one abode (in God); the Guru drew back the veil and showed (it).
The treasure of the Naam, (all) the nine treasures, is in one place (within); to what place outside, then, should one go?
(As) from one gold, ornaments of many kinds are fashioned, (so the Lord) has made (this world) in many forms.
Says Nanak, the Guru has dispelled doubt, and so has merged the essence in the Essence. ॥4॥
205.2: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Day and night, the span of life wears away.
O mind, meet the Guru and set your affairs right.
I make one request, my friends; listen: this is the time to serve the Sants.
Earn the Lord's profit here before you depart, and your dwelling hereafter will be at ease.
This world is steeped in vice and caught in doubt; the Brahm Giani (one who knows God) has crossed over it.
Whom (God) has awakened and given the sweet essence of the Lord to drink, that one has come to know the story of the Indescribable.
Buy the very thing you came for; through the Guru, the Lord comes to dwell within the mind.
In your own home within, in the peace of Sahaj, you will find (his) mansion, and there will be no more round (of birth and death).
O Knower of hearts, all-pervading Being, Creator, fulfil the longing of my mind.
Servant Nanak begs for this one joy: make me the dust of the Sants' feet. ॥4॥
205.3: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
I am without virtue; all virtues are yours.
The troublemakers are five, and I am one, and poor; protect (me), O Protector.
They torment (me) and harass (me) sorely; I have come into your refuge.
I have tried countless ways of every kind until I am worn out, yet they will not let (me) go at all.
Hearing one thing, I looked to (that) shelter: in the Saadh Sangat they are wiped out.
By (your) grace I met the Sants, and from them I have gained courage.
The Sants gave me the mantra that makes one fearless, and I have lived by the Guru's Shabad.
Through the Bani that brings Sahaj and comfort, (I) have conquered those great troublemakers.
Says Nanak, light has dawned in (my) mind; (I) have attained the state of nirvana. ॥4॥
206.1: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(O Lord,) you are that King who never perishes.
Those who dwell with you are without fear; from where could this fear come (to them)?
In one body you are puffed up with pride, in another humble;
in one body you are all in all yourself, in another poor.
In one body you are a learned pandit and a fine speaker, in another you have become a fool;
in one body you are the one who takes hold of everything, in another you take nothing at all.
What can the poor wooden puppet do? The one who makes it play knows (how).
Whatever guise the showman makes it wear, that very costume it puts on.
(God) has made many little chambers (bodies) of many kinds, and he himself has become (their) keeper.
In whatever body he keeps (a being), in that it has to live; what can this poor (being) do?
The one who made (all) this, who fashioned this whole design, he alone knows (it).
Says Nanak, the Master is beyond the farthest beyond; (he alone knows) the worth of his own works. ॥5॥
206.2: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Give up, O (man), give up the relishes of Maya's poison.
You are caught up (in them), O crazed fool, like a beast in a green field of crops.
What you take to serve your own ends will not go with you even an inch.
Naked you came, naked you will depart; you have wandered round the cycle (of births), and death has seized you.
Watching again and again, O (man), the play of the safflower, you are lost and absorbed in it and laugh along with those (things).
Day and night the thread (of life) wears thin, yet you have done nothing at all for your soul.
Busy like this, on and on, you have grown old; your speech has failed and your body has wasted away.
As that enchantress (Maya) bewitched (you in your) youth, your fondness for her does not lessen one whit.
The Guru has shown me that the world is like this; so I have given up pride and fallen into (his) refuge.
The Sant (the Guru) has told (me) the way to God; servant Nanak has made devotion and the Lord's praise firm (within). ॥4॥
206.3: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Without you, (O Lord,) who is mine?
O my Beloved, support of my life-breath.
You alone know the state within me; you alone are (my) friend who brings comfort.
I have received every comfort from you, O my Master, beyond grasp and beyond weighing.
I cannot describe your wonders, O treasure of virtues, giver of peace.
O God, unreachable, beyond the senses, imperishable, you are known through the perfect Guru.
(The Guru) has cut away (their) doubt and fear and made (them) pure, ever since (they) killed their Haumai;
(their) dread of birth and death has ended through the sight (of the Guru) in the Saadh Sangat.
I wash (the Guru's) feet and serve the Guru; I am a sacrifice (to him) a hundred thousand times,
by whose grace (I) have crossed this terrifying world-ocean; servant Nanak has met the Beloved. ॥4॥
207.1: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Without you, (O Lord,) who can win your favour?
Beholding your form, all are enraptured.
In heaven, the netherworld, the mortal world and the spheres of the earth, that One alone pervades all.
Calling (you) Shiv, Shiv, the giver of good, all join their palms; O Master, merciful to all, they cry out to you alone.
O Master, your Name purifies the fallen; (you are) the giver of peace, pure and cooling.
O Nanak, converse (about you) with your Sants is itself knowledge, meditation and glory. ॥2॥
207.2: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Meet (me), O Beloved of all beings.
O God, what you have done has come to be.
Through countless births (the soul) has wandered in many species, suffering pain again and again.
By your grace (it) has obtained the human body; grant (me) your sight, O sovereign Lord.
That alone has happened which pleased him; no one else has done anything.
By your will (the being) lies lured by doubt and attachment; asleep, he does not wake.
Hear my prayer, O Lord of my life, O Beloved, treasure of mercy, compassionate one.
Save (us), O God, my Father; cherish those who have no protector.
Whomever you have shown your sight, (you have shown it) through the Saadh Sangat.
Show grace and give (me) the dust (of the feet) of the Sants; this is the comfort Nanak longs for. ॥4॥
207.3: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
I am a sacrifice to those (Sants)
whose one and only support is the Naam.
How far can the glory be counted of those servants who are dyed in the love of the Supreme Lord?
Peace, Sahaj and bliss are in their company; there are no other givers equal to them.
Those servants who thirst for (the Lord's) sight, they alone have come to save the world.
Whoever falls into their refuge is carried across; in the company of the Sants all hopes are fulfilled.
When I fall at their feet, then I live; in the company of (such) servants I am filled with joy.
Be merciful, O God, (that) my mind may become the dust (of the feet) of the devotees.
Kingship, youth, life-span, whatever is seen, all of it wanes in the world.
The treasure of the Naam is ever new and pure; O Nanak, (the Sants) have earned this wealth of the Lord. ॥4॥
208.1: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
I have come from the Guru, having heard the way of Yoga;
the True Guru has made me understand (it) through the Shabad.
The (Lord) of the earth's nine regions pervades this body; I bow (to him) at every moment.
The Guru's initiation is the earrings in my ears; I have fixed the One Formless Lord firmly (in my heart).
The five disciples (the senses) have come together as one; (I) have brought them under the sway of the One.
The ten (organs) have become detached and obedient; then I became a pure yogi.
Burning doubt, I have smeared (myself) with its ashes; to see the One (in all) is my sect.
I have made the peace of Sahaj my food, which the Master wrote on my forehead.
I have set my seat where there is no fear; the unstruck Bani is my horn (singi).
I have made reflection on the essence my staff; love of the Naam in the mind is my way.
Such a yogi is met by great good fortune; he cuts away the bonds of Maya.
I serve and worship that embodiment (of God); Nanak licks his feet. ॥5॥
208.2: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Listen, all of you: the Naam is a treasure beyond compare; meditate on it, O friends.
The one to whom the Guru has given the Lord's medicine, his mind becomes pure.
Darkness is gone from the body of the one (within whom) the Guru has lit the lamp through the Shabad.
The net of doubt is cut for the one who has faith in the Saadh Sangat.
He has crossed the world-ocean, deep and hard to swim, with the company of the holy as the ship.
The hope of the mind is fulfilled (for one) who has met the Guru, (steeped in) the Lord's love.
The devotees have gained the treasure of the Naam; in mind and body they are filled and content.
O Nanak, the revered Lord gives (it) to the one whom he makes accept his Hukam. ॥3॥
208.3: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Show kindness and mercy, O Lord of my life; I, without a protector, (have come to) your refuge, O God.
Give me your hand and save (me) in the blind well (of Maya); no cleverness or argument of mine (avails).
You alone do and cause all to be done; you are all-powerful, there is no other.
Your state and extent you alone know; they alone are your servants who have good fortune (written) on their foreheads.
O God, you are steeped in your servants; like warp and weft you are joined with your devotees.
(Your devotee,) crying Beloved, Beloved, longs for your Name and your sight, as the chakor's gaze (is fixed on) the moon.
There is no difference at all between Ram and (his) Sant; (yet such) a servant is one among many hundreds of thousands and millions.
The one in whose heart God has become manifest sings (his) Kirtan with the tongue, night and day.
You are all-powerful, infinite, most high, the giver of peace, O God, the support of life.
Show grace, O God, to Nanak, (that he may stay) in the company of those Sants. ॥4॥
209.1: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
O Sants, you are dyed in the Lord.
O all-pervading Creator, stand by me to the end; O Giver, carry (me) through to the goal.
Your secret you alone have known; you are the perfect Being, the Creator.
Keep (me), helpless and meek, in your refuge; grant me liberation.
To cross the ocean, your feet are the ship; you know your own ways.
Those whom you, in your grace, keep with you, each of them crosses over.
Here and hereafter you are all-powerful, O God; all is in your hands.
O servants of the Lord, give me such a treasure as will go along with me.
Grant virtue to (me), the one without virtue, (that) my mind may repeat the Lord's Name.
O Nanak, (those who) meet the Lord by the grace of the Sant (the Guru) are cooled and fulfilled in mind and body. ॥4॥
209.2: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
I have merged in Sahaj, O Divine Lord;
the True Guru has become merciful to me, O Divine Lord.
Cutting the noose (of Maya), (the Guru) has made me (your) humble slave and set me to serve the Sants.
I have become the worshipper of the One Name; to me the Guru has shown a wonder.
Light has dawned and all is radiant; the Guru has made (his) knowledge manifest in my mind.
I have drunk the Amrit of the Naam, and my mind is satisfied; (I) have settled in the fearless (Lord).
Obeying (the Guru's) command, (I) have found every comfort, and have lost the very home of sorrows.
When God the Master was fully pleased, he showed (me) all as the form of bliss.
Nothing comes and nothing goes; the sovereign Lord has made it all a play.
Says Nanak, the Master is unreachable, unreachable; the Lord's Name is the support of his devotees. ॥4॥
209.3: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
O mind, take the shelter of the perfect Supreme Lord, the Supreme God.
Repeat the Name of the Lord who upholds the universes and their regions.
O servants of the Lord, give up the mind's own counsel; peace is found by understanding (his) Hukam.
Whatever God does, accept it as good; in comfort and in pain, meditate on him alone.
The Creator saves tens of millions of the fallen in an instant; it takes him no time.
The Master is the destroyer of the pain and sorrow of the meek; whomever he pleases, him he honours.
He is mother, father and sustainer of all, the ocean of peace for soul and life-breath.
Giving, that Creator runs short of nothing; (he,) the mine of jewels, fills all.
The beggar begs for your Name, O Master; that (Lord) is within every heart.
Servant Nanak is in the refuge of the one from whom no one (goes away) empty. ॥4॥
210.1: Raag Gauri Poorbi, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Do not ever forget the Lord, Har Har, in (your) mind.
He gives every comfort here and hereafter; he cherishes every heart.
He cuts away great hardships in an instant (for the one whose) tongue remembers the Naam.
In the Lord's refuge are coolness, calm and peace; he puts out the burning fire.
He protects (one) from the hell-pit of the womb and ferries (one) over the world-ocean.
When (one) worships his lotus feet in the mind, he destroys the dread of Jam.
He is the perfect Supreme Lord, the Supreme God, lofty, unreachable and infinite.
Singing the virtues of the ocean of peace and meditating on him, one does not lose life in a gamble.
(My) mind is sunk in lust, anger, greed and attachment, O Giver to the meritless;
show grace and give (me) your own Name; Nanak is ever a sacrifice (to you). ॥4॥
210.2: Raag Gauri Cheti, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
There is no peace, O (friend), without devotion to the Lord.
Win (the game of) this priceless jewel, the human birth; in the Saadh Sangat repeat (the Naam), even for a moment.
Sons, wealth, the delights of a wife,
many people have left (such) pleasures and gone.
Fine horses, fine elephants, the joys of kingship,
the fool leaves (them all) and departs naked.
(One) swells with pride in a body (anointed) with perfume and sandal;
that body rolls in the dust.
Lured by attachment, (one) supposes (God) to be far off;
210.3: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
O mind, the Lord's Name is the support for crossing over (the world-ocean).
The world is an ocean whose waves are dread and doubt; the Guru is the ship that carries (one) across.
In Kalyug there is the blackness of (ignorance's) darkness;
the lamp of the Guru's wisdom (alone) gives light (in it).
The poison of Maya's vices has spread far and thick;
only by dwelling again and again on the Lord's virtues have (people) been saved from it.
on meeting the Guru, (his) doubt and fear were dispelled.
Says Nanak, (the one who) has meditated on the One
210.4: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(O God,) you alone are my Diwan (my master and support);
with the Guru's support I serve you.
By countless ways I could not find (you);
(now) the Guru has taken me and set me in (your) service.
I have slain the five quarrelsome (foes, lust and the rest);
by the Guru's grace I have subdued (their) army.
As reward and as wages I have received the Name of the One,
(and in it are) peace, Sahaj, bliss and rest.
Good are those who are God's servants;
O Nanak, their faces are radiant. ॥4॥
211.1: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
O my soul, (take) the shelter of the Name;
in all else that is done and caused to be done, there is the fear of Jam.
By no other effort is (God) found;
only by great good fortune is the Lord meditated upon.
One may know a hundred thousand clever devices,
(but) hereafter (in the Lord's court) one is not honoured even a sesame seed's worth.
Deeds done with a mind of ego
are houses of sand that the water washes away.
then, O Nanak, the Naam is found in the company of the Saadh (the Guru). ॥4॥
211.2: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice, a hundred thousand times (to the Lord's Name);
O brother, the Master's Name, the Name alone, is the support of life.
(O God,) you alone are the One who does and causes all to be done;
all beings and creatures rest on you alone as their support.
O God, you are the master of sovereignty and of youth;
you are Nirgun, and you are Sargun.
Here and hereafter you are the protector;
by the Guru's grace a rare one understands (this).
O God, you are the knower of hearts, the all-wise;
you alone are Nanak's prop and strength. ॥4॥
211.3: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Let us worship the Lord, Har, Har, Har.
In the company of the Sants the Lord comes to dwell in the mind, and doubt, attachment and fear are brought under control.
The Vedas, the Puranas and the Simritis say,
(and it is) heard, that (the Lord's) servants abide highest of all.
All other places are seen to be gripped by fear;
(the Lord) has made the servants of Ram free of fear.
(Beings) wander through the eighty-four lakh wombs;
Gobind's people are not born and do not die.
(My own) strength, intellect, cleverness and Haumai are gone;
Nanak has grasped the refuge of the Lord's Saadh (the Guru). ॥4॥
211.4: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
O mind, let us sing the Name of Ram and (his) virtues.
Let us serve the Lord day after day, and meditate on the Lord with every breath.
In the company of the Sants the Lord comes to dwell in the mind,
(and) sorrow, pain, darkness and doubt take flight.
(Whoever) repeats the Lord's Name by the grace of the Sant (the Guru),
that person is not gripped by sorrow.
The one to whom the Guru imparts the mantra of the Lord('s Name)
has been saved from the fire of Maya.
O God, show mercy to Nanak,
(that) the Lord's Name may dwell in my mind and in my body. ॥4॥
211.5: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Let us repeat with the tongue the Name of the One;
(by it there is) peace and great joy here, and hereafter it goes with the soul and serves it.
(By it) your sickness of ego is cut away;
by the Guru's grace, practise Raj Jog.
The person who has tasted the sweet essence of the Lord('s Name)
(The one who) has found the Lord, the treasure of rest,
does not run off in any direction again.
The one to whom the Guru has given the Name of the Lord, Har Har,
O Nanak, is rid of fear. ॥4॥
212.1: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The one who forgets the Name of Ram is the very one who suffers pain;
those who join the Saadh Sangat and remember the Lord become rich in virtue and profound.
The one in whose heart, through the Guru, (the) understanding (of Simran) has come
holds the nine treasures and the siddhis in the palm of his hand.
Those who know the Lord God as the Master (of all)
(The one who) has recognised the Creator
has enjoyed the delights of every comfort.
Those in whose house (the heart) the wealth of the Lord('s Name) dwells:
says Nanak, in their company sorrow takes flight. ॥4॥
212.2: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(O man, your) pride is great, (but your) origin is so slight;
(you are) not to stay (here), yet how tight is (your) grip!
What the Vedas and the Sants forbid, O brother, with that very thing (you) are in love.
As a gambler loses at the game of dice, (so you are losing); the senses have brought (you) under their sway and won (you).
From love for the lotus feet of the One fully able to take away and to fill up, (you) are empty.
O Nanak, in the Saadh Sangat (people) are saved; the treasure of mercy has given (it) to me. ॥2॥
212.3: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
I am the lowly servant of the Master;
I eat the grain that God gives.
Such, O brother, is our Master:
in an instant he fashions (beings) and adorns them.
Should I be pleasing to the Master, I would do (his) work,
(and) sing songs of God's wondrous deeds and (his) virtues.
I have come into the refuge of the Master's ministers (the Sants);
beholding them, my mind has taken heart.
The One alone is (my) prop, the One alone (my) support;
servant Nanak has set himself to the Lord's work. ॥4॥
212.4: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Is there anyone who would break (my) Haumai,
(and) turn this mind (of mine) back from this sweet (Maya)?
Man has become ignorant: what is not (to last), that he longs for.
(Within him) is a black and dark night; what is the way by which (the day of wisdom) may dawn?
Wandering and wandering, (I) grew weary; in countless ways I searched.
Says Nanak, (God's) mercy came, (and) the Saadh Sangat (became) a treasure for me. ॥2॥
212.5: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(God) is the wish-fulfilling jewel (Chintamani), compassion itself.
The Supreme Lord is merciful to the lowly; in remembering him there is peace.
Akal Purakh (the Timeless Being) is of unfathomable wisdom; hearing his praise, millions of sins have been destroyed.
O God, treasure of mercy, show kindness, (that) Nanak may take the Name of the Lord, Har Har. ॥3॥
212.6: Raag Gauri Poorbi, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
O my mind, (it is) in God's refuge (that one) finds peace;
on the day the giver of life and peace slips from memory, that day goes to waste.
You have come as guests for one night, (yet) you build hopes for many ages.
House, mansion and wealth, all that is seen, is like the shade of a tree.
This body is mine, all this wealth is mine, the gardens, the lands and all the places (are mine; so saying),
(man) has forgotten the Master, the Giver (of them all); in an instant (they) become another's.
(Man) bathes and puts on white clothes, and applies perfume and sandalwood;
(but if) he has not recognised the Fearless, Formless One, (it is all) like bathing an elephant.
When (God) becomes merciful, he unites (one) with the True Guru; all peace is in the Lord's Name.
(The one whose) bonds the Guru has undone is set free; servant Nanak sings the Lord's virtues. ॥4॥
213.1: Raag Gauri Poorbi, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
O my mind, let us ever repeat Guru, Guru, Guru;
the Guru has made (this) jewel of a (human) birth fruitful; let us be a sacrifice to (his) sight.
As many breaths and morsels as one takes, so many times let us sing (God's) virtues;
(but only) when one's own True Guru is merciful is this understanding and wisdom found.
O my mind, by taking the Name (you) will be freed from Jam's bonds, and the peace above all peace is found;
by serving the True Guru, the Master and Giver, the fruit the mind longs for comes into one's hands.
The Creator's Name is (your) beloved, friend and son; O mind, (it alone) goes along with you.
