Strife, anguish, fears, doubt and pain are gone;
says Nanak, my Guru is all-powerful. ॥8॥
240.1: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Meet me, my Gobind; give me your Name.
Without the Name, cursed, cursed is (every other) attachment.
One who wears and eats without the Name
is like a dog putting its mouth into leftovers.
All the dealings carried on without the Name
are as vain as the adorning of a corpse.
One who forgets the Name and indulges in pleasures
finds no peace even in dreams; diseases (beset his) body.
One who abandons the Name and busies himself with other tasks
comes to ruin; all (his) shows are false.
One who does not join his mind in love with the Name
goes to hell, though he performs millions of rites.
One who has not worshipped the Lord's Name in his mind
is bound like a thief in the city of Jam.
Lakhs of pompous shows and a vast spread of things:
without the Name, (all this) display is false.
That servant alone takes the Lord's Name
to whom, O Nanak, (God) gives it in his grace. ॥8॥
240.2: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The One who stands by (me) at the beginning, in the middle and at the end:
that Friend my mind longs for.
Love for the Lord goes along with (one) for ever;
the merciful, perfect Being, present in all, cherishes (all).
He does not perish, nor does he leave (us) and go;
wherever I look, there he is pervading.
(God) is beautiful, accomplished, wise, the Giver of life;
brother, son, father and mother: God is (all these to me).
(He is) the prop of (my) life and breath, my wealth;
enshrining (him) in my heart, I have given (him) my love.
Gopal has cut away (my) noose of Maya;
looking on (me) with his glance of grace, he has made (me) his own.
Remembering (him) again and again, all ills are cut away;
meditation on (his) feet is the enjoyment of every comfort.
The perfect Being is ever new, ever young;
the Lord is within and without, with (us), our protector.
Says Nanak: (the devotee) has recognised the state of (union with) the Lord, Har Har;
(the Lord) has given the devotee the Name, which is everything. ॥8॥
240.3: Raag Gauri Majh, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Countless have wandered searching, (but none) has found (your) limit;
they alone became devotees on whom (your) grace fell.
I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice to the Lord.
Hearing again and again that the road is fearsome, I was gripped by great fear;
I have looked to the shelter of the Sants: save (me).
O enchanting Beloved, incomparable, support of all,
bowing low again and again, I fall at the Guru's feet: (O Guru,) show (me the Lord).
I made friends of many, (but) it is to the One alone that I am a sacrifice;
all virtues are found in no one (else); the Lord's storehouses (alone) are full.
(Your) Name is repeated in all four directions; (those who repeat it) are made beautiful in peace.
I have sought your shelter; Nanak is a sacrifice (to you).
Stretching out his arm, the Guru has pulled (me) out of the well of attachment;
I have won (the game of) this life of boundless worth, never to lose again.
I have found (God), the treasure of all, whose story cannot be told;
in the Lord's court (I) am honoured, and walk swinging (my) arms, free of care.
Servant Nanak has found the priceless, boundless jewel (of the Name);
by serving the Guru, one crosses the terrifying world-ocean: this I proclaim aloud. ॥8॥
241.1: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Dye (your mind) in the love of Narayan, the Lord;
repeat (his Name) with your tongue, and ask for the one Lord alone.
Give up Haumai and, through the wisdom the Guru gives, worship (the Lord);
this is done, joining the Sangat, by one for whom grace was written from the Source.
Whatever is seen has gone along with no one;
the foolish Saakat clings to it and wastes away to death.
The Name of the Enchanter pervades (all) for ever;
among millions, only someone rare has found it, through the Guru.
Bow, bow in reverence to the Lord's Sants;
you will obtain the nine treasures and peace beyond measure.
May (my) eyes behold the holy ones;
sing in your heart of the treasure of the Name.
Give up lust, anger, greed and attachment;
(one who does) is spared both birth and death.
Pain and darkness have gone from the home (of the heart),
(since) the Guru has made divine wisdom firm (within), and the lamp is alight.
Whoever served (the Lord) has crossed to the far shore;
O servant Nanak, through the Guru the world crosses over. ॥8॥
241.2: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Uttering Har Har, Guru Guru, (my) doubts have gone;
my mind has found every comfort.
I was burning, ablaze; sprinkled with the Guru's sandalwood, I was cooled.
The darkness of ignorance is gone: the Guru's wisdom has shone forth.
The ocean of fire is deep; boarding the boat of the Sants, I have been carried across.
I had no (good) deeds, no righteousness, no purity; God took (me) by the arm and made (me) his own.
Destroyer of fear, dispeller of pain, is the Name of the Lord, the lover of devotion.
O Master of the masterless, compassionate to the humble, almighty, shelter of the Sants,
this is the prayer of one without virtue: grant (me) the sight of you, O Lord King.
Nanak is in your refuge, O Master; (your) servant has come to your door. ॥8॥
242.1: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(One) takes delight in the pleasures of Maya; engrossed in them, the blind one understands nothing.
I amass, I earn: (so) the whole span of life has passed.
I am a hero, I am a chief; there is no one like me;
I am young, of good conduct, of noble family: so (one) grows proud in (his) mind.
As the one of fettered understanding stays entangled (in Maya), even while dying he does not forget (her).
Brothers, friends, kin and companions: to them, afterwards, (all he gathered) is handed over.
The desire the mind is attached to is the one that shows itself at the last.
Performing rites of purity with a mind full of self, (one) is held fast in these bonds.
O merciful Being, present in all, have mercy: Nanak is the slave of your slaves.
242.2: There is one God, Ik Oankar, the One who pervades all and is ever the same; his Name is Sat (the One who truly is); he is the Creator, the Being who dwells in all, realised by the Guru's grace.
Raag Gauri Poorbi, Chhants, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
For the young bride the night is full of pain; sleep does not come;
the soul-bride has grown frail, sighing for her Husband.
Sighing for her Spouse, the bride has wasted away: how might she see (him) with her eyes?
Adornment, sweet tastes, pleasures and fine food: all is false, of no account.
She who is drunk with youth as with wine is worn away by pride; milk once drawn does not come back to the teats.
O Nanak, the soul-bride meets (her Husband) only when she is brought to meet (him); without the Husband, sleep does not come.
Without her beloved Master, the young bride is forlorn.
How will she find peace without holding (him) to her heart?
Without the Husband the home is no home to dwell in; ask (your) friends and companions.
Without the Name there is no love or affection (for him); those who dwell in the True One live at ease.
With truth in the mind, and in contentment, comes the meeting with the Friend; through the Guru's teaching the Husband is known.
O Nanak, the soul-bride who does not let go of the Name merges in Sahaj through the Name.
Come together, my friends and companions; let us enjoy our Husband.
Asking the Guru, I shall write (to him) a message through the Shabad.
The Guru has shown the true Shabad; the self-willed (brides) repent.
The (mind) that kept running off stays steady once the True One is recognised.
The understanding of the True One is ever new; through the Shabad love stays ever fresh.
O Nanak, by (his) glance of grace the True One (is met) in Sahaj; meet (him), my friends and companions.
My wish is fulfilled: the Friend has come to my home.
Groom and bride have met, and the song of joy has been sung.
Singing the joyful song of (his) virtues, the young bride rejoices in love; her mind is full of eager delight.
The friends rejoice, the wicked are distressed; meditating on the True One, the true profit (is gained).
With palms joined, the soul-bride prays, drenched night and day in the relish (of his love).
O Nanak, Husband and bride delight together; my wish is fulfilled. ॥4॥
243.1: Raag Gauri, a Chhant, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Hear me, O Husband, dear God: I am all alone in the forest (of this world).
How will (your bride) take heart without her Husband, O carefree Lord?
The bride cannot live without her Husband; the night is very hard (for her).
Sleep does not come; (your) love is dear (to me); hear my prayer.
Apart from the Beloved no one cares for (me); all alone, (the bride) cries out.
O Nanak, the soul-bride meets (her Husband) only when she is brought to meet (him); without the Beloved she suffers pain.
She whom the Husband has left: who can bring her to him?
She who has met (him) in the relish of love is made beautiful by the Shabad.
Made beautiful by the Shabad, she then gains honour; the lamp (of wisdom) lights up her body.
Listen, my friend and companion: she is at ease in the True One who cherishes the True One's virtues.
When the True Guru united her, the Husband delighted in her; through the Amrit Bani she blossomed.
O Nanak, the soul-bride enjoys her Husband only when she is pleasing to his mind.
Maya the enchantress has left her homeless; she who clings to falsehood is plundered by falsehood.
How can the noose at her neck be loosed without the most beloved Guru?
One who loves the Lord and reflects (on him) through the Shabad becomes his alone.
How can charity, alms and countless bathings wash away the filth within?
Without the Name no one is set free: not by stubborn will, not by curbing the senses, not by (living in) the wilderness.
O Nanak, the true home is recognised through the Shabad; what can (one caught in) duality know of the mansion?
Your Name is true, dear Lord; your Shabad is true, and reflection (on it).
Your mansion is true, dear Lord; true is the trade in the Name.
The trade in the Name is sweet; devotion is its profit, night and day.
Apart from it, no other merchandise is worth a thought; take the Name each and every moment.
The account is assayed, and (his) true glance of grace (falls); by (his) perfect grace (the Name) is obtained.
O Nanak, the Name is the supreme relish, and sweet; through the Perfect Guru the True One has been found. ॥4॥
243.2: Raag Gauri Poorbi, Chhants, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
There is one God, Ik Oankar, the One who pervades all and is ever the same; his Name is Sat (the One who truly is); he is the Creator, the Being who dwells in all, realised by the Guru's grace.
The soul-bride offers her prayer, cherishing the Lord's virtues;
she cannot live a moment, an instant, without her beloved Lord.
Without her beloved Lord she cannot live; (but) without the Guru (his) mansion is not found.
Whatever the Guru says, that should be done in full; (thus) the fire of craving is quenched.
The Lord alone is true; there is none but him; without service (to him), no peace is found.
O Nanak, the soul-bride meets (her Husband) only when she is brought to meet (him): she whom he himself unites.
The bride's night passes in ease when she fixes her mind on the Lord.
She serves the True Guru with love, and sheds self-conceit from within.
Shedding self-conceit from within, she sings the Lord's praises; night and day her love (for him) holds.
Listen, my friend and companion, dear to my heart: merge in the Guru's Shabad.
When she cherishes the Lord's virtues, she is dear to her Husband; she has set her love on the Name alone.
O Nanak, the soul-bride is dear to her Husband, the Lord's Name a garland at her neck.
Without her beloved Husband the bride is all alone;
she is robbed through the love of another, without the Guru's mighty Shabad.
Without the beloved Shabad, who can carry (her) across the ocean so hard to cross? Attachment to Maya has led her astray.
When falsehood ruined her, her Husband cast her off; that bride does not reach (his) mansion.
(She who is) dyed in the Guru's Shabad, absorbed in Sahaj, stays merged (in him) night and day.
O Nanak, the bride who is ever dyed in (his) love is united (with him) by the dear Lord himself.
One meets (him) only when the Lord brings (one) to meet; who but the Lord can unite?
Without one's own beloved Guru, who can dispel doubt?
The Guru dispels doubt; in this way, O mother, (he) is met, and then the soul-bride is at peace.
Without service to the Guru, there is pitch darkness; without the Guru the path is not found.
The bride dyed in (his) love, absorbed in Sahaj, reflects (on him) through the Guru's Shabad.
O Nanak, through love for the beloved Guru, the bride has found the Lord as her Groom. ॥4॥
244.1: Raag Gauri, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Without my Husband I am utterly forlorn; O my mother, how can I live without him?
Sleep will not come without the Husband, and no garment sits well on my body.
A garment looks fair on the body when (she) pleases her Husband; through the Guru's teaching the mind is fixed (on him).
When she serves the True Guru she is a happy wife for ever; it is in the Guru's embrace that one is absorbed.
Through the Guru's Shabad comes union, and then I enjoy my Husband; the Name is the (true) profit in the world.
O Nanak, the soul-bride is dear to her Husband when she cherishes the Lord's virtues.
The soul-bride enjoys delight with her own Beloved.
Day and night she is dyed in (his) love, and reflects on the Guru's Shabad.
She reflects on the Guru's Shabad and kills Haumai; in this way, (friends,) meet the Beloved.
That bride is a happy wife, ever dyed in (his) love, in love with the True Name.
Staying joined to one's own Guru, one lays hold of the amrit (of the Name), and she kills duality and casts it out.
O Nanak, the bride has found the Lord as her Groom, and has forgotten all her sorrows.
The bride strays from her Husband, in love with attachment to Maya.
False herself, she clings to the false; she who clings to falsehood is plundered by falsehood.
(If) she casts out falsehood and holds to the Guru's teaching, she does not gamble her life away.
She serves the Guru's Shabad, merges in the True One, and kills Haumai within.
She enshrines the Lord's Name in her heart: such is the adornment she makes.
O Nanak, the bride whose support is the True Name stays merged in Sahaj.
Meet me, my dear Beloved; without you I am utterly forlorn.
Sleep does not come to my eyes; neither food nor water pleases me.
Water and food do not please; one dies in sighs; without the Husband how can peace be found?
I make my prayer before the Guru: if it pleases the Guru, may he unite me (with the Lord) in whatever way he may be met.
The Giver of peace himself unites (her with him); he himself has come home and met (her).
O Nanak, that bride is a happy wife for ever: her Husband neither dies nor goes away. ॥4॥
245.1: Raag Gauri, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
The bride is pierced through by the Lord's essence, (steeped) in the Lord's Sahaj and love.
The Enchanter has captivated her mind; her duality has dissolved in Sahaj.
With her duality dissolved in Sahaj, the bride finds her Groom, and through the Guru's teaching she delights (in him).
This body is filled to the throat with falsehood and deceit, and commits sins.
Through the Guru comes the devotion by which the strain of Sahaj wells up; without devotion the filth does not go.
O Nanak, the bride who sheds self-conceit from within is dear to her Husband.
Through love for the beloved Guru, the bride has found her Husband.
She sleeps the night in peace, holding (him) within, in her heart.
Holding him within, in the heart, one meets the Beloved, who drives out pain night and day.
The mansion is within; there the bride enjoys her Husband, reflecting through the Guru's teaching.
Day and night she has drunk the amrit of the Name, and has killed duality and cast it out.
O Nanak, through boundless love for the Guru, the happy wife has met the True One.
Come in your mercy, O dearest Beloved.
So the bride prays, having adorned herself with the True (Name) and the Shabad.
Adorned with the True (Name) and the Shabad, she kills Haumai, and through the Guru she sets her affairs right.
In every age the One alone is true; through reflection on the Guru's word she comes to understand him.
The self-willed bride is gripped by lust and tormented by attachment: before whom can she go and cry out?
O Nanak, without the dearest Guru, the self-willed bride finds no place.
The young bride is unknowing, simple and without virtue; the Husband is unreachable and infinite.
He is met (only) when he himself unites; he himself is the Forgiver.
The bride's dear Husband pardons faults; he pervades every heart.
He is found through love, affection and loving devotion: this understanding the True Guru has given.
She stays ever in bliss, day and night; night and day she keeps her loving attention fixed (on him).
O Nanak, in Sahaj she has found the Lord as her Groom; that bride has obtained the nine treasures. ॥4॥
245.2: Raag Gauri, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
The pool of Maya surges in its might; how can it be crossed, so hard to cross?
Make the Lord's Name the ship, and set the Shabad in it as the boatman.
When one sets the Shabad in it as boatman, the Lord himself takes (one) over; in this way the hard crossing is made.
Through the Guru devotion is obtained; so one dies while yet alive.
The Lord's Name cuts away sins in an instant, and the body is made pure.
O Nanak, through the Lord's Name comes deliverance: even the slag of burnt iron is turned to gold.
Women and men are gripped by lust; they have never learnt the way of the Lord's Name.
They hold mother, father, sons and brothers very dear; they have drowned and died without water.
Drowned and dead without water, they never knew the higher state; the world rushes about in Haumai.
Whoever has come will depart, each one; those who reflect on the Guru's word have been saved.
Whoever becomes Gurmukh and utters the Lord's Name crosses over himself and carries his family across.
O Nanak, the Name dwells within (his) heart, and through the Guru's teaching he meets the Beloved.
Without the Lord's Name nothing lasts; the world is a play.
Fix true devotion firmly (in your heart), and make the Lord's Name your trade.
The trade in the Name of the unreachable, infinite Lord: this wealth is gained through the Guru's teaching.
Service and attention (fixed on the Lord): this is the true devotion, (by which) self-conceit is shed from within.
We are without wisdom, foolish, ignorant and blind; the True Guru has set (us) on the path.
O Nanak, the Gurmukhs are made beautiful by the Shabad, and sing the Lord's praises night and day.
He himself causes (all) to be done, he himself does (it), and he himself embellishes (lives) through the Shabad.
He himself is the True Guru, he himself the Shabad; in every age his devotees are dear (to him).
In every age his devotees are dear (to him); the Lord himself embellishes them, and himself attaches them to devotion.
He himself is the Knower, he himself the Seer; he himself has (his) service done.
He himself is the Giver of virtues; he cuts away faults and makes the Name dwell in the heart.
Nanak is ever a sacrifice to the True One, who himself does and causes all to be done. ॥4॥
246.1: Raag Gauri, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Serve the Guru, O my dear husband, and meditate on the Lord's Name.
Do not go far from me, O my dear husband: sitting at home, one finds the Lord.
Sitting at home one finds the Lord, keeping the mind ever fixed (on him), in Sahaj, in love for the True One.
Service of the Guru brings great ease, (but only to the one) whom (the Lord) himself has do it.
He sows the Name alone, the Name alone springs up, and he enshrines the Name alone in his mind.
O Nanak, in the True Name is glory; one obtains (it) by what was written before.
The Lord's Name is sweet, O my dear husband, when you taste it with your mind fixed (on it).
O wretched tongue, taste the Lord's essence, and give up the savour of other tastes.
When it pleases the Lord, the tongue tastes the Lord's essence for ever, and is made beautiful by the Shabad.
Whoever meditates on the Name finds peace for ever, and keeps his loving attention fixed on the Name.
Through the Name (the Lord's relish) springs up, through the Name (the pull of other tastes) is destroyed, and through the Name one merges in the True One.
O Nanak, through the Guru's teaching the Name is found; (the Lord) himself sets (one) to it.
This is service to another, O my dear husband: (a man) leaves his wife and goes off to foreign lands.
In (the love of) another no one has found peace, O my dear husband; (one is) lured by greed for Maya, the poison.
Lured by greed for Maya, the poison, and led astray by doubt, how can he find peace?
Service to another is very painful: one sells oneself and loses one's righteousness.
In Maya's bonds (the mind) finds no rest; every moment pain torments (it).
O Nanak, the pain of Maya ends only when one fixes the mind on the Guru's Shabad.
The manmukh is foolish and uncouth, O my dear husband; he does not enshrine the Shabad in his mind.
Maya's illusion blinds him, O my dear husband; how is he to find the way to the Lord?
How is he to find the way without love for the True Guru? The manmukh puts himself forward.
The Lord's servants, their minds fixed on the Guru's feet, are ever at ease.
The one on whom the dear Lord shows grace sings the Lord's praises for ever.
O Nanak, the jewel of the Name is the (true) profit in the world; (the Lord) himself gives this understanding through the Guru. ॥4॥
247.1: Raag Gauri, Chhants, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Bairag (longing for the Lord) has arisen in my mind: how may I behold you, O God, the Giver?
O my friend and companion, dear Lord, O great Being, Maker of all!
You are the all-pervading Being, the Maker, the One, Sridhar; how may I, forlorn, meet you?
My hands do (your) service, my head (lies) at (your) feet; in my humbled mind is the hope of your sight.
With every breath, day and night, you are not forgotten for a while, an instant or a moment.
Says Nanak: we thirst like the rain-bird; how may God, the Giver, be met?
I make one prayer: listen, O beloved Husband.
Watching your wondrous plays, my mind and body have been captivated.
Watching your plays I was beguiled; how can (this) forlorn bride now be consoled?
O virtuous Husband, merciful and ever young, full of every virtue!
The fault is not yours, O Husband, Giver of peace; it is I, the wrongdoer, who am separated (from you).
Nanak prays: show mercy and come home, O beloved Husband.
I would offer my mind, offer my whole body, offer all my lands;
I would offer my head to that dear friend who brings me word of God.
When I offered my head to the Guru, in that blessed place, he showed me God beside (me).
In an instant all pain vanished; I obtained what my mind had wished.
Day and night the bride delights; all her anxieties are gone.
Nanak prays: the Husband has met (us), just such a one as we longed for.
Bliss has arisen in my mind, and rejoicing resounds.
The dear Darling has come home; all thirst is quenched.
When I met the Darling, Gopal, the Master, my companions sang songs of joy.
All my friends and kin were filled with joy, and the foes (the vices) lost their foothold.
The unstruck music plays in the home; the bed has been spread (for union) with the Husband.
Nanak prays: she abides in Sahaj, for she has met the Lord, her Husband, the giver of peace. ॥4॥
248.1: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
O Enchanter (Mohan), lofty are your temples, and your mansions are boundless.
O Enchanter, beautiful are your gates, dear Lord: the dharamsalas (houses of worship) of the Sants.
In (your) dharamsalas, O boundless, merciful Master, (the Sants) ever sing your Kirtan.
Wherever Saadhs and Sants come together, it is you they meditate on.
Show kindness and mercy, O merciful Master; be gracious to the meek.
Nanak prays: (we) thirst for your sight; to meet you and behold you is the whole of peace.
O Enchanter, your words are incomparable, your ways unlike any other.
O dear Enchanter, (all) acknowledge you alone as the One; all else is dust.
They acknowledge (you), the One, the indescribable Master, who has set his power in all (creation).
Through the Guru's word (your devotees) have won you over, O Primal Being, Banwari (Lord of the world).
You yourself are what moves, you yourself are what stays still; you yourself have set your power in all (creation).
Nanak prays: save (our) honour; all (your) servants are in your refuge.
O Enchanter, the Sat Sangat meditates on you, its attention fixed on your sight.
O Enchanter, Jam does not come near those who repeat your Name, (even) at the end.
Jamkaal cannot touch those who meditate (on you) with one-pointed mind.
Those who worship you in mind, word and deed obtain all the fruits.
Those who were dull and foolish, (as foul as) dung and urine, have grown wise on beholding your sight.
Nanak prays: your rule is unshakeable, O perfect, all-pervading Lord.
O Enchanter, you have borne fair fruit, together with your family.
O Enchanter, you have carried across sons, friends, brothers and whole households.
You have carried the world across; those who have had your sight are rid of pride.
Those who have called you blessed: Jam has not come near them.
Your endless virtues cannot be told, O True Guru, all-pervading Being, Murari.
Nanak prays: I have taken hold of your support, holding to which the world has crossed over. ॥4॥
248.2: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(The Lord's Name) makes countless sinners pure; again and again I am a sacrifice (to it).
O Nanak, repeat the Name of Ram: (that Name) is a fire that burns up sins as it burns straw. ॥1॥
248.3: O mind, repeat (the Name of) Ram, Narain, Govind, Har, Madho.
O mind, meditate on Murari, on Mukand (the giver of liberation), (by whom) the noose of death and pain is cut.
Let us worship the lotus feet of Sridhar, remover of pain, shelter of the meek.
The hard road of Jam and the ocean of fire are overcome by remembering (him) for an instant.
Worship day and night the One who burns away the filth of sin and makes (one) pure.
Nanak prays: have mercy, O Gopal, Gobind, Madho.
O mind, remember Damodar, the remover of pain, the destroyer of fear, the Lord, the King;
Sri Rang, the merciful, the enchanter of the mind, whose very nature it is to love devotion.
From the perfect Being who loves devotion, what the mind longs for is obtained.
(If his) Name is enshrined in the mind, (he) lifts (one) out of the pitch-dark well.
Gods, Siddhas, ganas, gandharvas and silent sages have sung (his) countless virtues in devotion.
Nanak prays: have mercy, O Supreme Lord, O Lord King.
O mind, keep in mind the Supreme Lord, the Supreme God, who upholds all with his power;
the compassionate, all-powerful Master, the support of the breath of life in every heart;
the Giver of breath, mind, body and life, infinite, inaccessible, boundless;
the all-powerful, enchanting (Lord), able to shelter those who seek refuge, the destroyer of all faults.
Disease, grief and all faults perish as one repeats the Name of Murari.
Nanak prays: have mercy, O all-powerful One, who upholds all with your power.
O mind, sing the praises of the unshakeable, the imperishable, highest of all, the merciful;
he sustains the universe; he alone is the Giver; he cherishes all.
The cherisher, the greatly merciful, the all-knowing, shows compassion to everyone.
(The fear of) death, piercing like a thorn, and greed and attachment are destroyed for the one in whose heart God dwells.
(When) the divine Lord is well pleased, service bears fruit and the labour is fulfilled.
Nanak prays: repeating (the Name of the One) merciful to the meek, (my) wish has been fulfilled. ॥4॥
249.1: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Listen, my friend: let us come together and strive to win over the Lord, our Husband.
Giving up pride, let us make devotion our love-charm, and enchant (him) with the mantra of the Saadh (the Guru).
Friend, once he comes under (love's) sway, he does not leave again: such is the Lord's good way.
O Nanak, (he) takes away the fears of old age, death and hell, and makes that being pure.
Listen, my friend: this is a good plea; let us make this resolve firm:
that in Sahaj and in love, free of all guile, we sing the songs of Govind.
(So) strife and anguish are ended, doubts are dispelled, and the fruit the mind longs for is obtained.
O Nanak, let us meditate upon the Name of the Supreme Lord, the perfect Supreme God.
Friend, I long, and every day I make vows, that God may fulfil my hope.
Thirsting for (his) feet, yearning for (his) sight, I search every place.
Searching, I find the company of the Lord's Sants, (which) unites (one) with the all-powerful Being.
O Nanak, those who have met the Friend, the giver of peace, are fortunate indeed, O mother.
Friend, I dwell (now) with my beloved Husband; my mind and body have grown one with the Lord.
Listen, my friend: (even) my sleep is sweet, (for) I have met my own Beloved.
The Master has dispelled (my) doubt; (I abide) in peace and Sahaj; light has dawned, and the lotus (of the heart) has blossomed.
O Nanak, I have found God, the knower of hearts, as my Groom; (my) wedded joy never passes away. ॥4॥
250.1: Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Raag Gauri, Bavan Akhri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The Gurdev is mother, the Gurdev is father, the Gurdev is the Master, the Supreme God.
The Gurdev is the friend who destroys ignorance; the Gurdev is kinsman and brother born of the same womb.
The Gurdev is the Giver who teaches the Lord's Name; the Gurdev's mantra is one whose power nothing can stop.
The Gurdev is the embodiment of peace, truth and wisdom; the Gurdev is a paaras whose touch surpasses even the paaras.
The Gurdev is the tirath, the pool of Amrit; to bathe in the Guru's wisdom is beyond all else.
The Gurdev is the Creator, the remover of all sins; the Gurdev makes the fallen pure.
The Gurdev is from the beginning, from the start of the ages, in every age; repeating the Gurdev's mantra, the Lord's Name, one is saved.
O God, in your grace join (us) to the Gurdev's company, holding fast to which we foolish sinners may swim across.
The Gurdev is the True Guru, the Supreme Lord, the Supreme God; O Nanak, salutation to the Gurdev, the Lord. ॥1॥
250.2: (God) himself has done (all) and caused (all) to be done; he himself has the power to do (all).
O Nanak, the One alone pervades all; there has been no other, and there will be none. ॥1॥
250.3: Ong: salutation to Oankar, to the Saadh, the True Guru,
who in the beginning, in the middle and at the end is the Formless One.
He himself is in Sunn; he himself is seated in bliss;
he himself hears (his praise); he himself is the glorious One.
He himself brought himself into being;
he himself is (his own) father, he himself (his own) mother.
He himself is the subtle (unseen), he himself the gross (the visible world).
O Nanak, (his) play is beyond understanding.
Show grace, O God, merciful to the meek,
that (my) mind may become the dust of your Sants' feet.
250.4: The Formless One himself is (all) form; Nirgun and Sargun, he is the One.
The One is spoken of as the One alone; O Nanak, the One is the many. ॥1॥
250.5: Ong: Oankar made the world of forms (for beings to become) Gurmukh;
he is the One who strings (all) on a single thread.
(He) has spread out the three qualities, each apart;
from Nirgun (he) has come into sight as Sargun.
(O God,) making every kind (of being, you) have brought forth (the world);
(you) have made the mind's attachment, (the root of) birth and death, grow.
(Yet you) yourself are apart from both (birth and death).
O Nanak, (he) has no end, no near shore and no far shore. ॥2॥
250.6: They alone are bankers, they the wealthy, (who have) the wealth of truth, the capital of the Lord's (Name).
O Nanak, truth and purity are found with such Sants. ॥1॥
250.7: Sassa: True, true, true is he;
no one is apart from the True Being.
He alone comes to (God's) refuge whom (God himself) brings there;
remembering (him) again and again, he sings (his) praises and makes (others) hear them.
Fear and doubt do not touch him at all;
to him the glory of that (Lord) alone is plainly seen.
He who reaches this (state) is the Saadh;
Nanak is ever a sacrifice to him. ॥3॥
250.8: Why do (you) cry out, wealth, wealth? All attachment to Maya is false.
O Nanak, without the Name all are turning to dust. ॥1॥
251.1: Dhadha: (O God,) the dust (of the feet) of your servants is pure;
blessed are those whose mind longs for this (dust).
(They) do not want wealth, nor do they wish for heaven;
(they) are absorbed in the love of the most dear (Lord), and in the dust (of the feet) of the Saadh.
How can worldly entanglements take hold of those
who do not leave the One to go anywhere else?
The one in whose heart God has placed (his) Name,
O Nanak, that Saadh is the perfect Lord's own form. ॥4॥
251.2: By many religious garbs, by (talk of) knowledge and by meditation, by stubbornness of mind, no one has met (God).
Says Nanak, the one on whom (God's) grace has come is the devotee, is the wise one. ॥1॥
251.3: Nganga: spiritual wisdom (does not come) by words of the mouth,
nor by the many devices of the Shastras and their (many) ways.
He alone is wise in whom that (Lord) is firmly fixed;
by mere saying and hearing, no union (with God) comes about at all.
He is wise in whom (God's) command stays firm;
to him, heat and cold are all one.
He is wise who, through the Guru, reflects on the essence,
O Nanak, (the one) on whom (God) has bestowed his grace. ॥5॥
251.4: Those who came into the world without understanding came in name only; they are beasts and cattle.
O Nanak, he alone understands, through the Guru, on whose forehead (good) fortune is written. ॥1॥
251.5: (One) has come into this age for the One (Lord) alone,
(yet) from birth Maya the enchantress has enchanted (him).
In the hollow of the womb (beings) practise austerity upside down,
(and there) they keep remembering God with every breath;
(but once born) they are entangled in what they must leave behind,
and they forget the Giver from their minds.
O Master of the world, the one on whom (you) bestow grace
says Nanak, does not forget (you) here or hereafter. ॥6॥
251.6: By (God's) Hukam (one) comes, by Hukam (one) perishes; no one is outside (his) command.
Coming and going ends for him, O Nanak, in whose mind that (Lord dwells). ॥1॥
251.7: These beings dwell in many wombs;
absorbed in sweet attachment, (they) are snared in births.
This Maya has brought (them) under the three qualities;
(she) has put her own attachment into every heart.
by which I may cross this hard (ocean of) Maya.
(Whom God) in his grace joins to the Sat Sangat,
O Nanak, Maya does not come near him. ॥7॥
251.8: The deeds that are done, good and bad, that God himself has done;
(yet) the beast (of a man) cries, I, I, of himself; O Nanak, without the Lord what can (anyone) accomplish? ॥1॥
251.9: The One himself causes (all) to be done;
he himself has spread out sin and virtue.
In this age, to whatever (God) himself has attached (each one),
that alone (each one) has received which he himself has caused to be given.
whatever he does, that alone comes to pass.
From the One alone comes the whole expanse;
O Nanak, (he) himself is the One who sets (all) right. ॥8॥
251.10: (People) stay engrossed in the amusements of women; (yet) this clamour of poison (Maya) is (as fleeting as) the safflower's colour.
Nanak seeks the refuge of that (Lord), through whom the sense of I and mine is destroyed. ॥1॥
252.1: O mind, wherever you lose yourself apart from the Lord, there, in each place, bonds are laid (on you).
The Saakats practise the very ways by which there is no release anywhere.
Those devoted to ritual deeds keep on saying I, I; the burden of that (ego) is beyond bearing.
Without love for the Naam, these very deeds are vices.
Through the pleasures of sweet Maya they are bound with the rope of Jam.
Beguiled by delusion, they do not see that God stays with (them) always.
When the account is reckoned, there is no release; a wall of unbaked clay does not become clean (by washing).
O Nanak, the one to whom (God himself) gives understanding gains, through the Guru, a pure intellect. ॥9॥
252.2: The one whose bonds are broken has found the company of the Saadh.
O Nanak, those who are dyed in the love of the One: deep (and fast) is their colour. ॥1॥
252.3: Rara: dye this mind of yours (in the Lord's love);
repeat with your tongue the Name of the Lord, Har Har; keep up its repetition.
(Then) in the Lord's court no one will call out to you with contempt;
(rather, all) will greet you with honour: come, be seated.
You will gain a dwelling in that mansion (of the Lord);
(there) is no birth and death, nor any perishing.
The one on whose forehead (the Lord's) grace is written from the very beginning:
O Nanak, the wealth of the Lord (the Name) is in that one's home. ॥10॥
252.4: Greed, falsehood, vice and attachment hold sway over the blind fools;
O Nanak, in the bonds of Maya they lie clinging to what is foul. ॥1॥
252.5: Lala: clinging to the pleasures of the senses, (people) are steeped in them;
with an intellect full of ego, they are drunk on the wine of Maya.
Caught in this Maya, they are born and die;
as (God's) Hukam is, so do (beings) act.
(Of oneself) no one is lacking and no one is complete;
no one is wise and no one a fool.
(O God,) to whatever you attach (them), to that they are attached.
O Nanak, the Master is for ever untouched (by it all). ॥11॥
252.6: God is the Beloved, Gopal, Gobind; deep, profound and unfathomable is he.
There is no other, none second (to him); O Nanak, he is the carefree Lord. ॥1॥
252.7: Lala: there is no one equal to him;
he alone is, himself; there will be no other.
Ever-existent, he has been for ever;
no one has found his end.
He fully pervades the worm and the elephant;
the all-pervading Being is known to be manifest in every place.
The one to whom the Lord has given his own sweet essence,
O Nanak, repeats (the Name of) the Lord, Har Har, through the Guru. ॥12॥
252.8: Those who have known the relish of the spirit savour the Lord's love in Sahaj;
O Nanak, blessed, blessed, blessed are those people; their coming (into the world) is approved. ॥1॥
252.9: That one's coming (into the world) alone should be counted fruitful
whose tongue utters the praise of the Lord, Har Har.
Those who come and dwell in the Saadh's company
meditate on the Naam night and day with love.
That person, coming (into the world), stays dyed in the Naam
on whom the Creator bestows kindness and mercy.
He comes but once, and does not enter the cycle of births again;
O Nanak, he is absorbed in the sight of the Lord. ॥13॥
252.10: The One by repeating whom bliss wells up in the mind and the love of another perishes,
and pain, suffering and craving are quenched: O Nanak, merge in his Name. ॥1॥
253.1: Yaya: burn away evil-mindedness and duality;
abandoning it, you will abide in peace and Sahaj.
Yaya: go and seek the refuge of the Sants,
with whose support this world-ocean is crossed.
Yaya: that one does not come into birth (again)
who takes the Name of the One and strings it into his mind.
Yaya: with the support of the Perfect Guru, (this human) life is not lost;
O Nanak, that one has found peace in whose heart is the One. ॥14॥
253.2: The Friend of this world and the next dwells within mind and body;
the Perfect Guru has taught (this); O Nanak, one should repeat (his Name) every day. ॥1॥
253.3: Night and day remember him who will be your helper at the end.
This Maya lasts but four or six days; everyone leaves it and goes.
Whose are mother, father, son and daughter?
Home, wife, anything at all: (no one) has taken it along.
Gather such (wealth) as does not perish,
(so that) you go with honour to your own home.
Those who in Kalyug have sung (the Lord's) Kirtan in the Saadh Sangat:
O Nanak, none of them has come (into birth) again. ॥15॥
253.4: (Though they be) very handsome, of noble birth, clever, eminent, learned and wealthy,
O Nanak, those with no love for the Lord are called dead. ॥1॥
253.5: Nganga: (one may) be versed in the six Shastras,
practise drawing in, holding and letting out the breath (purak, kumbhak, rechak),
be given to knowledge and meditation, and bathe at places of pilgrimage,
cook his own food (for purity), let no one touch him, and live in the wilderness;
(but if) there is no love in his mind for the Name of the Lord, Ram,
all that he has done is perishable.
Higher than him I count the chandal
in whose mind Gopal dwells, says Nanak. ॥16॥
253.6: (People) wander the four quarters and the ten directions by the line drawn by the deeds they have done;
O Nanak, pleasure and pain, liberation and the cycle of births (come) by the writ that is written. ॥1॥
253.7: Kaka: he alone is the Creator, the maker of all causes;
no one can erase the writ he has written.
Nothing has to be done (by him) a second time;
the Maker is not one who errs.
To one he himself shows the path;
another he makes to wander in the wilderness and repent.
He himself has made his own play;
O Nanak, whatever he has given, that is what (each) has received. ॥17॥
253.8: (His servants) go on eating, spending and enjoying, (yet his) storehouses are never used up.
O Nanak, countless people repeat (the Name of) the Lord, Har Har; there is no counting them. ॥1॥
253.9: Khakha: nothing is wanting with that almighty (Lord);
whatever he is to give, he keeps giving, whatever place (one) may go to.
The wealth of the Naam is their provision and their treasure; this is the devotees' capital.
In forgiveness, humility, bliss and Sahaj, they keep repeating (the Name of) the Treasure of virtues.
Those to whom (God) is merciful play and blossom in bliss;
they are ever rich and graceful: the riches of the Lord's Name are in their home.
No anguish, no pain, no penalty is theirs on whom he has cast his glance of grace.
O Nanak, those who are pleasing to God have come through in full. ॥18॥
254.1: Count and measure, and see within your own mind: people must surely depart.
Through the Guru, hope in passing things is erased; O Nanak, the Naam (alone) makes one whole. ॥1॥
254.2: Gaga: sing the virtues of Gobind; repeat (his Name) with every breath, every day.
What trust can be placed in the body? Do not delay, my friend.
Childhood, youth or old age: at none of these is there any bar (to death).
No one knows the hour when the noose of Jam will come and fall.
See: the learned, the meditative, the clever, (none) is to stay in this place.
That which all the world has left behind and gone, to that the fools cling.
By the Guru's grace, the one with (good) fortune on the forehead keeps remembering (the Lord).
O Nanak, those granted the wedded love of the Beloved: their coming (into the world) bears fruit. ॥19॥
254.3: All the Shastras and Vedas have been searched through; none of them tells of any other (than him).
In the beginning, from the start of the ages, now and in time to come, O Nanak, he alone is. ॥1॥
254.4: Ghagha: set this firmly in your mind: apart from the Lord there is no other.
There has been none, nor will there be; everywhere he alone is contained.
O mind, you will melt into (him) only when you come to (his) refuge.
In Kalyug the Naam is the essence, (and it is the true) act of atonement.
Many toil and toil (at other efforts), and repent;
without devotion to the Lord, where can they find steadiness?
That one has mixed and drunk the supremely sweet Amrit,
O Nanak, (that one) to whom the Guru has given the Lord's (Name). ॥20॥
254.5: (God) has sent (each one into the world) with all the days and breaths counted; they do not grow or shrink by even a sesame seed's worth.
Those who, in delusion and attachment, long to live (longer), O Nanak, are fools. ॥1॥
254.6: Nganga: death seizes those whom God has made Saakats;
they are born and die in countless forms of life, (for) they have not recognised the Lord within (Atam Ram).
Divine knowledge and meditation come only to those
on whom (God) himself, in his grace, has had them bestowed.
By counting and reckoning (deeds) no one is set free;
the pitcher of unbaked clay will surely break.
He alone (truly) lives who, while alive, has repeated (the Name);
O Nanak, (such ones) become manifest; they do not stay hidden. ॥21॥
254.7: I fix my mind on (the Lord's) lotus feet, and the inverted lotus (of the heart) blossoms.
O Nanak, through the counsel of the Sants, Gobind himself becomes manifest (in the heart). ॥1॥
254.8: Chacha: (when I) was joined to the Guru's lotus feet,
blessed, blessed was that day, and fortunate that union.
(Before,) I had wandered through the four quarters and the ten directions;
when (the Lord's) grace came, then I was granted the sight (of him).
My thoughts were made fair, and all duality perished;
in the Saadh Sangat the mind became pure.
He puts away all worry and beholds the One (everywhere),
O Nanak, the one whose eyes bear the collyrium of (the Guru's) wisdom. ॥22॥
254.9: Singing songs of Gobind's virtues, the heart grows cool and the mind is at ease.
Show such grace, O God; Nanak is the servant of your servants. ॥1॥
254.10: Chhachha: (O God,) we are your little servants,
carriers of water for the servants of your servants.
Chhachha: (grant that we) become the dust (of the feet) of your Sants;
(One who,) giving up cleverness and much cunning,
has set the support of the Sants firm in the mind:
even (that) puppet of dust has attained the supreme state,
O Nanak, the one whom the Sants help. ॥23॥
255.1: (People) swell with pride through force and oppression; (their) frail body (is given over) to vice.
Through the proud intellect they are caught in bonds; O Nanak, release (comes only) through the Name. ॥1॥
255.2: Jaja: one who thinks, I have become someone,
is held fast in that delusion, like a parrot on the nalini.
When one thinks, I am a devotee, a man of wisdom,
hereafter the Master will not count it worth a sesame seed.
When one thinks, I am a preacher (of holy discourse),
he goes about the earth like a pedlar.
The one who has slain Haumai in the Saadh Sangat,
O Nanak, meets Murari, the Lord. ॥24॥
255.3: Rise in the early hours and repeat the Naam; worship (the Lord) night and day.
No fretting will take hold of you; says Nanak, (your) troubles will end. ॥1॥
255.4: trade in the Name of Ram.
Fretting and fretting, the Saakat dies,
the one in whose heart is the love of another.
The stains and sins of your mind will fall away
(if) you hear (the Lord's) nectar-like praise in the company of the Sants.
Lust, anger and wickedness fall away (from that one),
O Nanak, on whom is the grace of the Lord of the world. ॥25॥
255.5: You may try in many ways, friend, (but) you will not be allowed to stay (here).
Says Nanak: if you worship the Lord, Har Har, with love for the Name, you will (truly) live. ॥1॥
255.6: Nyanya: know this firmly as certain, that these attachments perish.
How many have risen and gone (from here) I do not reckon, nor can I count them.
Whatever I see is passing away; with whom, then, should one keep company?
O mind, know it truly in this way: the colour of Maya is false.
That one alone knows it, that one is a Sant, who has been set apart from delusion.
(O God,) the one with whom you are well pleased you draw out of the blind well (of attachment).
The One in whose hands is all power, who is able to bring every cause about,
Nanak sings the praise of him who has brought about (this) union. ॥26॥
255.7: The bonds of birth and death are broken, and peace is found, by serving the Saadh,
O Nanak, (by one) from whose mind Gobind the King, the treasure of virtues, is never forgotten. ॥1॥
255.8: If you would serve, serve the One, from whom no one (goes away) empty.
(When he) dwells in mind, body, mouth and heart, whatever you wish comes to be.
Service in (the Lord's) mansion is given to the one on whom the Saadh is kind;
and one comes to dwell in the Saadh Sangat only when (the Lord) himself is merciful.
I have searched through many places; without the Name there is no peace.
The messengers of Jam turn away from those who merge into the company of the Saadh.
Again and again I am a sacrifice to the Sants;
O Nanak, (in their company) the sins of ages long past have been destroyed. ॥27॥
255.9: (O God,) no bar is put in the way at (your) door of those with whom you are well pleased.
Blessed, blessed indeed, O Nanak, are those whom God has made his own. ॥1॥
256.1: Thattha: they do not wound (anyone's) heart
who leave all else behind and cling to the One alone.
Those who have died clashing and jostling (with others) for the sake of Maya
Coolness came upon the one who dwelt in the company of the Sants;
there the nectar of the Name filled (that one's) soul with its taste.
The one who has become pleasing to his Master,
O Nanak, that one's mind has been cooled and calmed. ॥28॥
256.2: Countless times I bow and lie prostrate (before you), O mighty (Lord) of every power.
Keep Nanak from wavering, O God: give him your hand. ॥1॥
256.3: Dadda: this is not (your lasting) dwelling; come to know where the dwelling is.
Through the Guru's Shabad, learn the way to that dwelling.
For this dwelling one toils and labours,
yet not a jot of it goes along (at the end).
The ways of that dwelling are known to that one
on whom rests the glance (of grace) of the perfect Lord.
(Those who) have found the unmoving, true dwelling in the Saadh Sangat —
O Nanak, those people do not waver. ॥29॥
256.4: When Dharam Raj (and his messengers) began to tear down (the body), no one put up a barrier (before them).
O Nanak, those bound in kinship with the Saadh Sangat were saved by repeating (the Name of) the Lord. ॥1॥
256.5: Dhaddha: where do you go searching? The search is within this mind.
God dwells with you; why do you roam from forest to forest?
In the Saadh Sangat, pull down the mound of the dreadful proud intellect;
(then) you will find peace, dwell in Sahaj, and be filled with joy beholding (the Lord).
(While) the mound (of ego) stands, one is born only to die, and suffers the pains of the womb and of births;
drunk with attachment, one stays clinging (to Maya), and, crying I, I, keeps coming and going.
Crumbling, crumbling, (we) have now fallen at the refuge of the holy;
the nooses of pain have been cut, and, O Nanak, (the Lord) has merged (us into himself). ॥30॥
256.6: (Dharam Raj says:) Where the Saadhs worship Gobind and sing his Kirtan day by day, O Nanak,
(go there, and) neither I nor you will escape: do not go near it, my messengers. ॥1॥
256.7: Nanna: on the battlefield (of life), the one who conquers the self wins.
One who fights Haumai and duality and dies (to the self) becomes a glorious warrior.
One who, by the teaching of the perfect Guru, wipes out the ego and dies while yet alive,
conquers the mind and meets the Lord: his is the garb of the warrior.
He counts no one as his own; the One alone is his shelter and stay.
Night and day he keeps remembering God, the boundless Being.
He makes this mind the dust (of the feet) of all; such are the deeds he lives by.
He understands (the Lord's) Hukam and (knows) lasting peace; O Nanak, he receives what was written (for him). ॥31॥
256.8: I would offer body, mind and wealth to the one who would unite me with God.
O Nanak, (meeting him,) doubt and fear are cut away, and the watching eye of Jam is gone. ॥1॥
256.9: Tata: love him, Gobind the King, the treasure of virtues;
you will obtain the fruits your mind longs for, and your burning will leave you.
Dread of the road of Jam is gone for the one in whose mind the Name dwells.
You will reach the high state, your understanding will be lit, and you will find a place in (the Lord's) mansion.
Wealth does not go along with (anyone at the end), nor house, nor youth, nor power.
In the company of the Sants keep remembering (the Lord); this alone will serve you.
No burning grief remains at all when (the Lord) himself takes the fever away.
O Nanak, (the Lord) cherishes us; he himself is mother and father. ॥32॥
257.1: (They) have grown weary toiling in many ways, yet are not satisfied, and (their) craving has not left them.
Amassing and amassing (Maya), the Saakats have died; O Nanak, Maya did not go with them. ॥1॥
257.2: Thatha: no one stays (here) for ever; why, then, do you stretch out your feet (as if to stay)?
You practise countless frauds, tricks and deceits, striving for Maya alone.
You fill your purse, you toil, and you drop exhausted, you fool;
(yet) it is of no use to the soul at the last hour.
You will find steadiness if you worship Gobind and take the teaching of the Sants;
love the One for ever: this is the true love.
(The Lord is) the cause, the doer and the one who has all things done; every means is in the hands of the One alone.
Says Nanak: wherever you set them, (O Lord,) there they are set; the creatures are helpless. ॥33॥
257.3: (The Lord's) servants have seen the One as the giver of everything;
with every breath they keep remembering (him); O Nanak, beholding (him) is what sustains them. ॥1॥
257.4: Dada: the Giver is the One, who gives to all;
his giving never runs short; numberless are (his) brimming storehouses.
O foolish mind, why have you forgotten him?
My friend, the fault lies with no one;
God (himself) has made the bond of attachment to Maya.
Those whose pain you yourself take away, (O Lord,)
O Nanak, each of them is fulfilled, through the Guru. ॥34॥
257.5: O my soul, take the One as your sole support, and put away hope in others;
O Nanak, the Naam should be meditated on; (then) every task turns out well. ॥1॥
257.6: Dhadha: the wandering (of the mind) ends only when one's dwelling is in the company of the Sants.
(O Lord,) when you yourself show grace from the very source, then light dawns in the mind.
They whose wealth is lasting are the true merchants,
whose capital is the Lord, Har Har, and who have traded in the Name.
Steadfastness, praise and honour become the lot of the one
who has heard the Name of the Lord, Har Har, with (his) ears.
The one in whose heart (the Lord) stays absorbed, through the Guru:
O Nanak, that servant (of the Lord) has received greatness. ॥35॥
257.7: O Nanak, (those who) have repeated the Naam, the Naam alone, with love, within and without,
have been taught by the Perfect Guru; in the Saadh Sangat there is no hell (for them). ॥1॥
257.8: Nana: they do not fall into hell
in whose mind and body the Naam dwells.
Those who, through the Guru, repeat the Naam, the treasure,
do not waste away in the poison of Maya.
those to whom the Guru has given the mantra of the Naam.
They are full of the Lord's Amrit, the treasure of treasures;
there (within them), O Nanak, the unstruck instruments play. ॥36॥
258.1: The Guru, the Supreme Lord, has kept the honour (of the one) who has given up deceit, attachment and vice;
O Nanak, let us worship that One alone, who has no end and no shore on either side. ॥1॥
258.2: Pappa: (the Lord) is beyond measure; (no one) has found his limit.
The Lord King is beyond reach, the purifier of the fallen.
who meet the Saadh and repeat the Naam, the Amrit.
Deceit, treachery and attachment are erased through (your) praise
in the one whom you yourself protect, O Master of the world.
He alone is the Emperor, with the canopy over (his) head;
O Nanak, there is no other, no second (like him). ॥37॥
258.3: The nooses are cut, the wanderings are over; victory has come by conquering the mind.
O Nanak, steadiness was found from the Guru, and the rounds (of birth) are over for ever. ॥1॥
258.4: Phapha: wandering and wandering (through births), you have come;
(now) in Kalyug you have obtained the (human) body, so rarely given.
Such a chance will not come to hand again.
Repeat the Naam, and the nooses (of Maya) will be cut;
there will be no coming and going again and again.
Repeat the remembrance of that One, the One alone.
Be merciful, O God, the Creator,
and unite helpless Nanak with yourself. ॥38॥
258.5: Hear (my) prayer, O Supreme Lord, Gopal, merciful to the meek:
for Nanak, the dust of the Saadhs' feet is comfort, wealth, many pleasures and delights. ॥1॥
258.6: Babba: those who know Brahm (God) are the (true) Brahmins;
(true) Vaishnavs are they who, through the Guru, (keep) the dharma of purity.
The hero is one who wipes out the evil in himself;
(Man) is bound by his own bond of I, I (Haumai),
(yet) the blind one puts the blame on others.
All talk and cleverness come to nothing;
only the one to whom you, (O Lord,) give understanding knows (this), says Nanak. ॥39॥
258.7: In your mind worship the Lord, the breaker of fear, the destroyer of sin and sorrow.
Those in whose heart (the Lord) has come to dwell through the company of the Sants, O Nanak, do not wander in delusion. ॥1॥
258.8: this whole world is a dream.
Heavenly beings, men, goddesses and gods have wandered in delusion;
Siddhas, seekers and (the likes of) Brahma have wandered in delusion.
Wandering on and on in delusion, people have been led astray.
This Maya is hard to cross, and most perilous.
Those who, through the Guru, have wiped out delusion, fear and attachment,
O Nanak, have found the supreme peace. ॥40॥
258.9: Maya wavers in many ways, (yet) the mind clings to it;
(O Lord,) the one you keep from begging (for Maya) is in love with the Name alone, says Nanak. ॥1॥
258.10: Mamma: the one who begs is ignorant;
the all-knowing Giver goes on giving.
What he gave, he gave once (for all).
O foolish mind, why do you keep crying out?
Whenever you ask, you ask for things other (than the Name),
through which no one has ever fared well.
If you must ask, then ask for the One alone,
by whom, says Nanak, you will cross to the far shore. ॥41॥
259.1: Their understanding is complete, and they are foremost, whose minds hold the teaching of the Perfect Guru;
those who have come to know their God, O Nanak, are blessed with good fortune. ॥1॥
259.2: Mamma: one who has recognised (the Lord's) secret
is content (in mind) as soon as he meets the Saadh Sangat.
Pain and pleasure are weighed alike in his mind;
he is spared from being born into hell or heaven.
(He sees that) the same (Lord) is with (all), and the same (Lord) is untouched (by all);
the Being fills each and every heart, (and he) sees (this) distinctly.
In that relish (of the Lord) he alone has found peace;
O Nanak, Maya does not stain him. ॥42॥
259.3: Listen, friends, companions, dear ones: without the Lord there is no release.
O Nanak, their bonds are cut who fall at the Guru's feet. ॥1॥
259.4: Yaya: (people) make efforts of many kinds,
(but) how far can success go without the one Name?
The effort by which release comes
is the company of the Saadh.
Everyone holds (in mind) this longing to be saved,
(but) without meditating on him there is no saving.
He alone is the boat that carries across, mighty to save;
save (us), the virtueless, O Lord of men.
Those to whom (the Lord) himself has given this understanding in mind, word and deed,
O Nanak, their understanding has come to light. ॥43॥
259.5: Hold no grudge against anyone; reflect on your own self.
Live humbly in the world; O Nanak, by (the Lord's) gracious glance you will cross over. ॥1॥
259.6: Rara: (become the dust of the Lord,) whose dust all (creation) becomes;
give up pride, and the arrears (in the account of your deeds) will be cleared.
O brother, you will win through on the battlefield (of the world) and in the Lord's court
when, through the Guru, you are lovingly attuned to the Name of Ram.
Little by little the vices fall away,
countless as they are, through the Shabad of the Perfect Guru.
Dyed in love, they are intoxicated with the relish of the Name,
those on whom, O Nanak, the Lord, the Guru, has bestowed this gift. ॥44॥
259.7: Greed, falsehood, vice and disease dwell in this body;
one who has drunk the Amrit of the Lord, Har Har, through the Guru, O Nanak, dwells in peace. ॥1॥
259.8: Lala: anyone to whom I apply the medicine (of the Name),
his pains and sorrows vanish in an instant.
One who holds the medicine of the Name dear in the heart
is not touched by disease even in a dream.
The Lord's medicine is in all hearts, O brother,
(but) without the Perfect Guru, the way (to take it) is not found.
The Perfect Guru has set the regimen (to keep with it);
then, O Nanak, pain does not come again. ॥45॥
259.9: Vasudev (the Lord) fills every place; in no place is he wanting.
He is with (all), within and without; O Nanak, how can anything be hidden (from him)? ॥1॥
259.10: Vava: bear enmity toward no one;
Brahm (God) dwells within each and every heart.
(but) only a rare one, by the Guru's grace, has reached (him).
Enmity and opposition are gone from the minds of those
who, through the Guru, listen to the Lord's Kirtan.
Above all castes and marks stands the one
who, O Nanak, utters Har Har through the Guru. ॥46॥
260.1: Crying I, I, the foolish, ignorant Saakats have passed (their lives);
writhing, they died like the thirsty; O Nanak, (it was) by the deeds they had earned. ॥1॥
260.2: Rarra: the rankling strife (of the mind) ends in the company of the Saadh;
worship of the Name is the essence of (all) rites and religious duties.
The one in whose heart the Beautiful (Lord) has come to dwell:
his strife is ended and destroyed.
The foolish Saakats keep up strife,
in whose hearts are the vices of the proud intellect.
Rarra: the one who through the Guru has wiped out the strife
is given understanding in an instant, O Nanak. ॥47॥
260.3: O mind, take hold of the Saadh's support; give up argument and cleverness.
O Nanak, the one in whose mind the Guru's teaching dwells has good fortune (written) on the forehead. ॥1॥
260.4: Sassa: (O God,) defeated, we have now fallen at (your) refuge.
The Shastras, the Smritis and the Vedas cry it aloud,
and searching and searching, (we too) have searched and reflected:
without worship of the Lord there is no release.
With every breath we go astray;
you are all-powerful, beyond count, boundless.
O Merciful One, keep (the honour) of the one who has fallen at your refuge.
Says Nanak, we are your children, O Gopal. ॥48॥
260.5: When self-conceit was gone, then peace came, and mind and body were made whole.
O Nanak, (then) the One worthy of praise came into sight. ॥1॥
260.6: Khakha: I praise him with all my heart,
who in an instant fills the empty to the brim.
When the mortal becomes truly humble,
(he) meditates night and day on God, who is free of all desire.
If it pleases the Master, he gives that one peace.
Such is the Supreme Lord, beyond all count:
(he) forgives countless sins in an instant.
O Nanak, the Master is merciful for ever. ॥49॥
260.7: I tell you the truth, listen, O my mind: fall at the refuge of the Lord King.
O Nanak, when (one) gives up all argument and cleverness, (the Lord) takes (that one) into himself. ॥1॥
260.8: Sassa: give up cleverness, you ignorant one;
God is not won over by cunning or by commanding.
You may practise cleverness in a thousand ways,
(yet) not one of them goes with you.
Repeat him, him alone, day and night;
O soul, (he alone) goes with you as your companion.
The one whom (God) himself sets to serve the Saadh,
O Nanak, no suffering touches him. ॥50॥
260.9: Speak Har, Har with the mouth; (when the Lord) dwells in the mind, peace comes.
O Nanak, he pervades all; he is in every place and in the spaces between. ॥1॥
260.10: I look, and see the Lord filling every heart of all.
Ever and for ever (the Lord) has been the destroyer of suffering: (this is) the Guru's wisdom.
When Haumai is shed, bliss comes to that one; where there is no Haumai, there (God) himself is.
Through the power of the company of the Sants, the sufferings of birth and death are destroyed.
The one who lovingly holds firm (in the heart) the Name of the Merciful (Lord),
in the company of the Sants, (God) becomes kind (to him).
No one has done anything apart from him;
O Nanak, all has come from God. ॥51॥
261.1: If (our deeds) are reckoned, there is no release anywhere; moment by moment we go astray.
O Forgiver, forgive (us), and carry Nanak across. ॥1॥
261.2: (The mortal) is untrue to his salt, a sinner, a stranger (to God), of little understanding;
he does not know the One, the very essence, who gave him soul, body and comforts.
For the gain of Maya he goes searching in the ten directions,
(but) not for an instant does he keep in mind God, the bountiful Giver.
Greed, falsehood, vice and attachment: this is the wealth (he holds) in his mind.
With lechers, thieves and great slanderers his (life) goes by.
(O God,) if it pleases you, you forgive the false together with the true.
O Nanak, if it pleases the Supreme Lord, stones float on water. ॥52॥
261.3: Eating, drinking, playing and laughing, (we) have wandered through many births.
Lift (us) out of the world-ocean, God; Nanak leans on you (alone). ॥1॥
261.4: Playing and playing, (the soul) has come through many births, suffering pain.
Meeting the Saadh, merging in the True Guru's word, (its) troubles are ended.
(It) took up forgiveness, gathered truth, and ate the Amrit of the Naam;
the Master's great grace came, (and it found) bliss, peace and rest.
(It) carried its trading through, made great profit, and came home with honour;
the Guru gave (it) true comfort, and the Lord came and met (it).
(The Lord) himself has done (all), and he himself does it; he himself is ahead and behind.
O Nanak, let us praise him alone, who pervades every heart. ॥53॥
261.5: O God, treasure of mercy, merciful One, (we) have come to (your) refuge.
O Nanak, (when) the One, the imperishable Lord, dwells in the mind, (one) is filled with joy. ॥1॥
261.6: God has set the three worlds within letters;
with letters, written again and again, the Vedas were pondered.
In letters are the Shastras, the Smritis and the Puranas;
in letters, sacred sound, speech and exposition.
In letters (are told) fear and doubt and the way of release (from them);
in letters, rites, deeds, purity and dharma.
All that is seen is within letters;
(but) O Nanak, the Supreme Lord is untouched (by them). ॥54॥
261.7: The pen is in the hand of the Inaccessible; (he) writes (the destiny) on (every) forehead.
He of incomparable beauty is entwined with all.
(O God,) your praise cannot be told by the mouth.
Beholding your sight, Nanak is enraptured, and is a sacrifice (to you). ॥1॥
261.8: O Unshakeable One, O Supreme Lord, Imperishable, Destroyer of sins,
O Perfect One, O All-pervading, Destroyer of suffering, Treasure of virtues,
O Companion, O Formless, O Nirgun, Support of all,
O Gobind, O Treasury of virtues, in whom discernment ever abides,
O Lord beyond the beyond, Har Hare: you are, and you will be.
O ever-present with the Sants, Support of those who have none:
O Master, I am your lowly servant; I am without virtue, I have no virtue at all.
Grant Nanak the gift of the Naam, that I may keep it strung in my heart. ॥55॥
262.1: The Gurdev is mother, the Gurdev is father, the Gurdev is the Master, the Supreme God.
The Gurdev is the friend who destroys ignorance; the Gurdev is kinsman and brother born of the same womb.
The Gurdev is the Giver who teaches the Lord's Name; the Gurdev's mantra is one whose power nothing can stop.
The Gurdev is the embodiment of peace, truth and wisdom; the Gurdev is a paaras whose touch surpasses even the paaras.
The Gurdev is the tirath, the pool of Amrit; to bathe in the Guru's wisdom is beyond all else.
The Gurdev is the Creator, the remover of all sins; the Gurdev makes the fallen pure.
The Gurdev is from the beginning, from the start of the ages, in every age; repeating the Gurdev's mantra, the Lord's Name, one is saved.
O God, in your grace join (us) to the Gurdev's company, holding fast to which we foolish sinners may swim across.
The Gurdev is the True Guru, the Supreme Lord, the Supreme God; O Nanak, salutation to the Gurdev, the Lord.
This salok is to be read at the beginning and at the end (of the Bavan Akhri).
a01.title: Raag Gauri: Sukhmani, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
a01.salok: Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Salutation to the Primal Guru, who was before all.
Salutation to the Guru who has been since the ages began.
Salutation to the revered, divine Guru. ॥1॥
a01.p1: Let me practise Simran (meditative remembrance of God) and, remembering him again and again, find peace,
and rid my body of strife and anguish.
Let me remember the One, the Sustainer of the universe,
whose Naam (the Name, God's presence remembered) is repeated by multitudes beyond counting.
The Vedas, the Puranas and the Simritis
have held the one word of the Lord's Name to be the purest of words.
The one in whose heart God places even a particle of it
Some long for one thing only, the sight of you.
Says Nanak, save me along with them. ॥1॥
a01.rahao: Sukhmani, the jewel of peace, is God's Name, the nectar of peace.
It dwells in the minds of the devotees.
a01.p2: Through Simran of God, one does not come to lodge in the womb again.
Through Simran of God, sorrow and the messenger of Death flee.
Through Simran of God, death keeps away.
Through Simran of God, the enemy turns back.
While remembering God, no obstacle at all can touch one.
Through Simran of God, one stays awake night and day.
Through Simran of God, fear takes no hold.
Through Simran of God, pain does not torment.
Simran of God is found in the Saadh's company (the company of the holy one).
All treasures, O Nanak, are found in the Lord's love. ॥2॥
a01.p3: Through Simran of God come riches, spiritual powers and the nine treasures.
Through Simran of God come knowledge, meditation and insight into the essence.
Through Simran of God, one has performed chanting, austerity and worship.
Through Simran of God, duality is destroyed.
Through Simran of God, one has bathed at the places of pilgrimage.
Through Simran of God, one is honoured in the Lord's court.
Through Simran of God, whatever happens is good.
Through Simran of God, life bears its fruit in full.
They alone practise Simran whom God himself moves to it.
Says Nanak, I fall at their feet. ॥3॥
a01.p4: Simran of God is the highest of all.
Through Simran of God, multitudes have been saved.
Through Simran of God, craving is quenched.
Through Simran of God, everything becomes clear.
Through Simran of God, there is no terror of the messenger of Death.
Through Simran of God, hopes are fulfilled.
Through Simran of God, the mind's filth is washed away.
The ambrosial Naam settles in the heart.
God dwells on the tongue of the Saadh.
Nanak is the slave of the slaves of God's servants. ॥4॥
a01.p5: All who remember God are rich.
All who remember God are honoured.
All who remember God are accepted by him.
All who remember God are the foremost of people.
All who remember God depend on no one.
All who remember God are kings over all.
All who remember God dwell in peace.
All who remember God become forever imperishable.
They alone take to Simran to whom God himself is merciful.
Nanak begs for the dust of the feet of such a servant. ॥5॥
a01.p6: All who remember God do good to others.
To all who remember God I am a sacrifice, always.
All who remember God have radiant faces.
All who remember God pass their lives in peace.
All who remember God have conquered the self.
All who remember God live a spotless life.
All who remember God have joys in abundance.
All who remember God live close to the Lord.
By the grace of the Sant (saint), they stay awake night and day.
O Nanak, Simran comes through perfect good fortune. ॥6॥
a01.p7: Through Simran of God, one's tasks are accomplished.
Through Simran of God, one never grieves.
Through Simran of God, one utters the praises of the Lord.
Through Simran of God, one is absorbed in natural poise.
Through Simran of God, one gains a seat that never wavers.
Through Simran of God, the lotus of the heart blossoms.
Through Simran of God, the unstruck divine melody rings within.
The peace of Simran of God has no end and no limit.
They alone practise Simran on whom God has mercy.
Nanak has taken refuge with those servants. ॥7॥
a01.p8: By practising Simran of the Lord, the devotees became renowned.
Absorbed in Simran of the Lord, the sages brought forth the Vedas.
Through Simran of the Lord, people became Siddhas, celibates and givers.
Through Simran of the Lord, the lowly became known in all four directions.
Through Simran of the Lord, the whole earth is upheld.
Remember, remember the Lord, the Maker of all causes.
Through Simran of the Lord, all visible creation was made.
In Simran of the Lord, the Formless One himself is present.
When God, in his grace, has himself given someone understanding,
O Nanak, that Gurmukh (one who follows the Guru) has received Simran of the Lord. ॥8॥
a02.salok: O destroyer of the pain and sorrow of the poor, O Master present in every heart, Master of those who have none:
O God, in the company of Nanak (the Guru) I have come to your refuge. ॥1॥
a02.p1: Where there is no mother, father, son, friend or brother,
there, O mind, the Naam (the Name, God's presence remembered) is with you to help you.
Where the most dreadful messenger of Death would crush you,
there the Naam alone goes along with you.
Where the hardship is very heavy,
the Lord's Name rescues you in an instant.
Performing countless rites of atonement, one does not cross over.
The Lord's Name drives away millions of sins.
O my mind, repeat the Naam as a Gurmukh (one who follows the Guru).
Says Nanak, you will find joys in abundance. ॥1॥
a02.p2: Even a king of the whole world is unhappy.
Repeating the Lord's Name, he becomes happy.
Gathering hundreds of thousands and millions, one sets no bound to craving.
Repeating the Lord's Name, one is set free.
The countless pleasures of Maya (the world's illusion and lure) do not quench the thirst.
Repeating the Lord's Name, one is satisfied.
On the road where the soul travels alone,
there, with the Lord's Name beside it, it goes at ease.
O mind, meditate always on such a Naam.
O Nanak, as a Gurmukh one attains the supreme state. ॥2॥
a02.p3: Where one is not set free even by millions of helping arms,
there, repeating the Naam, people get across.
Where countless misfortunes come to destroy one,
the Lord's Name rescues at once.
Through countless species one is born, dies and is born again.
Repeating the Naam, one finds rest.
Soiled by Haumai (ego), one never washes the filth away.
The Lord's Name wipes out millions of sins.
O mind, repeat such a Naam with love.
O Nanak, it is found in the Saadh's company (the company of the holy one). ॥3॥
a02.p4: On the road whose miles cannot be counted,
the Lord's Name is your provision there.
On the journey that is pitch dark,
the Lord's Name goes with you as light.
On the path where no one knows you,
the Lord's Name is there with you as one who knows you.
Where there is fearful heat and a fierce sun,
there the Lord's Name gives you shade.
Where thirst, O mind, torments you,
there, O Nanak, the Lord's nectar, Har Har, rains down. ॥4॥
a02.p5: The Naam is what the devotees use every day.
It rests in the minds of the Sants (saints).
The Lord's Name is the shelter of his servant.
Through the Lord's Name millions of people have been saved.
The Sants sing the Lord's praise day and night.
The Saadhs make the Lord's Name, Har Har, their medicine.
The Lord's servant has the Lord's Name as his treasure.
The Supreme Lord has given it to his servant as a gift.
Their minds and bodies are dyed in the love of the One.
O Nanak, the servant's way is one of discernment. ॥5॥
a02.p6: To the servant, the Lord's Name is the way to liberation.
In the Lord's Name the servant finds contentment and his food.
The Lord's Name is the servant's beauty and delight.
Repeating the Lord's Name, he never meets an obstacle.
The Lord's Name is the servant's greatness.
Through the Lord's Name the servant has gained glory.
To the servant the Lord's Name is both enjoyment and Yoga.
Repeating the Lord's Name, he suffers no separation at all.
The servant is steeped in the service of the Lord's Name.
O Nanak, he worships the divine Lord, Har Har. ॥6॥
a02.p7: Har Har is the servant's wealth and treasure.
God himself has given the servant the wealth of the Lord.
Har Har is the servant's mighty shelter.
Through the Lord's glory, the servant knows no other.
Like warp and weft, through and through, his servants are steeped in the Lord's sweet essence.
In the deep stillness of Samadhi they are intoxicated with the taste of the Naam.
At all hours the servant repeats Har Har.
The Lord's devotee is known to all; he does not stay hidden.
Devotion to the Lord liberates many.
O Nanak, in the company of his servants so many have crossed over. ॥7॥
a02.p8: This Name of the Lord is the Parijat (the wish-fulfilling tree).
Singing the praises of Har Har is the Kamadhenu (the wish-fulfilling cow).
The discourse of the Lord is the most sublime of all.
When the Naam is heard, pain and sorrow fall away.
In the hearts of the Sants dwells the glory of the Naam.
Through the glory of the Sants all sin flees.
The company of the Sants is gained by great good fortune.
In the service of the Sants one meditates on the Naam.
Nothing else is equal to the Naam.
O Nanak, only a rare person, as a Gurmukh, obtains the Naam. ॥8॥
a03.salok: I have looked into many Shastras and many Simritis, searching through them all.
None of them equals Har, Haray: O Nanak, the Naam (the Name, God's presence remembered) is beyond price. ॥1॥
a03.p1: Chanting, austerities, all knowledge and meditation;
expounding the six Shastras and the Simritis;
the practice of Yoga, religious deeds and rites;
renouncing everything and wandering in the forest;
making many efforts of countless kinds;
good works, charity, and many jewels offered into the sacred fire;
having the body cut into tiny pieces and offering them into the fire;
keeping fasts and vows of many kinds:
none of these equals contemplation of the Lord's Name,
if, O Nanak, one repeats the Naam even once as a Gurmukh (one who follows the Guru). ॥1॥
a03.p2: One may roam the nine regions of the earth and live a long life;
become a great renunciant and a master of austerity;
offer one's life into the fire;
give gold, horses, the finest steeds and land in charity;
practise Neoli (the yogic cleansing of the bowels) and many postures;
follow the Jain way with its strict self-denial and disciplines;
have the body cut up bit by bit:
even then the filth of Haumai (ego) does not go.
O Nanak, repeating the Naam as Gurmukhs, people attain liberation. ॥2॥
a03.p3: One may give up the body at a place of pilgrimage with desire still in the mind,
yet pride and arrogance do not leave the mind.
One may perform cleansing rites day and night,
yet the mind's filth does not leave the body.
One may put this body through many disciplines,
yet the poison of Maya (the world's illusion and lure) never leaves the mind.
One may wash this perishable body with water again and again.
How can a wall of unbaked clay become clean?
O mind, the glory of the Lord's Name is high.
O Nanak, through the Naam a great multitude of the fallen have been saved. ॥3॥
a03.p4: For all one's cleverness, the fear of the messenger of Death still grips one.
For all one's countless efforts, craving is not satisfied.
