One whom God protects has no pain;
repeating the Naam, the mind finds peace.
Anxiety goes and pride is erased;
no one can equal that servant.
The valiant Guru stands over his head.
O Nanak, his tasks are all fulfilled. ॥7॥
a22.p8: Perfect is the wisdom of him whose glance is nectar;
at the sight of him the world is saved.
fruitful is the sight of the Lord, and beautiful his form.
Blessed is his service, and his servant is accepted;
he is the knower of hearts, the Supreme Being.
One in whose mind he dwells is filled with joy;
death does not come near him.
They have become immortal and attained the immortal state,
O Nanak, who meditated on the Lord in the Saadh Sangat. ॥8॥
a23.salok: The Guru has given the salve of divine knowledge for the eyes, and ignorance and its darkness are gone.
When by the Lord's grace one meets the Sant (saint), O Nanak, the mind is lit up. ॥1॥
a23.p1: In the company of the Sants I have seen God within;
God's Name tastes sweet to me.
All things are within the heart of the One,
though they appear in many colours and kinds.
God's Name is the nectar, the nine treasures;
its resting place is within the body.
There is the trance of the void, and there the unstruck melody sounds, the divine music that no instrument makes;
its wonder and amazement cannot be told.
He alone has seen it to whom God himself has shown it.
O Nanak, that servant gains understanding. ॥1॥
a23.p2: The Infinite One is within, and he is without;
In the earth, the sky and the regions below,
in all the worlds, he is the perfect sustainer.
In forest, grass and mountain is the Supreme Lord;
as his command is, so is every deed.
He is in air, water and fire;
he fills the four corners and the ten directions.
There is no place apart from him.
By the Guru's grace, says Nanak, find peace. ॥2॥
a23.p3: See him in Vedas, Puranas and Simritis;
the One is in moon, sun and stars.
Everyone speaks the speech of God;
he himself is steady and never wavers.
With all his powers he plays his play;
he cannot be bought at any price, and his virtues are priceless.
He whose light is in every light,
that Master upholds all, woven through like warp and weft.
By the Guru's grace doubt comes to an end.
O Nanak, in them this faith becomes firm. ॥3॥
a23.p4: To the Sants all they behold is God;
in the hearts of the Sants is all righteousness.
The Sants hear words of good;
they are merged in the Lord who pervades all.
Such is the conduct of one who has known him:
all that the Saadh (holy one) says is true.
Whatever happens, he accepts it gladly;
he knows God as the one who does and causes all to be done.
For him God dwells within, and outside too it is he alone.
O Nanak, at the sight of him all are enchanted. ॥4॥
a23.p5: He is true himself, and true is everything he has made;
from that God came the whole creation.
When it pleases him, he spreads out the creation;
when it pleases him, he is Ekankar (the One Creator) alone again.
His many powers cannot be grasped;
whom he pleases, he unites with himself.
Who can be called near, and who far?
He himself is all, filling everything.
One whom he himself makes aware of his presence within,
O Nanak, to that servant he himself gives understanding. ॥5॥
a23.p6: He himself is at work in all beings;
through all eyes he himself is the one who sees.
he himself hears his own praise.
The One has made coming and going a play;
he has made Maya (the world's illusion and lure) obey his command.
whatever there is to say, he says it himself.
By his command one comes, by his command one goes.
O Nanak, when it pleases him, he takes them back into himself. ॥6॥
a23.p7: Whatever comes from him is not bad;
tell me, apart from him, has anyone done anything?
He himself is good, and his works are excellent beyond measure;
he alone knows his own heart.
He himself is the Truth, and all he upholds is true;
woven through and through, he is absorbed in his own creation.
No one can tell his state or his extent;
only if there were another like him could that one understand.
All that he does is to be accepted.
By the Guru's grace, says Nanak, know this. ॥7॥
a23.p8: One who knows this has peace for ever;
that God himself unites him with himself.
He is wealthy, of noble family and honoured;
liberated while living is the one in whose heart the Lord dwells.
Blessed, blessed, blessed is that servant's coming,
by whose grace the whole world is carried across.
This is the purpose of such a servant's coming:
that in his company the Name comes to mind.
He himself is free, and he sets the world free.
O Nanak, salutations for ever to that servant. ॥8॥
a24.salok: I have worshipped the perfect God, whose Name too is perfect.
Says Nanak, I have found the Perfect One; sing the praises of the Perfect One. ॥1॥
a24.p1: Listen to the perfect Guru's teaching,
and behold the Supreme Lord near you.
Remember Gobind (the Lord of the universe) with every breath;
the worry in your mind will lift.
Let go of the waves of fleeting hope;
ask, my mind, for the dust of the feet of the Sants (saints).
Set aside self-conceit and make your prayer;
cross the ocean of fire in the Saadh Sangat (the company of the holy).
Fill your storehouses with the Lord's wealth.
O Nanak, salutations to the perfect Guru. ॥1॥
a24.p2: For well-being, happiness, poise and bliss,
worship the Lord of supreme bliss in the Saadh Sangat.
Ward off hell and save your soul;
drink the nectar of Gobind's praises.
In your heart dwell on the one all-pervading Lord,
whose form is one and whose colours are many.
He is Gopal (the sustainer of the world), Damodar (a name of the Lord), merciful to the meek,
Remember, remember the Naam (the Name, God's presence remembered), again and again.
O Nanak, this alone sustains the soul. ॥2॥
a24.p3: The words of the Saadh (holy one) are verses of the highest praise;
they are priceless rubies and gems.
Hearing them and living by them, one is saved;
such a one crosses over and carries others across.
Fruitful is the life, and fruitful the company,
of one whose mind is dyed in the Lord's love.
For him the unstruck Word of victory resounds;
hearing it again and again he rejoices, and God thunders forth within him.
Gopal shines forth on the foreheads of the great souls.
O Nanak, in their company people are saved. ॥3॥
a24.p4: Hearing that he is able to give refuge, we have come to his refuge;
in his grace God has united us with himself.
Enmity has vanished, and we have become the dust of all;
in the Saadh Sangat we receive the Naam, which is nectar.
The divine Guru is well pleased,
and his servant's service is fulfilled.
We are kept free of household entanglements and vice,
hearing the Lord's Name and repeating it with the tongue.
In his kindness God has shown mercy.
Says Nanak, our cargo has come safely through. ॥4॥
a24.p5: with a mind alert and fixed on him alone.
The Sukhmani, the jewel of peace, is poise, Gobind's praises and the Naam;
one in whose mind it dwells becomes a treasure-house.
he becomes the foremost of men, renowned in all the world.
He reaches the highest place of all,
and he comes and goes no more.
that servant alone departs having earned the wealth of the Lord:
O Nanak, the one to whom it is granted. ॥5॥
a24.p6: Well-being, peace, prosperity and the nine treasures;
wisdom, knowledge and every spiritual power;
learning, austerity, yoga and meditation on God;
the highest knowledge and the most purifying bath;
the four great blessings and the blossoming of the heart-lotus;
living amid all and yet detached from all;
beauty, insight and knowledge of the essence of reality;
looking on all alike and seeing the One alone:
these fruits come to that servant who utters with his mouth
and hears with his mind, O Nanak, the Guru's word and the Naam. ॥6॥
a24.p7: Whoever repeats this treasure in the mind,
he is liberated, in every age.
This Bani, the Guru's word, holds the praises of Gobind and the melody of the Naam,
of which the Simritis, Shastras and Vedas speak.
The Lord's Name alone is the essence of all creeds;
it rests in the minds of Gobind's devotees.
In the Saadh Sangat millions of sins are erased;
the Sant's grace frees one from the messenger of Death.
Those on whose foreheads God has written his grace,
O Nanak, they come to the refuge of the Saadh. ॥7॥
a24.p8: One in whose mind it dwells, who hears it lovingly:
into that servant's mind the Lord God comes.
His pain of birth and death is taken away;
this body, so hard to obtain, is redeemed at once.
Spotless is his glory, and his speech is nectar;
the one Name fills his mind.
Pain, sickness, fear and doubt are gone;
he is called a Saadh, and his deeds are spotless.
It is for these virtues, O Nanak, that its name is Sukhmani, the jewel of peace. ॥8॥
296.1: Thiti: Raag Gauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
The Master, the Creator, fills the water, the land and the sky;
O Nanak, the One Creator (Ekankar) has spread out in many forms. ॥1॥
296.2: Ekam: I meditate on God, the One Creator, and bow (to him);
I (sing) the virtues of Gobind, Gopal, God, and fall at the refuge of the Lord King.
Hope in him, from whom all things come, (brings) salvation and peace.
I have wandered the four corners and the ten directions: without him there is no other.
I have heard the Vedas, the Puranas and the Smritis, and I reflect in many ways:
the Formless (alone) is the saviour of the fallen, the remover of fear, the ocean of peace.
He is the Giver, the Enjoyer, the Bestower; without him there is no other place.
O Nanak, singing the Lord's virtues, you obtain whatever you wish.
Let us sing the praise of Gobind, the Lord, every day;
let us join the Saadh Sangat and worship (him), my friend.
296.3: I bow (to him) many times, and fall at the refuge of the Lord King.
O Nanak, in the Saadh Sangat doubt is cut away, as the love of another is erased. ॥2॥
296.4: Dutiya: drive out evil-mindedness, and serve the Guru every day.
The jewel of Ram (his Name) will dwell in your mind and body, if you give up lust, anger and greed, my friend.
Death is ended, (true) life is found, and all troubles perish.
Give up self-conceit, worship Gobind, (and) love and devotion enter (within).
Profit is gained, loss is taken away, (and one is) honoured in the Lord's court.
Whoever gathers the wealth of Ram's Name is a true banker, fortunate indeed.
Standing and sitting, worship the Lord, and love the Saadh.
O Nanak, evil-mindedness has left (those) in whose mind the Supreme Lord has come to dwell. ॥2॥
297.1: The three (qualities of Maya) hold the world in their grip; rare is the one who reaches the fourth state (turiya).
O Nanak, the Sants in whose minds he has come to dwell have become pure. ॥3॥
297.2: Tritiya: under the three qualities (beings reap) the fruits of vice: now high, now low.
(They) wander a great deal through hell and heaven, (and) death ever strikes them down.
Joy, grief and dread: (such is) the world; (life) passes in crying I, I.
They do not know the One who made them, and think up countless schemes.
Through (the world's) pleasures come ills of mind, ills of body and troubles; the fever never breaks.
(The mortal) does not grasp the glory of the Supreme Lord, the perfect Master.
Very many are drowning in attachment and doubt; (their) dwelling is in the great hell.
Have mercy, God, and save (me); Nanak's hope is in you. ॥3॥
297.3: Clever, wise and skilful is the one who has given up pride.
The four great gifts (padaarath) and the eight siddhis (are) the Lord's Name: O Nanak, repeat the Lord's Name. ॥4॥
297.4: Chaturthi: I have listened to all four Vedas and sifted out the essence of their thought:
to repeat the Name of Ram is the best, the treasure of all well-being and salvation.
(The Name) wards off hell and takes away pain, (and through it) countless troubles break away.
The one within whom the Lord's Kirtan comes to dwell is done with death and freed from Jam.
Those dyed in the love of the Formless lose their fear, and the Amrit (of the Name) permeates them within.
With the Name for support, sorrow, want and impurity are destroyed.
Gods, men and silent sages go searching for Gopal, the ocean of peace;
O Nanak, through the dust of the Saadh's feet (he is found), the mind becomes pure and the face bright. ॥4॥
297.5: The five vices dwell in the minds (of those) absorbed in Maya.
O Nanak, in the Saadh Sangat, (dyed) in God's love, (one) becomes pure. ॥5॥
297.6: Panchami: they alone are the Panch (the chosen), they the foremost, who have known (this) spread of the world (for what it is):
(it is like) the scent of flowers; for all its many colours, it is all a passing deceit.
(But the world) does not perceive (this), does not understand, and gives it no thought at all;
pierced through by tastes, attachment and pleasures, the world is sunk in ignorance.
(Mortals) wander through birth and death and many wombs, and have done countless deeds,
(but) have not remembered the Creator, nor weighed (right and wrong) with discernment in the mind.
(Those whose) love and devotion are with the Lord are not stained by Maya in the least;
O Nanak, rare are they to be found who are not caught up in the world's show. ॥5॥
297.7: The six Shastras proclaim aloud: (God) has no end, no near or far shore.
O Nanak, singing (his) virtues at God's door, the devotees are adorned. ॥6॥
297.8: Khastami: the six Shastras tell, and many Smritis expound,
that the Supreme Lord is the most exalted and the highest; not even Shesh Nag knows the end of his virtues.
Narad, the silent sages, Suk and Vyas sing the praise of Gobind;
the devotees, steeped in the relish (of the Name) and pierced through by the Lord, remain absorbed in him.
Their attachment, pride and doubt have perished, for they have found the refuge of the Merciful;
(his) lotus feet dwell in (their) mind and body, and beholding (him) they are in bliss.
Profit is gained, loss is taken away, by fixing (one's) attention (on him) in the Saadh Sangat.
O Nanak, meditate on the Naam, and earn the treasure of the Lord, the store of virtues. ॥6॥
298.1: The Sants, in their gatherings, tell the Lord's praise, and with love speak of the True One.
O Nanak, the mind is brought to contentment by fixing (one's) attention on the One. ॥7॥
298.2: Saptami: gather the wealth of the Name, whose stores are never used up.
(It) is found in the company of the Sants; (he) has no end, no near or far shore.
Give up self-conceit, worship Gobind, (and) fall at the refuge of the Lord King.
(Such a one) is rid of pain, crosses the world-ocean, and obtains the fruit the mind longs for.
Whoever repeats (the Name of) the Lord in the mind at all hours: fruitful is (that) life, (and it is) accepted.
Know the Creator to be ever with (you), within and without.
He alone is a friend, he a companion and comrade, who gives the counsel (to remember) the Lord.
Nanak is a sacrifice to the one who repeats the Name of the Lord, Har Har. ॥7॥
298.3: If (his) virtues are sung at all hours, and all other entanglements given up,
O Nanak, (then) God is merciful, and Jam's servant cannot so much as cast his eye (on that one). ॥8॥
298.4: Astami: the eight siddhis, the nine treasures,
all good things, a perfect understanding,
the opening of the (heart's) lotus, bliss for ever,
a pure way of life, a mantra whose power nothing can stop,
every righteous duty, the purifying bath,
(and) the highest, most excellent wisdom of all:
(all lie in) worshipping the Lord, Har Har, in the perfect Guru's company.
O Nanak, repeating the Name in the Lord's love, one swims across. ॥8॥
298.5: (One who) has not remembered Narayan is lured away by the tastes of vice.
O Nanak, when the Name is forgotten, there are births (again and again) in hell and heaven. ॥9॥
298.6: Naumi: all nine openings (of the body) are unclean (in those)
who do not repeat the Lord's Name, and act against the right way.
They enjoy other men's wives, and babble slander of the holy;
with their ears they do not hear the Lord's praise even for a moment.
For the sake of the belly they steal what belongs to others,
(yet the) fire (of greed) does not leave them, and the thirst is not quenched.
Without the Lord's service, these are the fruits they bear;
O Nanak, forgetting God, the luckless die and are born (again). ॥9॥
298.7: I have wandered, searching, in all ten directions; wherever my eyes turn, he is there.
O Nanak, the mind comes under control (only) if (his) perfect grace is given. ॥10॥
298.8: Dasmi: (those who) have brought the ten doors (of the senses) under control
have found contentment of mind by repeating the Name.
With the ears the praise of Gopal is heard,
with the eyes the merciful Saadh is beheld,
the tongue sings the virtues of the Infinite,
(and one) dwells in the mind on the all-pervading Lord;
with hands and feet the service of the Sants is done.
O Nanak, this discipline is gained by God's grace. ॥10॥
299.1: Let the One, the only One, be praised; rare is the one who knows its taste.
The virtues of Gobind cannot be known; O Nanak, all (of him) is wonder. ॥11॥
299.2: Ekadasi: see the Lord, Ram, near (you);
bring the senses under control and listen to the Lord's Name;
(let there be) contentment in the mind and compassion for all beings:
in this way the fast is fulfilled.
(One who) holds the wandering mind in one place
is made pure in mind and body, absorbed in the Lord's Name as he repeats it.
O Nanak, sing the Lord's Kirtan: this is the dharma that never fails. ॥11॥
299.3: (Those who) met the merciful Saadh did (his) service, and (their) evil-mindedness was taken away.
O Nanak, they remain united with God, and all (their) entanglements have perished. ॥12॥
299.4: Duadasi: (practise) giving, the Naam and the cleansing bath;
give up pride and worship the Lord with devotion;
drink the Lord's Amrit in the Saadh Sangat;
the mind is satisfied by Kirtan in God's love.
Gentle words bring contentment to everyone,
(and) the mind, born of the five elements, is nourished by the relish of the Lord's Name.
These (gifts) are surely obtained from the perfect Guru;
O Nanak, dwelling on Ram, one does not come into the womb again. ॥12॥
299.5: Gripped by the three qualities (of Maya, the mortal) never sees (his) desires fulfilled.
O Nanak, when the saviour of the fallen dwells in the mind, (one) is set free through the Name. ॥13॥
299.6: Traudasi: the world (is gripped by) the three fevers;
(it) keeps coming and going, born into hell.
Worship of the Lord, Har Har, has not entered (its) mind,
nor has it sung, even for a moment, of God, the ocean of peace.
Making its body (a home) of joy and sorrow, it lies bound;
(it has) the long sickness of Maya, past all cure.
By day it wears itself out doing evil,
(and by night), when sleep fills its eyes, it raves in its dreams.
Such is the state when the Lord is forgotten.
Nanak (has come to) the refuge of God, the merciful Being. ॥13॥
299.7: The four quarters, the fourteen worlds: Ram pervades them all.
O Nanak, no lack is seen (in him); his works are complete. ॥14॥
299.8: Chaudahi: in the four quarters is God himself;
his glory fills all the worlds.
The One God pervades all ten directions;
see God in earth and sky, in all.
Water, land, forests, mountains, the underworlds:
the merciful Supreme God dwells in them (all).
In all, the subtle (unseen) and the gross (the visible world), is the Lord.
O Nanak, through the Guru, recognise God (Brahm). ॥14॥
299.9: (One who) has conquered the self through the Guru's teaching, and sung the virtues of Gobind:
O Nanak, by the Sant's grace (his) fears are erased, and anxiety has perished. ॥15॥
299.10: Amavas: (those) to whom the Gurdev gave contentment have come to peace within.
Mind and body are cooled, (there is) peace and Sahaj, (for one who) has taken to God's service.
The bonds of many vices are broken; his works are fruitful and complete.
Evil-mindedness is erased and Haumai is shed, as he remembers the Lord's Name.
(One who) has taken hold of the refuge of the Supreme Lord is done with coming and going.
Uttering the virtues of Gubind, God, he has crossed over himself, together with (his) family.
Let us do the Lord's service and repeat God's Name.
O Nanak, the home of peace (God) has been found from the perfect Guru. ॥15॥
300.1: One made whole by God himself is whole, and never wavers.
Day by day he rises higher; O Nanak, he never falls short. ॥16॥
300.2: Puranma: the One God (alone) is perfect, the Cause of creation, all-powerful.
(He is) the Being merciful to all creatures, whose hand is over all.
(He is) the treasure of virtues, the great Gobind, by whose doing (all) comes to pass.
He is God, the knower of hearts, all-wise, the Unseen, the Immaculate.
The Supreme Lord, the Supreme God, knows every way;
(he is) the helper of the Sants, able to give refuge; salutation (to him) at all hours.
(His) story cannot be told, nor understood; remember the Lord's feet.
Nanak (has come to) the refuge of God, the saviour of the fallen, the Master of the masterless. ॥16॥
300.3: (For those who) have grasped the refuge of the Lord King, pains are destroyed and dread is gone.
O Nanak, singing the Lord's virtues, (they) have obtained the fruits their minds longed for. ॥17॥
300.4: Whoever sings (the Lord's praise), whoever hears it, whoever reflects on it,
whoever teaches it (to others), whoever makes it firm (within): that one is saved.
(He) cuts away his sins and becomes pure, and the filth of birth after birth departs.
His face is bright in this world and the next, and Maya does not take hold of him.
He is the one of true awareness, he the Vaishnav, he the wise one, he the wealthy;
he is the hero, he alone is of noble family, who has worshipped the Lord (Bhagvant).
Khatri, Brahmin, Shudra, Vaish or chandal: (each) is saved by remembering (him).
Nanak is the dust of the feet of the one who has known his own God. ॥17॥
300.5: Gauri ki Vaar: by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Salok, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
The True Guru is a merciful being, to whom everyone is alike.
He looks on all with the same eye; (yet) fulfilment comes by the faith in one's mind.
In the True Guru is the Amrit (of the Name) of the sublime Lord; that is the state of (union with) the Lord.
O Nanak, only by (his) grace is the Lord meditated on; some rare one obtains (this Amrit) through the Guru. ॥1॥
300.6: By the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Haumai and Maya are poison through and through; (because of them) there is ever loss in the world, in the universe.
Through the Guru, reflecting on the Shabad, (one) earns the profit, the wealth of the Lord.
The poison, the filth of Haumai, is washed away by enshrining in the heart the Lord's Amrit, the Lord.
All the tasks of those are fulfilled on whom (the Lord) has shown mercy through the Guru.
O Nanak, those united from the very first stay united; the Lord, the Creator, has united them (himself). ॥2॥
301.1: You are the True Master, ever true; you are the True One, ever true, the Lord of the world (Gosain).
All (creation) meditates on you, all falls at your feet.
Your praise is beautiful in form; whoever has sung it, it has carried him across.
To the Gurmukhs you give (its) fruit: absorption in the True Name.
O my great Master, great is your glory. ॥1॥
301.2: Salok, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
To praise anything other than the Name: all such talk has an insipid taste.
The manmukhs praise their pride; (all their talk) is Haumai, possessiveness and strife.
Those whom they praise waste away and die, and all the wrangling comes to nothing.
O servant Nanak, (those) are saved who, through the Guru, repeat (the Name of) the Lord, Har Har, the Supreme Bliss. ॥1॥
301.3: By the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
O True Guru, tell (me) of the Lord God, that I may meditate in my mind on the Name of the Lord.
O Nanak, the Lord's Name is pure; may I utter it with my mouth and cast off all pain. ॥2॥
301.4: You yourself, you alone, are the Formless, O Niranjan, O Lord King.
Those who have meditated on you, the True One, with a single mind: all their pain you have taken away.
You have no rival, whom one could set beside you and speak of (as your equal).
As great a Giver as you, O Niranjan, you alone are; you, the True One, are pleasing to my mind.
O my True Master, O True One, true and lasting is your glory. ॥2॥
301.5: Salok, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Within the mind is the disease of Haumai; the manmukhs, the wicked, are lost in doubt.
O Nanak, meet the True Guru, the Saadh, the friend, and be rid of this disease. ॥1॥
301.6: By the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Through the Guru, (one's) mind and body stay dyed with love for the Lord, the treasure of virtues.
O servant Nanak, those who have come to the Lord's refuge, the Lord unites (with himself), with the Guru's approval. ॥2॥
301.7: You are the Creator, the all-pervading Being, beyond reach; with whom could you be compared?
If any were as great as you, he could be named (as your like); as your like, only you yourself are spoken of.
You alone are at work in every heart; through the Guru you are revealed.
You are the True Master of all; you are higher than all.
O True One, what you do will come to pass; why then should we grieve? ॥3॥
301.8: Salok, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
In my mind and body is love for the Beloved; (mind and body) stay fixed (on him) through all the eight watches.
O servant Nanak, by God's mercy (they) dwell in the peace the True Guru gives. ॥1॥
301.9: By the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Those within whom is love for the Beloved look beautiful, however they speak.
O Nanak, the Lord himself knows (this), the Beloved who has instilled the love. ॥2॥
301.10: O Creator, you yourself are infallible; you are not subject to error.
What you do, O True One, is good; through the Guru's Shabad you make (this) understood.
You are the Cause of causes, all-powerful; there is no other.
You are the Master, beyond reach and merciful; all meditate on you.
All beings are yours, you are (the Master) of all; you set all free. ॥4॥
302.1: Salok, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Hearing the Friend's message of love, (their) eyes stay fixed (on him, waiting);
the Guru, pleased, has united (them) with the Friend; O servant Nanak, (now they) sleep in peace. ॥1॥
302.2: By the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
The True Guru is the merciful Giver, in whose heart compassion ever dwells.
The True Guru is without enmity within; everywhere he sees the one Brahm alone.
Of those who carry on enmity against the ones without enmity, not one has found rest.
The True Guru wishes good for all; how can harm come to him?
As one is minded towards the True Guru, so is the fruit one receives.
O Nanak, the Creator knows everything; nothing is hidden from him. ॥2॥
302.3: (The soul-bride) whom the Master makes great is the one known as great.
Whoever pleases the Master, he forgives; she is dear to the Master's heart.
If anyone imitates her, she is foolish and ignorant.
She whom the True Guru unites (with the Lord) dwells on (his) virtues, and speaks of virtues alone.
O Nanak, the True One is ever true; understanding (this), she merges in the True One. ॥5॥
302.4: Salok, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
The Lord is true, Niranjan, immortal, fearless, without enmity and formless.
Those who have repeated (his Name) with one mind and one attention: their burden of Haumai has been lifted.
Those who have worshipped the Lord through the Guru: those Sants are acclaimed.
If anyone slanders the perfect True Guru, the whole world cries shame, shame on him.
In the True Guru the Lord himself is at work; the Lord himself is the protector.
Blessed, blessed is the Guru, who sings the Lord's virtues; to him be homage for ever and ever.
Servant Nanak is a sacrifice to those who have repeated (the Name of) the Creator. ॥1॥
302.5: By the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
He himself fashioned the earth, and he himself the sky.
Within it he himself created beings, and he himself puts food in their mouths.
He himself, he alone, is at work everywhere; he himself is the treasure of virtues.
O servant Nanak, meditate on the Naam: (the Lord) cuts away all the sins of (the one who does). ॥2॥
302.6: You are the True Master, ever true; truth is pleasing to you, the True One.
Those who praise you, the True One: Jam's servant does not come near them.
Bright at (the Lord's) door are the faces of those in whose hearts the True Lord is dear.
The false are thrown behind; with falsehood and deceit in the heart, (each) suffers great pain.
The false have blackened faces; the false one ends as nothing but falsehood. ॥6॥
302.7: Salok, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
The True Guru is the soil of dharam; as one sows in it, so is the fruit one reaps.
The Gursikhs have sown Amrit (the Name), and have obtained the fruit of Amrit, the Lord.
In this world and the next their faces are bright; they are robed in honour in the Lord's true court.
Some have falseness within, and practise falseness every day; as one sows, so is the fruit one eats.
When the True Guru, the assayer, looks closely, all the self-seekers are laid bare.
As they think every day, so they receive; the Lord has shown them up for just what they are.
O Nanak, on both sides the Master himself is at work; ever making all these plays, he watches them. ॥1॥
303.1: By the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
The mind is one, and works one way (at a time); to whatever it is attached, that it obtains.
Someone may talk a great deal, but he eats only the thing that is in his house.
Without the True Guru understanding does not come, and pride does not leave from within.
Pain and hunger cling to the proud; they hold out their hands and beg from house to house.
Falsehood and fraud do not stay hidden; the gilt and the pretence peel away.
One for whom it is written from (deeds) past: the True Guru, God, comes and meets him.
As iron touching the paaras (turns to gold), so joining the Sangat one turns to gold.
O God of servant Nanak, you are the Master; as it pleases you, so you lead (us). ॥2॥
303.2: Those who have served the Lord in their hearts, the Lord himself has united (with himself).
(Whoever) has made a partnership in virtues with them has burned away all faults through the Shabad.
To sell faults off for the price of straw, (this partnership) is obtained, O True One, by the one to whom you give it.
I am a sacrifice to my Guru, who has wiped out faults and brought virtues to light.
The great glory of the Great One is uttered through the Guru. ॥7॥
303.3: Salok, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
In the True Guru is this great glory: night and day he meditates on the Name of the Lord, Har Har.
His purity and self-discipline is to dwell on the Name of the Lord, Har Har; with the Lord's Name alone he is content.
The Lord's Name is his strength, the Lord's Name his support; the Lord's Name alone keeps him safe.
Whoever, with the mind fixed, worships the Guru's form obtains the fruits the mind desires.
Whoever slanders the perfect True Guru, the Creator has him punished.
That moment never comes into his hands again; he himself eats what he has sown.
With blackened face he is taken to the terrible hell, like a thief with a rope round his neck.
Should he again fall at the True Guru's refuge, then (only) is he saved, when he meditates on the Name of the Lord, Har Har.
Nanak speaks and tells the Lord's words: so it pleases the Lord, the Creator. ॥1॥
303.4: By the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
One who does not obey the command of the Perfect Guru, that ignorant manmukh, is robbed by the poison of Maya.
Falsehood is within him, and he takes (all) as false; the Lord has hung baseless quarrels round his neck.
He peddles talk a great deal, but what he says pleases no one.
He roams from house to house like a forsaken wife; whoever keeps company with him is stained as well.
One who becomes Gurmukh stays apart; leaving his side, he goes and sits beside the Guru.
Whoever hides (disowns) his own Guru is not good, O Panch (chosen ones); he has lost profit and capital, all of it.
Nanak first tells (what) the Agam and the Nigam (the Shastras and the Vedas say); the word of the Perfect Guru has risen above (them).
The glory of the Perfect Guru is pleasing to the Gursikhs; the manmukhs have not had that moment in their hands. ॥2॥
304.1: The True One, ever true, is greatest of all; he alone receives (him) whom the True Guru marks with the tikka (of blessing).
The True Guru is the one who meditates on the True One; the True One, ever true, and the True Guru are one.
He alone is the True Guru, the Purakh, who has reined in the five enemies and brought them under control.
Those who count themselves (great) without serving the True Guru have falsehood within; shame, shame (on them), their faces are pale.
What they say pleases no one; their faces are black, (for) they have fallen away from the True Guru. ॥8॥
304.2: Salok, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
The whole (world) is the Lord God's field; the Lord himself has set (all beings) to farm it.
For the Gurmukhs he has, in his grace, made (the crop) spring up; the manmukhs have lost even the capital.
Everyone sows for his own good, (but) the Lord makes that field spring up which pleases him.
The Gursikhs have sown the Lord's Amrit, and have gained the fruit of Amrit, the Lord's Amrit Name.
Jam, the mouse that ever gnaws at the crop, the Lord, the Creator, has struck down and driven out.
The crop, (sown) with love, has sprung up, and the Lord has heaped up the pile of his grace.
(God) has lifted all fret and worry from those who have meditated on the True Guru, the Being.
O servant Nanak, whoever has worshipped the Naam has crossed over himself and carried the whole world across. ॥1॥
304.3: By the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
All day the manmukh, smeared with greed, talks of other things (than the Name).
At night he lies crushed by sleep, and all the nine openings (of the body) go slack.
Over the manmukhs' heads is the command of their women; every day they bring them good things.
Men who carry out what their women tell them are unclean, witless and foolish.
Impure men, in the grip of lust: they are the ones who ask their women and go by it.
One who walks by the True Guru's word is a true man, the best of the good.
Women and men, all of them, he himself created; every play is the Lord's own playing.
All this is of your making, (O Lord); says Nanak, all of it is good, the best of the good. ॥2॥
304.4: (O Lord,) you are free of all need and unfathomable; you are beyond weighing: how can you be weighed?
Fortunate are those who meditate on you, those who come to meet the True Guru.
The True Guru's Bani is the very form of Truth; through Gurbani one becomes (the same).
Others, aping the True Guru, babble half-baked words; those false ones, through their falsehood, wither and fall.
Within them is one thing, in their mouths another; for the poison of Maya they wear themselves out to death in anguish. ॥9॥
304.5: Salok, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Service of the True Guru is pure; one who is pure performs that service.
Those within whom are deceit, vice and falsehood, the True One himself has set apart and cast out, (as) lepers.
The truthful Sikhs sit by the True Guru and toil (in his service); the false are not found (there) anywhere, however one may search.
Those who do not like what the True Guru says go about with defiled faces, rebuked by the Master.
Those within whom there is no love for the Lord: how long can they be humoured, these manmukhs out of step (like goblins)?
One who meets the True Guru keeps his own mind in its place, and himself has the use of what is his own.
O servant Nanak, (God) unites some with the Guru and gives them peace; others, the cheats, he himself sets apart and casts out. ॥1॥
305.1: By the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Those within whom is the treasure of the Lord's Name: the Master has brought their affairs to fulfilment.
Their dependence on people is ended; the Lord God has taken their side and sits beside them.
When the Creator is on (their) side, everyone is on (their) side; all who look on them acclaim them.
Bankers and emperors are all of the Lord's making; all come and make supplication to the Lord's servant.
Great is the glory of the Perfect Guru: serving the great Lord, (his servant) has found peace beyond weighing.
The Perfect Guru has given the gift of the Lord('s Name), which never fails; the Lord bestows it every day, and it grows ever greater.
Any slanderer who cannot bear to see (this) glory, the Creator himself has consumed.
Servant Nanak speaks the virtues of the Creator, who has always kept his devotees safe. ॥2॥
305.2: (O Lord,) you are the Master, beyond reach and merciful, the great Giver, the Wise One.
I see no other as great as you; you alone, the accomplished one, are pleasing to my mind.
Attachment and family, all that is seen, is bound to pass; (it is all) coming and going.
Those who set their minds anywhere but on the True One are false, and their pride is false.
O Nanak, meditate on the True One; without the True One the ignorant burn and burn away to death. ॥10॥
305.3: Salok, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
First (the manmukh) gives (the Guru) no regard; what he says afterwards is of no use.
The poor manmukh wanders, caught halfway; how can he find peace by talk?
One within whom there is no love for the True Guru comes in falsehood and goes in falsehood.
If my Lord God, the Creator, shows grace, then (one) sees the True Guru as the Supreme Lord.
Then he drinks the Amrit, the Guru's Shabad, and puts an end to all fret, worry and doubt.
He stays in bliss for ever, day and night; O servant Nanak, he sings the Lord's virtues night and day. ॥1॥
305.4: By the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
One known as a Sikh of the Guru, the True Guru, rises early and meditates on the Lord's Name.
He makes the effort, early in the hours before dawn; he bathes, and dips in the pool of Amrit.
By the Guru's teaching he chants the Name of the Lord, Har Har, and all his sins, misdeeds and faults are washed away.
Then, as the day rises, he sings Gurbani; sitting down and rising up, he meditates on the Lord's Name.
Whoever, with every breath and every morsel, meditates on my Lord, Har Har: that Gursikh pleases the Guru's mind.
The one to whom my Master is merciful: to that Gursikh the Guru imparts his teaching.
Servant Nanak begs for the dust of that Gursikh's feet, who repeats the Naam himself and has others repeat it. ॥2॥
306.1: (O Lord,) those who meditate on you, the True One, are rare, and few.
Those who worship the One with mind and heart: countless millions eat by their blessing.
All (creation) meditates on you, (but) those alone are accepted whom the Master wants.
Those who eat and clothe themselves without serving the True Guru are lepers: they die, and having died are born (again).
To one's face they speak sweetly, but behind one's back they spit out poison mixed in their mouths.
The false at heart the Master has cut off (from himself). ॥11॥
306.2: Salok, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
A blue-black blanket full of dirt and lice: that renegade (one turned away from the Guru) put it on the renegade (his servant).
No one in the world lets him sit near; having fallen in filth, the manmukh came back smeared with still more dirt.
Made a renegade, he was sent to slander others and tell tales; there too the faces of both renegades were blackened.
At once it was heard all over the world, O brother, that the renegade and his servant were beaten with shoes, and, dazed, he got up and came home.
After that the renegade was not allowed to mix in gatherings or among his in-laws; then his wife and his niece brought him and laid him in the house again.
Both this world and the next are lost (to him); he cries out every day, hungry and thirsty.
Blessed, blessed is the Master, the Creator, the Being, who himself sat and had true justice done.
Whoever slanders the Perfect True Guru, the True One has struck down and consumed.
This word was spoken by the one who brought the whole world into being. ॥1॥
306.3: By the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
One whose master is naked and hungry: how can that servant eat his fill?
What is in the master's house comes into the servant's hands; what is not there, where can he get it?
One served who then demands an account: that service is hard.
Says Nanak, serve the Lord, the Guru, whose sight bears fruit; then no one asks for an account. ॥2॥
306.4: O Nanak, the Sants reflect, and the four Vedas declare,
that the words the devotees speak with their mouths come to pass.
This is plainly seen in the world, and all people hear (of it).
Foolish men who quarrel with the Sants find no peace.
The (Sants) long for their good, (but) they burn in their pride.
What can the wretches do, when their lot is evil from the first?
Those struck down by the Supreme Lord belong to no one.
They bear enmity to those who bear none, and by the justice of Dharam they burn.
All whom the Sant has cursed go wandering about.
When the tree is cut at the root, its branches wither. ॥12॥
306.5: Salok, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
The Guru meditates on the Lord within; great is (his) glory.
The Perfect One, well pleased, has given it to the True Guru; it does not lessen by a sesame seed for anyone's lessening.
The True Master is on the True Guru's side; so all the world may fret and fret itself to death.
The Lord, the Creator, makes the slanderers' faces black, and has himself increased (the Guru's) glory.
The more the slanderers slander, the more (this glory) grows, day after day.
O servant Nanak, (the Guru) has worshipped the Lord, and the Lord has brought all (the world) and laid it at (his) feet. ॥1॥
307.1: By the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Whoever keeps a grudge against the True Guru has lost all of this world and the next.
Every day he gnashes his teeth and foams at the mouth; fretting and fuming, he withers and falls.
Every day he schemes for Maya and wealth, (but) even the wealth he had before has flown away.
What can he earn, and what can he enjoy, within whom anxiety and pain have settled?
One who stirs up enmity against the one who bears none has taken the sin of the whole world on his head.
There is no shelter for him, here or hereafter, who has slander within and (the sweetness of) a mango in his mouth.
If he lays his hand on gold, it turns to dust.
If he comes back to the Guru's refuge, his past faults are forgiven.
O servant Nanak, (whoever) has meditated on the Naam night and day: remembering the Lord, his sins and misdeeds are gone. ॥2॥
307.2: (O Lord,) you alone are the True One, you are Truth; you are above all, you are the support (of all).
Those who meditate on you, the True One, and serve the True One, take pride in you, O True One.
Truth is within them, their faces are bright; they speak the Truth, and you, O True One, are their strength.
They are devotees who have praised (you) through the Guru; the true Shabad is their insignia.
Those who serve the True One in truth: to them I am ever a sacrifice. ॥13॥
307.3: Salok, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Those struck down from the very first by the Perfect True Guru, those same the True Guru has now struck down.
However much one may long to unite them (with the Guru), the Creator does not let them meet.
They find no shelter in the Sat Sangat; the Guru has weighed this and (declared it) in the Sangat.
Whoever goes and meets them now, cruel Jam strikes him down.
Those whom Guru Baba (Guru Nanak Dev Ji) rebuked stayed rebuked; Guru Angad (Dev Ji) declared them false.
The Guru of the third generation (Guru Amar Das Ji) reflected: what lies in the hands of these poor wretches?
(The Guru) who installed the Guru of the fourth generation (Guru Ram Das Ji) carried all the slanderers and the wicked across.
Whoever, son or Sikh, serves the True Guru has all his affairs set right.
He will obtain whatever fruit he wishes, sons, riches and prosperity; (the Guru) leads him to union (with God), and the Lord carries him across.
All treasures are in the True Guru, who keeps the Lord enshrined in his heart.
He alone finds the Perfect True Guru on whose forehead (this) writ is written.
Servant Nanak begs for the dust of those Gursikhs' feet, who are beloved friends. ॥1॥
308.1: By the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Those whom (God) himself grants glory: he himself also brings the world and lays it at their feet.
We would have cause to fear if we did anything of ourselves; it is the Creator who is increasing his own power in everything.
See, O brother: this is the arena of the Lord, the true Beloved, who by his own might has brought all to bow down.
The Lord, the Master, protects his devotees, and blackens the faces of the slanderers and the wicked.
The True Guru's glory grows ever greater; the Lord himself every day has (him) sing (his) praise and worship (him).
Repeat the Naam night and day, O Gursikhs; the Lord, the Creator, will make the True Guru dwell in (the home of your heart).
Know the True Guru's Bani to be true, true indeed, O Gursikhs; the Lord, the Creator, himself brings it forth from (the Guru's) mouth.
The beloved Lord makes the Gursikhs' faces bright, and has the Guru acclaimed everywhere in the world.
Servant Nanak is the Lord's slave; the Lord himself keeps the honour of his slaves. ॥2॥
308.2: (O Lord,) you yourself are the True Master, O our true Banker.
O God, make the true capital, the Naam, firm in us; (we are) your traders.
(We) serve the True One, buy the merchandise of Truth, and tell of (your) matchless virtues.
Those who live in the spirit of servants have met (you), adorned by the Guru's Shabad.
You are the True Master, the Unseen; through the Guru's Shabad you are made known. ॥14॥
308.3: Salok, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
One within whom is envy of others never comes to good.
No one heeds what he says; he is ever standing in a wilderness, crying out.
One within whom is backbiting comes to be known as a backbiter; all he has ever done is lost.
Every day he tells untrue tales against others; his face is blackened, and he cannot show it.
In Kalyug the body is the field of deeds; as one sows, so one eats.
Judgement is not passed on words; whoever eats poison dies at once.
O brother, see the true justice of the Creator: as one does, so one receives.
(God) has given servant Nanak full understanding; he tells the things of the Lord's court. ॥1॥
308.4: By the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Those who broke away from the Guru even while he was present before their eyes find no shelter at (the Lord's) door.
Whoever goes and meets those slanderers (shares their lot): their faces are pale, and spit upon spit falls on their faces.
Those cursed by the True Guru are cursed by the whole world; they ever stumble about, lost.
Those who have disowned their own Guru wander about, wailing aloud.
Their hunger never leaves them; they ever cry out: hunger, hunger.
No one listens to what they say; day after day they die in dread upon dread.
They cannot bear to see the True Guru's greatness; for them there is no place, here or hereafter.
Those who go and join the ones struck down by the True Guru lose whatever honour they had left.
Cursed by the Guru, they are lepers already; whoever meets such a one, leprosy breaks out on him too.
O Lord, let (me) not even see those who fix their minds on the love of another.
The Creator himself wrote (this) from the start and set it down; against it there is no remedy.
O servant Nanak, worship the Name in adoration; none can reach up to it.
Great is the greatness of the Name; it rises ever higher, growing more each day. ॥2॥
309.1: By the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
The one whom the Guru, while still present, sat and anointed with the tilak (as Guru): that servant's greatness has become great.
The whole world bows before him and falls at his feet; his praise has spread through all the world.
Continents and universes bow to him; the one on whose forehead the perfect Guru has placed his hand becomes perfect.
The Guru's greatness rises ever higher, growing more each day; none can reach up to it.
The Lord, the Creator, himself sat and installed servant Nanak (as Guru); that God himself keeps (his) honour. ॥3॥
309.2: The body is a boundless fortress, with market streets within.
One who trades (there) through the Guru gathers in the merchandise of the Lord.
(Here) one deals in the treasure of the Lord's Name: diamonds and corals.
Those who search for this wealth anywhere outside the body are fools and ghouls.
In doubt they are made to wander through the wilds, as the deer searches the bushes (for the musk within itself). ॥15॥
309.3: Salok, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Whoever slanders the perfect True Guru comes to grief in the world.
Terrible hell is a well of pain; he is seized and cast into it.
No one hears his cries and wails; in anguish upon anguish he weeps.
He has lost this world and the next entirely, and squandered profit and capital alike.
Making him an oil-presser's ox, God yokes him (to the press) as each morning comes.
The Lord ever sees and hears everything; nothing is hidden from him.
As one sows, so one reaps: whatever each has sown before.
The one on whom God bestows his grace washes the True Guru's feet.
Following the Guru, the True Guru, he crosses over, as iron (floats across) joined to wood.
O servant Nanak, meditate on the Name; repeat the Name of the Lord, Har Har: in the Name is peace. ॥1॥
309.4: By the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Greatly fortunate are the happy wives whom the Lord King has met through the Guru.
The light within (them) shines forth; O Nanak, they merge in the Name. ॥2॥
309.5: This whole body is (the dwelling of) dharma, within which is the light of the True One.
Secret jewels lie hidden in it; some rare Gurmukh, a servant (of the Lord), digs them out.
When he recognises the all-pervading Lord (Atam Ram) everywhere, then (he sees) the One alone pervading all, through and through like warp and weft.
He has seen the One, put his faith in the One, and heard with his ears of the One alone.
O servant Nanak, praise the Name: (this) is your true service of the True One. ॥16॥
310.1: Salok, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
All delights are in the hearts of those in whose minds the Lord has come to dwell.
In the Lord's court their faces shine; all go to see them.
No fear at all remains for those who have meditated on the Name of the Fearless One.
They alone have served the exalted Lord in whose lot it was written from the start.
Those in whose minds the Lord has come to dwell are robed in honour in the Lord's court.
They themselves cross over with all their families, and they set the whole world free in their wake.
O Lord, unite servant Nanak with (such) servants of yours, beholding whom again and again we live. ॥1॥
310.2: By the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
That ground has turned green where my True Guru came and sat.
Those beings have turned green who went and saw my True Guru.
Blessed, blessed the father, blessed, blessed the family, blessed, blessed the mother who gave birth to the Guru, O mother.
Blessed, blessed is the Guru, who worshipped the Name: he crossed over himself, and those who saw him he sets free as well.
O Lord, show mercy and bring (me) to the True Guru; let servant Nanak wash (his) feet. ॥2॥
310.3: The True Guru is true, ever true, and immortal, who has enshrined the Lord within his heart.
The True Guru is the Being, true, ever true, who has killed the poison of lust and anger.
When I saw the perfect True Guru, my mind within found its support.
I am a sacrifice to my Guru; for ever and ever I give myself up to him.
The Gurmukh has won (the game of life), and the manmukh has lost. ॥17॥
310.4: Salok, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
The one whom (God) in his mercy has united with the True Guru meditates on the Name with his mouth, through the Guru.
He does whatever is pleasing to the True Guru; the perfect Guru settles (the Name) in the home of his heart.
Those within whom is the treasure of the Name: (the Guru) takes away all their fear.
Those whom the Lord himself stands by to protect: how many others wear themselves out, toiling (against them), and are gone.
O servant Nanak, meditate on the Name; the Lord will set (you) free here and hereafter. ॥1॥
310.5: By the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
The Gursikhs' minds delight in the greatness of the Guru, the True Guru.
O Lord, you keep the True Guru's honour; (so his greatness) rises ever higher, growing more each day.
The Guru, the True Guru, holds the Supreme Lord in his mind; the Supreme Lord (himself) delivers (him).
The Lord is the might and mainstay of the Guru, the True Guru; he has brought all and made them bow (before the Guru).
Those who looked upon my True Guru with love: all their sins (the Guru) has taken away.
In the Lord's court their faces shine, and they have won great honour.
Servant Nanak asks for the dust (of the feet) of those who are the Guru's Sikhs, my brothers. ॥2॥
310.6: Let me speak his praise and extol (him); his praise is true, true is the greatness of the True One.
Let me praise the True One; the True One is worthy of praise; no one has found the True One's worth.
Those who have tasted the essence, true, ever true, remain fulfilled and satisfied.
They alone know this essence of the Lord, like a mute who has eaten sweets (and cannot tell of it).
Those who served the Lord God through the perfect Guru: in their minds the music of rejoicing has sounded. ॥18॥
311.1: Salok, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Those who have an abscess within, they alone know its stabbing pains.
(So) they alone know the pang of separation from the Lord (who feel it); I am ever a sacrifice, a sacrifice to them.
O Lord, unite (me with) my friend, the Being (the Guru); for them let my head roll beneath (their feet).
The Sikhs who carry out the Guru's work: I am the slave of their slaves.
Those dyed in the deep crimson of the Lord's love: their robe is soaked in the Lord's love.
(O Lord,) in your mercy unite Nanak with the Guru; he has sold his head to him at a price. ॥1॥
311.2: By the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
The body is filled with faults; O Sants, how can it become pure?
Through the Guru virtues are bought, (and so one) washes out the filth of Haumai.
Those who trade in Truth with love: (theirs) is a true bargain.
There is no loss in it at all; the profit is that they become pleasing to the Lord.
O Nanak, they alone have traded in Truth who receive it as was written for them from the start. ॥2॥
311.3: Let me praise the True One, who is worthy of praise, the Being, true, ever true, and apart from all.
Let me serve the True One, and let the True One dwell in (my) mind; the Lord, true, ever true, is the protector (of all).
Those who worshipped the True One, ever true, have gone and merged with the True One.
Those who did not serve the True One, ever true, are manmukhs, fools and ghouls.
They babble nonsense from their mouths, like drunkards who have drunk wine. ॥19॥
311.4: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Through Raag Gauri (the soul-bride) is of fine qualities only if she keeps her Master in her mind;
(if) she walks in the will of the True Guru, and makes this her adornment.
The true Shabad is (her) Husband; she enjoys (his love) for ever and ever.
As boiled madder yields a deep colour, so she gives her life to the True One.
She is dyed through and through in deep crimson; her love is bound to the True One.
Falsehood and fraud do not stay hidden, though you wrap falsehood in gilding.
(The false) make false boasts; their love is bound to what is false.
O Nanak, (the Lord) himself is the True One; he himself casts his glance of grace. ॥1॥
311.5: By the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
In the Sat Sangat is the praise of the Lord; (there) the beloved ones meet in the Saadh's company.
Blessed are those men, those mortals, (the Lord's) servants, who teach for the good of others.
They make the Lord's Name firm (in others), they make (them) hear the Lord's Name; through the Lord's Name they have carried the world across.
Everyone longs to see the Guru; the nine regions of the world bow to him.
You yourself have placed yourself within the True Guru, and you yourself have adorned the Guru.
You yourself worship the True Guru, and have (others) worship him, O Creator.
If anyone breaks away from the True Guru, his face is blackened, and Jam has struck him down.
For him there is no shelter, here or hereafter; this the Gursikhs have weighed in their minds.
Those who met the True Guru, they alone have been saved, who cherished the Name in their hearts.
O Gursikhs, sons of servant Nanak, repeat (the Name of) the Lord: the Lord has carried (the world) across. ॥2॥
312.1: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Haumai has led the world astray: (it is caught in) evil-mindedness, Maya and vice.
If the True Guru is met, then comes (God's) glance of grace; the manmukhs are in blind darkness.
O Nanak, he himself unites with himself the one whom he attaches in love to the Shabad. ॥3॥
312.2: True is the praise of the True One; that one alone sings it whose inner self is soaked (in love).
Those who worshipped the One with one-pointed mind: their body never wastes away.
Blessed, blessed are those beings, and praise be to them, who drink the true nectar with the tongue.
Those whose minds love the True One, ever true, are accepted in the true court.
Blessed, blessed is the life of the truthful; the True One makes their faces bright. ॥20॥
312.3: Salok, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
The Saakats go and bow before the Guru, but they are counterfeit at heart, false through and through.
When the Guru says: Rise, my brothers, they squeeze in (among the Sikhs) and sit down like cranes.
The True Guru is at work within the Gursikhs; at the sifting, (the false) are picked out and put out.
Seated now in front, now behind, they hide their faces; but the counterfeit do not mingle (with the true).
Their fodder is not to be found there; like sheep they go (elsewhere) and find falsehood.
Though one longs to feed a Saakat (with good food), he brings up poison, spewing it from his mouth.
O Lord, let (me) never keep company with the Saakat: such are struck down by the Creator.
The one whose play this is makes it and watches it; servant Nanak cherishes the Name. ॥1॥
312.4: By the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
The True Guru is the inaccessible Being, who has enshrined the Lord within his heart.
No one can reach up to the True Guru, on whose side is the Creator.
The True Guru's sword and armour are devotion to the Lord, with which he has struck down Death, the thorn, and driven it away.
The True Guru's protector is the Lord himself; all who follow the True Guru the Lord has saved.
Whoever wishes ill to the perfect True Guru is struck down by the Maker himself.
This is how it comes to pass in the court of the True Lord; servant Nanak has reflected on the Inaccessible One. ॥2॥
312.5: Those who have worshipped the True One even in their sleep utter the True One when they rise.
Such people are known to be rare in the world, who dwell on the True One through the Guru.
I am a sacrifice to those who take the True One's Name night and day.
Those whose minds and bodies love the True One reach the true court.
Servant Nanak utters the true Name: the True One, ever true, is new for ever. ॥21॥
312.6: Salok, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Asleep or awake, it is all one: the Gurmukhs are accepted.
Those who do not forget (God) with any breath or morsel are perfect and foremost among men.
By (God's) grace the True Guru is found, and the mind stays fixed (on God) night and day.
May I stay joined in their company, and win honour in (the Lord's) court.
As they lie down to sleep they utter Waah Waah (praise), and as they rise they praise him too.
O Nanak, bright are the faces of those who rise each day and cherish (the Lord in their hearts). ॥1॥
313.1: By the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
If one serves one's own True Guru, the infinite Naam is obtained.
The Lord, the Giver, grants (the Name as) his gift, and pulls out those who are drowning in the terrible world-ocean.
Blessed, blessed are those bankers who trade with (the capital of) the Name.
The Sikhs come (to the Guru) as traders, and (the Guru), through the Shabad, carries them across.
O servant Nanak, those on whom (God's) grace has fallen have served the Creator. ॥2॥
313.2: The true servants and devotees of the True One are those who have worshipped the True One, ever true.
Those who searched and sought through the Guru found the True One within themselves.
The Master is true; those who served the True One have struck down Death, the thorn, and brought it under control.
The True One, ever true, is greater than all; those who serve the True One are merged in the True One.
True praise be to the True One; serving the True One, ever true, (a life) bears fruit. ॥22॥
313.3: Salok, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
The manmukh is a fool; empty of the Name, he wanders astray.
Without the Guru his mind does not hold still, and again and again he falls into births.
When the Lord God himself is merciful, the True Guru comes and meets (him).
O servant Nanak, praise the Name, and the pain of birth and death will go. ॥1॥
313.4: By the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
I praise my Guru in many ways, with love and with all my heart.
(My) mind is dyed in (the love of) the True Guru; (the Guru) has shaped it well and kept it so.
(My) tongue is never sated with praising, the mind fixed on the Lord, the Beloved.
O Nanak, in the mind is a hunger for the Name; the mind is satisfied only when it tastes the Lord's nectar. ॥2॥
313.5: The True One, ever true, who made the days and the nights, is known through his creation.
I praise that True One for ever and ever; true are the glories of the True One.
The True One is worthy of praise, and true is (his) praise; no one has found the worth of the True One.
When the perfect True Guru was met, then (those glories) came plainly into view.
Those who praised the True One through the Guru have lost all their hungers. ॥23॥
313.6: Salok, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Searching and searching my mind and body, I have sought out and found that God.
I found the Guru, the go-between, who joined me to the Lord God. ॥1॥
313.7: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
One who holds Maya (in his heart) is utterly blind and deaf.
He does not hear the Shabad, but raises a great noise and clamour.
The Gurmukh is known by this: he fixes his loving attention on the Shabad.
Hearing the Lord's Name, he believes in it, and merges in the Lord's Name.
Whatever pleases him, that (the creature) does, as he is made to do.
O Nanak, the creature sounds (like an instrument) as (God) plays it. ॥2॥
314.1: You, O Creator, know everything that goes on within all beings.
You, the Creator, are yourself beyond all reckoning; the whole world is caught in reckoning.
All that happens is of your doing; all (creation) is of your making.
You, the One, are at work in every heart; O True Master, (all this is your) wondrous play.
Those who meet the True Guru meet the Lord; no one can turn them back (from him). ॥24॥
314.2: Salok, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Let us hold this mind firm, and through the Guru fix our consciousness (on the Lord).
Why should we forget (him) with any breath or morsel, sitting or rising, each day?
(Then) the worry of death and life is gone, and this soul (comes) into the power of the Lord God.
(O God,) keep (me) as it pleases you; grant servant Nanak the Name. ॥1॥
314.3: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
The proud manmukh does not know the mansion (of the True Guru); one moment he is forward, the next he holds back.
Though he is called again and again, he does not come to (the Guru's) mansion; how then can he succeed in (the Lord's) court?
Rare is the one who knows the True Guru's mansion, who stands always with palms joined.
O Nanak, (the one on whom) my Lord shows his grace, he turns (that one) back (to himself). ॥2॥
314.4: That service alone bears fruit by which the True Guru's mind is pleased.
Once the True Guru's mind was pleased, sins and stains were shattered.
The teaching the True Guru gave, the Sikhs heard with their own ears.
Those who accepted the True Guru's will took on a colour four times as deep.
This is the singular way of the Gurmukhs: hearing the Guru's teaching, (their) mind is drenched (in love). ॥25॥
314.5: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Whoever has slandered his own Guru has neither place nor resting place.
Both this world and the next are lost to him; in (the Lord's) court there is no place (for him).
That moment does not come to hand again, when (such people) might fall at the True Guru's feet.
If one goes astray in a grudge against the True Guru, (life) passes in sorrow upon sorrow.
The True Guru, the Being, is without enmity; he himself attaches (to his feet) whomever (he will).
O Nanak, those to whom (God) has granted the sight (of the Guru), he sets free in (his) court. ॥1॥
314.6: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
The manmukh is ignorant, evil-minded and proud.
Anger is within him, and he has gambled away his understanding.
He practises falsehood, deceit and sin.
What can he hear, and what is he to tell others?
Blind and deaf, he loses (the way) and falls into the wilderness.
The blind manmukh keeps coming and going.
Without meeting the True Guru he is not accepted (at the Lord's door).
O Nanak, he acts out what was written before (by his past deeds). ॥2॥
314.7: Those whose hearts are hard do not sit near the True Guru.
Truth is at work there, and (so) the minds of the false are cheerless.
With twists and tricks they pass the time (there), then go and sit again with the false.
Falsehood does not blend with the true: let anyone judge it in the mind and see.
The false go and join the false, and the truthful Sikhs sit by the True Guru. ॥26॥
315.1: Salok, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The slanderers who were left, (God) has struck down, himself taking the task in hand.
O Nanak, (God), the helper of the Sants, is at work everywhere, plain to see. ॥1॥
315.2: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Those who have strayed from the Root from the very start: where can they lay hold?
O Nanak, they are struck down by him who is the Cause of creation, all-powerful. ॥2॥
315.3: Pauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
They set out at night with nooses, but God knows (these) mortals.
Hidden in secret places, they eye the women of others.
They break in at places hard to reach, and enjoy wine, taking it for sweet.
By their own deeds, each one, they themselves come to regret.
Azrail, the angel (of death), crushes (them) like sesame seeds in the oil-press. ॥27॥
315.4: Salok, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Those who are servants of the True King, they alone are accepted.
O Nanak, those who serve another (than him), those ignorant ones burn and burn away and die. ॥1॥
315.5: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The writ God has written from the beginning cannot be erased.
O Nanak, the Lord's Name is (the true) wealth and merchandise: meditate on it always. ॥2॥
315.6: Pauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The one whom Narayan himself has thrust away: where can he set his foot?
He commits countless sins, and every day tastes nothing but poison.
Slandering, he has wasted away and died; he burns within his own body.
He is struck down by the True Master: who can save him?
Nanak is in the refuge of the one who is the unseen Being. ॥28॥
315.7: Salok, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Terrible hells and many heavy sorrows: (this) is the abode of the ungrateful.
O Nanak, that God has struck them down; they die as ones untrue to their salt. ॥1॥
315.8: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(God) has made every medicine, but for the slanderer there is no cure.
O Nanak, (God) himself has led them astray; wasting away, they fall into birth after birth. ॥2॥
315.9: Pauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The perfect True Guru, well pleased, has given the wealth of the Lord, true and inexhaustible.
All anxieties are erased, and the fear of Jam is gone.
Lust, anger and (other) evils are broken off in the company of the Saadh.
Those who serve another than the True One will die helpless, like a fledgling (fallen from the nest).
The Guru has blessed Nanak, and (he is) joined to the Name. ॥29॥
315.10: Salok, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
He is no ascetic who is greedy within and roams after Maya each day, a leper.
When first invited, he would not take the alms offered with respect; afterwards, regretting it, the ascetic brought his son and seated him in (the gathering).
All the elders began to laugh: the ascetic has been worn away by a wave of greed.
Where he sees little wealth, the ascetic will not go near; on seeing much wealth, the ascetic gave up his faith.
O brother, this is no ascetic but a crane (a hypocrite): so the holy people have judged, sitting together.
The ascetic slanders the true man and busies himself with the praise of the world; for this fault the Master has struck the ascetic down.
See the fruit the ascetic has reaped for slandering the great beings: all the ascetic's labour is lost.
Sitting outside among the elders, he has himself called an ascetic; sitting inside, the ascetic commits sins; the Lord has laid bare (his) hidden sin and shown it to the elders.
Dharam Raj has told Jam's servants: Take this ascetic and throw him where the worst of all murderers are.
And let none of you have any dealings with this ascetic again: he has been cursed by the True Guru.
What took place at the Lord's door, Nanak has told aloud; he alone understands it whom the Master has adorned. ॥1॥
316.1: By the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
The Lord's devotees have worshipped the Lord and (sung) the Lord's greatness.
The devotees sing the Lord's Kirtan every day; the Lord's Name gives peace.
(He) has granted the Lord's devotees the glory of the Name for ever, (and it) rises ever higher, growing more each day.
(He) has seated the Lord's devotees steady in their own home, (and so) has kept his own honour.
The Lord will call the slanderers to account, and give them heavy punishment.
As the slanderers act in their own hearts, such is the fruit they receive.
What is done in secret surely comes to light, even if one does it sitting beneath the earth.
Servant Nanak has blossomed, seeing the Lord's greatness. ॥2॥
316.2: Pauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The Lord himself guards his devotees; what can a sinner do (to them)?
The foolish proud take pride, and die from the poison (of pride) they have eaten.
Their few short days run out, as a ripe crop is reaped.
As are the deeds they do, so are they called.
Servant Nanak's Master is great; he is the Lord of all. ॥30॥
316.3: Salok, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
The manmukhs have strayed from the Root (God) itself; within them are craving, greed and pride.
Their time passes night and day in quarrels; they do not reflect through the Shabad.
The Creator has robbed them of all sense and understanding; all they speak is corrupt.
No gift whatever satisfies them; within them is great thirst, ignorance and darkness.
O Nanak, it is better to break with the manmukhs, whose love is attachment to Maya. ॥1॥
316.4: By the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Those within whom is the love of another: in them love (for God) does not arise through the Guru.
Such a one comes and goes, made to wander (through births); not even in a dream does he know any peace.
He practises falsehood and speaks falsehood; clinging to falsehood, he becomes false himself.
Attachment to Maya is nothing but pain; in pain he perishes, and over his pain he weeps.
O Nanak, the chase after Maya and loving absorption (in God) cannot be joined, however much anyone may wish it.
Those in whose treasury merit has been laid up find peace through the Guru's Shabad. ॥2॥
316.5: Pauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
O Nanak, the Sants and the silent sages reflect, and the four Vedas declare,
that the words the devotees speak with their mouths come to pass.
They are seen openly in the world; all people hear (of them).
Foolish men who quarrel with the Sants find no peace.
The (Sants) long for their good, (but) they burn in their pride.
What can the wretches do, when their lot is evil from the first?
Those struck down by the Supreme Lord belong to no one.
They bear enmity to those who bear none, and by the justice of Dharam they burn.
All whom the Sant has cursed go wandering about.
When the tree is cut at the root, its branches wither. ॥31॥
317.1: Salok, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
O Nanak, the Guru has firmly implanted (in the heart) the Name of the Lord, who has the power to break and to make.
O friend, if you keep God ever in mind, all (your) pain is gone. ॥1॥
317.2: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(As) a hungry man (begging) heeds no shame, disgrace or harsh word,
(so) Nanak begs for the Lord's Name: (O Lord,) in your mercy, grant the union (with you). ॥2॥
317.3: As are the deeds one does, such is the fruit they bear.
One who chews hot, hard iron finds it stuck in his throat.
Because of his deeds, the messenger (of Death) put a halter on his neck and drove him off.
Not one of his hopes was fulfilled; he was forever stealing others' filth (by slandering them).
The ingrate does not acknowledge the good done (to him); (so) he wanders through the births.
All his supports gave out, and he was snatched away from the earth.
He would not let the strife die down, so the Creator took him away.
All who act in ego wither and fall to the ground. ॥32॥
317.4: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Through the Guru, one comes to have knowledge and a discerning intellect;
he sings the Lord's praises, and strings (them) into a garland for his heart.
He is pure, and makes (others) pure, and is of the highest understanding.
Whoever meets him, he carries across (the world-ocean).
Within him the fragrance of the Lord's Name abides.
At the Lord's door he is honoured, and his words are most sublime.
Whoever hears (them) is filled with delight.
O Nanak, meeting the True Guru, (he) has gained the Naam, his wealth and riches. ॥1॥
317.5: By the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
The secret of the True Guru's heart cannot be known, what it is that pleases the perfect True Guru.
The True Guru is at work within the Gursikhs; whoever longs (to serve) the Sikhs comes into the Guru's favour.
What the True Guru says, that work (the Gursikhs) do, and that Jap (repetition of the Name) they practise; the True One accepts the toil of the Gursikhs.
One who wants work done by the Gursikhs without the True Guru's command: no Gursikh comes near him again.
If someone toils with his heart in it before the Guru, the True Guru, the Gursikh does service before him.
One who comes in deceit and rises to leave in deceit: no Gursikh ever goes near him.
Nanak speaks and proclaims (this) divine reflection: whoever has work done (by the Sikhs) without the True Guru's mind consenting, that creature suffers great pain. ॥2॥
317.6: (O God,) you are the True Master, exceedingly great; O greatest of the great, you alone are as great as you.
The one you unite (with you) meets you; you yourself forgive (him), setting his account aside.
The one you yourself unite serves the True Guru with his mind firmly fixed.
You are the True Master, you are the Eternal One; soul, body, skin and bones, all is yours.
Keep (me) as it pleases you, O True One; O greatest of the great, in Nanak's mind is hope in you alone.
318.1: Gauri ki Vaar: by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji); to be sung to the tune of the vaar of Rai Kamaldi Mojdi.
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Salok, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The one who repeats the Name of the Lord, Har Har: his coming (into the world) is approved.
I am a sacrifice to that one who has worshipped God, who is beyond all desire.
His pain of birth and death is cut away, (for) he has met the Lord, the all-knowing Being.
O servant Nanak, in the company of the Sants he crosses the (world-) ocean; the True One is (his) strength. ॥1॥
318.2: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
If, at the rising of the day, (a holy) guest were to come to my house,
I would wash his feet; he would be ever dear to my mind and body.
(Such a guest) would hear the Naam, gather the Naam, and keep himself attuned to the Naam alone.
(Through him my) home and wealth would all be made pure, and (I too) would sing the Lord's praises.
O Nanak, (such) a trader in the Lord's Name I find only by great good fortune. ॥2॥
318.3: (O God,) whatever pleases you is good; your will is true (and unfailing).
You, the One, are at work in all; you are contained in all.
You pervade every place and every space between; within (all) beings (you alone) are known.
Joining the Saadh Sangat, and accepting the True One's will, (he) is found.
Nanak has come to God's refuge, and is ever and ever a sacrifice (to him). ॥1॥
318.4: Salok, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
If you have any awareness, then remember the Master: that Lord alone is true (and eternal).
O Nanak, serve the True Guru, board (his) ship, and cross the terrifying world-ocean. ॥1॥
318.5: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Fools proudly wear clothes as fine as the air.
O Nanak, (those clothes) do not go along (at the end); they burn up and turn to ashes. ॥2॥
318.6: They alone are saved in the world whom the True One has kept safe.
Seeing the faces of those who have tasted the Lord's Amrit, one comes to (true) life.
In the company of the Saadhs, lust, anger, greed and attachment are consumed.
God has shown his own mercy; the Lord himself has tested (and accepted them).
O Nanak, (his) wonders cannot be known; no one can perceive (them). ॥2॥
318.7: Salok, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
O Nanak, that day alone is lovely on which God comes to mind.
The day on which the Supreme Lord is forgotten, cursed is that season, however fair. ॥1॥
318.8: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
O Nanak, (make) friends with him in whose hands is everything.
False friends are they who do not walk a single step with (you). ॥2॥
318.9: The Naam is Amrit, the treasure; O brothers, come together and drink it.
In remembering it there is peace, and every thirst is quenched.
Serve the Guru, the Supreme Lord, and no hunger remains.
All desires are fulfilled, and the deathless state is attained.
O Supreme Lord, you alone are as great as you; Nanak has come to your refuge. ॥3॥
318.10: Salok, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
I have seen (God) in every place; no place is empty (of him).
O Nanak, they have found the purpose (of life) who have met the True Guru. ॥1॥
319.1: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
As the flash of lightning, so is the way of the world.
O Nanak, this alone is the lovely thing: repeating the Name of that Master. ॥2॥
319.2: For all the searching of the Simritis and Shastras, no one has known (his) worth.
The one who joins the Saadh Sangat enjoys the Lord's love.
The True Name of the Creator, the all-pervading Being: this is the mine of jewels.
One on whose forehead it is written, that mortal remembers the Lord.
(O God,) let the True Name be given as provisions (for the journey): (this is) Nanak's welcome as a guest. ॥4॥
319.3: Salok, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Within is anxiety, while to the eye (one looks) happy; (one's) hunger never leaves at all.
O Nanak, no one's pain has been removed without the True Name. ॥1॥
319.4: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
