Robbed are those caravans that did not load (the goods of) Truth.
O Nanak, well done to those who, meeting the Guru, have recognised the One (Lord). ॥2॥
319.5: Where the Saadhs sit, that place is beautiful.
They serve their all-powerful (Lord), and all evil is destroyed.
O Supreme Lord, (you are) the uplifter of the fallen: so the Sants say, (and) so says the Veda.
To love devotion is your age-old way, and it holds good in every age.
Nanak begs for (your) Name alone, which is dear to (his) mind and body. ॥5॥
319.6: Salok, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(When) the sparrow chirps, the dawn breaks, and (the cool breeze) blows in many waves,
O Nanak, the Sants, steeped in the love of the Naam, take on a wondrous form. ॥1॥
319.7: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Joy is in those homes and mansions alone where you, (O God,) come to mind.
O Nanak, all the glories of the world are false friends. ॥2॥
319.8: The wealth of the Lord is the true capital; only a rare one has known it.
O brothers, it comes only to the one to whom the Maker gives it.
The servant dyed in the Lord's love blossoms within, in mind and body.
(He) has sung (the Lord's) praises in the Saadh Sangat, and has consumed all his faults.
O Nanak, he alone has truly lived who has recognised the One (Lord). ॥6॥
319.9: Salok, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The pods of the ak (swallow-wort) look lovely (as long as they) hang at the plant's neck;
O Nanak, (when) separation and parting from their master (the plant) come, (they burst) into a thousand tufts. ॥1॥
319.10: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Those who forget (the Lord) are as good as dead, yet they cannot die outright.
Turned away from Ram, (they writhe) like a thief upon the stake. ॥2॥
319.11: The One God alone is the treasure of peace; he is heard to be imperishable.
He fills the water, the land and the sky; in every heart dwells the Lord, so it is said.
In high and low alike he is the same; he himself has become the worm and the elephant.
Friends, companions, sons and kin are all brought forth by him.
The one to whom Nanak (the Guru), well pleased, gives the Name has enjoyed the Lord's love. ॥7॥
319.12: Salok, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Those who do not forget (the Lord) with every breath and every morsel, in whose minds is the mantra of the Lord's Name:
O Nanak, they alone are blessed; such a one alone is the perfect Sant. ॥1॥
319.13: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(One who) wanders about through all the eight watches, in the torment of (finding) food,
how can he escape falling into Dozakh, when the Rasul does not dwell in his mind? ॥2॥
320.1: Serve that (Guru), O mortals, who holds the Name (of the Lord) in his lap.
(Thus) you will live at ease here, and hereafter (the Name) goes along with (you).
Build the house of true dharma, setting up a pillar that cannot be shaken.
Take the shelter of Narayan, who upholds both faith and the world.
O Nanak, the one who has grasped the Lord's feet keeps firm hold of his place at his court. ॥8॥
320.2: Salok, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The beggar begs for alms: give, my Beloved.
You are the Giver, the Bountiful One; I remember you always.
(Your) measureless storehouses never run out at all.
O Nanak, the Shabad is infinite; it has set everything right. ॥1॥
320.3: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Learn the Shabad, dear ones: it is the support from birth to death.
O Nanak, remembering the One, faces stay bright and one is ever at peace. ॥2॥
320.4: There (in that house of true dharma) the Lord's Amrit is shared out, which makes (all) happy.
(Those who drink it) are not set on the road of Jam, and they do not have to die again.
The one who has come to taste the savour of love: that one alone has the strength to hold it.
(There) the Saadhs utter the Bani, (as if) springs of Amrit were flowing.
Nanak lives by beholding the sight (of them), and keeps (the Name) enshrined within his mind. ॥9॥
320.5: Salok, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
When the perfect True Guru is served, sorrows are destroyed.
O Nanak, when the Name is worshipped, (life's) purpose is fulfilled. ॥1॥
320.6: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The One by remembering whom troubles depart, and bliss and joy come to dwell:
O Nanak, let us repeat (the Name of) that Lord always; may the Name not be forgotten even for an instant. ॥2॥
320.7: Those who have found the Lord, Har Har: how can I count their glory?
Whoever falls at the refuge of the Saadhs is set free, bound though he was.
He sings the praises of the Imperishable One, and does not burn in the womb of births.
The Guru, the Supreme Lord, the Lord, meets him; reading (of the Lord) and understanding, he comes to rest in stillness.
O Nanak, he has found that Master, the Lord, who is inaccessible and unfathomable. ॥10॥
320.8: Salok, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(O mortal,) you do not do your own (true) work, and you roam the world headstrong.
O Nanak, once the Name is forgotten, what kind of peace can there be? ॥1॥
320.9: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The bitterness of the poison (of Maya) is in all; it clings (to everyone) in the world.
O Nanak, the servant (of God) has reflected and found that the Lord's Name (alone) is sweet. ॥2॥
320.10: This is the mark of the Saadh: meeting him, one swims across.
Jam's servant does not come near, and one does not die ever again.
The world-ocean, this world full of poison: one crosses over to its far shore.
Weave in your mind the garland of the Lord's virtues: (thus) the Lord takes all filth away.
O Nanak, (they) remain united with the Beloved, the Supreme Lord, Narhari. ॥11॥
320.11: Salok, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
O Nanak, approved is the coming of those in whose minds the Lord has come to dwell.
Idle talk, empty as chaff, is of no use, my friend. ॥1॥
320.12: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The Supreme Lord God, all-pervading, inaccessible, wondrous, has come into view to the one
who, O Nanak, by the perfect Guru's grace, has made the Name of Ram his wealth. ॥2॥
321.1: Deceit does not work with the Master; through greed and attachment (people) come to ruin.
They do evil deeds, asleep in the intoxication of Maya.
Again and again they are made to wander through births, and are abandoned on the road of Jam.
They reap what they themselves have done, yoked to sorrow.
O Nanak, once the Name is forgotten, every season is ill. ॥12॥
321.2: Salok, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Rising, sitting and sleeping, (such a one) has the same unbroken peace.
O Nanak, when the Name is praised, mind and body become cool. ॥1॥
321.3: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Smeared with greed, (the world) ever roams about; no one does what is truly for his own good.
O Nanak, the one whom the Guru meets: in that one's mind he (the Lord) comes to dwell. ॥2॥
321.4: All (worldly) things are bitter; the Name of the True One (alone) is sweet.
Those servants of the Lord have known (its) savour, the Saadhs who have tasted it and seen.
In the mind of that one alone does (the Name) come to dwell, for whom the Supreme Lord has so written.
(To that one) the one stainless Lord (is seen) pervading all, and the love of another is slain.
With palms joined Nanak begs (this of) the Lord; God gives (it) when he is pleased. ॥13॥
321.5: Salok, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
That asking is the best which asks for the One alone.
O Nanak, other talk, empty of the Master, is worthless. ॥1॥
321.6: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
One whose mind is pierced with love (of the Lord), such a knower (of God), is rare indeed.
Such a Sant is the uniter (with the Lord), O Nanak; (he) makes the path smooth and level. ॥2॥
321.7: Serve him alone, O my soul, the Giver, the Forgiver.
Remembering Govind, all sins are destroyed.
The Saadh (the Guru) has shown the way to the Lord: let us repeat the Guru's mantra.
(Then) all the tastes of Maya (seem) insipid, and the Lord is dear to the mind.
O Nanak, meditate on the Supreme God, who has given (you) life. ॥14॥
321.8: Salok, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The season for (sowing) the True Name has come; whoever sows, he eats (its fruit).
O Nanak, (it) is his alone in whose lot (it) has come written. ॥1॥
321.9: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
If one must ask, (let it be) for the One True (Name); (but it comes only to the one) to whom (God) himself gives it when pleased.
That (Name), eating which the mind is satisfied, is, O Nanak, the Master's gift. ॥2॥
321.10: They alone earn profit in the world whose capital is the wealth of the Lord.
They do not know the love of another; their hope is in the True One.
They have served the One, the Unshakable; all else is perishable.
One who forgets the Supreme Lord: (every) breath of his is in vain.
Hugging (his) servants to his breast, (God) has saved them; Nanak is a sacrifice (to him). ॥15॥
321.11: Salok, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The Supreme Lord gave the command, and the rain fell, gently, of its own accord.
Grain and wealth sprang up in plenty; the earth was filled, fully content.
(Such a one) utters (the Lord's) virtues for ever and ever, and pain and poverty have vanished.
What was written from before has been received; (it) has come by his will.
The Supreme God has given life; O Nanak, meditate on him. ॥1॥
321.12: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The state of true life (lies in this): to remember the One alone, (the Lord) beyond desire.
There is no other place; how else can (the mind) take comfort?
(I) have looked at the whole world: there is no peace without the Name.
Body and wealth will turn to ashes; only a rare one knows (this).
Pleasures, beauty and tastes are in vain; what are you doing, O mortal?
The one whom (God) himself leads astray has not known (his) power.
Those dyed in (the Lord's) love sing of the True One, (the Lord) beyond desire.
Says Nanak: if (beings) are pleasing to you, (they come) to your refuge, at your door. ॥2॥
322.1: There is no birth and death for those who cling to the Lord's hem.
Awake in the Lord's Kirtan, they have been approved while still living.
Those who have found the Saadh Sangat are the truly fortunate.
Once the Name is forgotten, life is cursed: (it) snaps like a raw thread.
O Nanak, holier than lakhs and crores of Prayags is the dust (of the feet) of the Saadh. ॥16॥
322.2: Salok, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Like the earth in its beauty, its grass studded with jewels (of dew), is the mind in which the Lord, the Being of love, has come to dwell.
All tasks become easy when Guru Nanak, the True Guru, is pleased. ॥1॥
322.3: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Roaming and roaming in the ten directions, over waters, mountains and forests,
wherever the kite saw a carcass, there it came down and settled. ॥2॥
322.4: From whom all comforts and fruits are sought: may I live by that True One.
May I see the Supreme Lord close at hand, and meditate on the Name of the One.
Becoming the dust (of the feet) of all, may I merge in the Lord.
May I cause no being pain, and go (to my true) home with honour.
May Nanak tell (all) of the Creator, the Being who makes the fallen pure. ॥17॥
322.5: Salok, a Doha, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
I have made the One my Friend, who is mighty with every power.
My soul is cut in pieces as a sacrifice (to him); the Lord is the (true) treasure of mind and body. ॥1॥
322.6: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
If you take (my) hand, dear Beloved, I will never let you go.
Those who forsake the Lord are the wicked; they fall into the (piercing) torment of Dozakh. ॥2॥
322.7: The Lord in whose house are all treasures: whatever he does comes to pass.
The Sants live by repeating (his Name) over and over; he washes off (their) filth of sins.
(Those) in whose hearts (his) lotus feet dwell: he takes away all (their) troubles.
The one whom the perfect Guru meets does not weep (in the round of) dying and being born.
Nanak thirsts greatly for the sight of God; (God) grants (it) out of (his) grace. ॥18॥
322.8: Salok Dakhna, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
If you cast off even a little of (your) doubt and love the Beloved alone,
then wherever you go, there he is present. ॥1॥
322.9: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Players of the stick game (khundi), they mount a fine horse and grip gun-butts;
with a chicken's flight, they stir up their hearts to (fly) with swans. ॥2॥
322.10: One who utters the Lord('s Name) with the tongue and listens to it with the ears is saved, O friend.
Pure are those hands that write the Lord's praise with devotion.
(It is as if) that one has bathed at the sixty-eight places of pilgrimage and done every good deed.
Such ones are saved from the world-ocean, and have won the fortress of Maya.
O Nanak, serve the infinite Beloved, who has attached (them) to his hem and saved them. ॥19॥
323.1: Salok, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Wretched affairs are a losing trade, (when through them) the One does not come to mind.
O Nanak, those very bodies split open, (the bodies of those) who forget the Master. ॥1॥
323.2: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
From a ghost, he, the Creator, has made (one) a god.
He has saved all the Sikhs; God has set their tasks right.
Seizing the slanderers, he has dashed them to the ground; false (they stand) at his court.
Great is the God of Nanak: he himself fashions (all) and puts (them) right. ॥2॥
323.3: God is without end; there is no limit to him at all; everything is his doing.
The Master is beyond reach and beyond the senses, the support of (all) beings.
Giving (his) hand, he protects (all), and does the feeding and sustaining (of all).
He himself is merciful and forgiving; repeating (the Name of) the True One, (beings) cross over.
(O Lord,) whatever pleases you is good; servant Nanak is in your refuge. ॥20॥
323.4: Salok, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Those whose (Master) is that God are left with no hunger of any kind.
O Nanak, by clinging to (his) feet everyone is saved. ॥1॥
323.5: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The beggar asks for the Name every day, and the Master grants (his plea).
O Nanak, (the one whose) patron (jajman) is the Supreme God has no hunger at all. ॥2॥
323.6: (The minstrel's) mind is dyed with Govind; the True One('s Name) is (his) food and clothing.
Love fixed on the Lord's Name: these are (his) elephants and horses.
To meditate (on God) and never turn his face away: (this is his) kingdom, lands and abundant joy.
The minstrel begs at God's door, and never leaves that door.
O Nanak, this is the longing in (his) mind and body: he yearns for God every day.
323.7: Raag Gauri, the hymns of the Bhagats.
There is one God, Ik Oankar, the One who pervades all and is ever the same; his Name is Sat (the One who truly is); he is the Creator, the Being who dwells in all, realised by the Guru's grace.
Raag Gauri Guareri, fourteen Chaupade of Sri Kabir Ji.
Now, as I burned, I have found the water of Ram.
The water of Ram has cooled my burning body.
One goes off to the forests to subdue the mind,
(but) that water is not found without the Lord (Bhagvant).
The fire that has burned gods and men:
from its burning the water of Ram has saved (his) servants.
In the world-ocean, (become for them) an ocean of peace,
they go on drinking, and the water never runs short.
the water of Ram has quenched my thirst. ॥4॥
323.8: Raag Gauri, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
O Madho, my thirst for the water (of your Name) does not leave;
in the water, a fire (of longing) has flared up all the more.
You are the ocean, and I the fish of (that) water:
in the water I live; without the water I waste away.
You are the cage, and I your little parrot:
what harm can Jam, the cat, do me?
You are the tree, and I the bird (in it);
unfortunate (that I am), I have not had the sight of you.
You are the True Guru, and I a new disciple;
says Kabir: meet me, (now) at the last hour. ॥4॥
324.1: Raag Gauri, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
When I came to know (God) as the One alone, (in all),
why then have people taken it ill?
I am without honour; I have lost my own honour:
let none of you come following in my track.
If I am bad, I am bad within my own mind;
I have no partnership or fellowship with anyone.
Of honour and dishonour I feel no shame;
you will know when your own pretence is laid bare.
Says Kabir: honour is (to be) accepted by the Lord;
leave all else, and worship Ram alone. ॥4॥
324.2: Raag Gauri, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
If union (with God) were found by roaming about naked,
every deer of the forest would be liberated.
What (comes) of going naked, what of wearing skins,
when you do not recognise the all-pervading Lord (Atam Ram)?
If attainment were won by shaving the head,
why has no sheep gone to liberation?
If one could cross over by holding back the seed, O brother,
why has the eunuch not attained the supreme state?
Says Kabir: listen, O men, O brothers:
without the Name of Ram, who has ever attained liberation? ॥4॥
324.3: Raag Gauri, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
(Those who) bathe at evening and at dawn
are like the frogs in the water.
If there is no love for Ram, Ram (in them),
they all go into the hands of Dharam Raj.
(Those who,) in love with the body, put on many guises
have no compassion in them, not even in a dream.
Many clever men recite the four Vedas,
(but only) the holy find peace in this ocean of strife.
Says Kabir: why go on at length?
Let us leave everything and drink the supreme essence (of the Name). ॥4॥
324.4: Raag Gauri, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
Of what use is chanting, austerity, fasting or worship
to one in whose heart is the love of another?
O people, let the mind be fixed on Madho;
by cleverness Chaturbhuj (the four-armed Lord) is not found.
Cast off greed and doing things for show;
cast off lust, anger and pride.
Performing rites, (people) are bound in self-conceit;
Says Kabir: (he) is found through devotion;
with an innocent love, Raghurai is met. ॥4॥
324.5: Raag Gauri, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
In the dwelling of the womb there is no family and no caste;
all have come into being from the seed of Brahm (God).
Tell me, O pandit, since when have you been Brahmins?
Do not waste your life calling (yourselves) Brahmins over and over.
If you are a Brahmin, born of a Brahmin woman,
then why did you not come (into the world) by some other way?
How are you Brahmins, and how are we Shudras?
How is there blood in us, and how milk in you?
Says Kabir: whoever reflects on Brahm (God)
is the one we call a Brahmin. ॥4॥
325.1: Raag Gauri, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
In darkness, (forgetting God,) no one ever sleeps in peace;
king and pauper both alike weep.
As long as the tongue does not utter (the Name of) Ram,
(people) will go on being born and dying, and weeping.
(Maya is) as the shade of a tree is seen to be;
when the breath of life is gone, tell me, whose is Maya then?
As the sound is absorbed into the instrument (when the playing stops),
how can anyone fathom the secret of the dead?
As the swan stays close to the lake, so death stays close to the body;
drink the elixir of Ram, O Kabir. ॥4॥
325.2: Raag Gauri, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
The creation is of the Light (God's making); the light (of mind) in the creation
bears fruits of glass and of pearl.
Which is that home which may be called free of fear,
where fear runs away and one may live fearless?
At a river's bank or a place of pilgrimage the mind is not set at ease;
(people there) remain entangled in good deeds and bad.
Sin and virtue: the two are alike.
In your own home (within) is the paras (the touchstone that turns iron to gold, the Lord); give up (seeking) other qualities.
O Kabir, do not turn sullenly from the Name of the Lord beyond the qualities (nirgun);
engage this (mind), and stay absorbed in this (Name). ॥4॥
325.3: Raag Gauri, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
Those people (who say they) have known the One beyond measure and beyond the mind
have entered Baikunth by talk alone.
I do not know where Baikunth is;
(yet) all say: we must go there, go there.
By saying and being told, the mind is not set at ease;
the mind is satisfied (only) when Haumai has departed from it.
As long as there is hope of Baikunth in the mind,
there is no dwelling at (the Lord's) feet.
Says Kabir: what more is there to say of this?
The Saadh Sangat is Baikunth itself. ॥4॥
325.4: Raag Gauri, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
(A being) comes into being, takes bodily form, and having taken form, passes away;
while our eyes look on, this world is going.
Do you not die of shame, saying: this house is mine?
At the end, nothing at all is yours.
With countless efforts the body is reared;
(yet) when death comes, it is burned with fire.
The body whose limbs are rubbed with perfume and sandalwood:
that body burns along with the wood.
Says Kabir: listen, O men of worth:
(this) form will perish, with all the world looking on. ॥4॥
325.5: Raag Gauri, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
Grieve (only) if you yourself were to live on.
I shall not die; it is the world that will die;
now I have met the Giver of life.
(One) makes this body fragrant with perfumes;
in those pleasures (he) forgets (the Lord of) supreme bliss.
(The body is) one little well, (the five senses) five women who draw its water;
the defeated intellect draws (water) with a broken rope.
Says Kabir: I have weighed one thought in my mind:
(now) there is neither that little well nor the drawers of water. ॥4॥
325.6: Raag Gauri, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
As the unmoving and the moving, as worms and moths,
(we) have taken countless births of many kinds.
Many such homes (bodies) have we lived in
when, O Ram, we came (again and again) into the womb.
(We have been) yogis, men of restraint, ascetics and celibates;
sometimes kings beneath the royal canopy, sometimes beggars.
The Saakats die, (but) the Sants all live:
with their tongues they drink the elixir of Ram.
Says Kabir: O God, show mercy;
worn out, we have fallen (at your door); now grant (us) the perfect (state). ॥4॥
326.1: Raag Gauri, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji, written together with (words of) the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Such a wonder Kabir has seen:
mistaking it for curd, one churns water.
The donkey grazes on green shoots;
rising each day, it laughs and brays, and (at last) dies.
leaping and leaping it grazes, and falls into the netherworld (Rasatal).
Says Kabir: the play has come into the open:
the ewe is ever suckling at her lamb.
Dwelling on Ram, understanding has come to light;
says Kabir: the Guru has given (this) insight. ॥4॥
326.2: Raag Gauri, Panchpade of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
(People say:) like a fish that has left the water and come out,
(so) I was empty of austerity in my former birth.
Now tell me, O Ram, what will my state be?
I have left Banaras; (is it true that) my wits have grown small?
(They say:) he wasted his whole life in Shiva's city (Kashi),
(and) at the hour of death he got up and came to Magahar.
For many years (he) did austerities at Kashi;
(yet) when death came, (he became) a dweller of Magahar.
(But I) have held Kashi and Magahar to be alike;
with shallow devotion, how will (anyone) cross over?
Says (Kabir): the gurus, Ganesh, Shiva and everyone know (it):
Kabir has died dwelling on Sri Ram. ॥5॥
326.3: Raag Gauri, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
The body whose limbs are rubbed with perfume and sandalwood:
that body burns along with the wood.
What greatness is there in this body and wealth?
They lie on the earth, (left) on this side; they do not go (with you).
Those who spend the night in sleep and the day at work,
and do not take the Lord's Name for a single moment;
who hold (the falcon's) cord in their hand and chew betel in their mouth:
when death comes, they are bound fast like a thief.
One who, through the Guru's teaching, sings the Lord's praises with deep relish
finds peace dwelling on Ram, Ram alone.
The one in whom (God), by his grace, implants the Naam firmly:
in him he makes the sweet fragrance of Har Har dwell.
Says Kabir: remember (him), O blind one;
Ram is true; all (worldly) business is false. ॥6॥
326.4: Raag Gauri, Tipade Chartuke of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
(Those who were) Jams have turned and become (forms of) Ram;
sorrows have perished, and peace has come to rest.
Enemies have turned and become friends;
the Saakats have turned and become good men at heart.
Now I take everything as well-being;
peace came when I came to know Gobind.
In the body there were millions of afflictions;
they have turned into peace, and samadhi in Sahaj.
(The mind) recognises its own self, and (sees) him alone, all in all;
no disease, nor the three fevers, afflict (it now).
Now the mind has turned and become (one with) the Eternal;
this I knew when I died while still alive.
Says Kabir: I am merged in peace and in Sahaj;
I neither fear, nor make others afraid. ॥3॥
327.1: Raag Gauri, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
When the body has died, into which home does the soul go?
(It stays) steeped, through the Shabad, in the Lord beyond (Maya), the Unending.
Whoever has known Ram, he alone has recognised (this joy),
as a mute's mind is satisfied with sugar (and he cannot tell of it).
Such wisdom Banwari (the Lord himself) imparts:
O mind, hold the breath steady in the Sukhmana channel.
Take such a Guru that you need not take another;
enjoy such a state that you need enjoy no other;
hold such meditation that you need hold no other;
die in such a way that you need not die again.
Turning (my mind) back, I join the Ganga and the Jamuna;
without water, I bathe at (their) confluence within the mind.
To look on (all) with even eyes: this is (my) way of dealing;
having reflected on the Essence, what need of other reflection?
Like water, fire, air, earth and sky
is the life I live, (abiding) near the Lord.
Says Kabir: I meditate on the Niranjan;
I go to that home from which I shall not come back again. ॥4॥
327.2: Raag Gauri, Tipade of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
(Ram) is not won by weighing out gold;
I have bought Ram at the price of my mind.
Now I know Ram as my own;
my mind has come to trust (in him), naturally, in Sahaj.
Brahma, telling of (him) over and over, did not find his end;
through devotion to Ram, (he) has come to (my) home while I sat (there).
Says Kabir: I have given up the restless intellect;
devotion to Ram alone is my own share. ॥3॥
327.3: Raag Gauri, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
The death that has struck terror into the whole world:
(what) that death (is), the Guru's Shabad has made plain (to me).
Now how can I die? My mind has embraced (that) death (to self).
Those who have not known Ram die and die (again), and depart.
(but) one who dies in Sahaj, he alone becomes immortal.
Says Kabir: bliss has arisen in my mind;
doubt has gone; the supreme bliss remains. ॥3॥
327.4: Raag Gauri, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
There is no (one) place (of the pain); where shall I put the remedy?
Searching the body, I do not find the place.
Only the one it has struck knows the pain:
(the pain of) the sharp-pointed arrows of devotion to Ram.
I see all the brides alike;
how am I to know which one the Husband holds dear?
Says Kabir: she on whose forehead good fortune is (written):
her the Husband, leaving all (others), comes to meet. ॥3॥
328.1: Raag Gauri, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
One who has such a Master as the Lord, O brother:
to (his door) go liberations without number, to plead.
Now say: O Ram, (my) trust is in you;
then why be beholden to anyone?
He who bears the weight of the three worlds:
Says Kabir: I have weighed one thought in my mind:
what can (the child) do if the mother herself gives poison? ॥3॥
328.2: Raag Gauri, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
Without sat (faithfulness), how can a woman be a sati?
O pandit, reflect in your heart and see.
Without love, how can affection take hold?
As long as (Maya's) relish (remains), there is no love (for the Lord).
One who, in his heart, holds the Shah's wife (Maya) to be true
will not meet Ramaiya (the all-pervading Lord), even in a dream.
She who gives over body, mind, wealth, home and self (to the Husband):
she alone is the happy wife, says Kabir. ॥3॥
328.3: Raag Gauri, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
The whole world is in the grip of the poison of Maya;
this poison has drowned the whole family.
O man, why have you sunk your boat in the shallows?
You have broken (your love) with the Lord and joined it to the poison.
Gods and men are burnt up, for a fire (of craving) has broken out;
the water is near at hand, yet the beast (man) will not make the effort to drink it.
Through remembering and remembering, the water (of the Name) has sprung forth;
says Kabir: that water is pure. ॥3॥
328.4: Raag Gauri, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
The family in which no son reflects on divine wisdom —
why did his mother not become a widow?
The man who has not practised devotion to Ram —
why did that sinner not die at birth?
Many, many pregnancies have miscarried; why was this one spared?
He lives in the world like a leper with wasted arms.
Says Kabir: those who are handsome and fair of form
are, without the Name, like the hunchbacked and the ugly. ॥3॥
328.5: Raag Gauri, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
The servants who take the Name of the Master —
to them I am ever a sacrifice.
One who sings the praises of the pure Lord is pure;
that brother is dear to my mind.
Those in whose hearts Ram dwells in fullness —
I am the dust of their lotus feet.
A weaver by caste, but steadfast of mind,
Kabir, in Sahaj, ever in Sahaj, utters (the Lord's) praises. ॥3॥
328.6: Raag Gauri, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
My still is in the sky (of the raised mind), and from it the sweet nectar drips;
to gather this supreme essence, the body has become the firewood.
That one is called intoxicated in Sahaj
who drinks the elixir of Ram through reflection on divine wisdom.
When Sahaj, the woman who pours the wine, comes and meets (one),
then, intoxicated in bliss, (one's life) passes night and day.
When, recognising (him), (I) fixed my mind on the Niranjan,
says Kabir: then (I) attained the inner experience (of God). ॥3॥
328.7: Raag Gauri, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
Whatever the mind's nature, it pervades the whole mind;
(so) by killing the mind, what perfection has anyone established?
Who is that silent sage who kills the mind?
Tell me, by killing the mind, whom does he carry across?
Everyone speaks from within the mind;
without killing the mind, there is no devotion.
Says Kabir: for one who knows this secret,
(his) mind becomes Madhusudan, the God who lights the three worlds. ॥3॥
329.1: Raag Gauri, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
Those stars that are seen in the sky —
Tell me, O pandit, on whom does the sky rest?
Only a fortunate one, wise of understanding, understands (this).
The sun and the moon give light;
in all is spread the expanse of Brahm (God).
Says Kabir: he alone will know (this)
in whose heart is Ram, and in whose mouth is Ram alone. ॥3॥
329.2: Raag Gauri, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
The Smriti, O brother, is the daughter of the Veda;
she has come bringing a chain and a rope.
She herself has bound her own city (those who follow her);
(holding them) in the noose of attachment, she has aimed the arrow of death.
(This noose) cannot be cut, cut as one may, nor will it break;
she has become a she-serpent, and devours the world.
She who has plundered the whole world before my eyes —
says Kabir: I have escaped (her) by uttering (the Name of) Ram. ॥3॥
329.3: Raag Gauri, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
I put the halter (on the horse of the mind) and fit it with the bridle;
with the saddle of (seeing the Lord in) all, I gallop (it) through the sky.
Let us ride (the horse of) reflection on our own (true self),
and set our foot in the stirrup of Sahaj.
Come, (my horse,) let me take you and carry you across to Baikunth;
if you balk, I shall strike (you) with the whip of love.
who stay apart from the Vedas and the Kateb. ॥3॥
329.4: Raag Gauri, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
The mouth with which the five ambrosial foods were eaten —
to that mouth, before (one's own people's) eyes, the burning brand is put.
O Ram, my King, cut away this one pain of mine:
the burning in the fire, and the dwelling in the womb.
The body comes to ruin in many ways and manners:
some burn it, some bury it in the earth.
Says Kabir: O Lord, let (me) see (your) feet;
after that, why not send Jam, if you will? ॥3॥
329.5: Raag Gauri, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
(The Master) himself is the fire, and himself the wind;
if the Master burns (one), who can save?
While repeating Ram, what if the body should burn?
The mind remains absorbed in the Name of Ram.
What of anyone's is burnt? Who suffers loss?
Saringpani is playing, like an actor in his play.
Says Kabir: utter (just) these two words:
if the Master (so wills), he will keep (me) safe. ॥3॥
329.6: Raag Gauri, Dupade of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
I have not set my mind on the meditation of Yoga;
without detachment, there is no release from Maya.
when the support of the Name of Ram is not there?
Says Kabir: I search (as far as) the heavens,
yet I see no other equal to Ram. ॥2॥
330.1: Raag Gauri, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
The head on which (one) ties the turban, arranging it with care —
that head the crows will dress with their beaks.
Why take pride in this body and wealth?
Why do you not hold fast to the Name of Ram?
Says Kabir: listen, O my mind,
this same will be your state too.
The thirty-five Pade of Gauri Guareri.
330.2: Raag Gauri Guareri, an Ashtapadi of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
In asking for comfort, pain comes to meet one;
I do not care to ask for that comfort.
The attention is still on the poison of Maya, with hope of comforts;
how, (then,) shall there be a dwelling in Ram the King?
Of this comfort even Shiv and Brahma were afraid;
that comfort we have taken to be true.
Sanak and his brothers, the sage Narad, and Shesh Nag:
even they did not see the mind within the body.
Let someone search out this mind, O brother:
when the body falls away, where is the mind absorbed?
By the Guru's grace, Jaidev and Namdev —
these have known (it), through the love of devotion.
For this mind there is no coming and going;
one whose doubt is gone has recognised the True One.
This mind has no form or outline at all;
it came to be by Hukam, and understanding the Hukam, it merges (in the Lord).
Rare is the one who knows the secret of this mind;
absorbed in this mind, (one) becomes Sukhdev (bliss and light itself).
The Soul is One, and (it is in) all bodies;
Kabir remembers this Mind (the One in all). ॥9॥
330.3: Raag Gauri Guareri, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
Those who stay awake night and day in the Name of the One —
so many of them, their attention attuned (to it), have reached perfection.
Seekers at their disciplines, Siddhas and all the sages have failed;
the One Name alone is the Kalp tree (that grants every wish), and it carries (them) across.
Those whom the Lord has drawn (to himself) do not become other (than him);
says Kabir: (they) have recognised the Name of Ram. ॥2॥
330.4: Raag Gauri, and Sorath too: the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
O shameless soul, have you no shame?
Forsaking the Lord, why do you go to (the door of) another?
it does not become that servant to go to another's house.
the Lord is ever with (you), not far away.
He at whose feet even Kavla (Lakshmi, the goddess of wealth) has taken refuge —
tell me, O man, what is lacking in his house?
is all-powerful, (our) own Master, and the Giver.
Says Kabir: in the world he alone is complete
in whose heart there is no other (but the Lord). ॥5॥
331.1: Who is anyone's son, and who anyone's father?
Who dies, and who causes (another) grief?
The Lord, the cheat, has given the world his cheat's drug;
parted from the Lord, how can I live, O my mother?
Who is anyone's husband, and who anyone's wife?
Reflect within the body, and grasp this truth.
Says Kabir: (my) mind is won over by the cheat;
the drug's spell is gone, (for I) have recognised the cheat. ॥3॥
331.2: Now Ram, the King, has become my helper;
cutting away birth and death, I have attained the supreme state.
He has joined me to the Saadh Sangat,
and set me free from the five enemies.
With my tongue I chant the Naam, the nectar of life;
he has made me his own servant, without price.
The True Guru has done (me) a great kindness:
he has drawn me out of the world-ocean.
Love for (the Lord's) lotus feet has taken hold (of me);
Gobind dwells in my mind day after day.
The live coal of Maya's burning heat has gone out;
there is contentment in the mind, and the Naam is (its) support.
God, the Master, is present in water and on land;
whichever way I turn my eyes, the Knower of hearts is there.
He himself has made his devotion firm (in me).
O my brother, the writ of the past has come to me.
Whomever (God) blesses with grace, for him all is made complete;
Kabir's Master is the One who raises up the poor. ॥4॥
331.3: Sutak is in the water, Sutak is on the land; Sutak keeps arising (everywhere).
At birth there is Sutak, and at death again Sutak; by Sutak the people are ruined.
Tell me, O pandit, who is pure?
Dwell on such knowledge, O my friend.
In the eyes is Sutak, in speech is Sutak, and Sutak is in the ears;
rising or sitting, Sutak clings (to one); Sutak falls on the kitchen (too).
Everyone knows the way to be caught; the way to get free, hardly one (knows).
Says Kabir: one who reflects on Ram in the heart is not touched by Sutak. ॥3॥
331.4: Raag Gauri, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
Settle one dispute (for me), O Ram,
if you have any work for your servant.
Is this mind the greater, or he in whom the mind has come to trust?
Is Ram the greater, or one who has come to know Ram?
Is Brahma the greater, or the One who brought him forth?
Is the Veda the greater, or the source from which it came?
Says Kabir: I have grown uneasy (over this):
is the place of pilgrimage the greater, or the servant of the Lord? ॥3॥
331.5: Raag Gauri Cheti, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
Look, O brother: the storm of (divine) knowledge has come;
all the thatch of doubt has blown away; tied though it was by Maya, it does not stay.
The two posts of double-mindedness have fallen, the ridge-beam of attachment has snapped;
the roof-thatch of craving has come down to the earth, and the vessel of evil counsel is smashed.
In the rain that pours down after the storm, your servant is soaked through.
Says Kabir: light filled my mind when I recognised the risen sun. ॥2॥
332.1: Raag Gauri Cheti, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
(Some) neither listen to the Lord's praise nor sing of the Lord's virtues,
yet by talk alone they pull the sky down.
What is there to say to such people?
Those whom God has kept outside devotion: let us always stay wary of them.
They themselves give no one even a palmful of water,
yet they slander the one who brought the Ganga down (to earth).
Sitting or rising, they walk in crooked ways;
lost themselves, they bring others to ruin too.
Apart from evil talk they know nothing else;
they do not heed even what Brahma says.
Lost themselves, they lead others astray too;
they set fire to the house and sleep inside it.
They mock others, though they are one-eyed themselves;
332.2: Raag Gauri Bairagan, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
No one honours his forebears while they live; once they are dead, people have the shraadh done for them.
Tell me, how can the poor forebears receive (that food)? Crows and dogs eat it.
Let someone tell me what well-being is.
Crying for well-being, well-being, the world perishes; how can well-being come at all?
They shape gods and goddesses from clay, and before them offer up a life.
Such are those called your forebears: they take nothing by asking for it with their own mouths.
They kill the living and worship the lifeless; at the last hour it will weigh heavy (on them).
They have not known the state that Ram's Name brings; the worldly are drowned in fears.
They worship gods and goddesses and stay unsteady; the Supreme Lord they have not known.
Says Kabir: they have not remembered the Lord who has no lineage (Akul); they cling to the poison (of Maya). ॥4॥
332.3: Raag Gauri, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
One who dies while living, and, so dying, lives again, is thus absorbed in Sunn (the stillness where no worldly thought stirs):
amid the black stain of Maya one dwells in the Niranjan, and is not cast into the world-ocean again.
O my Ram, let the milk be churned in this way:
keep the mind steady through the Guru's teaching; this is how the Amrit is drunk.
By the Guru's arrow (of the Word) the adamant-hard (veil of illusion) has been pierced, and the state of light has shone forth;
the illusion of the rope (taken for a snake) in the darkness of Shakti (Maya) is ended, and the dwelling is fixed, unmoving, in the home of Shiv (the Lord, the source of good).
She (Maya) has pierced this world, O brother, drawing her bow without an arrow;
the wind tosses the kite about in all ten directions, but (my) string has stayed tied in loving attention.
In the state of unman the mind is absorbed in Sunn; duality and evil-mindedness have fled.
Says Kabir: I have seen a wonder known from within; my attention is fixed on Ram's Name. ॥4॥
333.1: Raag Gauri Bairagan, Tipade of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
As the wind (of the mind) is turned back, the six chakras are pierced, and the attention falls in love with Sunn.
He neither comes nor goes, neither dies nor is born: seek him, O bairagi.
O my mind, the mind itself, turned back (from the world), has merged (in the Lord).
By the Guru's grace the understanding has become other; else (it) was a stranger (to the Lord).
The near grows far, and the far grows near again, for one who has known (the Lord) as he truly is.
It is like a syrup made from sugar-candy: only one who has drunk it knows (its taste).
To whom can the tale of you, beyond the qualities (nirgun), be told? Rare is one so discerning.
Says Kabir: whoever has put fire to the fuse has seen a flash to match. ॥3॥
333.2: Raag Gauri, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
There, there is neither rain nor sea, neither sun nor shade; there, nothing is created or dissolved.
Neither life nor death, pain nor pleasure touches (one) there; Sunn and Samadhi, neither of the two, is there.
The tale of Sahaj cannot be told; it is unlike any other:
it goes on no scale, and is never used up; it seems neither light nor heavy.
Below and above, neither of the two is there; neither night nor day is there.
Water is not there, nor wind, nor fire either; there the True Guru abides.
The Lord, beyond reach and beyond the senses, dwells there unbroken; by the Guru's grace he is found.
Says Kabir: I am a sacrifice to my Guru; let us stay joined in the Sat Sangat. ॥3॥
333.3: Raag Gauri, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
Sin and virtue, a pair of oxen, have been bought; the breath has been laid out as capital;
within the body the sack is filled with craving: in this way the caravan (of laden oxen) has been bought.
Such a master-merchant is our Ram:
he has made the whole world a banjara (a travelling trader).
Lust and anger, the two, have become toll-collectors; the mind's waves are the robbers on the road;
the five elements, joining together, settle the toll, and the caravan has crossed to the far side.
Says Kabir: listen, O Sants, this is how it has now turned out:
climbing the steep pass, one ox has tired, and has gone off, throwing down its load. ॥3॥
333.4: Raag Gauri, a Panchpada of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
In the parents' home there are but four days; to the in-laws' home (the soul-bride) must go.
The blind world, foolish and childish, does not know this.
Tell me: the bride stands still in her workaday wrap (dadia),
and the guests have come to the house: those come to take her away in the muklava have arrived.
That little well that is seen: who is it lowering the rope into it?
The rope has broken along with the pitcher, and the water-carrier has risen and gone.
If the Master becomes kind and shows grace, (the soul-bride) accomplishes her own task;
then she is known as a happy wife, (when) she reflects on the Guru's Shabad.
All (the world) wanders bound by its past deeds: reflect, and see.
What is to be said to her? What can the poor thing do?
Without hope she has risen and gone; her mind finds no steadiness to hold.
Stay at the Lord's feet; run to his refuge, O Kabir. ॥5॥
334.1: Raag Gauri, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
Yogis say: yoga is good and sweet, there is nothing else, O brother.
The shaven ascetics, the shorn sannyasis, and those who cry the one word (Alakh): these all say they have attained siddhi.
Without the Lord, the blind wander lost in doubt;
those to whom I go to get myself released are themselves bound in many nooses.
(The soul) merges back into that from which it sprang only when this way (of pride) is forgotten:
these all say: we are pandits, men of virtue, warriors, givers; we alone are great.
Only the one whom (the Lord) gives understanding understands; without understanding, how can one live?
(When) the True Guru is met, the darkness ends; in this way the ruby (of the Name) is found.
Casting off the vices to left and right, let us hold fast to the state of (union with) the Lord.
Says Kabir: the mute has eaten molasses; asked about it, what can he say? ॥4॥
334.2: Raag Gauri Poorbi, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Where once there was something, nothing remains; nor are the five elements there.
Ida, Pingala and Sukhmana: O man, where have these flawed (practices) gone?
The thread is broken, the sky (the Tenth Gate) has perished; where has the one who spoke in you been absorbed?
This doubt troubles me night and day; no one explains it to me.
Where the universe (was beheld), the body is not there; nor is the mind, the maker (of it all), there.
The Joiner is ever detached; in whom, then, can this (speaker) be said to be?
(The body) is not held together by joining, nor broken apart by breaking, until its time to perish comes.
Who is whose master, and who whose servant? Who will go to whom?
Says Kabir: (my) attention stays fixed (there) where (the Lord) dwells day and night.
His secret he alone truly knows; he is forever imperishable. ॥4॥
334.3: Raag Gauri, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
Attention (fixed on the Lord) and remembrance (of him) are the earrings in my two ears; true knowledge (of him) is the patched coat I wear.
My seat, where I sit, is in the cave of Sunn; to be free of (worldly) imaginings is my path.
O my King, I am a bairagi yogi;
I neither die, nor grieve, nor know separation.
Through all the realms and the universe (sounds) my horn (singi); the whole world is my pouch for ashes.
My trance has set in: the three qualities are turned back, and one is freed even while living amid the world's spread.
Mind and breath, the two, I have made the gourds, and (the Lord) of all the ages the stem (of my kingri);
the string has grown steady and will not break; the kingri sounds, unstruck (Anhad).
Hearing it, the mind is wholly absorbed, and Maya's shaking does not reach it.
Says Kabir: there is no birth again for the bairagi who has played (this game) and departed. ॥4॥
335.1: Raag Gauri, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
Nine yards, ten yards and twenty-one yards: one full warp has been stretched (on the loom of the body);
(in it are) sixty threads and nine joined pieces, and a weft of seventy-two (threads) is added over and above.
Maho, (the mind's craving,) has gone to have (this cloth) woven;
when (his true) home is left, the weaver (the soul) sets out (into birth).
It is not measured in yards, nor weighed on scales, (yet each day) its sizing is two and a half seers;
if it does not get its sizing in good time, it raises a quarrel within the house itself.
For a stay of a few days (the soul) turns against the Master; how will this hour come (again)?
The troughs are left behind, the bobbins stay wet, and the weaver departs in vexation.
The bobbin is empty, no thread comes out, and the beam stays tangled (in the threads) no more.
Says Kabir, teaching her: poor wretch, leave this spread (of entanglement) and stay here. ॥4॥
335.2: Raag Gauri, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
When one's light has merged in the One, does (a separate self) remain? It does not.
The one in whose heart the Naam does not spring up, that person bursts (with ego) and dies.
O dark and beautiful Ram, my dear one,
my mind is fixed on you.
When the Saadh (the Guru) is met, fulfilment is attained, whether one lives in yoga or in the world's enjoyments.
When the two (the Guru and the disciple) meet, the work bears fruit: union through the Name of Ram.
People take this for a song, but it is reflection on God (Brahm),
like the teaching given in Kashi to a man at the hour of his death.
Whoever sings or hears the Name of the Lord with the mind attuned,
says Kabir: there is no doubt; in the end he attains the supreme state. ॥4॥
335.3: Raag Gauri, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
All who make (such) efforts have drowned; (these efforts) have not carried (them) across the world-ocean, O brother.
Performing rites, religious duties and many disciplines, (their) mind is burnt up by the ego-intellect, O brother.
The Master is the giver of breath and food; why have you forgotten him from your mind, O brother?
(Human) birth is a diamond, a priceless ruby; you have lost it in exchange for a cowrie shell, O brother.
Through wandering, craving, thirst and hunger cling to you; you have not reflected in your heart, O brother.
Intoxicated, robbed by pride within your mind, you have not held the Guru's Shabad (within), O brother.
Greedy for tastes, driven by the pleasures of the senses, you take the heady relish of vices, O brother.
Those whose destiny holds good deeds join the Sants; (the Lord) saves them, as wood carries iron across, O brother.
Running, wandering through species and births, I am weary; now, worn by suffering, I have given up, O brother.
Says Kabir: on meeting the Guru (I found) the supreme relish; loving devotion has carried (me) across, O brother. ॥4॥
335.4: Raag Gauri, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
Like the she-elephant built on a frame (to trap an elephant), O crazed mind, is the play the Lord of the world has staged:
through the lure of lust the elephant is caught, O crazed mind, and bears the goad upon his head.
Keep clear of vices and merge in the Lord; understand this, O crazed mind.
You have not become fearless and worshipped the Lord, O crazed mind; you have not taken hold of the ship of Ram.
The monkey stretched out his hand and grabbed a fistful of grain, O crazed mind;
then the worry of getting free fell on him, O crazed mind, and he was made to dance at the door of house after house.
As the parrot is caught by the nalini, O crazed mind, such is the dealing of Maya.
As is the colour of safflower (bright, and soon gone), O crazed mind, so is this expanse spread out.
There are many tiraths to bathe at, O crazed mind, and many gods to worship;
says Kabir: (by these) there is no release, O crazed mind; release lies in the service of the Lord. ॥4॥
336.1: Raag Gauri, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
Fire does not burn it, wind does not blow it away, no thief comes near it:
gather the wealth of the Name of Ram; that wealth goes nowhere.
My wealth is Madho, Gobind, who upholds the earth; this, it is said, is wealth of the finest kind.
The peace that lies in serving God, Gobind, is not to be had in kingship.
For this wealth Shiv and Sanak and his brothers searched, and became detached (from the world).
With Mukand in the mind and Narayan on the tongue, the noose of Jam does not fall (on one).
The Guru has given (me) wealth truly my own, divine knowledge and devotion; with good understanding (my) mind is fixed on it.
(It is) water for the burning, a pillar for the running mind; the fear of doubt's bonds has fled.
Says Kabir: O you drunk with desire, reflect and see in your heart:
your house holds lakhs and crores of horses and elephants; my house holds the one Murari. ॥4॥
336.2: Raag Gauri, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
As the monkey, in his greed, would not let go the fistful of chickpeas in his hand,
(so) whatever deeds were done in greed, those in turn fell around (one's) neck.
Without devotion, life has gone in vain;
without the Saadh Sangat and the worship of the Lord (Bhagvan), the True One has abided nowhere.
As a flower blossoms in the wilderness and no one takes its fragrance,
so (beings) wander through many species, and are slain by death again and again.
This wealth, youth, sons and wife, which (the Lord) gave (only) to behold:
those who stick fast in these very things and are entangled, the senses have pulled them along.
The passing of life is a fire, the body a house of straw; on all four sides this is how it is built.
Says Kabir: to cross the terrifying ocean, I have taken refuge with the True Guru. ॥4॥
336.3: Raag Gauri, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
The water (the father's seed) is unclean, the clay (the mother's blood) is red;
of this clay a puppet has been put together.
I am nothing, and nothing is mine;
body, wealth and all (its) life-sap are yours, O Gobind.
Into this clay the breath (of life) has entered,
and (on it) a false show has been put together and set going.
Someone has amassed five lakh (in wealth);
at the last hour the pitcher (of the body) broke.
Says Kabir: the foundation that has been raised
is destroyed in an instant, O proud one. ॥4॥
337.1: Raag Gauri, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
O my soul, let me repeat (the Name of) Ram in such a way,
as Dhru and Prahlad repeated (the Name of) the Lord.
O merciful to the meek, trusting in you
I have put all my family aboard the boat.
When it pleases him, he makes (them) obey his Hukam,
By the Guru's grace such understanding has entered (me)
that coming and going (in births) again has ended.
on this shore and the far shore, know the One alone in all. ॥4॥
337.2: Raag Gauri 9, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
When, leaving the womb, (a being) came into the world,
as soon as the air (of the world) touched it, it forgot the Master.
O my soul, sing the praises of the Lord.
In the womb it practised austerity, hanging head down;
then it lived (unharmed) in the fire of the belly.
Wandering through the eighty-four lakh forms of life, it has come (to this birth);
if it misses this time, there is no place or resting place (for it).
(a being) is seen coming, but its going is not known. ॥4॥
337.3: Raag Gauri Poorbi, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
Let us not crave a dwelling in heaven, nor fear a dwelling in hell;
what is to be will be; let us not build hopes in the mind.
Let us sing the praises of the dear Lord (Ramaiya),
from whom the supreme treasure is obtained.
What use is chanting, what use austerity and self-discipline, what use fasting, what use bathing (at tiraths),
as long as the way of loving devotion to the Lord (Bhagvan) is not known?
Let us not be elated at the sight of prosperity, nor weep at the sight of adversity;
as prosperity is, so is adversity: what the Creator has ordained comes to pass.
Says Kabir: now I have come to know (that the Lord dwells) within the hearts of the Sants;
those servants are good in (their) service in whose hearts Murari dwells. ॥4॥
337.4: Raag Gauri, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
O mind, no one is yours; do not drag (others') burden onto yourself.
Like the birds' night-roost in a tree, such is this world.
I have drunk the relish of Ram, O brother,
through which relish all other relishes are forgotten.
Why weep when others die, when one's own self does not stay fixed?
Whatever is born will perish; let misfortune weep in grief, not I.
(My soul) is absorbed in the One from whom it sprang, drinking (this relish) in the company of the brave (devotees).
Says Kabir: I have kept (Ram) in my mind; remembering Ram, (I have found) detachment. ॥3॥
337.5: Raag Gauri, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
The woman watches the road; her eyes brimming (with tears), she heaves deep sighs;
her heart is not soothed, her foot does not stir, in the hope of the sight of the Lord.
that I may soon meet my beloved Ram.
Says Kabir: to attain the state of (true) life, let devotion to the Lord be practised;
the Name of Narayan is the one support: let the tongue repeat Ram. ॥2॥
338.1: Raag Gauri 11, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
(He) around whom grew thick clumps of tulsi (holy basil), who sang with love in the midst of the woods:
beholding his form, the milkmaid was enchanted (and said): do not leave me to come or go (elsewhere).
My mind is fixed on your feet, O Saringdhar (the Lord who bears the bow);
he alone meets you who is greatly fortunate.
In Brindaban, he who steals the mind, the enchanting Krishna, grazes the cows;
O Saringdhar, (I am the one) whose Master you are; my name is Kabir. ॥2॥
338.2: Raag Gauri Poorbi 12, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
Many have put on ample (holy) robes; what (comes) of living in the forest?
What came of it, O man, if gods were worshipped with incense? What, if (the body) was knowingly drowned in water?
O soul, you will depart: this I know.
Understand the Unmanifest (Lord), O ignorant one.
Whatever I look upon, I do not see again; (yet you) are wrapped up in Maya.
The learned, the meditative, the great preachers: this whole world is (caught in Maya's) entanglement.
Says Kabir: lacking the Name of the one Ram, this world goes blind in Maya. ॥2॥
338.3: Raag Gauri 12, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
O mind, you whom this Maya holds to punishment, give up doubt and dance in the open.
What warrior is he who shrinks from the battle he faces? What sati is she who gathers up her pots?
Give up wavering, O crazed mind;
now that the sindhaura has been taken in hand, fulfilment comes only by burning and dying.
Seized by lust, anger and Maya, in this way the world is ruined.
Says Kabir: I will not forsake Ram, the King, the highest of all the high. ॥2॥
338.4: Raag Gauri 13, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
I bear your command upon my head; I do not turn round to weigh it.
You are the river, you are the boatman; from you alone comes deliverance.
O man, take up the worship (of the Lord),
whether the Master shows anger or love.
Your Name is my support, as the flower lives in water.
Says Kabir: I am the slave of your house; keep me alive or kill me, as you please. ॥2॥
338.5: Raag Gauri, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
(You say that) Nand grew very weary, wandering among the beings of the eighty-four lakh forms of life,
and for (his) devotion (God) took birth (in his house): great was the fortune of that poor man.
You who say, O brother, that (God became) the son of Nand: whose son, then, was that Nand?
When there was neither earth nor sky, nor the ten directions, where then was this Nand?
He falls into no affliction (of birth and death) and enters no womb, the One whose Name is Niranjan.
Such is Kabir's Lord and Master: he has neither mother nor father. ॥2॥
339.1: Raag Gauri, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
Let people slander me, slander me, slander me (as much as they like);
to (the Lord's) servant, slander is truly dear;
If slander comes, one goes to Baikunth,
and the treasure of the Naam is made to dwell in the mind.
If slander comes while the heart is pure,
Whoever slanders me is my friend;
my mind stays on the slanderer.
The (true) slanderer is the one who holds back slander (of me);
the slanderer wants my life (to be made good).
Slander of me is love and affection (to me);
For the servant Kabir, slander is the best (of things):
the slanderer has drowned, and I have crossed over. ॥3॥
339.2: O Ram, the King, so fearless are you; you are the boat that carries (beings) across, O Sovereign Ram.
When I was (in my ego), you were not (in me); now you are, and I am not.
Now we two, you and I, are one; beholding the One alone, my mind is at rest.
When (pride in my own) cleverness held sway, what strength (of spirit) was there? Now (pride in) cleverness and strength no longer holds.
Says Kabir: (the Lord) has taken away my (proud) intellect; my intellect is changed, and (I) have reached fulfilment. ॥2॥
339.3: Raag Gauri, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
Of six rings (the five elements and the mind) the little room (of the body) has been built, and an incomparable thing has been placed within it;
the breath of life has been made its lock and key; in making it, (the Creator) took no time.
Now stay awake, O mind, O brother:
heedless, (you) have wasted your life; the thief goes in and plunders the house.
Five watchmen (the senses) stay at the door, but there is no trusting them.
Keep (the Lord) in mind, stay alert in your thought, and then you will receive the light, the brightness (within).
The soul-bride who, seeing the nine houses (of the body), went astray has not found the incomparable thing.
Says Kabir: when the nine houses are plundered (their hold stripped away), in the tenth the essence (of the Lord) is found abiding. ॥3॥
339.4: Raag Gauri, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
O mother, I have known no other, none besides (the Lord):
my breath of life dwells in him whose virtues Shiv and Sanak and the others sing.
By the wisdom the Guru has imparted, the heart is lit, and attention is fixed in the realm of the sky (the Tenth Gate).
The diseases of the senses' pleasures, fear and bonds have fled; in its own home the mind has known peace.
(My) good understanding is in love with the One; knowing God and trusting him, (I) bring no second into my mind.
The mind's cravings given up, there is (within) the fragrance of sandalwood, and pride has dwindled.
The servant who sings and meditates on the Master's praise: in him God makes his dwelling.
Great is the fortune of one in whose mind (God) has come to dwell; the highest destiny is on his forehead.
Shakti (Maya) cut away, the Sahaj of Shiv (the Lord) has shone forth, and (the mind) has merged in the One alone.
Says Kabir: in meeting the Guru there is supreme peace; the wandering has ended, and the mind is at rest. ॥4॥
340.1: Raag Gauri Poorbi, Bavan Akhri: the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
There is one God, Ik Oankar, the One who pervades all and is ever the same; his Name is Sat (the One who truly is); he is the Creator, the Being who dwells in all, realised by the Guru's grace.
Fifty-two letters (serve) the three worlds; all things are (held) in these alone.
These letters will wear away; those letters (that could tell of union with the Lord) are not among them. ॥1॥
340.2: Where there is speech, letters come in;
where (the state) beyond speech is, there the mind itself does not remain.
In speech and in the speechless alike, he alone is;
(yet) as he truly is, so no one can perceive him. ॥2॥
340.3: If I find the Unfindable, what can I say (of him)? And if I do speak, what good is it?
As the banyan lies in its seed, so he pervades (all), the One whose spread is the three worlds. ॥3॥
340.4: Seeking the Unfindable, (my) sense of separateness has been destroyed, and I have grasped something of (his) mystery.
With separateness overturned, the mind is pierced (with the Lord), and (I) have found the One who cannot be broken or pierced. ॥4॥
340.5: The Turk (the Muslim) is known by the tariqat, the Hindu by the Vedas and the Puranas;
(but) for the mind's instruction, one should read something of (divine) wisdom. ॥5॥
340.6: Oankar (the all-pervading Lord) I have known as the Origin (of all);
the one whom he writes and erases I do not accept (as God).
then, having perceived him, (that one) is not destroyed. ॥6॥
340.7: Kaka: if I bring the ray (of the sun of wisdom) into the lotus (of the heart),
then in the light of the moon (of Maya) it does not close (again).
And if there I taste the nectar of the flower,
it is beyond telling: what can I say? What can I explain by speaking? ॥7॥
340.8: Khakha: (when) this mind comes into the hollow (of its own true self),
it does not leave the hollow to run off in the ten directions.
One who, knowing the Master, abides in forbearance
then becomes imperishable and attains the undying state. ॥8॥
340.9: Gaga: one who has recognised the Guru's word
lends no ear to any other talk.
He lives like a bird (unattached), and strays nowhere;
he takes hold of the Ungraspable (in his heart), and, holding him, keeps to the sky within (the Tenth Gate). ॥9॥
340.10: Ghagha: in every body he alone dwells;
when the pitcher (of the body) breaks, he is never lessened.
When one finds within that very body the ford (for crossing over),
why would he leave that ford and run into pathless ravines? ॥10॥
340.11: Nganga: restrain (the senses), love (the Lord), and cast out doubt.
Do not run away on seeing that (it seems) it cannot be done: this is the highest wisdom. ॥11॥
340.12: Chacha: (this world) that he has made is a vast picture;
leave the picture and keep the Painter in mind.
This is the snare: the picture is wondrous (and enticing);
leave the picture, and keep your mind on the Painter. ॥12॥
340.13: Chhachha: the Sovereign of the royal canopy is right here beside (you);
why not stay absorbed (in him)? Why not give up (other) hopes?
O mind, every moment I counsel you:
leaving him, where are you getting yourself bound? ॥13॥
340.14: Jaja: when one burns (the cravings of) the body while still alive,
burning away (the pride of) youth, he finds the (true) way (to live).
When, burning away (the sense of) mine and others', he lives on, enduring (all),
then he goes on (to the higher state) and finds the brightness of the (divine) Light. ॥14॥
341.1: Jhajha: one who (learned only) to be entangled, and never knew how to get free,
stayed hesitating, and was not accepted.
What (use) is it to wrangle and wrangle to instruct others?
By quarrelling, only quarrels are gained. ॥15॥
341.2: Nyanya: he dwells close by, in the heart; forsaking him, where do you go so far?
The One for whom I searched the world, I found close at hand. ॥16॥
341.3: Tatta: the hard ford (to the Lord) is within the heart itself;
why not open the doors (of Maya) and go into (the Lord's) mansion?
Seeing the Unmoving One, (the mind) does not waver and go elsewhere;
it stays clinging (to him), and in the heart comes to know him intimately. ॥17॥
341.4: Thattha: this (Maya) is deceiving water seen from afar (a mirage);
looking closely, again and again, I have made (my) mind steady.
The cheat who by cheating has swallowed the whole world:
by cheating that cheat, (my) mind has come to its place of rest. ॥18॥
341.5: Dadda: when (God's) fear arises, (worldly) fear goes;
in that fear (every other) fear is absorbed.
If one shrinks in fear from (God's) fear, then (worldly) fear clings again.
One who has (so) become fearless: whatever fear is in his heart runs away. ॥19॥
341.6: Dhaddha: (the Lord is) near; why search for (him) elsewhere?
In the very searching, the breath of life is spent.
When, having climbed Sumer and searched, (I) came back,
the One who built the fortress (of the body) I found within the fortress. ॥20॥
341.7: Nanna: the man who, engaged on the battlefield, holds firm,
who neither bows down (to the vices) nor goes along (with them):
his birth alone (the world) counts blessed,
(for he) slays the one (the mind) and leaves the many (vices) behind. ॥21॥
341.8: Tata: (the world-ocean) is uncrossable; it cannot be crossed,
(while) the body (with its senses) stays sunk in (the things of) the three worlds.
When the three worlds are absorbed within the body,
then essence (the soul) merges with essence (the Lord), and the True One is found. ॥22॥
341.9: Thatha: the depth of the Fathomless cannot be found;
he is fathomless, and this (mind) does not stay still.
On a little patch of ground it sets about (building great) towns,
and would hold up a mansion with no pillars at all. ॥23॥
341.10: Dada: all that is seen is bound to perish;
keep in your thought the One who is unseen, as he is.
When the key is turned in the Tenth Gate,
then one has the sight of the Merciful One. ॥24॥
341.11: Dhadha: the lower (the soul) finds its settlement in the Higher (the Lord),
(when) the lower dwells within the Higher.
When (the soul) leaves the lower (state) and comes up to the higher,
then the lower and the Higher meet, and peace is found. ॥25॥
341.12: Nana: night and day pass in watching (for the Lord);
watching, the eyes have grown red (with love).
When, watching and watching, (one) at last finds (him),
then the One watched for takes the watcher and unites (him with himself). ॥26॥
341.13: Pappa: the end of the One beyond whom there is none cannot be found;
one who has formed a bond with the Supreme Light
holds all five senses in check,
and puts away both sin and virtue. ॥27॥
341.14: Phapha: without flowering (into pride), the fruit (of life) comes;
if anyone perceives even a sliver of that fruit
and reflects on that sliver, he does not fall into the valley (of birth and death);
a sliver of that fruit tears apart all (attachment to) the body. ॥28॥
341.15: Babba: (as) a drop merges with a drop,
(so the soul) that comes to know (the Lord) even for a moment cannot be parted (from him again).
One who becomes (the Lord's) servant and holds fast to his worship,
becoming one who sings his praise, sees through the bonds (of Maya). ॥29॥
342.1: Bhabha: (the one who) has pierced the gulf (between him and the Lord) and joined (his mind to him),
now, with fear shattered, has come to trust (in the Lord).
The (Lord) who is outside (in all the world) he has known (dwelling) within;
(when) the secret was opened, he recognised the Master of the earth. ॥30॥
342.2: Mamma: holding fast to the Root (of all), the mind is won over (and stops wandering);
one who knows this secret comes to understand the mind.
When the mind is coming to meet (the Lord), let no one delay:
absorbed (in him), one finds the True (Lord). ॥31॥
342.3: Mamma: (one's real) task is with the mind; by disciplining the mind, success is won.
Says Kabir: (the dealing) is with the mind alone, with the mind; I have met no other like the mind. ॥32॥
342.4: This mind is Shakti (Maya), this mind is Shiv (the Lord, the giver of good);
this mind is what gives life to the body of five elements.
When (one) takes this mind in hand and dwells in the state of unman,
then he speaks of (the Lord who fills) the three worlds. ॥33॥
342.5: Yaya: if you would know (the way), destroy your evil-mindedness and bring the village of the body under your rule.
Locked in battle, if (you) do not run away, (only) then do you bear the name of hero. ॥34॥
342.6: Rara: (the one who) has known the relish (of Maya) as tasteless,
becoming free of (these) relishes, has recognised that relish (of the Name).
By giving up these relishes, that relish has been found;
(whoever) has drunk that nectar, this relish does not please (him). ॥35॥
342.7: Lala: if the mind fixes its attention (on the Lord) in such a way
that it goes nowhere else, it finds the Supreme, the True (Lord);
and if there it fixes the attention of love,
then it finds the Unfindable (Lord), and having found him, merges in his feet. ॥36॥
342.8: Vava: again and again remember Bisan (the Lord);
remembering Bisan, one does not come away defeated (in the game of life).
I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice, to the son of Bisan (his devotee) who sings his praise;
meeting Bisan, one finds the True (Lord) everywhere. ॥37॥
342.9: Vaava: him alone should we know; by knowing him, this (soul) becomes (one with him).
When this (soul) and that (Lord) meet, then, once met, no one can know them apart. ॥38॥
342.10: Sassa: search him out (and remember him) with all care;
hold (the mind) to the words by which the heart is won over (to the Lord).
When the heart is won over and love wells up,
there the King of the three worlds is (seen) filling all. ॥39॥
342.11: Khakha: if anyone sets out to search (for the Lord),
whoever finds (him) does not come (into birth) again.
If (one) understands the signs (of the Lord) and reflects (on his virtues),
then (he) is not long in crossing the world-ocean. ॥40॥
342.12: Sassa: she (the soul-bride) adorns the bed (of the heart) for her Husband Lord;
she alone, the friend, is rid of (her) doubt,
(who) has given up petty pleasure and gained the supreme bliss;
then this one is called the wife, and that one the Husband. ॥41॥
342.13: Haha: having come into (human) being, (one) has not known (the Lord) who truly is.
Only when (the certainty of his being) comes is the mind won over.
He surely is, if anyone could perceive it;
then (the soul) is he himself, and is no longer this (separate self). ॥42॥
342.14: All the world goes about crying, Let me take, let me take;
for its sake, great sorrow besets (them).
When (one) fixes his attention on the Husband of Lakshmi (the Lord),
sorrow is wiped out, and he finds every comfort. ॥43॥
342.15: Khakha: wasting and wearing away, many (lives) have gone by;
wasting and wearing away, (one) does not remember (the Lord) even now.
Now, if knowing (what) the world (is), the mind holds steady (in the Lord),
it finds a firm place there, (in the Lord) from whom it was parted. ॥44॥
343.1: (People) have brought the fifty-two letters and joined them together,
(but) they could not recognise the One Akhar (the Imperishable).
Kabir speaks the Shabad of the True (Lord);
one who is a (true) pandit abides in the direct experience (of the Lord).
For pandits (these letters) are a trade,
for the wise, (a means of) reflecting on the essence.
As the understanding is in one's heart,
Says Kabir: so will that one know. ॥45॥
343.2: Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Raag Gauri, Thiti: the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
(People keep) the fifteen lunar days and the seven weekdays;
Says Kabir: (I sing the Lord, who has) neither a near shore nor a far one.
When seekers and Siddhas come to know his secret,
(they see that) he himself is the Creator, he himself the Lord of light. ॥1॥
343.3: Amavas: on the new-moon day, let go of the hopes (you set on fasts and rites);
remember Ram, the Knower of hearts.
(So) while yet alive you will reach the gate of liberation,
and the Shabad, known by direct experience, (will be) the finest essence of your own self. ॥1॥
343.4: One who is dyed with love for the lotus feet of Gobind,
by the grace of the Sant (the Guru) has become pure in mind; night and day he stays awake in the Kirtan of the Lord.
343.5: Pariva: reflect on (the virtues of) the Beloved,
who, bodiless and boundless, plays within every body.
The dread of death never eats away at (the one who reflects on him),
(for) he stays merged in the Primal Being. ॥2॥
343.6: Dutiya: (such a one) knows (the world) as made of two parts,
Maya and Brahm (God); (God) pervades along with all.
without lineage, the Niranjan stays ever the same. ॥3॥
343.7: Tritiya: one who brings the three (qualities of Maya) into balance
attains the supreme state, the source of bliss.
In the Saadh Sangat faith wells up (in him)
that outside and within there is always (the Lord's) light. ॥4॥
343.8: Chauthahi: keep hold of the fickle mind,
and never sit in the company of lust and anger.
He who is himself all in all, in the water and on the land:
(joined) to him, repeat the chant that is truly your own. ॥5॥
343.9: Panchai: (this world) is a spread of the five elements;
(in it) the business of the two, gold and woman, (goes on).
Rare is the one who drinks the nectar of love (for the Lord);
the pain of old age and death does not come (to him) again. ॥6॥
343.10: Chhath: the six wheels (the five senses and the mind) run in all six directions;
unless won over (to the Lord), they do not stay still.
Erase duality and hold fast to forbearance,
(and) do not suffer the torment of rituals and rites. ॥7॥
343.11: Saatain: know the Word (of the Guru) as true,
(and) take the all-pervading Lord (Atam Ram) to heart.
(So) doubt is cast off, sorrows are wiped away,
and in the pool of Sunn you will find peace. ॥8॥
343.12: Astami: the body is (made) of eight elements;
within it dwells the (Lord) without lineage, the King of the great treasure.
The one to whom the wisdom of the Guru, who has reached (him), tells this secret
turns back (from love of the body) and dwells in the Indestructible, the Impenetrable. ॥9॥
343.13: Naumi: discipline the nine doors (of the body),
and keep bound the desires of the mind that flow out (through them).
Forget greed, attachment and all (the vices);
(then) you will live through the ages and eat the fruit that never perishes. ॥10॥
344.1: Dasmi: there is bliss in all ten directions,
doubt departs, and Gobind is met,
who is the embodiment of light, the essence (of all), beyond compare,
stainless, without any stain; (there) is neither shade nor sunshine. ॥11॥
344.2: Ekadasi: if (the mind) runs in one direction (to the One),
then (one) does not come into the anguish of births again.
the (Lord) said to be far off is found close by. ॥12॥
344.3: Baras: twelve suns rise (within, as it were);
day and night the unstruck trumpets sound;
(one) sees the Master of the three worlds;
a wonder comes to pass: from a (mere) creature he becomes Shiv (one with the Lord). ॥13॥
344.4: Teras: (one who) on the thirteenth (day) tells of the Unreachable (Lord)
recognises (him) as the same, from below to above.
(For him) there is no low or high, no honour or dishonour:
344.5: in every hair (of them), dwells Murari (the Lord).
Fix your mind on truth and contentment,
(and) speak the words (that bring) the knowledge of Brahm (God). ॥15॥
344.6: Puniu: (as on the full-moon night) the moon is full in the sky,
(and all its) phases spread out, (so within) shines the light of Sahaj.
(The Lord) stays unmoving at the beginning, at the end and in between;
Kabir delights in (him), the ocean of peace. ॥16॥
344.7: Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Raag Gauri, Vaar Sat (the seven days): the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
Again and again I sing the virtues of the Lord;
reaching the Guru, I find that secret of the Lord.
Aadit: (one who) makes a beginning of devotion,
and in the temple of the body holds desire in check,
(his) attention flows on unbroken, day and night;
then the unstruck flute plays in Sahaj.
Somvar: the Amrit of the moon (its cool peace) trickles (within);
the moment it is tasted, it takes away every poison.
Held back by the Bani, (the mind) stays at (the Lord's) door;
then the mind, intoxicated, becomes the drinker (of that Amrit).
Mangalvar: (one) draws a wall (around the mind),
and comes to know the ways of the five thieves (lust and the rest).
Do not leave (this) house and go outside,
or else the King (the Lord) will be sorely angered.
Budhvar: (one) brings the light (of the Name) to the intellect,
(and) makes the heart-lotus the dwelling of the Lord.
Meeting the Guru, (one) holds the two (the soul and the Lord) as one,
(and) takes the upturned lotus (of the heart) and sets it upright.
Brihaspati: (one) washes away the poison (of Maya),
(and) joins the three gods to the One.
(Those who live) in the trikuti, (the fretting of Maya,) are (swept along) there in the three rivers (of the three qualities);
day and night they do not wash away (their) sins.
Sukrit: one who makes good deeds his support climbs (the steep path of) this vow:
night and day he fights against his own self;
he keeps all five senses in check;
then the eye of duality never enters (him).
Thavar: (one) keeps it steady,
the little lamp of (the Lord's) light that (burns) in the heart;
outside and within, light shines;
then all (past) karma is destroyed.
As long as the heart leans on another,
so long is there no entering the mansion (of the Lord).
Remembering Ram, love for Ram takes hold;
Says Kabir: then every limb becomes pure. ॥8॥
345.1: Raag Gauri Cheti, the hymn of Bhagat Namdev Ji.
